+# Used by `cargo nextest run`. `cargo test` does not read this file.
+
+# These suites start a whole cluster of processes each — a coordinator, three
+# data nodes and a gateway — and pick their ports by binding, releasing, and
+# re-binding, which only stays race-free while one of them does it at a time.
+# They say so with an in-process lock, but nextest gives every test its own
+# process, so the lock cannot see the others. The group restores the same
+# guarantee across binaries.
+[test-groups]
+cluster = { max-threads = 1 }
+
+[[profile.default.overrides]]
+filter = 'binary(process_cluster)'
+test-group = "cluster"
+
+[[profile.default.overrides]]
+filter = 'binary(redis_gateway)'
+test-group = "cluster"
+
+[[profile.default.overrides]]
+filter = 'binary(experimental_redis_gateway)'
+test-group = "cluster"

-## Replication and guarantees
-
-### Acknowledgement policies
-
-| Policy                | A write succeeds when…                           | If the owner crashes                                                                                                 |
-| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
-| `OwnerOnly` (default) | the owner has applied it                         | **Acknowledged writes that the promoted follower had not yet applied are lost.** A key can revert to an older value. |
-| `FirstSuccessor`      | the first clockwise follower has also applied it | No loss from a single owner failure. Correlated failures can still lose data.                                        |
-| `AllReplicas`         | every desired follower has applied it            | Writes block unless the full placement is healthy.                                                                   |
-
-Followers are always updated asynchronously in the background. The policy only
-decides how long the client waits.
-
-Data nodes are in-memory under every policy. Losing enough processes loses data.
-`OwnerOnly` has no time bound on its loss window: `--max-replica-lag-ms`
-affects only the write guard and is not a recovery-point objective.
-
-### Write guard
-
-The write guard is a readiness check that runs before a write is accepted:
-
-- `--minimum-admitted-copies` (default 1, so the owner alone is enough)
-- `--minimum-healthy-followers` (default 0)
-- `--max-replica-lag-ms` (default 5000), which defines a "healthy" follower
-
-When the guard or the ACK policy cannot be met, writes fail. The cluster does
-not silently weaken the guarantee. A follower is admitted only after it has
-caught up from a verified snapshot and stream. The guard controls availability
-only; it does not make data durable.
-
-### Request semantics
-
-- **Versions** are `(topology_epoch, owner_sequence, owner_node_id)` and
-  migrations preserve them.
-- **`DELETE` is idempotent.** Success means the key is absent afterward,
-  whether or not it existed before.
-- **Retries.** Every logical operation has one overall deadline. Within it, the
-  client retries `Moved`, `RangeBusy`, and retryable `Unavailable` or
-  `ResourceExhausted` responses with jittered backoff, refreshing the topology
-  as needed. `NotFound`, `TooLarge`, `InvalidArgument`, and permanent gRPC
-  errors return immediately.
-- **Unknown outcomes.** If a mutation was sent but its response was lost, the
-  final error reports `unknown_write_outcome=true`. A follow-up `DELETE` that
-  succeeds confirms the key is absent.
-- **Deduplication.** The client keeps one request ID across retries of a
-  logical write. Nodes keep in-memory receipts for the cluster's receipt
-  retention period (60 seconds by default), so a retry is not applied twice,
-  and the client stops retrying a mutation within that period. A new CLI
-  invocation uses a new ID, and receipts are lost if the node restarts.
-
-### Limits
-
-| Limit                                | Value     |
-| ------------------------------------ | --------- |
-| Key size                             | 64 KiB    |
-| Value size                           | 8 MiB     |
-| Members per cluster                  | 1,024     |
-| Virtual nodes per member             | 4,096     |
-| Total token assignments              | 1,048,576 |
-| Ranges moved per change              | 16,384    |
-| Pending replication buffer per node  | 64 MiB    |
-| Deduplication receipt store per node | 128 MiB   |
-| Migration journal per node (default) | 16 MiB    |
-
-### Not provided
-
-Transactions, durable data-node storage, and coordinator failover or consensus.
-
-## Changing the cluster
-
-All changes follow the same two steps. `begin-*` stages the change and prints
-its ID and epochs. `execute-change` then runs it. Passing the ID and both
-epochs back means an ambiguous retry can never execute a different change.
-
-### Add or remove nodes
-
-Pass the **complete** target membership. For example, to add `node-4`:
-
-```sh
-cargo run -- begin-change \
-  --member node-1=http://127.0.0.1:50051 \
-  --member node-2=http://127.0.0.1:50052 \
-  --member node-3=http://127.0.0.1:50053 \
-  --member node-4=http://127.0.0.1:50054
-
-# Start the new node once it appears in the pending topology.
-cargo run -- node --id node-4 --listen 127.0.0.1:50054
-
-# Use the change ID and epochs printed by begin-change.
-cargo run -- execute-change --change-id CHANGE_ID --base-epoch 1 --target-epoch 2
-
-cargo run -- change-status
-cargo run -- replica-status
-```
-
-Rules:
-
-- Existing nodes must keep their endpoints. Each node ID is fenced to the
-  process instance that registered it, so the coordinator rejects an empty
-  replacement under the same ID instead of letting it serve false misses.
-- Removed nodes are told to shut down once their ranges have been handed off.
-- Interrupted changes resume automatically when the coordinator restarts.
-
-What happens during a move: the source keeps serving while a snapshot is
-copied. Up to 16 ranges move in parallel (`--range-move-concurrency`).
-Concurrent writes are replayed from a changelog. At cutover, affected writes
-get a retryable `RangeBusy`. The coordinator then checks the record count,
-watermark, and a BLAKE3 digest before it publishes the new epoch. A failure
-before publication aborts cleanly. After publication, the epoch never rolls
-back.
-
-See [docs/operations.md](docs/operations.md) for failure recovery during a
-change, `replica-status` fields, and internal timers.
-
-### Change the ACK policy, RF, or write guard
-
-```sh
-cargo run -- begin-policy-change --policy first-successor
-# or: cargo run -- begin-config-change --desired-replication-factor 2
-cargo run -- execute-change --change-id CHANGE_ID --base-epoch E --target-epoch E_PLUS_1
-```
-
-Writes pause briefly, and the new epoch is published only after its readiness
-check passes. See
-[replica ACK performance](docs/optimizations/replica-ack-performance.md) for
-the cost of each policy.
-
-## Experiments
-
-`experiment` starts a coordinator and data nodes as real child processes,
-drives a workload through the client, and writes the results into a new or
-empty directory:
-
-```sh
-cargo build --release
-
-# Scale 9 → 10 → 9 nodes under concurrent writes and deletes, verifying every key.
-target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode correctness --require-clean-source \
-  --output results/correctness
-
-# Throughput and latency with 10 nodes and 1,000,000 keys.
-target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode performance --require-clean-source \
-  --output results/performance
-
-# Kill an owner, measure failover, data loss, and repair time.
-target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode availability --policy first-successor \
-  --output results/availability
-
-# Kill three owners in a row, replacing each one before the next failure.
-target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode availability --availability-rounds 3 \
-  --nodes 9 --output results/availability-consecutive
-
-# Offer a fixed rate and measure the latency of that load, one stage per rate.
-target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode latency --target-rates 5000,10000,20000 \
-  --output results/latency
-
-# Keep mixed reads and writes running across 9 -> 10 -> 9 nodes, and verify
-# every cohort after each change.
-target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode scaling \
-  --output results/scaling
-
-# Keep a mixed load running while a follower or an owner fails, and verify the
-# request ledger and every key after the replacement reaches full RF.
-target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode fault --fault-scenario follower \
-  --nodes 5 --output results/fault-follower
-target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode fault --fault-scenario owner \
-  --nodes 5 --output results/fault-owner
-```
-
-Experiment settings can also come from a YAML file whose keys are the flag
-names with `_` for `-` (see [`examples/experiment.yaml`](examples/experiment.yaml)).
-Flags on the command line win over the file:
-
-```sh
-target/release/hashring-rs experiment --config examples/experiment.yaml \
-  --output results/availability
-```
-
-The output directory holds a manifest of the configuration and build, an
-event log, per-process logs, the coordinator database, and a JSON summary. See
-[docs/experiments.md](docs/experiments.md) for defaults, summary fields,
-profiling, and how to compare runs.

+# hashring-rs
+
+A replicated, in-memory key-value cache built on consistent hashing.
+
+- **Single owner per key.** Each virtual-node range on the hash ring has one
+  owner and up to `RF-1` followers on distinct physical nodes. `PUT`, `GET`,
+  and `DELETE` are linearizable per key.
+- **Durable coordinator.** One coordinator stores membership, epochs, token
+  assignments, and in-flight migrations in a transactional
+  [redb](https://github.com/cberner/redb) file. Data nodes keep everything in
+  memory.
+- **Online membership changes.** Ranges move while the cluster serves traffic.
+  Writes to a moving range pause briefly at cutover. Reads continue throughout.
+- **One binary, plain gRPC.** The same executable runs the coordinator, a data
+  node, or the client/admin CLI. Processes can run locally, in containers, or
+  on separate hosts.
+
+> **Status: experimental.** There are no compatibility guarantees for the CLI,
+> wire protocol, or coordinator state file. You may have to delete old state
+> after upgrading.
+
+## Quick start
+
+Start a coordinator with three members, then the three data nodes, each in its
+own terminal:
+
+```sh
+cargo run -- coordinator --state ./coordinator.redb \
+  --member node-1=http://127.0.0.1:50051 \
+  --member node-2=http://127.0.0.1:50052 \
+  --member node-3=http://127.0.0.1:50053
+
+cargo run -- node --id node-1 --listen 127.0.0.1:50051
+cargo run -- node --id node-2 --listen 127.0.0.1:50052
+cargo run -- node --id node-3 --listen 127.0.0.1:50053
+```
+
+The coordinator listens on `127.0.0.1:50050` by default, and every other
+command connects there unless you pass `--coordinator`.
+
+Read and write some keys:
+
+```sh
+cargo run -- put    --key greeting --value hello
+cargo run -- get    --key greeting
+cargo run -- delete --key greeting
+```
+
+Use `--key-hex`, `--value-hex`, and `get --hex` for binary data.
+
+Inspect the cluster:
+
+```sh
+cargo run -- topology        # ring layout as JSON
+cargo run -- replica-status  # per-range owner, followers, lag, and repair state
+```

+`--member` is only read when the state file is first created. To restart the
+coordinator, pass just `--state`. Everything else is loaded from the file.
+Passing `--member` on a restart compares those flags with the stored topology,
+so a cluster whose membership or configuration changed since the store was
+created has to be restarted with `--state` alone.

+| `execute-change`                 | Run the staged change through to publication                                                         |
+| `change-status`                  | Show the active change, if any                                                                       |
+| `redis-gateway`                  | Serve the Redis protocol on a port, over this cluster                                                |
+| `redis-lua-experimental-gateway` | Serve the shared gateway with experimental Lua support; requires `--features redis-lua-experimental` |
+| `experiment`                     | Run a reproducible multi-process experiment                                                          |
+
+Run `cargo run -- <command> --help` for each command's flags.
+For the Lua command, use
+`cargo run --features redis-lua-experimental -- redis-lua-experimental-gateway --help`.
+
+## Replication and guarantees
+
+### Acknowledgement policies
+
+| Policy                | A write succeeds when…                           | If the owner crashes                                                                                                 |
+| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `OwnerOnly` (default) | the owner has applied it                         | **Acknowledged writes that the promoted follower had not yet applied are lost.** A key can revert to an older value. |
+| `FirstSuccessor`      | the first clockwise follower has also applied it | No loss from a single owner failure. Correlated failures can still lose data.                                        |
+| `AllReplicas`         | every desired follower has applied it            | Writes block unless the full placement is healthy.                                                                   |
+
+Followers are always updated asynchronously in the background. The policy only
+decides how long the client waits.
+
+Data nodes are in-memory under every policy. Losing enough processes loses data.
+`OwnerOnly` has no time bound on its loss window: `--max-replica-lag-ms`
+affects only the write guard and is not a recovery-point objective.
+
+### Write guard
+
+The write guard is a readiness check that runs before a write is accepted:
+
+- `--minimum-admitted-copies` (default 1, so the owner alone is enough)
+- `--minimum-healthy-followers` (default 0)
+- `--max-replica-lag-ms` (default 5000), which defines a "healthy" follower
+
+When the guard or the ACK policy cannot be met, writes fail. The cluster does
+not silently weaken the guarantee. A follower is admitted only after it has
+caught up from a verified snapshot and stream. The guard controls availability
+only; it does not make data durable.
+
+### Request semantics
+
+- **Versions** are `(topology_epoch, owner_sequence, owner_node_id)` and
+  migrations preserve them.
+- **`DELETE` is idempotent.** Success means the key is absent afterward,
+  whether or not it existed before.
+- **Retries.** Every logical operation has one overall deadline. Within it, the
+  client retries `Moved`, `RangeBusy`, and retryable `Unavailable` or
+  `ResourceExhausted` responses with jittered backoff, refreshing the topology
+  as needed. `NotFound`, `TooLarge`, `InvalidArgument`, and permanent gRPC
+  errors return immediately.
+- **Unknown outcomes.** If a mutation was sent but its response was lost, the
+  final error reports `unknown_write_outcome=true`. A follow-up `DELETE` that
+  succeeds confirms the key is absent.
+- **Deduplication.** The client keeps one request ID across retries of a
+  logical write. Nodes keep in-memory receipts for the cluster's receipt
+  retention period (60 seconds by default), so a retry is not applied twice,
+  and the client stops retrying a mutation within that period. A new CLI
+  invocation uses a new ID, and receipts are lost if the node restarts.
+
+### Limits
+
+| Limit                                | Value     |
+| ------------------------------------ | --------- |
+| Key size                             | 64 KiB    |
+| Value size                           | 8 MiB     |
+| Members per cluster                  | 1,024     |
+| Virtual nodes per member             | 4,096     |
+| Total token assignments              | 1,048,576 |
+| Ranges moved per change              | 16,384    |
+| Pending replication buffer per node  | 64 MiB    |
+| Deduplication receipt store per node | 128 MiB   |
+| Migration journal per node (default) | 16 MiB    |
+
+### Not provided
+
+Transactions, durable data-node storage, and coordinator failover or consensus.
+
+## Changing the cluster
+
+All changes follow the same two steps. `begin-*` stages the change and prints
+its ID and epochs. `execute-change` then runs it. Passing the ID and both
+epochs back means an ambiguous retry can never execute a different change.
+
+### Add or remove nodes
+
+Pass the **complete** target membership. For example, to add `node-4`:
+
+```sh
+cargo run -- begin-change \
+  --member node-1=http://127.0.0.1:50051 \
+  --member node-2=http://127.0.0.1:50052 \
+  --member node-3=http://127.0.0.1:50053 \
+  --member node-4=http://127.0.0.1:50054
+
+# Start the new node once it appears in the pending topology.
+cargo run -- node --id node-4 --listen 127.0.0.1:50054
+
+# Use the change ID and epochs printed by begin-change.
+cargo run -- execute-change --change-id CHANGE_ID --base-epoch 1 --target-epoch 2
+
+cargo run -- change-status
+cargo run -- replica-status
+```
+
+Rules:
+
+- Existing nodes must keep their endpoints. Each node ID is fenced to the
+  process instance that registered it, so the coordinator rejects an empty
+  replacement under the same ID instead of letting it serve false misses.
+- Removed nodes are told to shut down once their ranges have been handed off.
+- Interrupted changes resume automatically when the coordinator restarts.
+
+What happens during a move: the source keeps serving while a snapshot is
+copied. Up to 16 ranges move in parallel (`--range-move-concurrency`).
+Concurrent writes are replayed from a changelog. At cutover, affected writes
+get a retryable `RangeBusy`. The coordinator then checks the record count,
+watermark, and a BLAKE3 digest before it publishes the new epoch. A failure
+before publication aborts cleanly. After publication, the epoch never rolls
+back.
+
+See [docs/operations.md](docs/operations.md) for failure recovery during a
+change, `replica-status` fields, and internal timers.
+
+### Change the ACK policy, RF, or write guard
+
+```sh
+cargo run -- begin-policy-change --policy first-successor
+# or: cargo run -- begin-config-change --desired-replication-factor 2
+cargo run -- execute-change --change-id CHANGE_ID --base-epoch E --target-epoch E_PLUS_1
+```
+
+Writes pause briefly, and the new epoch is published only after its readiness
+check passes. See
+[replica ACK performance](docs/optimizations/replica-ack-performance.md) for
+the cost of each policy.
+
+## Experiments
+
+`experiment` starts a coordinator and data nodes as real child processes,
+drives a workload through the client, and writes the results into a new or
+empty directory:
+
+```sh
+cargo build --release
+
+# Scale 9 → 10 → 9 nodes under concurrent writes and deletes, verifying every key.
+target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode correctness --require-clean-source \
+  --output results/correctness
+
+# Throughput and latency with 10 nodes and 1,000,000 keys.
+target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode performance --require-clean-source \
+  --output results/performance
+
+# Kill an owner, measure failover, data loss, and repair time.
+target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode availability --policy first-successor \
+  --output results/availability
+
+# Kill three owners in a row, replacing each one before the next failure.
+target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode availability --availability-rounds 3 \
+  --nodes 9 --output results/availability-consecutive
+
+# Offer a fixed rate and measure the latency of that load, one stage per rate.
+target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode latency --target-rates 5000,10000,20000 \
+  --output results/latency
+
+# Keep mixed reads and writes running across 9 -> 10 -> 9 nodes, and verify
+# every cohort after each change.
+target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode scaling \
+  --output results/scaling
+
+# Keep a mixed load running while a follower or an owner fails, and verify the
+# request ledger and every key after the replacement reaches full RF.
+target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode fault --fault-scenario follower \
+  --nodes 5 --output results/fault-follower
+target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode fault --fault-scenario owner \
+  --nodes 5 --output results/fault-owner
+```
+
+Experiment settings can also come from a YAML file whose keys are the flag
+names with `_` for `-` (see [`examples/experiment.yaml`](examples/experiment.yaml)).
+Flags on the command line win over the file:
+
+```sh
+target/release/hashring-rs experiment --config examples/experiment.yaml \
+  --output results/availability
+```
+
+The output directory holds a manifest of the configuration and build, an
+event log, per-process logs, the coordinator database, and a JSON summary. See
+[docs/experiments.md](docs/experiments.md) for defaults, summary fields,
+profiling, and how to compare runs.
+
+## Repository layout
+
+| Path                          | Contents                                                                          |
+| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `src/`                        | The `hashring-rs` binary (CLI)                                                    |
+| `crates/hashring-core`        | Protobuf contract, topology and migration types, shared limits                    |
+| `crates/hashring-client`      | Routing, deadlines, retries, client errors                                        |
+| `crates/hashring-coordinator` | Durable cluster state and migration orchestration                                 |
+| `crates/hashring-node`        | In-memory storage, replication, and the data-node service                         |
+| `crates/hashring-redis`       | The Redis-protocol gateway over the cluster                                       |
+| `crates/hashring-experiment`  | Multi-process experiment runner                                                   |
+| `docs/report/`                | [Preliminary report](docs/report/preliminary-report.md) on the design and results |
+| `docs/configuration.md`       | Every flag and config key, with defaults and scopes                               |
+| `docs/redis-compatibility.md` | What the Redis gateway answers, and where it differs                              |
+| `docs/rfcs/`                  | Design RFCs                                                                       |
+| `docs/optimizations/`         | Performance work, with measurements                                               |
+
+The client, coordinator, and node crates depend on `hashring-core`, and none
+of them depend on each other.
+
+## Development
+
+```sh
+cargo test --workspace --all-targets
+cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
+```
+
+The default test run skips the full correctness, latency, and availability
+experiments and the 96 MiB migration transport check. Run those four explicitly:
+
+```sh
+cargo test --test process_cluster -- --ignored
+```
+
+The node crate also has separately ignored microbenchmarks and an isolated RSS
+regression check; run those individually as described in `docs/optimizations/`.

-//! Walking the keyspace: every live key, from every owner.
-//!
-//! A whole walk (`keys`, `key_count`) pages through every owner at once.
-//! Every page names the epoch the walk started from, and a node at a newer
-//! epoch refuses it: a range that changed hands mid-walk may hold keys the
-//! walk already passed over at its old owner. The walk then catches up with
-//! the topology and starts over, within the operation deadline, so a finished
-//! walk saw every key that was live throughout it exactly once.
-//!
-//! A scan (`scan`) instead goes round the ring in token order, a stretch at a
-//! time, each stretch from whichever node owns it when asked. Its cursor is a
-//! token, which means the same thing in every epoch, so a scan can span
-//! topology changes, and calls on different clients, without starting over.
-
-use futures::future::try_join_all;
-use hashring_core::proto::{ListKeysRequest, ListKeysResponse};
-use tokio::sync::Semaphore;
-
-use super::*;
-
-const KEYS_PER_PAGE: u32 = 1_000;
-const COUNT_PER_PAGE: u32 = 10_000;
-const KEY_BYTES_PER_PAGE: u64 = 1 << 20;
-/// Pages one walk holds at once, from request to the end of filtering. Every
-/// owner is walked concurrently, and a page is buffered whole whether or not
-/// any of its keys are kept, so without this a walk over a thousand owners
-/// could hold a gigabyte of pages that its result never needed.
-const PAGES_IN_FLIGHT: usize = 16;
-/// Pages one `scan` call reads, across however many owners' stretches it
-/// crosses. A call ends sooner once it has seen its `count` of keys; this
-/// bounds a call over a sparse stretch of the ring, which may see none.
-const SCAN_PAGES_PER_CALL: usize = 64;

-/// framing a reply wraps it in. Charged against `keys`' budget so that many
-/// tiny keys cannot pass a budget meant to bound memory.
-pub const PER_KEY_OVERHEAD_BYTES: usize = 64;
-

-    /// transport failure. The walk catches up and starts over.
-    Retry(Option<OperationError>),
-    /// The owner could not be reached at all: the connection failed. It is
-    /// counted as a connect retry and not as a generic rpc one, so a walk
-    /// that lost its connection is told apart from one that got an answer.
-    Connect,
-    Failed(ClientError),

-impl From<ClientError> for Interrupted {
-    fn from(error: ClientError) -> Self {
-        Self::Failed(error)

+//! Walking the keyspace: every live key, from every owner.
+//!
+//! A whole walk (`keys`, `key_count`) pages through every owner at once.
+//! Every page names the epoch the walk started from, and a node at a newer
+//! epoch refuses it: a range that changed hands mid-walk may hold keys the
+//! walk already passed over at its old owner. The walk then catches up with
+//! the topology and starts over, within the operation deadline, so a finished
+//! walk saw every key that was live throughout it exactly once.
+//!
+//! A scan (`scan`) instead goes round the ring in token order, a stretch at a
+//! time, each stretch from whichever node owns it when asked. Its cursor is a
+//! token, which means the same thing in every epoch, so a scan can span
+//! topology changes, and calls on different clients, without starting over.
+
+use futures::future::try_join_all;
+use hashring_core::proto::{ListKeysRequest, ListKeysResponse};
+use tokio::sync::Semaphore;
+
+use super::*;
+
+const KEYS_PER_PAGE: u32 = 1_000;
+const COUNT_PER_PAGE: u32 = 10_000;
+const KEY_BYTES_PER_PAGE: u64 = 1 << 20;
+/// Pages one walk holds at once, from request to the end of filtering. Every
+/// owner is walked concurrently, and a page is buffered whole whether or not
+/// any of its keys are kept, so without this a walk over a thousand owners
+/// could hold a gigabyte of pages that its result never needed.
+const PAGES_IN_FLIGHT: usize = 16;
+/// Pages one `scan` call reads, across however many owners' stretches it
+/// crosses. A call ends sooner once it has seen its `count` of keys; this
+/// bounds a call over a sparse stretch of the ring, which may see none.
+const SCAN_PAGES_PER_CALL: usize = 64;
+/// What holding one key costs beyond its bytes: its allocation, and the
+/// framing a reply wraps it in. Charged against `keys`' budget so that many
+/// tiny keys cannot pass a budget meant to bound memory.
+pub const PER_KEY_OVERHEAD_BYTES: usize = 64;
+
+/// Why one owner's part of a walk stopped short.
+enum Interrupted {
+    /// The owner could not answer for this epoch, or not at all: `None` for a
+    /// transport failure. The walk catches up and starts over.
+    Retry(Option<OperationError>),
+    /// The owner could not be reached at all: the connection failed. It is
+    /// counted as a connect retry and not as a generic rpc one, so a walk
+    /// that lost its connection is told apart from one that got an answer.
+    Connect,
+    Failed(ClientError),
+}
+
+impl From<ClientError> for Interrupted {
+    fn from(error: ClientError) -> Self {
+        Self::Failed(error)

+    /// length plus [`PER_KEY_OVERHEAD_BYTES`], add up to more than
+    /// `max_bytes`.

+        &self,
+        cursor: u64,
+        count: usize,
+        keep: impl Fn(&[u8]) -> bool,
+        max_bytes: usize,

+                let topology = self.inner.topology.read().await;

+                topology_epoch: epoch,
+                start_token: position,
+                max_keys: u32::try_from(count - seen).unwrap_or(u32::MAX),
+                max_bytes: KEY_BYTES_PER_PAGE,
+                one_stretch: true,
+                ..Default::default()

+            // now knows it, so nothing is skipped or seen twice.

+                Err(Interrupted::Failed(error)) => return Err(error),
+                Err(failure) => {

+        // read one is past token 0, which a caller may use to mean "done".
+        debug_assert!(position > cursor || pages == 0);

-async fn refresh_topology_for_inner(
-    inner: &Arc<ClientInner>,
-    timeout: Duration,
-    unknown_write_outcome: bool,
-    minimum_epoch: Option<u64>,
-) -> Result<TopologySnapshot, ClientError> {
-    let deadline = Instant::now() + timeout;
-    if let Some(minimum_epoch) = minimum_epoch
-        && inner.topology.read().await.epoch >= minimum_epoch
-    {
-        return Ok(inner.topology.read().await.clone());
-    }
-    let _refresh = tokio::time::timeout(
-        remaining(deadline, unknown_write_outcome)?,
-        inner.refresh_lock.lock(),
-    )
-    .await
-    .map_err(|_| ClientError::deadline(unknown_write_outcome))?;
-    if let Some(minimum_epoch) = minimum_epoch
-        && inner.topology.read().await.epoch >= minimum_epoch
-    {
-        return Ok(inner.topology.read().await.clone());
-    }
-    let mut attempt = 0_u32;
-    loop {
-        let fetched = tokio::time::timeout(
-            remaining(deadline, unknown_write_outcome)?,
-            fetch_topology_for_refresh(&inner.coordinator_endpoint),
-        )
-        .await;
-        match fetched {
-            Ok(Ok(topology)) => {
-                let mut current = inner.topology.write().await;
-                if topology.epoch > current.epoch {
-                    *current = topology;
-                } else if topology.epoch == current.epoch && topology != *current {
-                    return Err(ClientError::TopologyRefresh {
-                        source: TopologyRefreshError::ConflictingEpoch {
-                            epoch: topology.epoch,
-                            cached_digest: current.digest.clone(),
-                            fetched_digest: topology.digest,
-                        }
-                        .into(),
-                        outcome: unknown_write_outcome.into(),
-                    });
-                }
-                inner.refresh_generation.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
-                if minimum_epoch.is_none_or(|minimum| current.epoch >= minimum) {
-                    return Ok(current.clone());
-                }
-                drop(current);
-                refresh_retry_delay(inner, deadline, &mut attempt, unknown_write_outcome).await?;
-            }
-            Ok(Err(error)) if error.is_retryable() => {
-                refresh_retry_delay(inner, deadline, &mut attempt, unknown_write_outcome).await?;
-            }
-            Ok(Err(error)) => {
-                return Err(ClientError::TopologyRefresh {
-                    source: error.into(),
-                    outcome: unknown_write_outcome.into(),
-                });
-            }
-            Err(_) => {

-/// Waits before the next attempt of a topology refresh, and counts it.
-///
-/// A refresh that has to try again is a retry of the client, like a request
-/// that has to try again, so it is counted with them. A counter that left
-/// these out would count a client that never had to try a request twice as a
-/// client that never had to try anything twice.
-async fn refresh_retry_delay(
-    inner: &ClientInner,
-    deadline: Instant,
-    attempt: &mut u32,
-    unknown_write_outcome: bool,
-) -> Result<(), ClientError> {
-    inner.retries.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
-    inner.retry_reasons[RetryReason::TopologyRefresh.index()].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
-    retry_delay(deadline, attempt, unknown_write_outcome).await
-}

-async fn retry_delay_with_hint(
-    deadline: Instant,
-    attempt: &mut u32,
-    unknown_write_outcome: bool,
-    minimum_delay: Duration,
-) -> Result<(), ClientError> {
-    let base_ms = 5_u64.saturating_mul(1_u64 << (*attempt).min(5));
-    let jitter_ms = rand::random::<u64>() % (base_ms + 1);
-    *attempt = attempt.saturating_add(1);
-    let delay = Duration::from_millis((base_ms + jitter_ms).min(200)).max(minimum_delay);
-    let available = remaining(deadline, unknown_write_outcome)?;
-    if delay >= available {
-        tokio::time::sleep(available).await;
-        return Err(ClientError::deadline(unknown_write_outcome));
-    }
-    tokio::time::sleep(delay).await;
-    Ok(())
-}

-        let Some(inner) = inner.upgrade() else {

-        let refresh_timeout = inner.topology_refresh_timeout;

-async fn run_background_refresh(inner: Arc<ClientInner>) {
-    loop {
-        let handled_generation = inner.background_trigger_generation.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
-        let requested_epoch = inner.background_minimum_epoch.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
-        let _ = refresh_topology_for_inner(
-            &inner,
-            inner.topology_refresh_timeout,
-            false,
-            Some(requested_epoch),
-        )
-        .await;
-
-        let newest_generation = inner.background_trigger_generation.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
-        if newest_generation > handled_generation {
-            continue;
-        }
-        inner
-            .background_refresh_running
-            .store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
-        let raced_generation = inner.background_trigger_generation.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
-        if raced_generation > newest_generation
-            && inner
-                .background_refresh_running
-                .compare_exchange(false, true, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst)
-                .is_ok()
-        {
-            continue;
-        }
-        return;
-    }
-}

-fn jittered_poll_delay(interval: Duration) -> Duration {
-    let jitter_steps = POLL_JITTER_PERCENT.saturating_mul(2).saturating_add(1);

-        .saturating_sub(POLL_JITTER_PERCENT)
-        .saturating_add(rand::random::<u32>() % jitter_steps);
-    interval.mul_f64(f64::from(percent) / 100.0)
-}

+    /// How many internal retries this client has made.

+    /// A retry is one attempt a client made after a retryable failure, of a
+    /// request or of a topology refresh. The count is cumulative over the
+    /// client's lifetime, so a caller that wants the retries of one phase

+    /// every few milliseconds needs one value, not the whole map.

+    /// The internal retries by reason, cumulative over the client's lifetime.
+    pub fn retry_reasons(&self) -> BTreeMap<&'static str, u64> {
+        RetryReason::ALL
+            .into_iter()
+            .map(|reason| {
+                (
+                    reason.name(),
+                    self.inner.retry_reasons[reason.index()].load(Ordering::Relaxed),
+                )
+            })
+            .collect()

+    /// reconciled: recording the reason first and the total after a refresh
+    /// that returns `Err` leaves `sum(retry_reasons) > retry_count`.
+    fn record_retry(&self, reason: RetryReason) {

+    pub async fn get(&self, key: Vec<u8>) -> Result<GetOutput, ClientError> {
+        validate_key_size(&key)?;
+        let deadline = Instant::now() + self.inner.operation_timeout;
+        let request_id = new_request_id();
+        let mut attempt = 0_u32;
+
+        loop {
+            let (epoch, endpoint) = self.route(&key).await?;
+            let mut client = match self.data_node_client(&endpoint, deadline).await {
+                Ok(client) => client,
+                Err(ClientError::DeadlineExceeded { .. }) => {
+                    return Err(ClientError::deadline(false));
+                }
+                Err(_) => {
+                    self.refresh_after_unavailable(epoch, deadline, false)
+                        .await?;
+                    self.retry_delay(deadline, &mut attempt, false, RetryReason::Connect)
+                        .await?;
+                    continue;
+                }
+            };
+
+            let request = GetRequest {
+                key: key.clone(),
+                topology_epoch: epoch,
+                request_id: request_id.clone(),
+            };
+            let rpc_timer = hashring_core::rpc_profile::CLIENT_GET_RPC.start();
+            let response =
+                tokio::time::timeout(remaining(deadline, false)?, client.get(request)).await;
+            drop(rpc_timer);
+            let response = match response {
+                Ok(Ok(response)) => response.into_inner(),
+                Ok(Err(status)) => {
+                    if retryable_status(&status) {
+                        self.refresh_after_unavailable(epoch, deadline, false)
+                            .await?;
+                        self.retry_delay(deadline, &mut attempt, false, RetryReason::Rpc)
+                            .await?;
+                        continue;
+                    }
+                    return Err(rpc_error(status, false));
+                }
+                Err(_) => {
+                    return Err(ClientError::deadline(false));
+                }
+            };
+
+            if let Some(error) = response.error {
+                if self
+                    .handle_retryable(error.clone(), epoch, deadline, &mut attempt, false)
+                    .await?
+                {
+                    continue;
+                }
+                return Err(OperationFailure::from(error).into());
+            }
+            let output = GetOutput {
+                value: response.value,
+                version: response.version.ok_or(ClientError::MissingVersion)?,
+                topology_epoch: response.current_epoch,
+                expires_at_unix_millis: response.expires_at_unix_millis,
+            };
+            if response.current_epoch > epoch {
+                self.trigger_background_refresh(response.current_epoch);
+            }
+            return Ok(output);
+        }
+    }

+    pub async fn put(&self, key: Vec<u8>, value: Vec<u8>) -> Result<PutOutput, ClientError> {
+        self.put_with_expiry(key, value, Expiry::Keep).await

+    /// Stores `value` under a caller-chosen mutation ID.
+    ///
+    /// Every internal retry of this call reuses the ID, and a later call with
+    /// the same ID and payload is answered from the owner's receipt instead of
+    /// being applied again. That is what lets a caller retry a request whose
+    /// response it never saw.
+    ///
+    /// The ID must not be empty and must not exceed
+    /// [`MAX_MUTATION_ID_BYTES`] bytes; a call that breaks either rule fails
+    /// without contacting a node. The ID must also stay unique to this
+    /// operation for at least the cluster's receipt retention period: a later
+    /// call that reuses the ID with a different payload is rejected with
+    /// `MutationIdConflict`, and a call that reuses it with the same payload
+    /// is answered from the receipt instead of being applied again.
+    pub async fn put_with_mutation_id(
+        &self,
+        key: Vec<u8>,
+        value: Vec<u8>,
+        mutation_id: impl Into<String>,
+    ) -> Result<PutOutput, ClientError> {
+        let mutation_id = mutation_id.into();
+        validate_mutation_id(&mutation_id)?;
+        match self
+            .put_record(key, value, Expiry::Keep, false, None, mutation_id)
+            .await?
+        {
+            PutResult::Applied(output) => Ok(output),
+            PutResult::KeyMissing | PutResult::ConditionFailed => Err(ClientError::MissingVersion),
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Stores `value` and sets the record's deadline.
+    ///
+    /// The deadline is absolute and is fixed when this is called, so every
+    /// retry of one logical write carries the deadline it was first sent with.
+    /// A caller that wants a deadline relative to the moment the write is
+    /// accepted computes it from its own clock.
+    pub async fn put_with_expiry(
+        &self,
+        key: Vec<u8>,
+        value: Vec<u8>,
+        expiry: Expiry,
+    ) -> Result<PutOutput, ClientError> {
+        match self
+            .put_record(key, value, expiry, false, None, new_request_id())
+            .await?
+        {
+            PutResult::Applied(output) => Ok(output),
+            // Only a conditional or expiry-only write is answered this way.
+            PutResult::KeyMissing | PutResult::ConditionFailed => Err(ClientError::MissingVersion),
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Stores `value` only if `precondition` holds for the key's live record
+    /// when the owner applies the write. `None` means it did not hold and
+    /// nothing was written.
+    ///
+    /// A retry inside this call reuses the mutation ID, and the owner answers
+    /// it from the first attempt's receipt before checking the condition
+    /// again, so a write that was applied is never reported as failed.
+    pub async fn put_if(
+        &self,
+        key: Vec<u8>,
+        value: Vec<u8>,
+        expiry: Expiry,
+        precondition: Precondition,
+    ) -> Result<Option<PutOutput>, ClientError> {
+        match self
+            .put_record(
+                key,
+                value,
+                expiry,
+                false,
+                Some(precondition),
+                new_request_id(),
+            )
+            .await?
+        {
+            PutResult::Applied(output) => Ok(Some(output)),
+            PutResult::ConditionFailed => Ok(None),
+            PutResult::KeyMissing => Err(ClientError::MissingVersion),
+        }
+    }

+    /// Replaces the deadline of an existing record, keeping its value:
+    /// `Some` stores that absolute deadline and `None` removes it.

+    /// [`HashringClient::set_expiry`] applied only if `precondition` holds;
+    /// `None` when it did not or the key is absent, which the precondition

+    async fn expiry_record(
+        &self,
+        key: Vec<u8>,
+        expires_at_unix_millis: Option<u64>,
+        precondition: Option<Precondition>,
+    ) -> Result<Option<PutOutput>, ClientError> {
+        let expiry = expires_at_unix_millis.map_or(Expiry::Clear, Expiry::At);
+        match self
+            .put_record(
+                key,
+                Vec::new(),
+                expiry,
+                true,
+                precondition,
+                new_request_id(),
+            )
+            .await?
+        {
+            PutResult::Applied(output) => Ok(Some(output)),
+            PutResult::KeyMissing | PutResult::ConditionFailed => Ok(None),
+        }
+    }
+
+    async fn put_record(
+        &self,
+        key: Vec<u8>,
+        value: Vec<u8>,
+        expiry: Expiry,
+        preserve_value: bool,
+        precondition: Option<Precondition>,
+        request_id: String,
+    ) -> Result<PutResult, ClientError> {
+        let _operation_timer = hashring_core::rpc_profile::CLIENT_PUT_OPERATION.start();
+        validate_key_size(&key)?;
+        // The transport, not the cluster's own settings, decides what one
+        // message may carry, so this is the ceiling any cluster can hold.
+        if value.len() > MAX_VALUE_BYTES {
+            return Err(size_failure(format!(
+                "value exceeds {MAX_VALUE_BYTES} bytes"
+            )));
+        }
+        let deadline = self.mutation_deadline();
+        let mut attempt = 0_u32;
+        let mut unknown_write_outcome = false;
+
+        loop {
+            let (epoch, endpoint) = self.route(&key).await?;
+            let mut client = match self.data_node_client(&endpoint, deadline).await {
+                Ok(client) => client,
+                Err(ClientError::DeadlineExceeded { .. }) => {
+                    return Err(ClientError::deadline(unknown_write_outcome));
+                }
+                Err(_) => {
+                    self.refresh_after_unavailable(epoch, deadline, unknown_write_outcome)
+                        .await?;
+                    self.retry_delay(
+                        deadline,
+                        &mut attempt,
+                        unknown_write_outcome,
+                        RetryReason::Connect,
+                    )
+                    .await?;
+                    continue;
+                }
+            };
+
+            let request = PutRequest {
+                key: key.clone(),
+                value: value.clone(),
+                topology_epoch: epoch,
+                request_id: request_id.clone(),
+                expires_at_unix_millis: expiry.into(),
+                preserve_value,
+                precondition: precondition.clone().map(Into::into),
+            };
+            let rpc_timer = hashring_core::rpc_profile::CLIENT_PUT_RPC.start();
+            let response = tokio::time::timeout(
+                remaining(deadline, unknown_write_outcome)?,
+                client.put(request),
+            )
+            .await;
+            drop(rpc_timer);
+            let response = match response {
+                Ok(Ok(response)) => response.into_inner(),
+                Ok(Err(status)) => {
+                    unknown_write_outcome =
+                        accumulated_write_ambiguity(unknown_write_outcome, &status);
+                    if retryable_status(&status) {
+                        tracing::debug!(operation = "put", request_id, attempt, epoch = epoch, code = ?status.code(), message = status.message(), "retrying node RPC status");
+                        self.refresh_after_unavailable(epoch, deadline, unknown_write_outcome)
+                            .await?;
+                        self.retry_delay(
+                            deadline,
+                            &mut attempt,
+                            unknown_write_outcome,
+                            RetryReason::Rpc,
+                        )
+                        .await?;
+                        continue;
+                    }
+                    return Err(rpc_error(status, unknown_write_outcome));
+                }
+                Err(_) => {
+                    return Err(ClientError::deadline(true));
+                }
+            };
+
+            if let Some(error) = response.error {
+                let error_unknown_write_outcome =
+                    unknown_write_outcome || operation_may_have_applied(&error);
+                // Kept for later attempts: a retry the owner then rejects, or
+                // fails permanently, still follows this ambiguous one.
+                unknown_write_outcome = error_unknown_write_outcome;
+                if error.retryable {
+                    tracing::debug!(operation = "put", request_id, attempt, epoch = epoch, code = ?ErrorCode::try_from(error.code).unwrap_or(ErrorCode::Unspecified), message = error.message, "retrying operation response");
+                }
+                if self
+                    .handle_retryable(
+                        error.clone(),
+                        epoch,
+                        deadline,
+                        &mut attempt,
+                        error_unknown_write_outcome,
+                    )
+                    .await?
+                {
+                    continue;
+                }
+                let mut failure = OperationFailure::from(error);
+                failure.outcome = error_unknown_write_outcome.into();
+                return Err(failure.into());
+            }
+            if response.current_epoch > epoch {
+                self.trigger_background_refresh(response.current_epoch);
+            }
+            if response.condition_failed || response.key_missing {
+                // A rejection answers for this attempt only, and keeps no
+                // receipt. An earlier attempt whose outcome is unknown may
+                // still be on its way to the owner and apply afterwards.
+                if unknown_write_outcome {
+                    return Err(rejected_after_ambiguity());
+                }
+                return Ok(match response.condition_failed {
+                    true => PutResult::ConditionFailed,
+                    false => PutResult::KeyMissing,
+                });
+            }
+            return Ok(PutResult::Applied(PutOutput {
+                version: response.version.ok_or(ClientError::MissingVersion)?,
+                topology_epoch: response.current_epoch,
+            }));
+        }
+    }

+                    return Err(rpc_error(status, unknown_write_outcome));
+                }
+                Err(_) => {
+                    return Err(ClientError::deadline(true));
+                }
+            };
+
+            if let Some(error) = response.error {
+                let error_unknown_write_outcome =
+                    unknown_write_outcome || operation_may_have_applied(&error);
+                // Kept for later attempts: a retry the owner then rejects, or
+                // fails permanently, still follows this ambiguous one.
+                unknown_write_outcome = error_unknown_write_outcome;
+                if error.retryable {
+                    tracing::debug!(operation = "delete", request_id, attempt, epoch = epoch, code = ?ErrorCode::try_from(error.code).unwrap_or(ErrorCode::Unspecified), message = error.message, "retrying operation response");
+                }
+                if self
+                    .handle_retryable(
+                        error.clone(),
+                        epoch,
+                        deadline,
+                        &mut attempt,
+                        error_unknown_write_outcome,
+                    )
+                    .await?
+                {
+                    continue;
+                }
+                let mut failure = OperationFailure::from(error);
+                failure.outcome = error_unknown_write_outcome.into();
+                return Err(failure.into());
+            }
+            if response.current_epoch > epoch {
+                self.trigger_background_refresh(response.current_epoch);
+            }
+            if response.condition_failed {
+                // See `put_record`: an earlier ambiguous attempt may still
+                // apply after this one was rejected.
+                if unknown_write_outcome {
+                    return Err(rejected_after_ambiguity());
+                }
+                return Ok(None);
+            }
+            return Ok(Some(DeleteOutput {
+                topology_epoch: response.current_epoch,
+                version: response.version.ok_or(ClientError::MissingVersion)?,
+            }));
+        }
+    }
+
+    async fn handle_retryable(
+        &self,
+        error: OperationError,
+        attempted_epoch: u64,
+        deadline: Instant,
+        attempt: &mut u32,
+        unknown_write_outcome: bool,
+    ) -> Result<bool, ClientError> {
+        let code = ErrorCode::try_from(error.code).unwrap_or(ErrorCode::Unspecified);
+        match code {
+            ErrorCode::Moved => {
+                let required_epoch = error.current_epoch.max(attempted_epoch.saturating_add(1));
+                self.refresh_topology_before(deadline, unknown_write_outcome, Some(required_epoch))
+                    .await?;
+                self.retry_delay(deadline, attempt, unknown_write_outcome, RetryReason::Moved)
+                    .await?;
+                Ok(true)
+            }
+            ErrorCode::Unavailable if error.retryable => {
+                self.refresh_after_unavailable(attempted_epoch, deadline, unknown_write_outcome)
+                    .await?;
+                self.retry_delay(
+                    deadline,
+                    attempt,
+                    unknown_write_outcome,
+                    RetryReason::Unavailable,
+                )
+                .await?;
+                Ok(true)
+            }
+            ErrorCode::RangeBusy if error.retryable => {
+                self.retry_code(
+                    RetryCode {
+                        code,
+                        reason: RetryReason::RangeBusy,
+                        attempted_epoch,
+                        deadline,
+                        attempt,
+                        unknown_write_outcome,
+                    },
+                    &error,
+                )
+                .await
+            }
+            ErrorCode::ResourceExhausted if error.retryable => {
+                self.retry_code(
+                    RetryCode {
+                        code,
+                        reason: RetryReason::ResourceExhausted,
+                        attempted_epoch,
+                        deadline,
+                        attempt,
+                        unknown_write_outcome,
+                    },
+                    &error,
+                )
+                .await
+            }
+            ErrorCode::TemporarilyUnavailable if error.retryable => {
+                self.retry_code(
+                    RetryCode {
+                        code,
+                        reason: RetryReason::TemporarilyUnavailable,
+                        attempted_epoch,
+                        deadline,
+                        attempt,
+                        unknown_write_outcome,
+                    },
+                    &error,
+                )
+                .await
+            }
+            ErrorCode::ReplicaNotReady if error.retryable => {
+                self.retry_code(
+                    RetryCode {
+                        code,
+                        reason: RetryReason::ReplicaNotReady,
+                        attempted_epoch,
+                        deadline,
+                        attempt,
+                        unknown_write_outcome,
+                    },
+                    &error,
+                )
+                .await
+            }
+            ErrorCode::OutcomeUnknown if error.retryable => {
+                self.retry_code(
+                    RetryCode {
+                        code,
+                        reason: RetryReason::OutcomeUnknown,
+                        attempted_epoch,
+                        deadline,
+                        attempt,
+                        unknown_write_outcome,
+                    },
+                    &error,
+                )
+                .await
+            }
+            ErrorCode::LeaseExpired if error.retryable => {
+                self.refresh_topology_before(deadline, unknown_write_outcome, None)
+                    .await?;
+                self.retry_delay(
+                    deadline,
+                    attempt,
+                    unknown_write_outcome,
+                    RetryReason::LeaseExpired,
+                )
+                .await?;
+                Ok(true)
+            }
+            _ => Ok(false),
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Retries a request whose error code names its own retry reason.
+    ///
+    /// Every code in the retryable group names the reason it is counted
+    /// with, so a new code cannot join the group without one.
+    async fn retry_code(
+        &self,
+        retry: RetryCode<'_>,
+        error: &OperationError,
+    ) -> Result<bool, ClientError> {
+        let RetryCode {
+            code,
+            reason,
+            attempted_epoch,
+            deadline,
+            attempt,
+            unknown_write_outcome,
+        } = retry;
+        if error.current_epoch > attempted_epoch {
+            self.refresh_topology_before(
+                deadline,
+                unknown_write_outcome,
+                Some(error.current_epoch),
+            )
+            .await?;
+        }
+        self.retry_delay_with_hint(
+            deadline,
+            attempt,
+            unknown_write_outcome,
+            if code == ErrorCode::ResourceExhausted {
+                Duration::from_millis(error.retry_after_millis)
+            } else {
+                Duration::ZERO
+            },
+            reason,
+        )
+        .await?;
+        Ok(true)
+    }
+
+    async fn refresh_topology_before(
+        &self,
+        deadline: Instant,
+        unknown_write_outcome: bool,
+        minimum_epoch: Option<u64>,
+    ) -> Result<TopologySnapshot, ClientError> {
+        let available = remaining(deadline, unknown_write_outcome)?;
+        self.refresh_topology_for(available, unknown_write_outcome, minimum_epoch)
+            .await
+    }
+
+    async fn refresh_topology_for(
+        &self,
+        timeout: Duration,
+        unknown_write_outcome: bool,
+        minimum_epoch: Option<u64>,
+    ) -> Result<TopologySnapshot, ClientError> {
+        refresh_topology_for_inner(&self.inner, timeout, unknown_write_outcome, minimum_epoch).await
+    }
+
+    async fn refresh_after_unavailable(
+        &self,
+        observed_epoch: u64,
+        deadline: Instant,
+        unknown_write_outcome: bool,
+    ) -> Result<(), ClientError> {
+        if self.inner.topology.read().await.epoch > observed_epoch {
+            return Ok(());
+        }
+        let generation = self.inner.refresh_generation.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
+        let _guard = tokio::time::timeout(
+            remaining(deadline, unknown_write_outcome)?,
+            self.inner.refresh_lock.lock(),
+        )
+        .await
+        .map_err(|_| ClientError::deadline(unknown_write_outcome))?;
+        if self.inner.topology.read().await.epoch > observed_epoch
+            || self.inner.refresh_generation.load(Ordering::SeqCst) != generation
+        {
+            return Ok(());
+        }
+        match tokio::time::timeout(
+            remaining(deadline, unknown_write_outcome)?,
+            fetch_topology_for_refresh(&self.inner.coordinator_endpoint),
+        )
+        .await
+        {
+            Ok(Ok(topology)) => {
+                let mut current = self.inner.topology.write().await;
+                if topology.epoch > current.epoch {
+                    *current = topology;
+                } else if topology.epoch == current.epoch && topology != *current {
+                    return Err(ClientError::TopologyRefresh {
+                        source: TopologyRefreshError::ConflictingEpoch {
+                            epoch: topology.epoch,
+                            cached_digest: current.digest.clone(),
+                            fetched_digest: topology.digest,
+                        }
+                        .into(),
+                        outcome: unknown_write_outcome.into(),
+                    });
+                }
+                self.inner.refresh_generation.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
+            }
+            Ok(Err(_)) => {}
+            Err(_) => {
+                return Err(ClientError::deadline(unknown_write_outcome));
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+
+    fn trigger_background_refresh(&self, minimum_epoch: u64) {
+        self.inner
+            .background_minimum_epoch
+            .fetch_max(minimum_epoch, Ordering::SeqCst);
+        self.inner
+            .background_trigger_generation
+            .fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
+        if self
+            .inner
+            .background_refresh_running
+            .compare_exchange(false, true, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst)
+            .is_err()
+        {
+            return;
+        }
+        let inner = Arc::clone(&self.inner);
+        tokio::spawn(run_background_refresh(inner));
+    }
+
+    /// Bounds the retries of one mutation ID by the cluster's receipt
+    /// retention period: a receipt's clock starts when a replica applies the
+    /// mutation, after the first attempt was sent, so retries before this
+    /// deadline find it.
+    fn mutation_deadline(&self) -> Instant {
+        Instant::now()
+            + self
+                .inner
+                .operation_timeout
+                .min(self.inner.receipt_retention)
+    }
+
+    async fn retry_delay(
+        &self,
+        deadline: Instant,
+        attempt: &mut u32,
+        unknown_write_outcome: bool,
+        reason: RetryReason,
+    ) -> Result<(), ClientError> {
+        self.record_retry(reason);
+        retry_delay(deadline, attempt, unknown_write_outcome).await
+    }
+
+    async fn retry_delay_with_hint(
+        &self,
+        deadline: Instant,
+        attempt: &mut u32,
+        unknown_write_outcome: bool,
+        minimum_delay: Duration,
+        reason: RetryReason,
+    ) -> Result<(), ClientError> {
+        self.record_retry(reason);
+        retry_delay_with_hint(deadline, attempt, unknown_write_outcome, minimum_delay).await
+    }
+
+    async fn data_node_client(
+        &self,
+        endpoint: &str,
+        deadline: Instant,
+    ) -> Result<DataNodeClient<Channel>, ClientError> {
+        if let Some(channel) = self.inner.channels.read().await.get(endpoint).cloned() {
+            return Ok(configure_data_client(DataNodeClient::new(channel)));
+        }
+        let transport = Endpoint::from_shared(endpoint.to_owned())
+            .map_err(anyhow::Error::from)
+            .map_err(ClientError::from)?;
+        let channel = tokio::time::timeout(remaining(deadline, false)?, transport.connect())
+            .await
+            .map_err(|_| ClientError::deadline(false))?
+            .map_err(anyhow::Error::from)
+            .map_err(ClientError::from)?;
+        self.inner
+            .channels
+            .write()
+            .await
+            .insert(endpoint.to_owned(), channel.clone());
+        Ok(configure_data_client(DataNodeClient::new(channel)))
+    }
+}
+
+async fn refresh_topology_for_inner(
+    inner: &Arc<ClientInner>,
+    timeout: Duration,
+    unknown_write_outcome: bool,
+    minimum_epoch: Option<u64>,
+) -> Result<TopologySnapshot, ClientError> {
+    let deadline = Instant::now() + timeout;
+    if let Some(minimum_epoch) = minimum_epoch
+        && inner.topology.read().await.epoch >= minimum_epoch
+    {
+        return Ok(inner.topology.read().await.clone());
+    }
+    let _refresh = tokio::time::timeout(
+        remaining(deadline, unknown_write_outcome)?,
+        inner.refresh_lock.lock(),
+    )
+    .await
+    .map_err(|_| ClientError::deadline(unknown_write_outcome))?;
+    if let Some(minimum_epoch) = minimum_epoch
+        && inner.topology.read().await.epoch >= minimum_epoch
+    {
+        return Ok(inner.topology.read().await.clone());
+    }
+    let mut attempt = 0_u32;
+    loop {
+        let fetched = tokio::time::timeout(
+            remaining(deadline, unknown_write_outcome)?,
+            fetch_topology_for_refresh(&inner.coordinator_endpoint),
+        )
+        .await;
+        match fetched {
+            Ok(Ok(topology)) => {
+                let mut current = inner.topology.write().await;
+                if topology.epoch > current.epoch {
+                    *current = topology;
+                } else if topology.epoch == current.epoch && topology != *current {
+                    return Err(ClientError::TopologyRefresh {
+                        source: TopologyRefreshError::ConflictingEpoch {
+                            epoch: topology.epoch,
+                            cached_digest: current.digest.clone(),
+                            fetched_digest: topology.digest,
+                        }
+                        .into(),
+                        outcome: unknown_write_outcome.into(),
+                    });
+                }
+                inner.refresh_generation.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
+                if minimum_epoch.is_none_or(|minimum| current.epoch >= minimum) {
+                    return Ok(current.clone());
+                }
+                drop(current);
+                refresh_retry_delay(inner, deadline, &mut attempt, unknown_write_outcome).await?;
+            }
+            Ok(Err(error)) if error.is_retryable() => {
+                refresh_retry_delay(inner, deadline, &mut attempt, unknown_write_outcome).await?;
+            }
+            Ok(Err(error)) => {
+                return Err(ClientError::TopologyRefresh {
+                    source: error.into(),
+                    outcome: unknown_write_outcome.into(),
+                });
+            }
+            Err(_) => {
+                return Err(ClientError::deadline(unknown_write_outcome));
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+async fn retry_delay(
+    deadline: Instant,
+    attempt: &mut u32,
+    unknown_write_outcome: bool,
+) -> Result<(), ClientError> {
+    retry_delay_with_hint(deadline, attempt, unknown_write_outcome, Duration::ZERO).await
+}
+
+/// Waits before the next attempt of a topology refresh, and counts it.
+///
+/// A refresh that has to try again is a retry of the client, like a request
+/// that has to try again, so it is counted with them. A counter that left
+/// these out would count a client that never had to try a request twice as a
+/// client that never had to try anything twice.
+async fn refresh_retry_delay(
+    inner: &ClientInner,
+    deadline: Instant,
+    attempt: &mut u32,
+    unknown_write_outcome: bool,
+) -> Result<(), ClientError> {
+    inner.retries.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
+    inner.retry_reasons[RetryReason::TopologyRefresh.index()].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
+    retry_delay(deadline, attempt, unknown_write_outcome).await
+}
+
+async fn retry_delay_with_hint(
+    deadline: Instant,
+    attempt: &mut u32,
+    unknown_write_outcome: bool,
+    minimum_delay: Duration,
+) -> Result<(), ClientError> {
+    let base_ms = 5_u64.saturating_mul(1_u64 << (*attempt).min(5));
+    let jitter_ms = rand::random::<u64>() % (base_ms + 1);
+    *attempt = attempt.saturating_add(1);
+    let delay = Duration::from_millis((base_ms + jitter_ms).min(200)).max(minimum_delay);
+    let available = remaining(deadline, unknown_write_outcome)?;
+    if delay >= available {
+        tokio::time::sleep(available).await;
+        return Err(ClientError::deadline(unknown_write_outcome));
+    }
+    tokio::time::sleep(delay).await;
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+/// A random 128-bit operation id, as unique as a v4 UUID. `rand`'s thread-local
+/// generator is seeded from the OS once and reseeds only after 64 KiB of output,
+/// where `Uuid::new_v4` makes a `getentropy` syscall per call, which cost 4.5-7%
+/// of a load driver's CPU.
+fn new_request_id() -> String {
+    format!("{:032x}", rand::random::<u128>())
+}
+
+fn configure_data_client(
+    client: DataNodeClient<tonic::transport::Channel>,
+) -> DataNodeClient<tonic::transport::Channel> {
+    client
+        .max_decoding_message_size(MAX_DATA_MESSAGE_BYTES)
+        .max_encoding_message_size(MAX_DATA_MESSAGE_BYTES)
+}
+
+fn retryable_status(status: &tonic::Status) -> bool {
+    status.code() == Code::Unavailable
+}
+
+async fn poll_for_topology_changes(inner: Weak<ClientInner>, interval: Duration) {
+    loop {
+        tokio::time::sleep(jittered_poll_delay(interval)).await;
+        let Some(inner) = inner.upgrade() else {
+            return;
+        };
+        let refresh_timeout = inner.topology_refresh_timeout;
+        let observed_epoch = match tokio::time::timeout(
+            refresh_timeout,
+            fetch_current_epoch(&inner.coordinator_endpoint),
+        )
+        .await
+        {
+            Ok(Ok(epoch)) => epoch,
+            Ok(Err(_)) | Err(_) => continue,
+        };
+        if inner.topology.read().await.epoch < observed_epoch {
+            let _ =
+                refresh_topology_for_inner(&inner, refresh_timeout, false, Some(observed_epoch))
+                    .await;
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+async fn run_background_refresh(inner: Arc<ClientInner>) {
+    loop {
+        let handled_generation = inner.background_trigger_generation.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
+        let requested_epoch = inner.background_minimum_epoch.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
+        let _ = refresh_topology_for_inner(
+            &inner,
+            inner.topology_refresh_timeout,
+            false,
+            Some(requested_epoch),
+        )
+        .await;
+
+        let newest_generation = inner.background_trigger_generation.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
+        if newest_generation > handled_generation {
+            continue;
+        }
+        inner
+            .background_refresh_running
+            .store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
+        let raced_generation = inner.background_trigger_generation.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
+        if raced_generation > newest_generation
+            && inner
+                .background_refresh_running
+                .compare_exchange(false, true, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst)
+                .is_ok()
+        {
+            continue;
+        }
+        return;
+    }
+}
+
+fn jittered_poll_delay(interval: Duration) -> Duration {
+    let jitter_steps = POLL_JITTER_PERCENT.saturating_mul(2).saturating_add(1);
+    let percent = 100_u32
+        .saturating_sub(POLL_JITTER_PERCENT)
+        .saturating_add(rand::random::<u32>() % jitter_steps);
+    interval.mul_f64(f64::from(percent) / 100.0)
+}
+
+async fn fetch_current_epoch(endpoint: &str) -> Result<u64, TopologyRefreshError> {
+    let mut client =
+        configure_coordinator_client(CoordinatorClient::connect(endpoint.to_owned()).await?);
+    Ok(client
+        .get_current_epoch(proto::Empty {})
+        .await
+        .map_err(|status| TopologyRefreshError::Rpc(Box::new(status)))?
+        .into_inner()
+        .epoch)
+}
+
+async fn fetch_topology_for_refresh(
+    endpoint: &str,
+) -> Result<TopologySnapshot, TopologyRefreshError> {
+    let mut client =
+        configure_coordinator_client(CoordinatorClient::connect(endpoint.to_owned()).await?);
+    let response = client
+        .get_topology(proto::Empty {})
+        .await
+        .map_err(|status| TopologyRefreshError::Rpc(Box::new(status)))?
+        .into_inner();
+    Ok(response.try_into()?)
+}
+
+fn status_may_have_applied(status: &tonic::Status) -> bool {
+    matches!(
+        status.code(),
+        Code::Cancelled
+            | Code::Unknown
+            | Code::DeadlineExceeded
+            | Code::Internal
+            | Code::Unavailable
+            | Code::DataLoss
+    )
+}
+
+fn accumulated_write_ambiguity(already_unknown: bool, status: &tonic::Status) -> bool {
+    already_unknown || status_may_have_applied(status)
+}
+
+fn operation_may_have_applied(error: &OperationError) -> bool {
+    error.unknown_write_outcome || error.code == ErrorCode::OutcomeUnknown as i32
+}
+
+fn rpc_error(status: tonic::Status, unknown_write_outcome: bool) -> ClientError {
+    ClientError::Rpc {
+        code: status.code(),
+        message: status.message().to_owned(),
+        outcome: unknown_write_outcome.into(),
+    }
+}
+
+fn validate_key_size(key: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ClientError> {
+    if key.len() > DEFAULT_MAX_KEY_BYTES {
+        return Err(size_failure(format!(
+            "key exceeds {DEFAULT_MAX_KEY_BYTES} bytes"
+        )));
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+/// Rejects a mutation ID a node would refuse anyway.
+///
+/// The check is here so a caller learns about a bad ID without a round trip,
+/// and so the error names the rule instead of the transport.
+fn validate_mutation_id(mutation_id: &str) -> Result<(), ClientError> {
+    if mutation_id.is_empty() || mutation_id.len() > MAX_MUTATION_ID_BYTES {
+        return Err(OperationFailure {
+            code: ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
+            message: format!(
+                "mutation id must contain 1 to {MAX_MUTATION_ID_BYTES} bytes, not {}",
+                mutation_id.len()
+            ),
+            retryable: false,
+            outcome: MutationOutcome::KnownNotApplied,
+        }
+        .into());
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn size_failure(message: String) -> ClientError {
+    OperationFailure {
+        code: ErrorCode::TooLarge,
+        message,
+        retryable: false,
+        outcome: MutationOutcome::KnownNotApplied,
+    }
+    .into()
+}
+
+fn remaining(deadline: Instant, unknown_write_outcome: bool) -> Result<Duration, ClientError> {
+    deadline
+        .checked_duration_since(Instant::now())
+        .filter(|remaining| !remaining.is_zero())
+        .ok_or(ClientError::deadline(unknown_write_outcome))
+}

+        let before = Instant::now();

-    /// Returns the range's committed progress and the source digest that was
-    /// just verified against the destination's.
-    ///
-    /// The digest is returned rather than left to be fetched again because it
-    /// was already computed and compared here, and `finish_replica` used to
-    /// issue a second `source_range_digest` round trip immediately afterwards
-    /// purely to read back the same value from the same frozen range.
-    pub(super) async fn finalize_range(
-        &self,
-        change: &TopologyChange,
-        range: &RangeMigration,
-        final_watermark: u64,
-        deadline: Instant,
-    ) -> Result<(RangeMigration, String), Status> {
-        let mut source = self.connect_node(&range.source_endpoint, deadline).await?;
-        let mut destination = self
-            .connect_node(&range.destination_endpoint, deadline)
-            .await?;
-        let replay_started = Instant::now();
-        let watermark = replay_changelog(
-            &mut source,
-            &mut destination,
-            change,
-            range,
-            range.changelog_watermark,
-            Some(final_watermark),
-            deadline,
-        )
-        .await?;
-        // Stop the replay clock here: the digest round trips, the comparison,
-        // and the destination commit that follow are verification and commit
-        // work, not changelog replay.
-        let replay_ms = millis(replay_started.elapsed());
-        let control = RangeControlRequest {
-            change_id: change.change_id.clone(),
-            range_id: range.range_id.clone(),
-        };
-        let source_digest = rpc_before(deadline, source.source_range_digest(control.clone()))
-            .await?
-            .into_inner();
-        let destination_digest = rpc_before(
-            deadline,
-            destination.destination_range_digest(control.clone()),
-        )
-        .await?
-        .into_inner();
-        if source_digest.record_count != destination_digest.record_count
-            || source_digest.digest != destination_digest.digest
-            || source_digest.changelog_watermark != destination_digest.changelog_watermark
-            || destination_digest.changelog_watermark != final_watermark
-            || watermark != final_watermark
-        {
-            return Err(Status::data_loss(format!(
-                "range verification failed for {}",
-                range.range_id
-            )));
-        }
-        rpc_before(deadline, destination.commit_destination_range(control)).await?;
-
-        let mut progress = range.clone();
-        progress.changelog_watermark = final_watermark;
-        progress.changelog_replay_ms = range.changelog_replay_ms.saturating_add(replay_ms);
-        progress.verified = true;
-        Ok((progress, source_digest.digest))
-    }

-            let old_sources: Vec<_> = change
-                .ranges

-            .target_topology
-            .members
-            .iter()

-            .target_topology
-            .members
-            .iter()
-            .filter(|member| !destination_ids.contains(member.node_id.as_str()))

-            .collect();
-        self.install_on_members_with_lease(

-        self.install_on_members_with_lease(
-            &change.target_topology,
-            &other_targets,
-            deadline,

-        for range in change

+    async fn finish_recovered_change(

+            })?;

+        self.install_on_members_with_lease(
+            &change.target_topology,
+            &change.target_topology.members,
+            deadline,
+            false,
+        )
+        .await?;
+        let last_grant = self
+            .lease_grants
+            .lock()
+            .await
+            .values()
+            .map(|grant| grant.expires_at)
+            .max()
+            .unwrap_or(self.startup_at);
+        tokio::time::sleep_until(last_grant.max(self.startup_at + self.lease_duration)).await;
+        // The activation clock starts after the lease wait: waiting for an old
+        // grant to expire is a safety wait, not activation work.
+        let activation_started = Instant::now();
+        let deadline = Instant::now() + self.migration_timeout;
+        for range in &original.ranges {
+            let mut source = self.connect_node(&range.source_endpoint, deadline).await?;
+            rpc_before(
+                deadline,
+                source.abort_range_migration(RangeControlRequest {
+                    change_id: original.change_id.clone(),
+                    range_id: range.range_id.clone(),
+                }),
+            )
+            .await?;
+        }
+        let guard = &change.target_topology.write_availability_guard;
+        if change.target_topology.write_ack_policy != WriteAckPolicy::OwnerOnly
+            || guard.minimum_admitted_copies > 1
+            || guard.minimum_healthy_followers > 0

+            self.seed_repairs_for_activation().await?;
+        }
