+impl TopologyChange {
+    pub fn plan(
+        committed: &TopologySnapshot,
+        target_members: Vec<Member>,
+    ) -> Result<Self, MigrationError> {
+        Self::plan_with_policy(committed, target_members, committed.write_ack_policy)
+    }
+
+    pub fn plan_with_policy(
+        committed: &TopologySnapshot,
+        target_members: Vec<Member>,
+        target_policy: WriteAckPolicy,
+    ) -> Result<Self, MigrationError> {
+        let mut config = committed.config();
+        config.write_ack_policy = target_policy;
+        Self::plan_with_config(committed, target_members, config)
+    }
+
+    pub fn plan_with_config(
+        committed: &TopologySnapshot,
+        target_members: Vec<Member>,
+        config: TopologyConfig,
+    ) -> Result<Self, MigrationError> {
+        for current in &committed.members {
+            if let Some(target) = target_members
+                .iter()
+                .find(|target| target.node_id == current.node_id)
+                && target.endpoint != current.endpoint
+            {
+                return Err(MigrationError::EndpointChangeUnsupported(
+                    current.node_id.clone(),
+                ));
+            }
+        }
+        let target_epoch = committed
+            .epoch
+            .checked_add(1)
+            .ok_or(MigrationError::EpochOverflow)?;
+        let target_topology = TopologySnapshot::new_with_timings(
+            target_epoch,
+            committed.hash_seed,
+            committed.virtual_nodes,
+            target_members,
+            config,
+            committed.timings.clone(),
+        )?;
+        if target_topology.members == committed.members
+            && target_topology.config() == committed.config()
+        {
+            return Err(MigrationError::NoTopologyChange);
+        }
+
+        let (ranges, replica_obligations) = topology_delta(committed, &target_topology)?;
+        Ok(Self {
+            change_id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
+            base_epoch: committed.epoch,
+            base_topology: Some(committed.clone()),
+            supersedes_change_id: None,
+            ranges,
+            replica_obligations,
+            target_topology,
+            phase: MigrationPhase::Planned,
+            stopped_node_ids: Vec::new(),
+            stopping_node_ids: Vec::new(),
+            stop_prepared_node_ids: Vec::new(),
+            failed_node_id: None,
+            activation_ready: false,
+            direct_merge: false,
+            timings: MigrationTimings::default(),
+        })
+    }
+}

+pub fn moving_ranges(
+    committed: &TopologySnapshot,
+    target: &TopologySnapshot,
+) -> Result<Vec<RangeMigration>, MigrationError> {
+    Ok(topology_delta(committed, target)?.0)
+}
+
+pub fn topology_delta(
+    committed: &TopologySnapshot,
+    target: &TopologySnapshot,
+) -> Result<(Vec<RangeMigration>, Vec<ReplicaObligation>), MigrationError> {
+    let boundaries: BTreeSet<_> = committed
+        .assignments
+        .iter()
+        .chain(&target.assignments)
+        .map(|assignment| assignment.token)
+        .collect();
+    if boundaries.is_empty() {
+        return Err(TopologyError::NoAssignments.into());
+    }
+
+    let ordered: Vec<_> = boundaries.into_iter().collect();
+    let mut previous = *ordered
+        .last()
+        .expect("boundaries were checked as non-empty");
+    let mut ranges = Vec::new();
+    let mut replica_obligations = Vec::new();
+    for end in ordered {
+        let committed_replicas = committed.replica_node_ids_for_token(end)?;
+        let target_replicas = target.replica_node_ids_for_token(end)?;
+        let source_node_id = committed_replicas[0];
+        let destination_node_id = target_replicas[0];
+        if source_node_id != destination_node_id {
+            if ranges.len() == MAX_MIGRATION_RANGES {
+                return Err(MigrationError::TooManyRanges);
+            }
+            let source = committed.owner_for_token(end)?;
+            let destination = target.owner_for_token(end)?;
+            let range_id = range_id(previous, end, source_node_id, destination_node_id);
+            ranges.push(RangeMigration {
+                range_id,
+                start_exclusive: previous,
+                end_inclusive: end,
+                source_node_id: source.node_id.clone(),
+                destination_node_id: destination.node_id.clone(),
+                source_endpoint: source.endpoint.clone(),
+                destination_endpoint: destination.endpoint.clone(),
+                source_process_instance_id: String::new(),
+                destination_process_instance_id: String::new(),
+                source_cleaned: false,
+                snapshot_records: 0,
+                changelog_watermark: 0,
+                changelog_replay_ms: 0,
+                verified: false,
+            });
+        }
+        for follower_node_id in &target_replicas[1..] {
+            if !committed_replicas.contains(follower_node_id) {
+                if replica_obligations.len() == MAX_REPLICA_OBLIGATIONS {
+                    return Err(MigrationError::TooManyReplicaObligations);
+                }
+                replica_obligations.push(ReplicaObligation {
+                    start_exclusive: previous,
+                    end_inclusive: end,
+                    source_node_id: source_node_id.to_owned(),
+                    destination_node_id: (*follower_node_id).to_owned(),
+                });
+            }
+        }
+        previous = end;
+    }
+    Ok((ranges, replica_obligations))
+}
+
+fn range_id(start: u64, end: u64, source: &str, destination: &str) -> String {
+    let mut digest = blake3::Hasher::new();
+    digest.update(b"hashring-rs:range:v1\0");
+    digest.update(&start.to_be_bytes());
+    digest.update(&end.to_be_bytes());
+    digest.update(&(source.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
+    digest.update(source.as_bytes());
+    digest.update(&(destination.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
+    digest.update(destination.as_bytes());
+    digest.finalize().to_hex().to_string()
+}

+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+
+    fn member(id: &str, port: u16) -> Member {
+        Member {
+            node_id: id.into(),
+            endpoint: format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}"),
+        }
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn scale_out_plan_moves_only_ranges_with_changed_owners() {
+        let committed = TopologySnapshot::new(1, 42, 16, vec![member("a", 1)]).unwrap();
+        let change =
+            TopologyChange::plan(&committed, vec![member("a", 1), member("b", 2)]).unwrap();
+
+        assert_eq!(change.base_epoch, 1);
+        assert_eq!(change.target_topology.epoch, 2);
+        assert_eq!(change.phase, MigrationPhase::Planned);
+        assert!(!change.ranges.is_empty());
+        assert!(
+            change
+                .ranges
+                .iter()
+                .all(|range| { range.source_node_id == "a" && range.destination_node_id == "b" })
+        );
+        assert!(
+            change
+                .replica_obligations
+                .iter()
+                .all(|obligation| obligation.source_node_id == "a"
+                    && obligation.destination_node_id == "b")
+        );
+        assert!(!change.replica_obligations.is_empty());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn topology_delta_reports_only_new_follower_coverage() {
+        let committed =
+            TopologySnapshot::new(1, 42, 16, vec![member("a", 1), member("b", 2)]).unwrap();
+        let target = TopologySnapshot::new_with_config(
+            2,
+            42,
+            16,
+            vec![member("a", 1), member("b", 2), member("c", 3)],
+            committed.config(),
+        )
+        .unwrap();
+
+        let (_, obligations) = topology_delta(&committed, &target).unwrap();
+        assert!(!obligations.is_empty());
+        for obligation in obligations {
+            let old = committed
+                .replica_node_ids_for_token(obligation.end_inclusive)
+                .unwrap();
+            let new = target
+                .replica_node_ids_for_token(obligation.end_inclusive)
+                .unwrap();
+            assert!(!old.contains(&obligation.destination_node_id.as_str()));
+            assert!(new[1..].contains(&obligation.destination_node_id.as_str()));
+            assert_eq!(old[0], obligation.source_node_id);
+        }
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn identical_membership_is_not_a_change() {
+        let committed = TopologySnapshot::new(1, 42, 16, vec![member("a", 1)]).unwrap();
+        assert!(matches!(
+            TopologyChange::plan(&committed, committed.members.clone()),
+            Err(MigrationError::NoTopologyChange)
+        ));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn rf_and_guard_changes_are_committed_topology_changes() {
+        let committed = TopologySnapshot::new(
+            1,
+            42,
+            16,
+            vec![member("a", 1), member("b", 2), member("c", 3)],
+        )
+        .unwrap();
+        let mut config = committed.config();
+        config.desired_replication_factor = 2;
+        config.write_availability_guard.minimum_healthy_followers = 0;
+        let decrease =
+            TopologyChange::plan_with_config(&committed, committed.members.clone(), config.clone())
+                .unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(decrease.target_topology.config(), config);
+        assert_ne!(decrease.target_topology.digest, committed.digest);
+        assert!(decrease.ranges.is_empty());
+        assert!(decrease.replica_obligations.is_empty());
+
+        config.desired_replication_factor = 3;
+        let increase = TopologyChange::plan_with_config(
+            &decrease.target_topology,
+            decrease.target_topology.members.clone(),
+            config,
+        )
+        .unwrap();
+        assert!(increase.ranges.is_empty());
+        assert!(!increase.replica_obligations.is_empty());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn endpoint_only_replacement_is_rejected() {
+        let committed = TopologySnapshot::new(1, 42, 16, vec![member("a", 1)]).unwrap();
+        assert!(matches!(
+            TopologyChange::plan(&committed, vec![member("a", 2)]),
+            Err(MigrationError::EndpointChangeUnsupported(node)) if node == "a"
+        ));
+    }
+}

+//! Diagnostic RPC latency histograms, enabled with `HASHRING_PROFILE_RPC=1`.
+//!
+//! Each process that calls [`start_reporter`] prints every non-empty histogram
+//! to stderr twice a second as one line:
+//!
+//! ```text
+//! rpc_profile <unix_ms> <role> <name> <count> <sum_ns> <bucket>:<count>,...
+//! ```
+//!
+//! The values are cumulative, so a phase is measured by subtracting the last
+//! line before it from the last line inside it. Bucket `i` holds samples in
+//! `[2^(i/4), 2^((i+1)/4))` microseconds; bucket 0 also holds everything below
+//! 1 µs and the last bucket everything above its lower bound.
+
+use std::sync::OnceLock;
+use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
+use std::time::{Duration, Instant, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
+
+const BUCKETS: usize = 112;
+
+pub fn enabled() -> bool {
+    static ENABLED: OnceLock<bool> = OnceLock::new();
+    *ENABLED.get_or_init(|| std::env::var_os("HASHRING_PROFILE_RPC").is_some_and(|v| v == "1"))
+}
+
+pub struct Histogram {
+    name: &'static str,
+    count: AtomicU64,
+    sum_ns: AtomicU64,
+    buckets: [AtomicU64; BUCKETS],
+}
+
+impl Histogram {
+    const fn new(name: &'static str) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            name,
+            count: AtomicU64::new(0),
+            sum_ns: AtomicU64::new(0),
+            buckets: [const { AtomicU64::new(0) }; BUCKETS],
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub fn record(&self, elapsed: Duration) {
+        let nanos = u64::try_from(elapsed.as_nanos()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX);
+        let micros = nanos as f64 / 1000.0;
+        let bucket = if micros < 1.0 {
+            0
+        } else {
+            ((micros.log2() * 4.0) as usize).min(BUCKETS - 1)
+        };
+        self.count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
+        self.sum_ns.fetch_add(nanos, Ordering::Relaxed);
+        self.buckets[bucket].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
+    }
+
+    /// Records a plain count (such as entries per batch) in the microsecond scale.
+    pub fn record_value(&self, value: u64) {
+        if enabled() {
+            self.record(Duration::from_micros(value));
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Returns a guard that records the time until it is dropped, or `None`
+    /// when profiling is off.
+    pub fn start(&'static self) -> Option<Timer> {
+        enabled().then(|| Timer {
+            histogram: self,
+            started: Instant::now(),
+        })
+    }
+}
+
+pub struct Timer {
+    histogram: &'static Histogram,
+    started: Instant,
+}
+
+impl Drop for Timer {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        self.histogram.record(self.started.elapsed());
+    }
+}
+
+/// Owner handler time for a client `Put`, from request decode to response.
+pub static NODE_PUT: Histogram = Histogram::new("node_put_handler");
+/// Owner handler time for a client `Get`.
+pub static NODE_GET: Histogram = Histogram::new("node_get_handler");
+/// Follower handler time for one `ReplicateMutations` batch.
+pub static NODE_REPLICATE_BATCH: Histogram = Histogram::new("node_replicate_batch_handler");
+/// Owner-observed round trip of one `ReplicateMutations` RPC.
+pub static OWNER_REPLICATION_RPC: Histogram = Histogram::new("owner_replication_rpc");
+/// Entries per replication batch, recorded as microseconds.
+pub static REPLICATION_BATCH_ENTRIES: Histogram = Histogram::new("replication_batch_entries");
+/// Client-observed time of one `Put` RPC attempt.
+pub static CLIENT_PUT_RPC: Histogram = Histogram::new("client_put_rpc");
+/// Client-observed time of one `Get` RPC attempt.
+pub static CLIENT_GET_RPC: Histogram = Histogram::new("client_get_rpc");
+/// One logical client `put`, including routing and retries.
+pub static CLIENT_PUT_OPERATION: Histogram = Histogram::new("client_put_operation");
+
+static ALL: [&Histogram; 8] = [
+    &NODE_PUT,
+    &NODE_GET,
+    &NODE_REPLICATE_BATCH,
+    &OWNER_REPLICATION_RPC,
+    &REPLICATION_BATCH_ENTRIES,
+    &CLIENT_PUT_RPC,
+    &CLIENT_GET_RPC,
+    &CLIENT_PUT_OPERATION,
+];
+
+/// Starts the stderr reporter thread when profiling is on.
+pub fn start_reporter(role: &str) {
+    if !enabled() {
+        return;
+    }
+    let role = role.to_owned();
+    std::thread::Builder::new()
+        .name("rpc-profile".into())
+        .spawn(move || {
+            loop {
+                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));
+                let now = SystemTime::now()
+                    .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
+                    .map_or(0, |d| d.as_millis());
+                for histogram in ALL {
+                    let count = histogram.count.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
+                    if count == 0 {
+                        continue;
+                    }
+                    let buckets: Vec<String> = histogram
+                        .buckets
+                        .iter()
+                        .enumerate()
+                        .filter_map(|(i, b)| {
+                            let n = b.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
+                            (n > 0).then(|| format!("{i}:{n}"))
+                        })
+                        .collect();
+                    eprintln!(
+                        "rpc_profile {now} {role} {} {count} {} {}",
+                        histogram.name,
+                        histogram.sum_ns.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
+                        buckets.join(",")
+                    );
+                }
+            }
+        })
+        .expect("spawning the rpc profile reporter");
+}

+pub const DEFAULT_MINIMUM_ADMITTED_COPIES: u32 = 1;
+pub const DEFAULT_MINIMUM_HEALTHY_FOLLOWERS: u32 = 0;
+pub const DEFAULT_MAX_REPLICA_LAG_MILLIS: u64 = 5_000;
+pub const DEFAULT_RECEIPT_RETENTION_MILLIS: u64 = 60_000;
+pub const DEFAULT_LEASE_DURATION_MILLIS: u64 = 5_000;
+/// Bounds both cluster timings, so deadlines computed from them cannot
+/// overflow and a lease outlives a renewal round trip.
+pub const MIN_CLUSTER_TIMING_MILLIS: u64 = 1_000;
+pub const MAX_CLUSTER_TIMING_MILLIS: u64 = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000;
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub enum WriteAckPolicy {
+    #[default]
+    OwnerOnly,
+    FirstSuccessor,
+    AllReplicas,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct WriteAvailabilityGuard {
+    pub minimum_admitted_copies: u32,
+    pub minimum_healthy_followers: u32,
+    pub max_replica_lag_millis: u64,
+}
+
+impl Default for WriteAvailabilityGuard {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            minimum_admitted_copies: DEFAULT_MINIMUM_ADMITTED_COPIES,
+            minimum_healthy_followers: DEFAULT_MINIMUM_HEALTHY_FOLLOWERS,
+            max_replica_lag_millis: DEFAULT_MAX_REPLICA_LAG_MILLIS,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct TopologyConfig {
+    pub desired_replication_factor: u32,
+    pub write_ack_policy: WriteAckPolicy,
+    pub write_availability_guard: WriteAvailabilityGuard,
+}
+
+impl Default for TopologyConfig {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            desired_replication_factor: DEFAULT_DESIRED_REPLICATION_FACTOR,
+            write_ack_policy: WriteAckPolicy::OwnerOnly,
+            write_availability_guard: WriteAvailabilityGuard::default(),
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// Timings every process in the cluster must agree on. They are chosen when the
+/// coordinator creates its store and never change afterwards: every later
+/// topology copies them, like the hash seed.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct ClusterTimings {
+    /// Every replica keeps a deduplication receipt for at least this long after
+    /// it applies a mutation. A client must stop retrying one mutation ID
+    /// within this window, or a retry could apply the mutation a second time.
+    pub receipt_retention_millis: u64,
+    /// How long a coordinator lease grant lasts. Nodes renew at a fifth of it.
+    /// A restarted coordinator waits this long before acting on any lease,
+    /// which is safe only because the duration cannot change.
+    pub lease_duration_millis: u64,
+}
+
+impl Default for ClusterTimings {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            receipt_retention_millis: DEFAULT_RECEIPT_RETENTION_MILLIS,
+            lease_duration_millis: DEFAULT_LEASE_DURATION_MILLIS,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+impl ClusterTimings {
+    pub fn receipt_retention(&self) -> Duration {
+        Duration::from_millis(self.receipt_retention_millis)
+    }
+
+    pub fn lease_duration(&self) -> Duration {
+        Duration::from_millis(self.lease_duration_millis)
+    }
+
+    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), TopologyError> {
+        let range = MIN_CLUSTER_TIMING_MILLIS..=MAX_CLUSTER_TIMING_MILLIS;
+        if !range.contains(&self.receipt_retention_millis) {
+            return Err(TopologyError::ReceiptRetentionOutOfRange);
+        }
+        if !range.contains(&self.lease_duration_millis) {
+            return Err(TopologyError::LeaseDurationOutOfRange);
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}

+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]

+pub struct DerivedRange {
+    /// Hash interval `(start_exclusive, end_inclusive]`, wrapping at `u64::MAX`.
+    pub start_exclusive: u64,
+    pub end_inclusive: u64,

+}

+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct TopologySnapshot {
+    pub epoch: u64,
+    pub hash_seed: u64,
+    pub hash_algorithm: String,
+    pub encoding_version: u32,
+    pub virtual_nodes: u32,
+    pub desired_replication_factor: u32,
+    pub write_ack_policy: WriteAckPolicy,
+    pub write_availability_guard: WriteAvailabilityGuard,
+    pub timings: ClusterTimings,
+    pub members: Vec<Member>,
+    pub assignments: Vec<TokenAssignment>,
+    pub digest: String,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Error)]
+pub enum TopologyError {
+    #[error("a topology must contain at least one member")]
+    NoMembers,
+    #[error("virtual node count must be greater than zero")]
+    NoVirtualNodes,
+    #[error("member count exceeds {MAX_MEMBERS}")]
+    TooManyMembers,
+    #[error("virtual node count exceeds {MAX_VIRTUAL_NODES}")]
+    TooManyVirtualNodes,
+    #[error("token assignment count exceeds {MAX_TOKEN_ASSIGNMENTS}")]
+    TooManyAssignments,
+    #[error("node id must not be empty")]
+    EmptyNodeId,
+    #[error("node id exceeds {MAX_NODE_ID_BYTES} bytes")]
+    NodeIdTooLong,
+    #[error("endpoint must not be empty")]
+    EmptyEndpoint,
+    #[error("endpoint exceeds {MAX_ENDPOINT_BYTES} bytes")]
+    EndpointTooLong,
+    #[error("duplicate node id: {0}")]
+    DuplicateNodeId(String),
+    #[error("duplicate endpoint: {0}")]
+    DuplicateEndpoint(String),
+    #[error("topology has no token assignments")]
+    NoAssignments,
+    #[error("unsupported hash configuration: {algorithm}, encoding version {encoding_version}")]
+    UnsupportedHashConfiguration {
+        algorithm: String,
+        encoding_version: u32,
+    },
+    #[error("topology digest mismatch")]
+    DigestMismatch,
+    #[error("members or token assignments are not in canonical form")]
+    NonCanonical,
+    #[error("token assignment references unknown node: {0}")]
+    UnknownAssignedNode(String),
+    #[error("desired replication factor must be greater than zero")]
+    NoReplicas,
+    #[error("desired replication factor exceeds {MAX_MEMBERS}")]
+    TooManyReplicas,
+    #[error("FirstSuccessor requires a desired replication factor of at least two")]
+    FirstSuccessorRequiresFollower,
+    #[error("minimum admitted copies must be greater than zero")]
+    NoMinimumAdmittedCopies,
+    #[error("maximum replica lag must be greater than zero")]
+    NoMaximumReplicaLag,
+    #[error("minimum admitted copies exceeds the desired replication factor")]
+    MinimumAdmittedCopiesExceedReplicationFactor,
+    #[error("minimum healthy followers exceeds the desired follower count")]
+    MinimumHealthyFollowersExceedReplicationFactor,
+    #[error("unknown write acknowledgement policy: {0}")]
+    UnknownWriteAckPolicy(i32),
+    #[error(
+        "receipt retention must be between {MIN_CLUSTER_TIMING_MILLIS} and \
+         {MAX_CLUSTER_TIMING_MILLIS} ms"
+    )]
+    ReceiptRetentionOutOfRange,
+    #[error(
+        "lease duration must be between {MIN_CLUSTER_TIMING_MILLIS} and \
+         {MAX_CLUSTER_TIMING_MILLIS} ms"
+    )]
+    LeaseDurationOutOfRange,
+}
+
+impl TopologySnapshot {
+    pub fn new(
+        epoch: u64,
+        hash_seed: u64,
+        virtual_nodes: u32,
+        members: Vec<Member>,
+    ) -> Result<Self, TopologyError> {
+        Self::new_with_config(
+            epoch,
+            hash_seed,
+            virtual_nodes,
+            members,
+            TopologyConfig::default(),
+        )
+    }
+
+    pub fn new_with_config(
+        epoch: u64,
+        hash_seed: u64,
+        virtual_nodes: u32,
+        members: Vec<Member>,
+        config: TopologyConfig,
+    ) -> Result<Self, TopologyError> {
+        Self::new_with_timings(
+            epoch,
+            hash_seed,
+            virtual_nodes,
+            members,
+            config,
+            ClusterTimings::default(),
+        )
+    }
+
+    pub fn new_with_timings(
+        epoch: u64,
+        hash_seed: u64,
+        virtual_nodes: u32,
+        mut members: Vec<Member>,
+        config: TopologyConfig,
+        timings: ClusterTimings,
+    ) -> Result<Self, TopologyError> {
+        validate_members(&members, virtual_nodes)?;
+        validate_config(&config)?;
+        timings.validate()?;
+        members.sort_by(|left, right| left.node_id.cmp(&right.node_id));
+
+        let assignment_count = members
+            .len()
+            .checked_mul(virtual_nodes as usize)
+            .ok_or(TopologyError::TooManyAssignments)?;
+        let mut assignments = Vec::with_capacity(assignment_count);
+        for member in &members {
+            for vnode in 0..virtual_nodes {
+                let mut encoded = Vec::with_capacity(member.node_id.len() + 24);
+                encoded.extend_from_slice(b"hashring-rs:vnode:v1\0");
+                encoded.extend_from_slice(&(member.node_id.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
+                encoded.extend_from_slice(member.node_id.as_bytes());
+                encoded.extend_from_slice(&vnode.to_be_bytes());
+                assignments.push(TokenAssignment {
+                    token: xxh3_64_with_seed(&encoded, hash_seed),
+                    node_id: member.node_id.clone(),
+                });
+            }
+        }
+        assignments.sort_by(|left, right| {
+            left.token
+                .cmp(&right.token)
+                .then_with(|| left.node_id.cmp(&right.node_id))
+        });
+
+        let mut snapshot = Self {
+            epoch,
+            hash_seed,
+            hash_algorithm: HASH_ALGORITHM.to_owned(),
+            encoding_version: ENCODING_VERSION,
+            virtual_nodes,
+            desired_replication_factor: config.desired_replication_factor,
+            write_ack_policy: config.write_ack_policy,
+            write_availability_guard: config.write_availability_guard,
+            timings,
+            members,
+            assignments,
+            digest: String::new(),
+        };
+        snapshot.digest = snapshot.calculate_digest();
+        Ok(snapshot)
+    }
+
+    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), TopologyError> {
+        validate_members(&self.members, self.virtual_nodes)?;
+        validate_config(&self.config())?;
+        if self.hash_algorithm != HASH_ALGORITHM || self.encoding_version != ENCODING_VERSION {
+            return Err(TopologyError::UnsupportedHashConfiguration {
+                algorithm: self.hash_algorithm.clone(),
+                encoding_version: self.encoding_version,
+            });
+        }
+        if self.assignments.is_empty() {
+            return Err(TopologyError::NoAssignments);
+        }
+        let member_ids: HashSet<_> = self.members.iter().map(|member| &member.node_id).collect();
+        for assignment in &self.assignments {
+            if !member_ids.contains(&assignment.node_id) {
+                return Err(TopologyError::UnknownAssignedNode(
+                    assignment.node_id.clone(),
+                ));
+            }
+        }
+        let canonical = Self::new_with_timings(
+            self.epoch,
+            self.hash_seed,
+            self.virtual_nodes,
+            self.members.clone(),
+            self.config(),
+            self.timings.clone(),
+        )?;
+        if canonical.digest != self.digest {
+            return Err(TopologyError::DigestMismatch);
+        }
+        if canonical.members != self.members || canonical.assignments != self.assignments {
+            return Err(TopologyError::NonCanonical);
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+
+    pub fn key_token(&self, key: &[u8]) -> u64 {
+        key_token(key, self.hash_seed)
+    }
+
+    pub fn owner(&self, key: &[u8]) -> Result<&Member, TopologyError> {
+        self.owner_for_token(self.key_token(key))
+    }
+
+    pub fn owner_for_token(&self, token: u64) -> Result<&Member, TopologyError> {
+        let index = self
+            .assignments
+            .partition_point(|assignment| assignment.token < token);
+        let assignment = &self.assignments[index % self.assignments.len()];
+        self.members
+            .iter()
+            .find(|member| member.node_id == assignment.node_id)
+            .ok_or_else(|| TopologyError::UnknownAssignedNode(assignment.node_id.clone()))
+    }
+
+    pub fn config(&self) -> TopologyConfig {
+        TopologyConfig {
+            desired_replication_factor: self.desired_replication_factor,
+            write_ack_policy: self.write_ack_policy,
+            write_availability_guard: self.write_availability_guard.clone(),
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub fn replica_node_ids_for_token(&self, token: u64) -> Result<Vec<&str>, TopologyError> {
+        let owner_index = self
+            .assignments
+            .partition_point(|assignment| assignment.token < token)
+            % self.assignments.len();
+        let target_count = usize::min(self.desired_replication_factor as usize, self.members.len());
+        let mut seen = HashSet::with_capacity(target_count);
+        let mut replicas = Vec::with_capacity(target_count);
+        for offset in 0..self.assignments.len() {
+            let assignment = &self.assignments[(owner_index + offset) % self.assignments.len()];
+            if seen.insert(assignment.node_id.as_str()) {
+                replicas.push(assignment.node_id.as_str());
+                if replicas.len() == target_count {
+                    break;
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        if replicas.is_empty() {
+            return Err(TopologyError::NoAssignments);
+        }
+        Ok(replicas)
+    }
+
+    pub fn derived_ranges(&self) -> Result<Vec<DerivedRange>, TopologyError> {
+        let mut boundaries: Vec<_> = self
+            .assignments
+            .iter()
+            .map(|assignment| assignment.token)
+            .collect();
+        boundaries.dedup();
+        let mut previous = *boundaries.last().ok_or(TopologyError::NoAssignments)?;
+        let mut ranges = Vec::with_capacity(boundaries.len());
+        for end in boundaries {
+            let replicas = self.replica_node_ids_for_token(end)?;
+            ranges.push(DerivedRange {
+                start_exclusive: previous,
+                end_inclusive: end,
+                owner_node_id: replicas[0].to_owned(),
+                follower_node_ids: replicas[1..]
+                    .iter()
+                    .map(|node_id| (*node_id).to_owned())
+                    .collect(),
+            });
+            previous = end;
+        }
+        Ok(ranges)
+    }
+
+    fn calculate_digest(&self) -> String {
+        let mut unsigned = self.clone();
+        unsigned.digest.clear();
+        let canonical =
+            serde_json::to_vec(&unsigned).expect("serializing an in-memory topology cannot fail");
+        blake3::hash(&canonical).to_hex().to_string()
+    }
+}
+
+fn validate_config(config: &TopologyConfig) -> Result<(), TopologyError> {
+    if config.desired_replication_factor == 0 {
+        return Err(TopologyError::NoReplicas);
+    }
+    if config.desired_replication_factor as usize > MAX_MEMBERS {
+        return Err(TopologyError::TooManyReplicas);
+    }
+    if config.write_ack_policy == WriteAckPolicy::FirstSuccessor
+        && config.desired_replication_factor < 2
+    {
+        return Err(TopologyError::FirstSuccessorRequiresFollower);
+    }
+    if config.write_availability_guard.minimum_admitted_copies == 0 {
+        return Err(TopologyError::NoMinimumAdmittedCopies);
+    }
+    if config.write_availability_guard.max_replica_lag_millis == 0 {
+        return Err(TopologyError::NoMaximumReplicaLag);
+    }
+    let guard = &config.write_availability_guard;
+    if guard.minimum_admitted_copies > config.desired_replication_factor {
+        return Err(TopologyError::MinimumAdmittedCopiesExceedReplicationFactor);
+    }
+    if guard.minimum_healthy_followers > config.desired_replication_factor.saturating_sub(1) {
+        return Err(TopologyError::MinimumHealthyFollowersExceedReplicationFactor);
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn validate_members(members: &[Member], virtual_nodes: u32) -> Result<(), TopologyError> {
+    if members.is_empty() {
+        return Err(TopologyError::NoMembers);
+    }
+    if virtual_nodes == 0 {
+        return Err(TopologyError::NoVirtualNodes);
+    }
+    if members.len() > MAX_MEMBERS {
+        return Err(TopologyError::TooManyMembers);
+    }
+    if virtual_nodes > MAX_VIRTUAL_NODES {
+        return Err(TopologyError::TooManyVirtualNodes);
+    }
+    if members
+        .len()
+        .checked_mul(virtual_nodes as usize)
+        .is_none_or(|assignments| assignments > MAX_TOKEN_ASSIGNMENTS)
+    {
+        return Err(TopologyError::TooManyAssignments);
+    }
+    let mut node_ids = HashSet::new();
+    let mut endpoints = HashSet::new();
+    for member in members {
+        if member.node_id.is_empty() {
+            return Err(TopologyError::EmptyNodeId);
+        }
+        if member.node_id.len() > MAX_NODE_ID_BYTES {
+            return Err(TopologyError::NodeIdTooLong);
+        }
+        if member.endpoint.is_empty() {
+            return Err(TopologyError::EmptyEndpoint);
+        }
+        if member.endpoint.len() > MAX_ENDPOINT_BYTES {
+            return Err(TopologyError::EndpointTooLong);
+        }
+        if !node_ids.insert(&member.node_id) {
+            return Err(TopologyError::DuplicateNodeId(member.node_id.clone()));
+        }
+        if !endpoints.insert(&member.endpoint) {
+            return Err(TopologyError::DuplicateEndpoint(member.endpoint.clone()));
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}

+                    max_replica_lag_millis: guard.max_replica_lag_millis,
+                })
+                .ok_or(TopologyError::NoMinimumAdmittedCopies)?,
+            timings: ClusterTimings {
+                receipt_retention_millis: snapshot.receipt_retention_millis,
+                lease_duration_millis: snapshot.lease_duration_millis,

+                .members

+                    endpoint: "http://127.0.0.1:5002".into(),
+                },
+                Member {
+                    node_id: "node-c".into(),
+                    endpoint: "http://127.0.0.1:5003".into(),
+                },
+            ],
+            TopologyConfig {
+                desired_replication_factor,
+                write_ack_policy,
+                write_availability_guard: WriteAvailabilityGuard::default(),
+            },
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn derived_ranges_cover_wraparound_and_skip_repeated_nodes() {
+        let topology = configured_topology(3, WriteAckPolicy::OwnerOnly);
+        let ranges = topology.derived_ranges().unwrap();
+
+        assert_eq!(ranges.len(), topology.assignments.len());
+        assert_eq!(
+            ranges[0].start_exclusive,
+            topology.assignments.last().unwrap().token
+        );
+        assert_eq!(ranges[0].end_inclusive, topology.assignments[0].token);
+        for range in ranges {
+            let replicas = topology
+                .replica_node_ids_for_token(range.end_inclusive)
+                .unwrap();
+            assert_eq!(replicas[0], range.owner_node_id);
+            assert_eq!(replicas[1..], range.follower_node_ids);
+            assert_eq!(replicas.len(), 3);
+            assert_eq!(replicas.iter().copied().collect::<HashSet<_>>().len(), 3);
+        }
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn desired_replication_factor_above_membership_is_visibly_under_replicated() {
+        let topology = TopologySnapshot::new_with_config(
+            1,
+            42,
+            16,
+            members(),
+            TopologyConfig {
+                desired_replication_factor: 5,
+                ..TopologyConfig::default()
+            },
+        )
+        .unwrap();
+
+        assert_eq!(topology.desired_replication_factor, 5);
+        assert!(topology.derived_ranges().unwrap().iter().all(|range| {
+            1 + range.follower_node_ids.len() < topology.desired_replication_factor as usize
+        }));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn first_successor_becomes_owner_when_the_owner_is_removed() {
+        let topology = configured_topology(3, WriteAckPolicy::OwnerOnly);
+        for range in topology.derived_ranges().unwrap() {
+            let expected_successor = range.follower_node_ids[0].clone();
+            let remaining = topology
+                .members
+                .iter()
+                .filter(|member| member.node_id != range.owner_node_id)
+                .cloned()
+                .collect();
+            let after_removal = TopologySnapshot::new_with_config(
+                topology.epoch + 1,
+                topology.hash_seed,
+                topology.virtual_nodes,
+                remaining,
+                topology.config(),
+            )
+            .unwrap();
+            assert_eq!(
+                after_removal
+                    .owner_for_token(range.end_inclusive)
+                    .unwrap()
+                    .node_id,
+                expected_successor
+            );
+        }
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn topology_configuration_is_part_of_digest_and_wire_encoding() {
+        let base = configured_topology(3, WriteAckPolicy::OwnerOnly);
+        let policy = configured_topology(3, WriteAckPolicy::AllReplicas);
+        let rf = configured_topology(2, WriteAckPolicy::OwnerOnly);
+        let mut guard_config = base.config();
+        guard_config.write_availability_guard.max_replica_lag_millis += 1;
+        let guard = TopologySnapshot::new_with_config(
+            base.epoch,
+            base.hash_seed,
+            base.virtual_nodes,
+            base.members.clone(),
+            guard_config,
+        )
+        .unwrap();
+
+        assert_ne!(base.digest, policy.digest);
+        assert_ne!(base.digest, rf.digest);
+        assert_ne!(base.digest, guard.digest);
+        let first = crate::proto::TopologySnapshot::from(&base).encode_to_vec();
+        let second = crate::proto::TopologySnapshot::from(&base).encode_to_vec();
+        assert_eq!(first, second);
+        assert_eq!(
+            TopologySnapshot::try_from(crate::proto::TopologySnapshot::from(&base)).unwrap(),
+            base
+        );
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn first_successor_policy_requires_a_follower() {
+        let error = TopologySnapshot::new_with_config(
+            1,
+            42,
+            16,
+            members(),
+            TopologyConfig {
+                desired_replication_factor: 1,
+                write_ack_policy: WriteAckPolicy::FirstSuccessor,
+                write_availability_guard: WriteAvailabilityGuard::default(),
+            },
+        )
+        .unwrap_err();
+
+        assert!(matches!(
+            error,
+            TopologyError::FirstSuccessorRequiresFollower
+        ));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn impossible_write_guards_are_rejected_including_rf_one() {
+        let mut config = TopologyConfig::default();
+        config.write_availability_guard.minimum_admitted_copies = 4;
+        assert!(matches!(
+            TopologySnapshot::new_with_config(1, 42, 16, members(), config),
+            Err(TopologyError::MinimumAdmittedCopiesExceedReplicationFactor)
+        ));
+
+        let mut config = TopologyConfig::default();
+        config.write_availability_guard.minimum_healthy_followers = 3;
+        assert!(matches!(
+            TopologySnapshot::new_with_config(1, 42, 16, members(), config),
+            Err(TopologyError::MinimumHealthyFollowersExceedReplicationFactor)
+        ));
+
+        let rf_one = TopologyConfig {
+            desired_replication_factor: 1,
+            ..TopologyConfig::default()
+        };
+        TopologySnapshot::new_with_config(1, 42, 16, members(), rf_one).unwrap();
+
+        let impossible_rf_one = TopologyConfig {
+            desired_replication_factor: 1,
+            write_availability_guard: WriteAvailabilityGuard {
+                minimum_admitted_copies: 2,
+                minimum_healthy_followers: 1,
+                ..WriteAvailabilityGuard::default()
+            },
+            ..TopologyConfig::default()
+        };
+        assert!(matches!(
+            TopologySnapshot::new_with_config(1, 42, 16, members(), impossible_rf_one),
+            Err(TopologyError::MinimumAdmittedCopiesExceedReplicationFactor)
+        ));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn maximum_assignment_topology_fits_control_plane_limit() {
+        let members = (0..256)
+            .map(|index| Member {
+                node_id: format!("n{index:03}{}", "x".repeat(MAX_NODE_ID_BYTES - 4)),
+                endpoint: format!(
+                    "http://127.0.0.1/{index:03}{}",
+                    "x".repeat(MAX_ENDPOINT_BYTES - 21)
+                ),
+            })
+            .collect();
+        let topology = TopologySnapshot::new(1, 42, MAX_VIRTUAL_NODES, members).unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(topology.assignments.len(), MAX_TOKEN_ASSIGNMENTS);
+        let wire = crate::proto::TopologySnapshot::from(&topology);
+        assert!(wire.encoded_len() <= crate::limits::MAX_CONTROL_MESSAGE_BYTES);
+
+        let source = &topology.members[0];
+        let destination = &topology.members[1];
+        let range = crate::migration::RangeMigration {
+            range_id: "f".repeat(64),
+            start_exclusive: u64::MAX - 1,
+            end_inclusive: u64::MAX,
+            source_node_id: source.node_id.clone(),
+            destination_node_id: destination.node_id.clone(),
+            source_endpoint: "s".repeat(MAX_ENDPOINT_BYTES),
+            destination_endpoint: "d".repeat(MAX_ENDPOINT_BYTES),
+            source_process_instance_id: "s".repeat(36),
+            destination_process_instance_id: "d".repeat(36),
+            source_cleaned: false,
+            snapshot_records: u64::MAX,
+            changelog_watermark: u64::MAX,
+            changelog_replay_ms: 0,
+            verified: true,
+        };
+        let change = crate::migration::TopologyChange {
+            change_id: "c".repeat(36),
+            base_epoch: 0,
+            base_topology: None,
+            supersedes_change_id: None,
+            target_topology: topology,
+            phase: crate::migration::MigrationPhase::Planned,
+            ranges: vec![range; crate::migration::MAX_MIGRATION_RANGES],
+            replica_obligations: Vec::new(),
+            stopped_node_ids: Vec::new(),
+            stopping_node_ids: Vec::new(),
+            stop_prepared_node_ids: Vec::new(),
+            failed_node_id: None,
+            activation_ready: false,
+            direct_merge: false,
+            timings: crate::migration::MigrationTimings::default(),
+        };
+        let wire = crate::proto::TopologyChangeSnapshot::from(&change);
+        assert!(wire.encoded_len() <= crate::limits::MAX_CONTROL_MESSAGE_BYTES);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn cluster_timings_travel_with_every_later_topology() {
+        let timings = ClusterTimings {
+            receipt_retention_millis: 90_000,
+            lease_duration_millis: 3_000,
+        };
+        let committed = TopologySnapshot::new_with_timings(
+            1,
+            42,
+            16,
+            members(),
+            TopologyConfig::default(),
+            timings.clone(),
+        )
+        .unwrap();
+        let wire = crate::proto::TopologySnapshot::from(&committed);
+        assert_eq!(TopologySnapshot::try_from(wire).unwrap(), committed);
+
+        let mut target_members = members();
+        target_members.push(Member {
+            node_id: "node-c".into(),
+            endpoint: "http://127.0.0.1:5003".into(),
+        });
+        let change = crate::migration::TopologyChange::plan(&committed, target_members).unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(change.target_topology.timings, timings);
+
+        // The timings are covered by the digest like the hash seed.
+        let mut tampered = committed;
+        tampered.timings.lease_duration_millis = 4_000;
+        assert!(matches!(
+            tampered.validate(),
+            Err(TopologyError::DigestMismatch)
+        ));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn cluster_timings_are_bounded() {
+        let build = |receipt_retention_millis, lease_duration_millis| {
+            TopologySnapshot::new_with_timings(
+                1,
+                42,
+                16,
+                members(),
+                TopologyConfig::default(),
+                ClusterTimings {
+                    receipt_retention_millis,
+                    lease_duration_millis,
+                },
+            )
+        };
+        assert!(build(MIN_CLUSTER_TIMING_MILLIS, MAX_CLUSTER_TIMING_MILLIS).is_ok());
+        assert!(matches!(
+            build(MIN_CLUSTER_TIMING_MILLIS - 1, 5_000),
+            Err(TopologyError::ReceiptRetentionOutOfRange)
+        ));
+        assert!(matches!(
+            build(60_000, MAX_CLUSTER_TIMING_MILLIS + 1),
+            Err(TopologyError::LeaseDurationOutOfRange)
+        ));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn tampering_is_detected() {
+        let mut topology = TopologySnapshot::new(1, 42, 16, members()).unwrap();
+        topology.epoch = 2;
+        assert!(matches!(
+            topology.validate(),
+            Err(TopologyError::DigestMismatch)
+        ));
+    }
+}

+use std::{
+    env, fs,
+    path::{Path, PathBuf},
+    process::Command,
+};
+
+const SOURCE_PATHS: &[&str] = &[
+    "Cargo.toml",
+    "Cargo.lock",
+    "PLAN.md",
+    "README.md",
+    "src",
+    "crates",
+    "tests",
+];
+
+fn main() {
+    let manifest_dir = env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").expect("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR");
+    let workspace = Path::new(&manifest_dir)
+        .join("../..")
+        .canonicalize()
+        .expect("canonical workspace path");
+    emit("HASHRING_BUILD_SOURCE_ROOT", workspace.to_string_lossy());
+    emit(
+        "HASHRING_BUILD_GIT_COMMIT",
+        command_output(&workspace, "git", &["rev-parse", "HEAD"])
+            .unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown".into()),
+    );
+    emit(
+        "HASHRING_BUILD_GIT_DIRTY",
+        command_output(&workspace, "git", &["status", "--porcelain"])
+            .map(|output| (!output.is_empty()).to_string())
+            .unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown".into()),
+    );
+    emit(
+        "HASHRING_BUILD_RUSTC",
+        command_output(&workspace, "rustc", &["--version"]).unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown".into()),
+    );
+    emit(
+        "HASHRING_BUILD_PROFILE",
+        env::var("PROFILE").unwrap_or_else(|_| "unknown".into()),
+    );
+    emit(
+        "HASHRING_BUILD_TARGET",
+        env::var("TARGET").unwrap_or_else(|_| "unknown".into()),
+    );
+    emit(
+        "HASHRING_BUILD_SOURCE_TREE_BLAKE3",
+        source_tree_digest(&workspace).expect("hashing workspace source inputs"),
+    );
+
+    println!(
+        "cargo:rerun-if-changed={}",
+        workspace.join(".git/HEAD").display()
+    );
+    println!(
+        "cargo:rerun-if-changed={}",
+        workspace.join(".git/index").display()
+    );
+    for path in SOURCE_PATHS {
+        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", workspace.join(path).display());
+    }
+}
+
+fn emit(name: &str, value: impl AsRef<str>) {
+    println!("cargo:rustc-env={name}={}", value.as_ref());
+}
+
+fn source_tree_digest(workspace: &Path) -> std::io::Result<String> {
+    let mut files = Vec::new();
+    for path in SOURCE_PATHS {
+        collect_files(&workspace.join(path), &mut files)?;
+    }
+    files.sort();
+    let mut hasher = blake3::Hasher::new();
+    hasher.update(b"hashring-rs:source-tree:v1\0");
+    for path in files {
+        let relative = path.strip_prefix(workspace).unwrap_or(&path);
+        let encoded = relative.to_string_lossy();
+        let contents = fs::read(&path)?;
+        hasher.update(&(encoded.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
+        hasher.update(encoded.as_bytes());
+        hasher.update(&(contents.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
+        hasher.update(&contents);
+    }
+    Ok(hasher.finalize().to_hex().to_string())
+}
+
+fn collect_files(path: &Path, files: &mut Vec<PathBuf>) -> std::io::Result<()> {
+    if path.is_file() {
+        files.push(path.to_owned());
+    } else if path.is_dir() {
+        for entry in fs::read_dir(path)? {
+            collect_files(&entry?.path(), files)?;
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn command_output(cwd: &Path, program: &str, arguments: &[&str]) -> Option<String> {
+    let output = Command::new(program)
+        .current_dir(cwd)
+        .args(arguments)
+        .output()
+        .ok()?;
+    output
+        .status
+        .success()
+        .then(|| String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_owned())
+}

-/// A worker's request ledger is flushed this often, so a failed run still has
-/// nearly all of its completed requests.
-const LEDGER_FLUSH_INTERVAL: u64 = 64;
-const NEVER: u64 = u64::MAX;

-#[derive(Clone, Default)]
-struct OperationMix {
-    /// The number of slots that carry a GET.
-    get: u64,
-    /// The number of slots that carry a PUT.
-    put: u64,
-    /// The number of slots that carry a DELETE.
-    delete: u64,
-    /// The number of slots the mix divides the operations into.
-    total: u64,
-    /// The step of the walk over the slots.
-    stride: u64,
-}
-
-impl OperationMix {
-    fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<Self> {
-        let parts: Vec<u64> = text
-            .split(':')
-            .map(|part| {
-                part.trim()
-                    .parse::<u64>()
-                    .with_context(|| format!("parsing the operation mix {text:?}"))
-            })
-            .collect::<Result<_>>()?;
-        ensure!(
-            parts.len() == 3,
-            "the operation mix must be GET:PUT:DELETE, not {text:?}"
-        );
-        let total = parts
-            .iter()
-            .fold(0_u64, |sum, part| sum.saturating_add(*part));
-        ensure!(total > 0, "the operation mix is empty");
-        Ok(Self {
-            get: parts[0],
-            put: parts[1],
-            delete: parts[2],
-            total,
-            stride: coprime_stride(total),
-        })
-    }
-
-    fn choose(&self, step: u64, worker: usize) -> Operation {
-        // A walk whose step shares no factor with the total reaches every
-        // slot, so every worker offers every operation instead of only the
-        // ones its own step happens to land on.
-        let slot = (step
-            .wrapping_mul(self.stride)
-            .wrapping_add(worker as u64 * 11))
-            % self.total;
-        if slot < self.get {
-            Operation::Get
-        } else if slot < self.get.saturating_add(self.put) {
-            Operation::Put
-        } else {
-            Operation::Delete
-        }
-    }
-
-    /// Whether the mix offers the operation at all.
-    fn offers(&self, operation: Operation) -> bool {
-        match operation {
-            Operation::Get => self.get > 0,
-            Operation::Put => self.put > 0,
-            Operation::Delete => self.delete > 0,
-        }
-    }
-}
-
-/// The smallest step at or above 37 that shares no factor with the total.
-///
-/// A fixed step only reaches every slot when it is coprime with the total, so
-/// the step is searched for instead of assumed: a step of 37 leaves a worker
-/// without one of the three operations whenever the total is a multiple of 37.
-fn coprime_stride(total: u64) -> u64 {
-    if total <= 1 {
-        return 1;
-    }
-    let mut stride = 37;
-    while gcd(stride, total) != 1 {
-        stride += 1;
-    }
-    stride
-}
-
-fn gcd(mut left: u64, mut right: u64) -> u64 {
-    while right != 0 {
-        let remainder = left % right;
-        left = right;
-        right = remainder;
-    }
-    left
-}

-/// One state the run acknowledged, kept as digests.
-#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
-struct AcknowledgedState {
-    /// `None` when the key was absent.

-    version: Option<VersionDigest>,

-impl AcknowledgedState {
-    fn of(state: &PossibleState) -> Self {
-        Self {
-            value: state.value.as_deref().map(ValueDigest::of),
-            version: state.version.as_ref().map(VersionDigest::of),
-        }
-    }

-    /// The state an observation describes.
-    ///
-    /// The digests are taken once per observation: the history holds up to
-    /// [`KeyModel::window`] states, and hashing the value once per state would
-    /// cost a hash per state per read.
-    fn of_observation(value: Option<&[u8]>, version: Option<&RecordVersion>) -> Self {
-        Self {
-            value: value.map(ValueDigest::of),
-            version: version.map(VersionDigest::of),
-        }
-    }
-
-    /// Whether the observation is this acknowledged state.
-    fn matches(&self, observation: &AcknowledgedState) -> bool {
-        match (&self.value, &observation.value) {
-            (None, None) => true,
-            (Some(expected), Some(observed)) => {
-                expected == observed
-                    && self
-                        .version
-                        .as_ref()
-                        .is_none_or(|expected| Some(expected) == observation.version.as_ref())
-            }
-            _ => false,

-    /// A fingerprint for the window's membership index.
-    ///
-    /// The index holds a 64-bit hash rather than a second copy of the state,
-    /// which keeps the window's memory close to the digests themselves. Two
-    /// states can share a fingerprint: the index counts it, so a hit that
-    /// finds no matching state is a collision, and the state is new after all.
-    fn fingerprint(&self) -> u64 {
-        let mut hasher = DefaultHasher::new();
-        self.hash(&mut hasher);
-        hasher.finish()
-    }
-}

-enum Observation {
-    Matches,
-    /// The observation is an older acknowledged state. Under `OwnerOnly` an
-    /// owner failure may allow this; the caller decides whether it is a
-    /// failure.
-    Rollback {
-        first: bool,
-        kind: &'static str,
-        eligible: bool,
-    },
-    /// The observation is not explainable by the recorded history, and the
-    /// history is too short to say whether it is an allowed rollback.
-    Undecidable,
-    /// The observation is not explainable by the recorded history.
-    Impossible,
-}

-#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
-struct KeyModel {
-    possible: Vec<PossibleState>,
-    /// Definite and uncertain mutation candidates and concretely observed
-    /// states, as digests, in the order each was last recorded. A later read
-    /// that matches one of these but not `possible` is a rollback rather than an arbitrary
-    /// value. The list is bounded by `window`, and the states it dropped are
-    /// counted.
-    acknowledged: VecDeque<AcknowledgedState>,
-    /// The states `acknowledged` holds, by fingerprint and count, so
-    /// acknowledging a state the window has never held does not scan the
-    /// window: only a state that is already in it needs its position. A
-    /// fingerprint is one hash instead of a second copy of the state, and two
-    /// states can share one: the count keeps the index right when one of them
-    /// leaves the window.
-    known: HashMap<u64, usize>,
-    /// How many acknowledged states the bound dropped.
-    dropped_acknowledged: u64,
-    /// How many acknowledged states the key keeps. It has to cover the writes
-    /// the key takes during the load: a rollback to a state that left the
-    /// window cannot be told apart from a value the history never held.
-    window: usize,
-    rolled_back: bool,
-    /// The newest topology in which a mutation or read established this key.
-    /// A failure of an older owner cannot undo a state established after it.
-    established_epoch: u64,
-}
-
-impl KeyModel {
-    fn new(state: PossibleState, window: usize) -> Self {
-        let mut model = Self {
-            possible: Vec::new(),
-            acknowledged: VecDeque::new(),
-            known: HashMap::new(),
-            dropped_acknowledged: 0,
-            window,
-            rolled_back: false,
-            established_epoch: 0,
-        };
-        model.resync(state);
-        model
-    }
-
-    fn begin_round(&mut self) {
-        self.rolled_back = false;
-    }
-
-    fn resync(&mut self, state: PossibleState) {
-        if let Some(version) = &state.version {
-            self.established_epoch = self.established_epoch.max(version.topology_epoch);
-        }
-        self.possible = vec![state.clone()];
-        self.remember(&state);
-    }
-
-    /// Keeps an acknowledged state, and forgets the oldest one when the key's
-    /// history is full.
-    ///
-    /// The window holds the most recently acknowledged states: a state that is
-    /// acknowledged again moves to the back, so a rollback to it is still
-    /// recognized after newer writes pushed it out of the window.
-    fn remember(&mut self, state: &PossibleState) {
-        let acknowledged = AcknowledgedState::of(state);
-        let fingerprint = acknowledged.fingerprint();
-        if self.acknowledged.back() == Some(&acknowledged) {
-            return;
-        }
-        if self.known.contains_key(&fingerprint) {
-            // A state the window already holds is acknowledged again, which is
-            // rare: find its place in the order and move it to the back.
-            if let Some(position) = self
-                .acknowledged
-                .iter()
-                .position(|entry| *entry == acknowledged)
-            {
-                if position + 1 != self.acknowledged.len() {
-                    let entry = self
-                        .acknowledged
-                        .remove(position)
-                        .expect("the position is inside the window");
-                    self.acknowledged.push_back(entry);
-                }
-                return;
-            }
-            // A fingerprint hit that finds no state is a collision: another
-            // state in the window has the same fingerprint. This state is new,
-            // and the count it adds keeps the other one indexed when it leaves.
-        }
-        if self.acknowledged.len() >= self.window
-            && let Some(evicted) = self.acknowledged.pop_front()
-        {
-            self.forget(evicted.fingerprint());
-            self.dropped_acknowledged += 1;
-        }
-        *self.known.entry(fingerprint).or_insert(0) += 1;
-        self.acknowledged.push_back(acknowledged);
-    }
-
-    /// Drops one state with this fingerprint from the index.
-    fn forget(&mut self, fingerprint: u64) {
-        let remaining = match self.known.get_mut(&fingerprint) {
-            Some(count) => {
-                *count -= 1;
-                *count
-            }
-            None => return,
-        };
-        if remaining == 0 {
-            self.known.remove(&fingerprint);
-        }
-    }
-
-    fn on_put(&mut self, value: Vec<u8>, version: RecordVersion) {
-        self.resync(PossibleState::present(value, version));
-    }
-
-    fn on_delete(&mut self, version: RecordVersion) {
-        self.resync(PossibleState::absent(Some(version)));
-    }
-
-    fn on_ambiguous_put(&mut self, value: Vec<u8>) {
-        let state = PossibleState {
-            value: Some(value),
-            version: None,
-        };
-        self.remember(&state);
-        self.possible.push(state);
-    }
-
-    fn on_ambiguous_delete(&mut self) {
-        let state = PossibleState::absent(None);
-        self.remember(&state);
-        self.possible.push(state);
-    }
-
-    fn observe_at(
-        &mut self,
-        value: Option<&[u8]>,
-        version: Option<&RecordVersion>,
-        response_epoch: u64,
-        failure_epoch: u64,
-        failure_injected: bool,
-    ) -> Observation {
-        let eligible = failure_injected
-            && response_epoch > failure_epoch
-            && self.established_epoch <= failure_epoch
-            && version.is_none_or(|version| version.topology_epoch <= failure_epoch);
-        let observation = self.observe(value, version);
-        // A successful read from the promoted owner establishes its state,
-        // even when the record itself still carries the old owner's version.
-        self.established_epoch = self.established_epoch.max(response_epoch);
-        match observation {
-            Observation::Rollback { first, kind, .. } => Observation::Rollback {
-                first,
-                kind,
-                eligible,
-            },
-            other => other,
-        }
-    }
-
-    fn observe(&mut self, value: Option<&[u8]>, version: Option<&RecordVersion>) -> Observation {
-        if let Some(uncertain) = self
-            .possible
-            .iter()
-            .find(|state| state.matches(value, version))
-            .map(|state| state.version.is_none())
-        {
-            let state = PossibleState {
-                value: value.map(<[u8]>::to_vec),
-                version: version.cloned(),
-            };
-            // Once a GET identifies an ambiguous PUT's version, that concrete
-            // state replaces its wildcard. Keep other historical candidates.
-            let concrete = AcknowledgedState::of(&state);
-            if uncertain
-                && concrete.value.is_some()
-                && concrete.version.is_some()
-                && let Some(index) = self
-                    .acknowledged
-                    .iter()
-                    .position(|entry| entry.value == concrete.value && entry.version.is_none())
-            {
-                let removed = self.acknowledged.remove(index).expect("known index");
-                self.forget(removed.fingerprint());
-            }
-            self.resync(state);
-            return Observation::Matches;
-        }
-        let observation = AcknowledgedState::of_observation(value, version);
-        if self
-            .acknowledged
-            .iter()
-            .any(|state| state.matches(&observation))
-        {
-            let first = !self.rolled_back;
-            self.rolled_back = true;
-            let expected_absent = self.possible.iter().any(|state| state.value.is_none());
-            let kind = match (value, expected_absent) {
-                (Some(_), true) => "acknowledged_delete_lost",
-                (Some(_), false) => "older_value_reappeared",
-                (None, _) => "acknowledged_value_lost",
-            };
-            // The read establishes the current state. Newer and uncertain
-            // states remain historical candidates, rather than live branches.
-            let state = match value {
-                Some(value) => PossibleState {
-                    value: Some(value.to_vec()),
-                    version: version.cloned(),
-                },
-                None => PossibleState::absent(None),
-            };
-            self.resync(state);
-            return Observation::Rollback {
-                first,
-                kind,
-                eligible: false,
-            };
-        }
-        if self.dropped_acknowledged > 0 {
-            // The history no longer holds every acknowledged state, so this
-            // read cannot be told apart from a rollback to a state that was
-            // dropped. It is undecidable, not impossible.
-            return Observation::Undecidable;
-        }
-        Observation::Impossible
-    }
-}

-    fn record_reduced_rf(&self, entry: &RequestEntry, invoked_ms: u64, victim_epoch: u64) {
-        let kill = self.kill_ms.load(Ordering::Acquire);
-        let published = self.published_ms.load(Ordering::Acquire);
-        if kill == NEVER
-            || invoked_ms <= kill
-            || invoked_ms >= published
-            || entry.start_epoch != victim_epoch
-            || entry.operation == "get"
-        {
-            return;
-        }
-        let mut reduced = self.reduced_rf.lock().expect("progress lock");
-        if entry.result == "ok"
-            && entry
-                .version
-                .as_ref()
-                .is_some_and(|v| v.topology_epoch == victim_epoch)
-        {
-            match entry.operation {
-                "put" => reduced.puts += 1,
-                "delete" => reduced.deletes += 1,
-                _ => {}
-            }
-        }
-        for reason in ["temporarily_unavailable", "replica_not_ready"] {
-            reduced.admission_rejections += entry.retry_reasons.get(reason).copied().unwrap_or(0);
-        }
-        if matches!(
-            entry.error_code.as_deref(),
-            Some("TemporarilyUnavailable" | "ReplicaNotReady")
-        ) {
-            reduced.admission_rejections += 1;
-        }
-        reduced.capacity_errors +=
-            u64::from(entry.error_code.as_deref() == Some("ResourceExhausted"));
-        reduced.capacity_retries += entry
-            .retry_reasons
-            .get("resource_exhausted")
-            .copied()
-            .unwrap_or(0);
-    }

-    fn record_failure(&self, invoked_ms: u64, completed_ms: u64) {

-        }

-            Operation::Delete => (&self.first_delete_after_kill_ms, &self.deletes_after_kill),

-fn retry_delta(
-    before: &BTreeMap<&'static str, u64>,
-    after: &BTreeMap<&'static str, u64>,

-        .filter_map(|(reason, count)| {

-/// The checks one round of a fault run has to pass.
-///
-/// The checks are collected instead of raised one by one: a round that fails
-/// ends the run, and the run then reports everything the round found instead
-/// of only the first problem.
-struct RoundChecks<'a> {
-    round: u32,
-    scenario: FaultScenario,
-    write_ack_policy: WriteAckPolicy,
-    mix: &'a OperationMix,
-    reads_after_kill: u64,
-    writes_after_kill: u64,
-    owner_unchanged: bool,
-    reduced_rf: &'a ReducedRfProgress,
-}
-
-impl RoundChecks<'_> {
-    /// The problems the round found. An empty list means the round passed.
-    fn failures(&self, stats: &WorkerStats) -> Vec<String> {
-        let mut failures = Vec::new();
-        if stats.impossible > 0 {
-            failures.push(format!(
-                "round {} observed {} values the history does not allow: {:?}",
-                self.round, stats.impossible, stats.violations
-            ));
-        }
-        if stats.requests() == 0 {
-            failures.push(format!(
-                "round {} completed no requests under load",
-                self.round
-            ));
-        }
-        // The load has to keep working after the failure, not only before it:
-        // a run whose writes stopped at the kill would still have completed
-        // requests before it.
-        for (operation, completed) in [
-            (Operation::Get, self.reads_after_kill),
-            (Operation::Put, self.writes_after_kill),
-        ] {
-            if self.mix.offers(operation) && completed == 0 {
-                failures.push(format!(
-                    "round {}: the load completed no {} after the kill",
-                    self.round,
-                    operation.name()
-                ));
-            }
-        }
-        if self.scenario == FaultScenario::Follower
-            && self.write_ack_policy == WriteAckPolicy::OwnerOnly
-        {
-            for (operation, count) in [
-                (Operation::Put, self.reduced_rf.puts),
-                (Operation::Delete, self.reduced_rf.deletes),
-            ] {
-                if self.mix.offers(operation) && count == 0 {
-                    failures.push(format!(
-                        "round {}: no {} succeeded at reduced RF before failover publication",
-                        self.round,
-                        operation.name()
-                    ));
-                }
-            }
-            if self.reduced_rf.admission_rejections > 0 {
-                failures.push(format!(
-                    "round {}: {} unexpected ACK/admission rejections at reduced RF",
-                    self.round, self.reduced_rf.admission_rejections
-                ));
-            }
-        }
-        if !self.owner_unchanged {
-            failures.push(format!(
-                "round {}: killing a follower changed the owner of a selected key",
-                self.round
-            ));
-        }
-        let forbidden = if self.scenario == FaultScenario::Follower
-            || self.write_ack_policy != WriteAckPolicy::OwnerOnly
-        {
-            stats.rollbacks
-        } else {
-            stats.forbidden_rollbacks
-        };
-        if forbidden > 0 {
-            failures.push(format!(
-                "round {} rolled back {} acknowledged changes: {:?}",
-                self.round, forbidden, stats.rollback_kinds
-            ));
-        }
-        if stats.undecidable > 0 {
-            // A read the history cannot explain is not a verified read. The
-            // run does not count it as a pass, in either scenario: under
-            // `OwnerOnly` a rollback is allowed, but once the history has been
-            // shortened it cannot be told apart from an impossible value, and
-            // a follower loss allows no rollback at all. The dropped figure is
-            // the round's total across its keys, not the number of states the
-            // keys of these reads dropped.
-            failures.push(format!(
-                "round {}: {} reads cannot be verified, because the acknowledged history was \
-                 shortened: {} states have been dropped in total from the history of the round's \
-                 keys, so a read cannot be told apart from a rollback to a dropped state: {:?}",
-                self.round,
-                stats.undecidable,
-                stats.dropped_acknowledged,
-                stats.undecidable_samples
-            ));
-        }
-        failures
-    }
-}

-/// One injected failure and everything the run measured about it.

-    pre_failure_replica_progress: Value,
-    reduced_rf_progress: ReducedRfProgress,
-    replica_status_after_failure: Value,
-    /// The seconds from the kill to the failover's publication.
-    kill_to_publish_seconds: f64,
-    /// The seconds from the kill to the first successful read.
-    read_recovery_seconds: Option<f64>,
-    /// The seconds from the kill to the first successful write.
-    write_recovery_seconds: Option<f64>,
-    /// The seconds from the kill to the first successful delete.

-    /// The milliseconds from the kill to the first failed request.

-    failure_to_full_rf_seconds: f64,
-    final_epoch: u64,
-    collateral_victim_owned_keys: u64,
-    collateral_rollbacks: u64,
-    load: Value,
-    rollbacks: u64,
-    /// The reads the history cannot explain, because the bounded history had
-    /// already dropped a state the read may have rolled back to. A run with
-    /// such a read does not count as a pass.
-    undecidable_reads: u64,
-    undecidable_samples: Vec<String>,
-    impossible_reads: u64,
-    /// The acknowledged states this round dropped. The history of a key is
-    /// cumulative over the run, so the round reports the difference from the
-    /// start of its own load, and the run's total is in

-fn select_victim(
-    config: &ExperimentConfig,
-    topology: &TopologySnapshot,
-    round: u32,
-    killed: &BTreeSet<String>,
-) -> Result<Victim> {
-    let candidates: Vec<&Member> = topology
-        .members
-        .iter()
-        .filter(|member| !killed.contains(&member.node_id))
-        .collect();
-    ensure!(!candidates.is_empty(), "fault run has no live candidate");
-    let minimum = (config.key_count as usize).clamp(1, MIN_COHORT);
-    let start = (round as usize - 1) % candidates.len();
-    for offset in 0..candidates.len() {

-/// What the cohort's ranges looked like in one sample of the replica status.
-///
-/// The reasons a range was not writable are counted per range, so the caller
-/// adds them up over its samples: the sum counts the (poll, range) pairs that
-/// were blocked, not the number of distinct ranges.
-fn cohort_replica_stats(
-    status: &ReplicaStatusResponse,
-    topology: &TopologySnapshot,
-    keys: &[u64],
-) -> (Option<usize>, usize, usize, BTreeMap<String, usize>) {
-    let mut live_rf = usize::MAX;
-    let mut under_replicated = 0;
-    let mut not_writable = 0;
-    let mut block_reasons: BTreeMap<String, usize> = BTreeMap::new();
-    let mut seen = BTreeMap::new();
-    for &key in keys {
-        let token = topology.key_token(&key.to_be_bytes());
-        let Some(range) = status.ranges.iter().find(|range| {
-            if range.start_exclusive < range.end_inclusive {
-                token > range.start_exclusive && token <= range.end_inclusive
-            } else {
-                token > range.start_exclusive || token <= range.end_inclusive
-            }
-        }) else {
-            continue;
-        };
-        if seen
-            .insert((range.start_exclusive, range.end_inclusive), range.live_rf)
-            .is_some()
-        {
-            continue;
-        }
-        live_rf = live_rf.min(range.live_rf as usize);
-        under_replicated += usize::from(range.under_replicated);
-        not_writable += usize::from(!range.writable);
-        if !range.writable {
-            // The reason a range was not writable is what tells a reader
-            // whether the load could have written to it.
-            let reason = if range.write_block_reason.is_empty() {
-                "unnamed".to_owned()
-            } else {
-                range.write_block_reason.clone()
-            };
-            *block_reasons.entry(reason).or_default() += 1;
-        }
-    }
-    (
-        (live_rf != usize::MAX).then_some(live_rf),
-        under_replicated,
-        not_writable,
-        block_reasons,
-    )
-}

-/// Records what the run measured, and then fails it if a round failed.
-///
-/// The record goes in before the check: a failed run still says what it saw,
-/// because the summary keeps the rounds it completed and the reasons it failed
-/// in `fault_failures` rather than only in the error text.
-fn record_run(
-    observations: &mut BTreeMap<String, Value>,
-    scenario_name: &str,
-    rounds_requested: u32,
-    acknowledged_window: usize,
-    rounds: &[FaultRound],
-    totals: &RunTotals,
-    failures: &[String],
-) -> Result<()> {
-    save_run(
-        observations,
-        scenario_name,
-        rounds_requested,
-        acknowledged_window,
-        rounds,
-        totals,
-        failures,
-    )?;
-    ensure!(failures.is_empty(), "{}", failures.join("; "));
-    Ok(())
-}

+//! node.
+//!
+//! `FaultScenario::Follower` kills a node that is only a follower for the
+//! selected keys and checks that the surviving owner keeps serving them.
+//! `FaultScenario::Owner` kills the owner and checks the failover, the ledger,
+//! and the permitted `OwnerOnly` rollbacks. Both scenarios keep the load
+//! running through the automatic removal, the replacement join, and RF repair,
+//! then verify every key the run touched.

+/// A worker's request ledger is flushed this often, so a failed run still has
+/// nearly all of its completed requests.
+const LEDGER_FLUSH_INTERVAL: u64 = 64;
+const NEVER: u64 = u64::MAX;
+const MIN_COHORT: usize = 8;
+
+#[derive(Clone, Default)]
+struct OperationMix {
+    /// The number of slots that carry a GET.
+    get: u64,
+    /// The number of slots that carry a PUT.
+    put: u64,
+    /// The number of slots that carry a DELETE.
+    delete: u64,
+    /// The number of slots the mix divides the operations into.
+    total: u64,
+    /// The step of the walk over the slots.
+    stride: u64,
+}
+
+impl OperationMix {
+    fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<Self> {
+        let parts: Vec<u64> = text
+            .split(':')
+            .map(|part| {
+                part.trim()
+                    .parse::<u64>()
+                    .with_context(|| format!("parsing the operation mix {text:?}"))
+            })
+            .collect::<Result<_>>()?;
+        ensure!(
+            parts.len() == 3,
+            "the operation mix must be GET:PUT:DELETE, not {text:?}"
+        );
+        let total = parts
+            .iter()
+            .fold(0_u64, |sum, part| sum.saturating_add(*part));
+        ensure!(total > 0, "the operation mix is empty");
+        Ok(Self {
+            get: parts[0],
+            put: parts[1],
+            delete: parts[2],
+            total,
+            stride: coprime_stride(total),
+        })
+    }
+
+    fn choose(&self, step: u64, worker: usize) -> Operation {
+        // A walk whose step shares no factor with the total reaches every
+        // slot, so every worker offers every operation instead of only the
+        // ones its own step happens to land on.
+        let slot = (step
+            .wrapping_mul(self.stride)
+            .wrapping_add(worker as u64 * 11))
+            % self.total;
+        if slot < self.get {
+            Operation::Get
+        } else if slot < self.get.saturating_add(self.put) {
+            Operation::Put
+        } else {
+            Operation::Delete
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Whether the mix offers the operation at all.
+    fn offers(&self, operation: Operation) -> bool {
+        match operation {
+            Operation::Get => self.get > 0,
+            Operation::Put => self.put > 0,
+            Operation::Delete => self.delete > 0,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// The smallest step at or above 37 that shares no factor with the total.
+///
+/// A fixed step only reaches every slot when it is coprime with the total, so
+/// the step is searched for instead of assumed: a step of 37 leaves a worker
+/// without one of the three operations whenever the total is a multiple of 37.
+fn coprime_stride(total: u64) -> u64 {
+    if total <= 1 {
+        return 1;
+    }
+    let mut stride = 37;
+    while gcd(stride, total) != 1 {
+        stride += 1;
+    }
+    stride
+}
+
+fn gcd(mut left: u64, mut right: u64) -> u64 {
+    while right != 0 {
+        let remainder = left % right;
+        left = right;
+        right = remainder;
+    }
+    left
+}

+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
+enum Operation {
+    Get,
+    Put,
+    Delete,

+struct RequestLedger {

+impl RequestLedger {
