+    #[test]
+    fn the_window_keeps_its_index_in_step_with_its_order() {
+        // The index is what makes acknowledging a new state constant time, so
+        // it must count exactly the states the window holds.
+        let mut model = KeyModel::new(PossibleState::absent(None), WINDOW);
+        for sequence in 1..=(WINDOW as u64 * 4) {
+            model.on_put(sequence.to_be_bytes().to_vec(), version(sequence));
+            // Acknowledge a state the window already dropped, which inserts it
+            // again, and one it holds, which moves it to the back.
+            if sequence % 3 == 0 {
+                model.on_put((sequence / 2).to_be_bytes().to_vec(), version(sequence / 2));
+            }
+            assert_eq!(
+                model.known.values().sum::<usize>(),
+                model.acknowledged.len(),
+                "the index and the order disagree after {sequence} writes"
+            );
+            for entry in &model.acknowledged {
+                assert!(
+                    model
+                        .known
+                        .get(&entry.fingerprint())
+                        .is_some_and(|count| *count > 0),
+                    "the order holds a state the index does not after {sequence} writes"
+                );
+            }
+        }
+    }

+    #[test]
+    fn a_fingerprint_collision_keeps_the_state_in_the_window() {
+        // Two states can share a fingerprint. A window whose index hits one and
+        // holds the other has to add the new state anyway: dropping it would
+        // take an acknowledged state out of the history, and a later read of it
+        // would look impossible instead of being a rollback.
+        let mut model = KeyModel::new(PossibleState::absent(None), WINDOW);
+        let state = PossibleState::present(b"collided".to_vec(), version(7));
+        let entry = AcknowledgedState::of(&state);
+        // Stand in for another state in the window with the same fingerprint.
+        model.known.insert(entry.fingerprint(), 1);
+
+        model.remember(&state);
+        assert_eq!(model.acknowledged.back(), Some(&entry));
+        assert_eq!(model.known.get(&entry.fingerprint()), Some(&2));
+        // The state is in the history, so the read is a rollback, not a value
+        // the history never held.
+        assert!(
+            matches!(
+                model.observe(state.value.as_deref(), state.version.as_ref()),
+                Observation::Rollback { .. }
+            ),
+            "the collided state did not enter the window"
+        );
+
+        // When it leaves the window the index falls back to the other state's
+        // count instead of losing a fingerprint the window still holds.
+        for sequence in 1..=WINDOW as u64 {
+            model.on_put(sequence.to_be_bytes().to_vec(), version(100 + sequence));
+        }
+        assert!(!model.acknowledged.contains(&entry));
+        assert_eq!(model.known.get(&entry.fingerprint()), Some(&1));
+        // The injected count is the only one that is not a state in the window.
+        assert_eq!(
+            model.known.values().sum::<usize>(),
+            model.acknowledged.len() + 1
+        );
+    }

-    if let Some(message) = payload.downcast_ref::<&str>() {
-        (*message).to_owned()
-    } else if let Some(message) = payload.downcast_ref::<String>() {
-        message.clone()
-    } else {
-        "the thread panicked".to_owned()

-/// Sleep until just before the absolute deadline, then spin. Adapt the margin
-/// to the kernel's last overshoot; Tokio's millisecond timer is too coarse.
-pub(super) fn wait_until(due: Instant, margin: &mut Duration) {
-    let coarse = due.checked_sub(*margin).unwrap_or(due);
-    let now = Instant::now();
-    if coarse > now {
-        std::thread::sleep(coarse - now);
-        let overshoot = Instant::now().saturating_duration_since(coarse);
-        *margin = (overshoot + SEND_MARGIN).clamp(SEND_MARGIN, Duration::from_millis(5));
-    }
-    while Instant::now() < due {
-        std::hint::spin_loop();
-    }
-}

-/// Sends the requests of a phase, and returns how many it sent, how many it
-/// had to drop, and how many windows it did not keep up with.
-fn send_requests(
-    handle: tokio::runtime::Handle,
-    client: HashringClient,
-    plan: Arc<LoadPlan>,
-    metrics: Arc<Metrics>,
-    stage: StageSettings,
-    start: Instant,
-    end: Instant,
-) -> (u64, u64, u64) {
-    let rate = stage.target_rate as f64;
-    let mut margin = Duration::from_micros(100);
-    let mut issued = 0_u64;
-    let mut late = 0_u64;
-    let mut saturated_windows = 0_u64;
-    let mut index = 0_u64;
-    let mut window_end = start + Duration::from_secs(1);
-    while index < u64::MAX {
-        let due = start + Duration::from_secs_f64(index as f64 / rate);
-        if due >= end {
-            break;
-        }
-        if metrics.stopped.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
-            break;
-        }
-        wait_until(due, &mut margin);
-        // The limit is enforced by the one sender, so the check and the
-        // reservation cannot race with each other.
-        if metrics.in_flight.load(Ordering::Acquire) >= plan.max_in_flight {
-            late += 1;
-            metrics.late.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
-        } else {
-            metrics.in_flight.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
-            issued += 1;
-            metrics.issued.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
-            let request = Request {
-                client: client.clone(),
-                plan: Arc::clone(&plan),
-                metrics: Arc::clone(&metrics),
-                due,
-            };
-            handle.spawn(async move { request.run().await });
-        }
-        index += 1;
-        let now = Instant::now();
-        if now >= window_end {
-            // Measure phase-level lag separately from the sampler's per-window lag.
-            // More than 50 ms of unscheduled requests invalidates this phase.
-            let expected = ((now.duration_since(start).as_secs_f64()) * rate).floor() as u64 + 1;
-            let sender_lag = expected.saturating_sub(issued + late);
-            metrics.sender_lag.store(sender_lag, Ordering::Relaxed);
-            if sender_lag > 2 + stage.target_rate / 20 {
-                saturated_windows += 1;
-            }
-            window_end += Duration::from_secs(1);
-        }
-    }
-    (issued, late, saturated_windows)
-}

-            Operation::Delete => self.client.delete(encoded).await.map(|_| ()),

-/// absent, which is what the delete asked for.
-fn classify(operation: Operation, outcome: Result<(), ClientError>) -> Result<(), &'static str> {

-        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
-        Err(ClientError::MissingVersion) if operation == Operation::Delete => Ok(()),
-        Err(ClientError::DeadlineExceeded { .. }) => Err("deadline"),
-        Err(ClientError::Operation(failure)) => {

-        Err(ClientError::Topology(_) | ClientError::TopologyRefresh { .. }) => Err("topology"),
-        Err(ClientError::MissingVersion) => Err("protocol"),

-    start: Instant,
-    end: Instant,

-/// Write one event per second, including warmup.
-async fn sample_windows(
-    metrics: Arc<Metrics>,
-    events: EventLog,
-    client: HashringClient,
-    window: SampleWindow,
-) {
-    let SampleWindow {
-        stage,
-        warmup,
-        start,
-        end,
-        retries_before,
-    } = window;
-    let mut window_start = start;
-    let mut retries_seen = retries_before;
-    while window_start < end {
-        let window_end = window_start + Duration::from_secs(1);
-        tokio::time::sleep_until(window_end.into()).await;
-        let (issued, late, completed, errors, latency_us) = {
-            let mut state = metrics
-                .state
-                .lock()
-                .expect("the metrics lock is not poisoned");
-            let (completed, errors, latency_us) = state.current.snapshot();
-            state.fold();
-            let issued = metrics.issued.swap(0, Ordering::AcqRel);
-            let late = metrics.late.swap(0, Ordering::AcqRel);
-            (issued, late, completed, errors, latency_us)
-        };
-        // Dropped requests count as scheduled; only unscheduled requests are behind.
-        let length = window_end.min(end).saturating_duration_since(window_start);
-        let expected = (length.as_secs_f64() * stage.target_rate as f64).floor() as u64;
-        let behind = expected.saturating_sub(issued + late);
-        let sender_lag = metrics.sender_lag.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
-        let retries_now = client.retry_count();
-        let retries = retries_now.saturating_sub(retries_seen);
-        retries_seen = retries_now;
-        let epoch = client.epoch().await;
-        let fields = json!({
-            "stage": stage.name,
-            "warmup": warmup,
-            "window_ms": 1000,
-            "target_rate": stage.target_rate,
-            "issued": issued,

+//! The open-loop load driver of the `latency` experiment mode.
+//!
+//! The driver sends requests on a fixed schedule: request `n` of a stage is
+//! due at `stage start + n / rate`. A request that cannot be sent because too
+//! many requests are still in flight is dropped and counted, never queued, so
+//! a cluster that cannot keep up shows up as a lower achieved rate instead of
+//! a longer queue inside the driver. Every request's latency is measured from
+//! the moment it was due, not from the moment it was sent, so a slow cluster
+//! cannot hide its tail behind a delayed send.
+
+use std::collections::BTreeMap;
+use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, AtomicUsize, Ordering};
+use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
+use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
+
+use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail, ensure};
+use hashring_client::{ClientError, HashringClient};
+use hashring_core::proto::ErrorCode;
+use hdrhistogram::Histogram;
+use rand::Rng;
+use serde_json::json;
+
+use crate::{EventLog, LatencyStageMeasurement, LatencySummary, deterministic_value};

+/// The operations the load issues.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum Operation {
+    Get,
+    Put,
+    Delete,
+}
+
+impl Operation {
+    const ALL: [Operation; 3] = [Operation::Get, Operation::Put, Operation::Delete];
+
+    fn index(self) -> usize {
+        match self {
+            Operation::Get => 0,
+            Operation::Put => 1,
+            Operation::Delete => 2,
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
+        match self {
+            Operation::Get => "get",
+            Operation::Put => "put",
+            Operation::Delete => "delete",
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// The share of the requests that are reads, writes, and deletes.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+pub struct OperationMix {
+    weights: [u64; 3],
+    total: u64,
+}
+
+impl OperationMix {
+    /// Parses a `GET:PUT:DELETE` ratio such as `90:9:1`.
+    pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<Self> {
+        let parts: Vec<&str> = text.split(':').map(str::trim).collect();
+        ensure!(
+            parts.len() == 3,
+            "a mix is GET:PUT:DELETE, like '90:9:1', not '{text}'"
+        );
+        let mut weights = [0_u64; 3];
+        for (index, part) in parts.iter().enumerate() {
+            weights[index] = part
+                .parse::<u64>()
+                .with_context(|| format!("the mix weight '{part}' is not a number"))?;
+        }
+        let total: u64 = weights.iter().sum();
+        ensure!(total > 0, "a mix must allow at least one operation");
+        Ok(Self { weights, total })
+    }
+
+    /// The share of the requests that delete a key.
+    pub fn delete_fraction(&self) -> f64 {
+        self.weights[2] as f64 / self.total as f64
+    }
+
+    pub fn pick(&self, rng: &mut impl Rng) -> Operation {
+        let mut draw = rng.gen_range(0..self.total);
+        for (index, weight) in self.weights.iter().enumerate() {
+            if draw < *weight {
+                return Operation::ALL[index];
+            }
+            draw -= *weight;
+        }
+        Operation::ALL[0]
+    }
+}
+
+/// How the load picks the key of a request.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
+pub enum KeyDistribution {
+    /// Every key is equally likely.
+    Uniform,
+    /// The keys follow a Zipf distribution, so a few keys take most of the
+    /// traffic.
+    Zipf {
+        theta: f64,
+        /// The cumulative share of the traffic up to and including each key.
+        cumulative: Vec<f64>,
+        total: f64,
+    },
+    /// A share of the keys takes most of the traffic.
+    Hotspot { hot_keys: u64, traffic_ratio: f64 },
+}
+
+impl KeyDistribution {
+    /// Parses `uniform`, `zipf:<theta>`, or `hotspot:<key share>:<traffic share>`.
+    pub fn parse(spec: &str, key_space: u64) -> Result<Self> {
+        let spec = spec.trim();
+        if spec.eq_ignore_ascii_case("uniform") {
+            return Ok(Self::Uniform);
+        }
+        if let Some(rest) = spec.strip_prefix("zipf:") {
+            let theta: f64 = rest
+                .trim()
+                .parse()
+                .with_context(|| format!("the Zipf exponent '{rest}' is not a number"))?;
+            ensure!(
+                theta > 0.0 && theta.is_finite(),
+                "the Zipf exponent must be a positive number"
+            );
+            ensure!(
+                key_space > 0,
+                "a key space of zero keys has no distribution"
+            );
+            // The cumulative share of every key. The weights are
+            // 1/(k+1)^theta, so the table is built once and sampled by a
+            // binary search.
+            let mut cumulative = Vec::with_capacity(key_space as usize);
+            let mut total = 0.0_f64;
+            for key in 0..key_space {
+                total += 1.0 / ((key + 1) as f64).powf(theta);
+                cumulative.push(total);
+            }
+            return Ok(Self::Zipf {
+                theta,
+                cumulative,
+                total,
+            });
+        }
+        if let Some(rest) = spec.strip_prefix("hotspot:") {
+            let parts: Vec<&str> = rest.split(':').map(str::trim).collect();
+            ensure!(
+                parts.len() == 2,
+                "a hotspot distribution is hotspot:<key share>:<traffic share>"
+            );
+            let key_share: f64 = parts[0]
+                .parse()
+                .with_context(|| format!("the hotspot key share '{}' is not a number", parts[0]))?;
+            let traffic_share: f64 = parts[1].parse().with_context(|| {
+                format!("the hotspot traffic share '{}' is not a number", parts[1])
+            })?;
+            ensure!(
+                key_share > 0.0 && key_share < 1.0,
+                "the hotspot key share must be between 0 and 1"
+            );
+            ensure!(
+                traffic_share > 0.0 && traffic_share < 1.0,
+                "the hotspot traffic share must be between 0 and 1"
+            );
+            let hot_keys = ((key_space as f64) * key_share).round() as u64;
+            ensure!(
+                hot_keys > 0 && hot_keys < key_space,
+                "the hotspot key share leaves no keys on one side of the split"
+            );
+            return Ok(Self::Hotspot {
+                hot_keys,
+                traffic_ratio: traffic_share,
+            });
+        }
+        bail!("unknown key distribution '{spec}'")
+    }
+
+    /// The distribution as it is written in a configuration file.
+    pub fn name(&self) -> String {
+        match self {
+            Self::Uniform => "uniform".to_owned(),
+            Self::Zipf { theta, .. } => format!("zipf:{theta}"),
+            Self::Hotspot {
+                hot_keys,
+                traffic_ratio,
+            } => format!("hotspot:{hot_keys}:{traffic_ratio}"),
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Picks one of the `key_space` keys.
+    pub fn sample(&self, rng: &mut impl Rng, key_space: u64) -> u64 {
+        match self {
+            Self::Uniform => rng.gen_range(0..key_space),
+            Self::Zipf {
+                cumulative, total, ..
+            } => {
+                let draw = rng.gen_range(0.0..1.0) * total;
+                let index = cumulative.partition_point(|share| *share <= draw) as u64;
+                // The table is built for the whole key space, so a draw at its
+                // very top can land on its last key.
+                index.min(key_space.saturating_sub(1))
+            }
+            Self::Hotspot {
+                hot_keys,
+                traffic_ratio,
+            } => {
+                if rng.gen_range(0.0..1.0) < *traffic_ratio {
+                    rng.gen_range(0..*hot_keys)
+                } else {
+                    *hot_keys + rng.gen_range(0..(key_space - hot_keys))
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// HDR histogram over all completed requests, with three significant figures.
+/// Out-of-range samples go in the top bucket; their actual maximum and count
+/// are retained separately.
+pub struct LatencyHistogram {
+    inner: Histogram<u64>,
+    highest_micros: u64,
+    /// The samples that were longer than the histogram's range.
+    over_range: u64,
+    /// The longest sample, whether or not it was in the range.
+    max_observed: u64,
+}
+
+impl LatencyHistogram {
+    pub fn new(highest_micros: u64) -> Result<Self> {
+        let highest_micros = highest_micros.max(1);
+        let inner = Histogram::new_with_bounds(1, highest_micros, 3)
+            .context("creating a latency histogram")?;
+        Ok(Self {
+            inner,
+            highest_micros,
+            over_range: 0,
+            max_observed: 0,
+        })
+    }
+
+    pub fn record(&mut self, micros: u64) {
+        self.max_observed = self.max_observed.max(micros);
+        if micros > self.highest_micros {
+            self.over_range += 1;
+        }
+        // A value inside the histogram's range is always recorded. A value
+        // above it is recorded in the top bucket, and counted above, so it
+        // is not lost.
+        let _ = self.inner.record(micros.clamp(1, self.highest_micros));
+    }
+
+    pub fn merge(&mut self, other: &Self) {
+        let _ = self.inner.add(&other.inner);
+        self.over_range += other.over_range;
+        self.max_observed = self.max_observed.max(other.max_observed);
+    }
+
+    pub fn reset(&mut self) {
+        self.inner.reset();
+        self.over_range = 0;
+        self.max_observed = 0;
+    }
+
+    pub fn summary(&self) -> LatencySummary {
+        if self.inner.is_empty() {
+            return LatencySummary::default();
+        }
+        LatencySummary {
+            p50: self.inner.value_at_quantile(0.50),
+            p95: self.inner.value_at_quantile(0.95),
+            p99: self.inner.value_at_quantile(0.99),
+            p999: self.inner.value_at_quantile(0.999),
+            max: self.inner.max(),
+            max_observed: self.max_observed,
+            over_range: self.over_range,
+            samples: self.inner.len(),
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+type MetricSnapshot = (
+    BTreeMap<String, u64>,
+    BTreeMap<String, u64>,
+    BTreeMap<String, LatencySummary>,
+);
+
+struct OperationMetrics {
+    histograms: Vec<LatencyHistogram>,
+    completed: [u64; 3],
+    errors: BTreeMap<String, u64>,
+}
+
+impl OperationMetrics {
+    fn new(highest_micros: u64) -> Result<Self> {
+        Ok(Self {
+            histograms: (0..3)
+                .map(|_| LatencyHistogram::new(highest_micros))
+                .collect::<Result<_>>()?,
+            completed: [0; 3],
+            errors: BTreeMap::new(),
+        })
+    }
+
+    fn reset(&mut self) {
+        for histogram in &mut self.histograms {
+            histogram.reset();
+        }
+        self.completed = [0; 3];
+        self.errors.clear();
+    }
+
+    fn snapshot(&self) -> MetricSnapshot {
+        let ops = Operation::ALL
+            .into_iter()
+            .map(|op| (op.name().to_owned(), self.completed[op.index()]))
+            .collect();
+        let latency = Operation::ALL
+            .into_iter()
+            .map(|op| (op.name().to_owned(), self.histograms[op.index()].summary()))
+            .collect();
+        (ops, self.errors.clone(), latency)
+    }
+}
+
+struct WindowState {
+    current: OperationMetrics,
+    total: OperationMetrics,
+}
+
+impl WindowState {
+    /// Include every completed request, including those drained after the final window.
+    fn fold(&mut self) {
+        for (total, current) in self
+            .total
+            .histograms
+            .iter_mut()
+            .zip(&self.current.histograms)
+        {
+            total.merge(current);
+        }
+        for (total, current) in self.total.completed.iter_mut().zip(self.current.completed) {
+            *total += current;
+        }
+        for (reason, count) in &self.current.errors {
+            *self.total.errors.entry(reason.clone()).or_insert(0) += count;
+        }
+        self.current.reset();
+    }
+}
+
+/// The counters of the running stage.
+struct Metrics {
+    state: Mutex<WindowState>,
+    in_flight: AtomicUsize,
+    issued: AtomicU64,
+    late: AtomicU64,
+    /// Phase-level lag at the last sender window boundary, not a running maximum.
+    sender_lag: AtomicU64,
+    /// Set when the stage is over, so a sender that is still running stops.
+    stopped: AtomicBool,
+}
+
+impl Metrics {
+    fn new(highest_micros: u64) -> Result<Self> {
+        Ok(Self {
+            state: Mutex::new(WindowState {
+                current: OperationMetrics::new(highest_micros)?,
+                total: OperationMetrics::new(highest_micros)?,
+            }),
+            in_flight: AtomicUsize::new(0),
+            issued: AtomicU64::new(0),
+            late: AtomicU64::new(0),
+            sender_lag: AtomicU64::new(0),
+            stopped: AtomicBool::new(false),
+        })
+    }
+
+    fn record_success(&self, operation: Operation, latency_micros: u64) {
+        let mut state = self.state.lock().expect("the metrics lock is not poisoned");
+        state.current.histograms[operation.index()].record(latency_micros);
+        state.current.completed[operation.index()] += 1;
+    }
+
+    fn record_error(&self, operation: Operation, reason: &'static str, latency_micros: u64) {
+        let mut state = self.state.lock().expect("the metrics lock is not poisoned");
+        state.current.histograms[operation.index()].record(latency_micros);
+        *state.current.errors.entry(reason.to_owned()).or_insert(0) += 1;
+    }
+}
+
+/// One stage of the load: one target rate.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
+pub struct StageSettings {
+    pub name: String,
+    pub target_rate: u64,
+    pub warmup_seconds: u64,
+    pub duration_seconds: u64,
+}
+
+/// Everything the load needs that does not change between stages.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
+pub struct LoadPlan {
+    pub key_space: u64,
+    pub value_bytes: usize,
+    pub mix: OperationMix,
+    pub distribution: KeyDistribution,
+    pub max_in_flight: usize,
+    /// The keys from here on are the ones the load deletes. They are disjoint
+    /// from the keys it reads and writes, so a delete never races another
+    /// operation on the same key.
+    pub delete_pool_start: u64,
+    /// The keys the load has deleted, so the key space can be checked
+    /// afterwards.
+    pub deleted: Arc<Vec<AtomicBool>>,
+    pub highest_latency_micros: u64,
+    /// How long the stage waits for the requests that are still in flight.
+    /// A request cannot take longer than the operation deadline, so this is
+    /// the deadline plus a margin.
+    pub drain_timeout: Duration,
+}
+
+impl LoadPlan {
+    /// Whether the load deleted the key.
+    pub fn is_deleted(&self, key: u64) -> bool {
+        if key < self.delete_pool_start {
+            return false;
+        }
+        self.deleted
+            .get((key - self.delete_pool_start) as usize)
+            .is_some_and(|deleted| deleted.load(Ordering::Acquire))

+    /// Records that the load deleted the key.
+    pub fn mark_deleted(&self, key: u64) {
+        if key < self.delete_pool_start {
+            return;
+        }
+        if let Some(deleted) = self.deleted.get((key - self.delete_pool_start) as usize) {
+            deleted.store(true, Ordering::Release);
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn sample_key(&self, operation: Operation, rng: &mut impl Rng) -> u64 {
+        match operation {
+            Operation::Delete => {
+                let pool = self.key_space - self.delete_pool_start;
+                if pool == 0 {
+                    return 0;
+                }
+                self.delete_pool_start + rng.gen_range(0..pool)
+            }
+            _ => self.distribution.sample(rng, self.delete_pool_start),
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn value(&self, key: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
+        deterministic_value(key, 0, self.value_bytes)
+    }
+}
+
+/// The load of one stage, warmup first and then the measured window.
+pub struct LoadRunner {
+    client: HashringClient,
+    plan: Arc<LoadPlan>,
+    metrics: Arc<Metrics>,
+}
+
+impl LoadRunner {
+    pub fn new(client: HashringClient, plan: LoadPlan) -> Result<Self> {
+        let metrics = Arc::new(Metrics::new(plan.highest_latency_micros)?);
+        Ok(Self {
+            client,
+            plan: Arc::new(plan),
+            metrics,
+        })
+    }
+
+    /// Runs the warmup of a stage. Its samples are thrown away, so only the
+    /// window that follows describes the stage.
+    pub async fn run_warmup(&self, stage: &StageSettings, events: &EventLog) -> Result<()> {
+        if stage.warmup_seconds == 0 {
+            return Ok(());
+        }
+        self.run_phase(stage, events, stage.warmup_seconds, true)
+            .await?;
+        Ok(())
+    }
+
+    /// Return the measured stage and its number of saturated sender windows.
+    pub async fn run_measured(
+        &self,
+        stage: &StageSettings,
+        events: &EventLog,
+    ) -> Result<(LatencyStageMeasurement, u64)> {
+        self.run_phase(stage, events, stage.duration_seconds, false)
+            .await
+    }
+
+    /// Reset both current and total metrics between warmup and measured phases.
+    fn forget(&self) {
+        let mut state = self
+            .metrics
+            .state
+            .lock()
+            .expect("the metrics lock is not poisoned");
+        state.current.reset();
+        state.total.reset();
+        self.metrics.issued.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
+        self.metrics.late.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
+    }
+
+    async fn run_phase(
+        &self,
+        stage: &StageSettings,
+        events: &EventLog,
+        seconds: u64,
+        warmup: bool,
+    ) -> Result<(LatencyStageMeasurement, u64)> {
+        let start = Instant::now();
+        let end = start + Duration::from_secs(seconds);
+        // The sender of the previous phase has stopped; this one starts fresh.
+        self.metrics.stopped.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
+        // Exclude warmup and preceding stages.
+        self.forget();
+        let retries_before = self.client.retry_count();
+        let sampler = tokio::spawn(sample_windows(
+            Arc::clone(&self.metrics),
+            events.clone(),
+            self.client.clone(),
+            SampleWindow {
+                stage: stage.clone(),
+                warmup,
+                start,
+                end,
+                retries_before,
+            },
+        ));
+        let (issued, late, saturated_windows) = self.drive(stage, start, end).await?;
+        // Empty warmup is allowed; an empty measured phase is invalid.
+        if !warmup {
+            ensure!(
+                issued > 0,
+                "the stage {} issued no requests at all",
+                stage.name
+            );
+        }
+        // Keep the final window, then fold requests completed during draining.
+        let _ = sampler.await;
+        let (ops, errors, latency_us) = {
+            let mut state = self
+                .metrics
+                .state
+                .lock()
+                .expect("the metrics lock is not poisoned");
+            state.fold();
+            state.total.snapshot()
+        };
+        let completed: u64 = ops.values().sum();
+        let failed: u64 = errors.values().sum();
+        if completed + failed != issued {
+            bail!(
+                "the stage issued {} requests, but {} of them came back",
+                issued,
+                completed + failed
+            );
+        }
+        let seconds = end.duration_since(start).as_secs_f64();
+        Ok((
+            LatencyStageMeasurement {
+                target_rate: stage.target_rate,
+                achieved_rate: completed as f64 / seconds.max(f64::EPSILON),
+                seconds,
+                sender_saturated: saturated_windows > 0,
+                issued,
+                late,
+                ops,
+                errors: complete_errors(&errors),
+                retries: self.client.retry_count().saturating_sub(retries_before),
+                latency_us,
+                load_balance: Default::default(),
+            },
+            saturated_windows,
+        ))
+    }
+
+    /// Run the sender and drain outstanding requests. Return issued, dropped,
+    /// and saturated-window counts.
+    async fn drive(
+        &self,
+        stage: &StageSettings,
+        start: Instant,
+        end: Instant,
+    ) -> Result<(u64, u64, u64)> {
+        let handle = tokio::runtime::Handle::current();
+        let client = self.client.clone();
+        let plan = Arc::clone(&self.plan);
+        let metrics = Arc::clone(&self.metrics);
+        let settings = stage.clone();
+        let (sender, sent) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
+        let mut thread = Some(
+            std::thread::Builder::new()
+                .name("latency-sender".to_owned())
+                .spawn(move || {
+                    let result = send_requests(handle, client, plan, metrics, settings, start, end);
+                    let _ = sender.send(result);
+                })?,
+        );
+        let reported = sent.await;
+        let (issued, late, saturated_windows) = match reported {
+            Ok(counts) => counts,
+            Err(error) => {
+                // A sender panic must fail the phase, not report an empty load.
+                let message = thread
+                    .take()
+                    .and_then(|thread| thread.join().err())
+                    .map(panic_message)
+                    .unwrap_or_else(|| {
+                        format!("the sender thread ended without reporting its counts: {error}")
+                    });
+                bail!("{message}");
+            }
+        };
+        // Drain every issued request within the operation deadline plus margin.
+        let deadline = Instant::now() + self.plan.drain_timeout;
+        while self.metrics.in_flight.load(Ordering::Acquire) > 0 {
+            if Instant::now() >= deadline {
+                bail!(
+                    "{} requests were still in flight {:?} after the stage ended",
+                    self.metrics.in_flight.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
+                    self.plan.drain_timeout
+                );
+            }
+            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5)).await;
+        }
+        self.metrics.stopped.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
+        if let Some(thread) = thread.take()
+            && let Some(message) = thread.join().err().map(panic_message)
+        {
+            bail!("the sender thread panicked: {message}");
+        }
+        Ok((issued, late, saturated_windows))
+    }
+}
+
+/// The margin the sender leaves between the end of its sleep and the moment
+/// a request was due. The sleep of the kernel overshoots by about this much,
+/// so the spin that finishes the wait is short.
+const SEND_MARGIN: Duration = Duration::from_micros(20);
+
+/// The message of a panic, if the panic carries one.
+fn panic_message(payload: Box<dyn std::any::Any + Send>) -> String {
+    if let Some(message) = payload.downcast_ref::<&str>() {
+        (*message).to_owned()
+    } else if let Some(message) = payload.downcast_ref::<String>() {
+        message.clone()
+    } else {
+        "the thread panicked".to_owned()
+    }
+}
+
+/// Sleep until just before the absolute deadline, then spin. Adapt the margin
+/// to the kernel's last overshoot; Tokio's millisecond timer is too coarse.
+pub(super) fn wait_until(due: Instant, margin: &mut Duration) {
+    let coarse = due.checked_sub(*margin).unwrap_or(due);
+    let now = Instant::now();
+    if coarse > now {
+        std::thread::sleep(coarse - now);
+        let overshoot = Instant::now().saturating_duration_since(coarse);
+        *margin = (overshoot + SEND_MARGIN).clamp(SEND_MARGIN, Duration::from_millis(5));
+    }
+    while Instant::now() < due {
+        std::hint::spin_loop();
+    }
+}
+
+/// Sends the requests of a phase, and returns how many it sent, how many it
+/// had to drop, and how many windows it did not keep up with.
+fn send_requests(
+    handle: tokio::runtime::Handle,
+    client: HashringClient,
+    plan: Arc<LoadPlan>,
+    metrics: Arc<Metrics>,
+    stage: StageSettings,
+    start: Instant,
+    end: Instant,
+) -> (u64, u64, u64) {
+    let rate = stage.target_rate as f64;
+    let mut margin = Duration::from_micros(100);
+    let mut issued = 0_u64;
+    let mut late = 0_u64;
+    let mut saturated_windows = 0_u64;
+    let mut index = 0_u64;
+    let mut window_end = start + Duration::from_secs(1);
+    while index < u64::MAX {
+        let due = start + Duration::from_secs_f64(index as f64 / rate);
+        if due >= end {
+            break;
+        }
+        if metrics.stopped.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
+            break;
+        }
+        wait_until(due, &mut margin);
+        // The limit is enforced by the one sender, so the check and the
+        // reservation cannot race with each other.
+        if metrics.in_flight.load(Ordering::Acquire) >= plan.max_in_flight {
+            late += 1;
+            metrics.late.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
+        } else {
+            metrics.in_flight.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
+            issued += 1;
+            metrics.issued.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
+            let request = Request {
+                client: client.clone(),
+                plan: Arc::clone(&plan),
+                metrics: Arc::clone(&metrics),
+                due,
+            };
+            handle.spawn(async move { request.run().await });
+        }
+        index += 1;
+        let now = Instant::now();
+        if now >= window_end {
+            // Measure phase-level lag separately from the sampler's per-window lag.
+            // More than 50 ms of unscheduled requests invalidates this phase.
+            let expected = ((now.duration_since(start).as_secs_f64()) * rate).floor() as u64 + 1;
+            let sender_lag = expected.saturating_sub(issued + late);
+            metrics.sender_lag.store(sender_lag, Ordering::Relaxed);
+            if sender_lag > 2 + stage.target_rate / 20 {
+                saturated_windows += 1;
+            }
+            window_end += Duration::from_secs(1);
+        }
+    }
+    (issued, late, saturated_windows)
+}
+
+/// One request of the load.
+struct Request {
+    client: HashringClient,
+    plan: Arc<LoadPlan>,
+    metrics: Arc<Metrics>,
+    /// The moment the request was due, which is where its latency starts.
+    due: Instant,
+}
+
+impl Request {
+    async fn run(self) {
+        let (operation, key) = {
+            let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
+            let operation = self.plan.mix.pick(&mut rng);
+            (operation, self.plan.sample_key(operation, &mut rng))
+        };
+        let encoded = key.to_be_bytes().to_vec();
+        let outcome = match operation {
+            Operation::Get => self.client.get(encoded).await.map(|_| ()),
+            Operation::Put => {
+                let value = self.plan.value(key);
+                self.client.put(encoded, value).await.map(|_| ())
+            }
+            Operation::Delete => self.client.delete(encoded).await.map(|_| ()),
+        };
+        let latency = Instant::now().saturating_duration_since(self.due);
+        let latency_micros = latency.as_micros().min(u64::MAX as u128) as u64;
+        match classify(operation, outcome) {
+            Ok(()) => {
+                if operation == Operation::Delete {
+                    self.plan.mark_deleted(key);
+                }
+                self.metrics.record_success(operation, latency_micros)
+            }
+            Err(reason) => self.metrics.record_error(operation, reason, latency_micros),
+        }
+        self.metrics.in_flight.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
+    }
+}
+
+/// Turns a failed operation into the reason it failed.
+///
+/// A delete of a key that is already gone is not a failure: the key is
+/// absent, which is what the delete asked for.
+fn classify(operation: Operation, outcome: Result<(), ClientError>) -> Result<(), &'static str> {
+    match outcome {
+        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
+        Err(ClientError::MissingVersion) if operation == Operation::Delete => Ok(()),
+        Err(ClientError::DeadlineExceeded { .. }) => Err("deadline"),
+        Err(ClientError::Operation(failure)) => {
+            if failure.code == ErrorCode::NotFound && operation == Operation::Get {
+                Err("not_found")
+            } else {
+                Err("operation")
+            }
+        }
+        Err(ClientError::Rpc { .. }) => Err("rpc"),
+        Err(ClientError::Topology(_) | ClientError::TopologyRefresh { .. }) => Err("topology"),
+        Err(ClientError::MissingVersion) => Err("protocol"),
+    }
+}
+
+/// Stable error categories, including zero-count reasons.
+pub const ERROR_REASONS: [&str; 6] = [
+    "deadline",
+    "not_found",
+    "operation",
+    "protocol",
+    "rpc",
+    "topology",
+];
+
+fn complete_errors(errors: &BTreeMap<String, u64>) -> BTreeMap<String, u64> {
+    let mut complete: BTreeMap<String, u64> = ERROR_REASONS
+        .iter()
+        .map(|reason| ((*reason).to_owned(), 0))
+        .collect();
+    for (reason, count) in errors {
+        *complete.entry(reason.clone()).or_insert(0) += count;
+    }
+    complete
+}
+
+/// One stage's sampling timeline, including its warmup.
+struct SampleWindow {
+    stage: StageSettings,
+    warmup: bool,
+    start: Instant,
+    end: Instant,
+    retries_before: u64,
+}
+
+/// Write one event per second, including warmup.
+async fn sample_windows(
+    metrics: Arc<Metrics>,
+    events: EventLog,
+    client: HashringClient,
+    window: SampleWindow,
+) {
+    let SampleWindow {
+        stage,
+        warmup,
+        start,
+        end,
+        retries_before,
+    } = window;
+    let mut window_start = start;
+    let mut retries_seen = retries_before;
+    while window_start < end {
+        let window_end = window_start + Duration::from_secs(1);
+        tokio::time::sleep_until(window_end.into()).await;
+        let (issued, late, completed, errors, latency_us) = {
+            let mut state = metrics
+                .state
+                .lock()
+                .expect("the metrics lock is not poisoned");
+            let (completed, errors, latency_us) = state.current.snapshot();
+            state.fold();
+            let issued = metrics.issued.swap(0, Ordering::AcqRel);
+            let late = metrics.late.swap(0, Ordering::AcqRel);
+            (issued, late, completed, errors, latency_us)
+        };
+        // Dropped requests count as scheduled; only unscheduled requests are behind.
+        let length = window_end.min(end).saturating_duration_since(window_start);
+        let expected = (length.as_secs_f64() * stage.target_rate as f64).floor() as u64;
+        let behind = expected.saturating_sub(issued + late);
+        let sender_lag = metrics.sender_lag.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
+        let retries_now = client.retry_count();
+        let retries = retries_now.saturating_sub(retries_seen);
+        retries_seen = retries_now;
+        let epoch = client.epoch().await;
+        let fields = json!({
+            "stage": stage.name,
+            "warmup": warmup,
+            "window_ms": 1000,
+            "target_rate": stage.target_rate,
+            "issued": issued,
+            "late": late,
+            "behind": behind,
+            "sender_lag": sender_lag,
+            "ops": completed,
+            "errors": complete_errors(&errors),
+            "retries": retries,
+            "epoch": epoch,
+            "latency_us": latency_us,
+        });
+        if events.record("metrics_sampled", fields).is_err() {
+            return;
+        }
+        window_start = window_end;
+    }
+}

+        assert_eq!(state.total.histograms[0].summary().samples, 2);
+    }

-async fn wait_for_full_rf(
-    client: &HashringClient,
-    desired_rf: u32,
-    timeout: Duration,
-    processes: &mut ProcessGroup,

-        processes.ensure_running()?;

-            tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(3), client.replica_status()).await
-            && !status.ranges.is_empty()
-            && status.ranges.iter().all(|range| {
-                range.live_rf == desired_rf
-                    && !range.repairing
-                    && range.followers.iter().all(|follower| follower.healthy)
-            })
-        {
-            return Ok(());
-        }
-        ensure!(
-            Instant::now() < deadline,
-            "full RF did not converge within {timeout:?}"
-        );
-        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(250)).await;
-    }

-/// Runs the `latency` mode: one stage per target rate, and a check of the key
-/// space the load left behind.
-async fn run_latency(context: RunContext<'_>) -> Result<u64> {
-    let RunContext {
-        config,
-        members,
-        admin_client,
-        workload_client,
-        processes,
-        events,
-        measurements,
-        observations,
-        ..
-    } = context;
-    ensure!(
-        !config.target_rates.is_empty(),
-        "the latency mode needs at least one target rate"
-    );
-    let key_space = config.key_count;
-    let mix = latency::OperationMix::parse(&config.mix)?;
-    let delete_pool = delete_pool_size(config, &mix, key_space);
-    // The distribution covers the keys the load reads and writes. The keys it
-    // deletes are a pool of their own, so a delete never races another
-    // operation on the same key.
-    let distribution =
-        latency::KeyDistribution::parse(&config.key_distribution, key_space - delete_pool)?;
-    let plan = latency::LoadPlan {
-        key_space,
-        value_bytes: config.value_bytes,
-        mix,
-        distribution: distribution.clone(),
-        max_in_flight: config.max_in_flight,
-        delete_pool_start: key_space - delete_pool,
-        deleted: Arc::new(
-            (0..delete_pool as usize)
-                .map(|_| AtomicBool::new(false))
-                .collect(),
-        ),
-        highest_latency_micros: highest_latency_micros(config),
-        drain_timeout: Duration::from_millis(config.operation_timeout_ms) + Duration::from_secs(5),
-    };
-    observations.insert("latency_key_space".into(), json!(key_space));
-    observations.insert("latency_delete_pool_keys".into(), json!(delete_pool));
-    observations.insert(
-        "latency_key_distribution".into(),
-        json!(distribution.name()),
-    );
-    observations.insert("latency_mix".into(), json!(config.mix));
-    // The `measurements` of a latency run hold one entry per rate stage, so
-    // the preload and the check that follows it move to the observations.
-    for name in ["initial_put", "initial_get_verify"] {
-        if let Some(measurement) = measurements.remove(name) {
-            observations.insert(name.into(), serde_json::to_value(measurement)?);
-        }
-    }
-
-    let topology = admin_client.refresh_topology().await?;
-    let owned_keys = owned_key_counts(&topology, key_space);
-    let runner = latency::LoadRunner::new(workload_client.clone(), plan.clone())?;
-    let pids = processes.pids();
-    let mut saturated_windows = serde_json::Map::new();
-    for (index, rate) in config.target_rates.iter().enumerate() {
-        let stage = latency::StageSettings {
-            name: format!("rate_{index}"),
-            target_rate: *rate,
-            warmup_seconds: config.warmup_seconds,
-            duration_seconds: config.duration_seconds,
-        };
-        runner.run_warmup(&stage, events).await?;
-        let before = sample_node_counters(members, &pids).await?;
-        let (mut measurement, saturated) = runner.run_measured(&stage, events).await?;
-        let after = sample_node_counters(members, &pids).await?;
-        measurement.load_balance = load_balance(&owned_keys, &before, &after, measurement.seconds)?;
-        saturated_windows.insert(stage.name.clone(), json!(saturated));
-        measurements.insert(stage.name, Measurement::LatencyStage(measurement));
-    }
-    observations.insert(
-        "latency_saturated_windows".into(),
-        Value::from(saturated_windows),
-    );
-    let expected = (0..key_space)
-        .map(|key| (!plan.is_deleted(key)).then_some(0))
-        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
-    verify_dataset(
-        workload_client,
-        Workload {
-            key_count: key_space,
-            value_bytes: config.value_bytes,
-            concurrency: config.concurrency,
-        },
-        &expected,
-    )
-    .await?;
-    observations.insert("latency_verified_keys".into(), json!(key_space));
-    processes.ensure_running()?;
-    let topology = admin_client.refresh_topology().await?;
-    events.record(
-        "verification_complete",
-        json!({ "epoch": topology.epoch, "members": topology.members.len() }),
-    )?;
-    record_topology(events, admin_client).await?;
-    Ok(topology.epoch)
-}

-/// The keys the load may delete.
-///
-/// The load deletes from a pool of its own, so a delete never races another
-/// operation on the same key and the key space can be checked afterwards. The
-/// pool is as large as the run's deletes need, and never more than half of the
-/// key space and never less than a twentieth of it.
-fn delete_pool_size(config: &ExperimentConfig, mix: &latency::OperationMix, key_space: u64) -> u64 {
-    if mix.delete_fraction() <= 0.0 {
-        return 0;
-    }
-    let expected: f64 = config
-        .target_rates
-        .iter()
-        .map(|rate| {
-            *rate as f64
-                * (config.duration_seconds + config.warmup_seconds) as f64
-                * mix.delete_fraction()
-        })
-        .sum();
-    let wanted = expected.ceil() as u64;
-    let minimum = (key_space as f64 * 0.05).floor() as u64;
-    let maximum = (key_space as f64 * 0.5).floor() as u64;
-    wanted
-        .clamp(minimum, maximum)
-        .min(key_space.saturating_sub(1))
-}

-/// The largest latency the histogram keeps.
-///
-/// A request cannot take longer than the operation deadline, and the driver
-/// measures from the moment the request was due, so the deadline plus a
-/// second covers every request it can issue.
-fn highest_latency_micros(config: &ExperimentConfig) -> u64 {
-    config
-        .operation_timeout_ms
-        .saturating_mul(1_000)
-        .saturating_add(1_000_000)
-        .min(600_000_000)
-}

-/// How the keys and the requests were spread over the nodes.
-fn load_balance(
-    owned_keys: &BTreeMap<String, u64>,
-    before: &BTreeMap<String, NodeCounters>,
-    after: &BTreeMap<String, NodeCounters>,
-    seconds: f64,
-) -> Result<LoadBalanceMeasurement> {
-    let mut per_node = BTreeMap::new();
-    let mut owned = Vec::new();
-    let mut handled = Vec::new();
-    for (node, keys) in owned_keys {
-        let start = before.get(node).context("missing initial node counters")?;
-        let end = after.get(node).context("missing final node counters")?;
-        let ops_handled = end
-            .ops_handled
-            .checked_sub(start.ops_handled)
-            .context("node operations counter decreased during the stage")?;
-        let cpu_percent = start
-            .cpu_seconds
-            .zip(end.cpu_seconds)
-            .and_then(|(a, b)| (seconds > 0.0 && b >= a).then_some((b - a) / seconds * 100.0));
-        owned.push(*keys as f64);
-        handled.push(ops_handled as f64);
-        per_node.insert(
-            node.clone(),
-            LoadBalanceNode {
-                owned_keys: *keys,
-                ops_handled,
-                cpu_percent,
-            },
-        );
-    }
-    Ok(LoadBalanceMeasurement {
-        per_node,
-        owned_keys_max_over_mean: max_over_mean(&owned),
-        owned_keys_cv: coefficient_of_variation(&owned),
-        ops_handled_max_over_mean: max_over_mean(&handled),
-        ops_handled_cv: coefficient_of_variation(&handled),
-    })

-/// The largest value divided by the mean of the values.
-fn max_over_mean(values: &[f64]) -> f64 {
-    if values.is_empty() {
-        return 0.0;
-    }
-    let mean = values.iter().sum::<f64>() / values.len() as f64;
-    if mean <= 0.0 {
-        return 0.0;
-    }
-    values.iter().copied().fold(0.0_f64, f64::max) / mean
-}
-
-/// The standard deviation of the values divided by their mean.
-fn coefficient_of_variation(values: &[f64]) -> f64 {
-    if values.is_empty() {
-        return 0.0;
-    }
-    let mean = values.iter().sum::<f64>() / values.len() as f64;
-    if mean <= 0.0 {
-        return 0.0;
-    }
-    let variance = values
-        .iter()
-        .map(|value| (value - mean).powi(2))
-        .sum::<f64>()
-        / values.len() as f64;
-    variance.sqrt() / mean
-}

-/// The CPU time a process has used, in seconds.
-///
-/// The counter is the kernel's, so it covers the whole life of the process,
-/// not only the time it spent in this run.
-fn process_cpu_seconds(pid: u32) -> Option<f64> {
-    let stat = fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{pid}/stat")).ok()?;
-    // The command name is in parentheses and may hold spaces, so the fields
-    // after it are found from the last closing parenthesis.
-    let rest = stat.rsplit_once(") ")?.1;
-    let fields: Vec<&str> = rest.split_whitespace().collect();
-    let utime: u64 = fields.get(11)?.parse().ok()?;
-    let stime: u64 = fields.get(12)?.parse().ok()?;
-    Some((utime + stime) as f64 / clock_ticks_per_second() as f64)
-}
-
-/// The clock ticks the kernel counts CPU time in.
-fn clock_ticks_per_second() -> u64 {
-    static TICKS: std::sync::OnceLock<u64> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
-    *TICKS.get_or_init(|| {
-        command_output(None, "getconf", &["CLK_TCK"])
-            .and_then(|value| value.trim().parse().ok())
-            .unwrap_or(100)
-    })
-}

-async fn wait_for_migration_activity(client: &HashringClient) -> Result<MigrationPhase> {
-    for _ in 0..2_000 {
-        if let Some(change) = client.topology_change().await? {
-            match change.phase {
-                MigrationPhase::CopyingSnapshot
-                | MigrationPhase::ReplayingChangelog
-                | MigrationPhase::PausingWrites
-                | MigrationPhase::Verifying
-                | MigrationPhase::ReadyToPublish => return Ok(change.phase),
-                MigrationPhase::Published
-                | MigrationPhase::CleaningUp
-                | MigrationPhase::Complete
-                | MigrationPhase::Aborting
-                | MigrationPhase::Aborted => {
-                    bail!(
-                        "migration reached {:?} before concurrent writes began",
-                        change.phase
-                    )
-                }
-                MigrationPhase::Planned | MigrationPhase::Resetting => {}
-            }
-        }
-        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(2)).await;
-    }
-    bail!("migration did not leave its planned phase")

-async fn wait_for_mutation_overlap(
-    client: &HashringClient,
-    completed_mutations: &AtomicU64,
-    writer: &tokio::task::JoinHandle<Result<MutationCounts>>,
-) -> Result<(MigrationPhase, u64)> {
-    for _ in 0..2_000 {
-        let mutations = completed_mutations.load(AtomicOrdering::Acquire);
-        if let Some(change) = client.topology_change().await? {
-            match change.phase {
-                MigrationPhase::CopyingSnapshot
-                | MigrationPhase::ReplayingChangelog
-                | MigrationPhase::PausingWrites
-                | MigrationPhase::Verifying
-                | MigrationPhase::ReadyToPublish
-                    if mutations > 0 =>
-                {
-                    return Ok((change.phase, mutations));
-                }
-                MigrationPhase::Published
-                | MigrationPhase::CleaningUp
-                | MigrationPhase::Complete
-                | MigrationPhase::Aborting
-                | MigrationPhase::Aborted => {
-                    bail!(
-                        "migration reached {:?} before any concurrent mutation completed",
-                        change.phase
-                    )
-                }
-                _ => {}
-            }
-        }
-        // Reload the count: the writer may have completed every mutation
-        // during the topology poll, after `mutations` was read.
-        if writer.is_finished() && completed_mutations.load(AtomicOrdering::Acquire) == 0 {
-            bail!("concurrent mutator finished without a successful mutation");
-        }
-        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(2)).await;
-    }
-    bail!("no successful mutation overlapped the active migration")

-fn deterministic_value(key: u64, round: u64, value_bytes: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
-    let mut state = key ^ round.rotate_left(17) ^ 0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15;
-    let mut value = Vec::with_capacity(value_bytes);
-    while value.len() < value_bytes {
-        state ^= state >> 12;
-        state ^= state << 25;
-        state ^= state >> 27;
-        let block = state.wrapping_mul(0x2545_f491_4f6c_dd1d).to_be_bytes();
-        let remaining = value_bytes - value.len();
-        value.extend_from_slice(&block[..remaining.min(block.len())]);
-    }
-    value
-}

-/// The most write operations per second a scaling run accepts.
-///
-/// The rate is split into whole operations per second and multiplied by the
-/// pool seconds, so an absurd rate would overflow those products. This ceiling
-/// is far above any rate the harness can drive on one host.
-const MAX_SCALING_RATE: u64 = 1_000_000;
-
-/// The longest one-shot pool window a scaling run accepts.
-///
-/// A pool is sized as the cohort's rate multiplied by this window, so a long
-/// window at a high rate would overflow that product. A pool only has to
-/// outlast one transition, and a day is far beyond any transition.
-const MAX_SCALING_POOL_SECONDS: u64 = 86_400;
-
-/// The most keys an experiment preloads.
-///
-/// The scaling plan multiplies the key count by the read share and adds the
-/// write quotas to it, so an absurd count would overflow those products. This
-/// ceiling is far above the largest run the harness is used for.
-const MAX_KEY_COUNT: u64 = 100_000_000;
-
-// The accepted maximums are only safe because the products the scaling plan
-// makes from them stay in range. Check that at compile time, so raising a
-// ceiling without checking the arithmetic cannot compile.
-const _: () = {
-    assert!(MAX_SCALING_RATE * 60 / 100 * MAX_SCALING_POOL_SECONDS < u64::MAX);
-    assert!(MAX_KEY_COUNT * 60 < u64::MAX);
-};
-
-/// The smallest rate that still offers the smallest write cohort one operation
-/// per second when the rate is split into whole operations.
-///
-/// The share is the one `scaling::cohort_rates` splits the rate with: 15% for
-/// the closed loop's delete cohort and 3% for the open loop's, so the two
-/// definitions have to stay in step.
-fn minimum_scaling_rate(smallest_share_percent: u64) -> u64 {
-    100_u64.div_ceil(smallest_share_percent)
-}

-fn write_json(path: &Path, value: &impl Serialize) -> Result<()> {
-    let file = File::create(path)?;
-    // The manifest inlines a multi-megabyte `git diff`. Serializing pretty JSON
-    // emits a few bytes at a time, so an unbuffered handle turns a single write
-    // into tens of thousands of `write` syscalls plus the ext4 metadata churn
-    // that follows them.
-    let mut writer = BufWriter::new(file);
-    serde_json::to_writer_pretty(&mut writer, value)?;
-    // Surface a deferred write error instead of losing it in `Drop`.
-    writer.flush()?;
-    Ok(())
-}

-fn file_digest(path: &Path) -> Result<String> {
-    let mut file = File::open(path)?;
-    let mut hasher = blake3::Hasher::new();
-    let mut buffer = [0_u8; 64 * 1024];
-    loop {
-        let read = file.read(&mut buffer)?;
-        if read == 0 {
-            break;
-        }
-        hasher.update(&buffer[..read]);
-    }
-    Ok(hasher.finalize().to_hex().to_string())
-}

-fn source_tree_digest(workspace: &Path) -> Result<String> {
-    let mut files = Vec::new();
-    for path in [
-        "Cargo.toml",
-        "Cargo.lock",
-        "PLAN.md",
-        "README.md",
-        "src",
-        "crates",
-        "tests",
-    ] {
-        collect_files(&workspace.join(path), &mut files)?;
-    }
-    files.sort();
-    let mut hasher = blake3::Hasher::new();
-    hasher.update(b"hashring-rs:source-tree:v1\0");
-    for path in files {
-        let relative = path.strip_prefix(workspace).unwrap_or(&path);
-        let encoded = relative.to_string_lossy();
-        let contents = fs::read(&path)?;
-        hasher.update(&(encoded.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
-        hasher.update(encoded.as_bytes());
-        hasher.update(&(contents.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
-        hasher.update(&contents);
-    }
-    Ok(hasher.finalize().to_hex().to_string())
-}
