+fn moving_key_cohorts(change: &TopologyChange, key_count: u64) -> Result<MovingKeyCohorts> {
+    let all = moving_keys(change, key_count);
+    let mut rewrite = Vec::new();
+    let mut delete = Vec::new();
+    let mut sentinels = Vec::new();
+    for (moving_index, key) in all.iter().copied().enumerate() {
+        match moving_index % 3 {
+            0 => rewrite.push(key),
+            1 => delete.push(key),
+            _ => sentinels.push(key),
+        }
+    }
+    ensure!(
+        !rewrite.is_empty(),
+        "migration has no moving rewrite cohort"
+    );
+    ensure!(!delete.is_empty(), "migration has no moving delete cohort");
+    ensure!(
+        !sentinels.is_empty(),
+        "migration has no untouched moving sentinel cohort"
+    );
+    Ok(MovingKeyCohorts {
+        all,
+        rewrite,
+        delete,
+        sentinels,
+    })
+}
+
+fn moving_keys(change: &TopologyChange, key_count: u64) -> Vec<u64> {
+    let base = change
+        .base_topology
+        .as_ref()
+        .expect("planned change includes its base topology");
+    let mut moving = Vec::new();
+    for key in 0..key_count {
+        let encoded = key.to_be_bytes();
+        if base
+            .owner(&encoded)
+            .expect("base topology is valid")
+            .node_id
+            != change
+                .target_topology
+                .owner(&encoded)
+                .expect("target topology is valid")
+                .node_id
+        {
+            moving.push(key);
+        }
+    }
+    moving
+}
+
+/// The size of the tail value: large enough to be a meaningful write, but
+/// never larger than the data nodes accept.
+///
+/// The value size the run writes is the floor, and the run's validation keeps
+/// it within the node's limit, so the tail never exceeds what the node takes.
+fn tail_value_bytes(max_value_bytes: usize, value_bytes: usize) -> usize {
+    (1024 * 1024).min(max_value_bytes).max(value_bytes)
+}
+
+fn deterministic_value(key: u64, round: u64, value_bytes: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut state = key ^ round.rotate_left(17) ^ 0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15;
+    let mut value = Vec::with_capacity(value_bytes);
+    while value.len() < value_bytes {
+        state ^= state >> 12;
+        state ^= state << 25;
+        state ^= state >> 27;
+        let block = state.wrapping_mul(0x2545_f491_4f6c_dd1d).to_be_bytes();
+        let remaining = value_bytes - value.len();
+        value.extend_from_slice(&block[..remaining.min(block.len())]);
+    }
+    value
+}

+fn measurement(operations: u64, duration: Duration) -> Measurement {
+    let seconds = duration.as_secs_f64();
+    Measurement::Throughput(ThroughputMeasurement {
+        operations,
+        seconds,
+        operations_per_second: operations as f64 / seconds.max(f64::EPSILON),
+    })
+}

+async fn connect_eventually(
+    endpoint: &str,
+    timeout: Duration,
+    processes: &mut ProcessGroup,
+) -> Result<HashringClient> {
+    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(10);
+    loop {
+        match HashringClient::connect(endpoint.to_owned(), timeout).await {
+            Ok(client) => return Ok(client),
+            Err(error) if Instant::now() < deadline => {
+                processes.ensure_running()?;
+                let _ = error;
+                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25)).await;
+            }
+            Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
+        }
+    }
+}

+async fn wait_for_listener(port: u16, processes: &mut ProcessGroup) -> Result<()> {
+    let address = format!("127.0.0.1:{port}").parse()?;
+    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(10);
+    loop {
+        if TcpStream::connect_timeout(&address, Duration::from_millis(20)).is_ok() {
+            return Ok(());
+        }
+        processes.ensure_running()?;
+        if Instant::now() >= deadline {
+            bail!("listener did not become ready on port {port}");
+        }
+        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
+    }
+}

+fn reserve_ports(count: usize) -> Result<Vec<u16>> {
+    let listeners: Vec<_> = (0..count)
+        .map(|_| TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0"))
+        .collect::<std::io::Result<_>>()?;
+    listeners
+        .iter()
+        .map(|listener| Ok(listener.local_addr()?.port()))
+        .collect()
+}
+
+/// The most write operations per second a scaling run accepts.
+///
+/// The rate is split into whole operations per second and multiplied by the
+/// pool seconds, so an absurd rate would overflow those products. This ceiling
+/// is far above any rate the harness can drive on one host.
+const MAX_SCALING_RATE: u64 = 1_000_000;
+
+/// The longest one-shot pool window a scaling run accepts.
+///
+/// A pool is sized as the cohort's rate multiplied by this window, so a long
+/// window at a high rate would overflow that product. A pool only has to
+/// outlast one transition, and a day is far beyond any transition.
+const MAX_SCALING_POOL_SECONDS: u64 = 86_400;
+
+/// The most keys an experiment preloads.
+///
+/// The scaling plan multiplies the key count by the read share and adds the
+/// write quotas to it, so an absurd count would overflow those products. This
+/// ceiling is far above the largest run the harness is used for.
+const MAX_KEY_COUNT: u64 = 100_000_000;
+
+// The accepted maximums are only safe because the products the scaling plan
+// makes from them stay in range. Check that at compile time, so raising a
+// ceiling without checking the arithmetic cannot compile.
+const _: () = {
+    assert!(MAX_SCALING_RATE * 60 / 100 * MAX_SCALING_POOL_SECONDS < u64::MAX);
+    assert!(MAX_KEY_COUNT * 60 < u64::MAX);
+};
+
+/// The smallest rate that still offers the smallest write cohort one operation
+/// per second when the rate is split into whole operations.
+///
+/// The share is the one `scaling::cohort_rates` splits the rate with: 15% for
+/// the closed loop's delete cohort and 3% for the open loop's, so the two
+/// definitions have to stay in step.
+fn minimum_scaling_rate(smallest_share_percent: u64) -> u64 {
+    100_u64.div_ceil(smallest_share_percent)
+}
+
+fn validate_config(config: &ExperimentConfig) -> Result<()> {
+    ensure!(config.node_count >= 2, "node_count must be at least 2");
+    if matches!(config.mode, ExperimentMode::Availability) {
+        ensure!(
+            config.availability_rounds >= 1,
+            "availability_rounds must be at least 1"
+        );
+        ensure!(
+            config.node_count >= 4,
+            "availability mode requires at least 4 nodes (3 initial and 1 replacement)"
+        );
+        // Compare before subtracting: `--nodes 4 --availability-rounds 5`
+        // must be rejected, not overflow.
+        ensure!(
+            config.node_count > config.availability_rounds as usize,
+            "availability mode needs at least one initial member besides its replacements"
+        );
+        ensure!(
+            config.desired_replication_factor == 3,
+            "availability mode requires desired_replication_factor=3"
+        );
+        ensure!(
+            config.write_ack_policy != WriteAckPolicy::AllReplicas,
+            "availability mode cannot keep AllReplicas writable after one node fails"
+        );
+    }
+    if matches!(config.mode, ExperimentMode::Fault) {
+        ensure!(config.fault_rounds >= 1, "fault_rounds must be at least 1");
+        ensure!(
+            config.node_count > config.fault_rounds as usize,
+            "fault mode needs at least one initial member besides its replacements"
+        );
+        ensure!(
+            config.fault_initial_members() >= 4,
+            "fault mode requires at least 4 initial members"
+        );
+        ensure!(
+            config.fault_initial_members() >= config.desired_replication_factor as usize,
+            "fault mode needs at least desired replication factor initial members"
+        );
+        ensure!(
+            config.desired_replication_factor == 3,
+            "fault mode requires desired_replication_factor=3"
+        );
+        ensure!(
+            config.write_ack_policy != WriteAckPolicy::AllReplicas,
+            "fault mode cannot keep AllReplicas writable after one node fails"
+        );
+        ensure!(
+            config.fault_pre_seconds > 0 && config.fault_post_seconds > 0,
+            "fault_pre_seconds and fault_post_seconds must be positive"
+        );
+        ensure!(
+            config.fault_acknowledged_window > 0,
+            "fault_acknowledged_window must be positive"
+        );
+        ensure!(
+            config.key_count >= 32,
+            "fault mode needs at least 32 keys to select a failure cohort"
+        );
+    }
+    // Only the scaling mode reads this; the other modes derive their initial
+    // membership from their own rules, so an explicit value would be silently
+    // ignored.
+    ensure!(
+        config.initial_nodes.is_none() || matches!(config.mode, ExperimentMode::Scaling),
+        "initial_nodes only applies to the scaling mode"
+    );
+    let initial_count = match config.mode {
+        ExperimentMode::Correctness => config.node_count - 1,
+        ExperimentMode::Performance | ExperimentMode::Latency => config.node_count,
+        ExperimentMode::Availability => config.availability_initial_members(),
+        ExperimentMode::Fault => config.fault_initial_members(),
+        ExperimentMode::Scaling => {
+            config
+                .initial_nodes
+                .unwrap_or_else(|| match config.scaling_scenario {
+                    ScalingScenario::Shrink | ScalingScenario::Control => config.node_count,
+                    ScalingScenario::Grow | ScalingScenario::RoundTrip => config.node_count - 1,
+                    ScalingScenario::Replace => config.node_count - 1,
+                    ScalingScenario::Churn => config.node_count.saturating_sub(3),
+                })
+        }
+    };
+    ensure!(
+        initial_count >= config.desired_replication_factor as usize,
+        "initial membership must be at least the desired replication factor"
+    );
+    ensure!(
+        config.minimum_admitted_copies > 0
+            && config.minimum_admitted_copies <= config.desired_replication_factor,
+        "minimum admitted copies must be between 1 and desired RF"
+    );
+    ensure!(
+        config.minimum_healthy_followers < config.desired_replication_factor,
+        "minimum healthy followers must be below desired RF"
+    );
+    ensure!(config.key_count > 0, "key_count must be positive");
+    ensure!(
+        usize::try_from(config.key_count).is_ok(),
+        "key_count exceeds the platform address space"
+    );
+    // The key space is multiplied by a share and extended by the write pools,
+    // so a count near the integer limit would overflow those products.
+    ensure!(
+        config.key_count <= MAX_KEY_COUNT,
+        "key_count must not exceed {MAX_KEY_COUNT}"
+    );
+    if matches!(config.mode, ExperimentMode::Latency) {
+        ensure!(
+            !config.target_rates.is_empty(),
+            "the latency mode needs at least one target rate"
+        );
+        ensure!(
+            config.target_rates.iter().all(|rate| *rate > 0),
+            "every target rate must be positive"
+        );
+        ensure!(
+            config.duration_seconds > 0,
+            "duration_seconds must be positive"
+        );
+        ensure!(config.max_in_flight > 0, "max_in_flight must be positive");
+    }
+    ensure!(config.concurrency > 0, "concurrency must be positive");
+    ensure!(
+        config.range_move_concurrency > 0 && config.replica_repair_concurrency > 0,
+        "range_move_concurrency and replica_repair_concurrency must be positive"
+    );
+    ensure!(config.value_bytes > 0, "value_bytes must be positive");
+    ensure!(
+        config.value_bytes <= config.node.max_value_bytes,
+        "value_bytes exceeds the data-node limit"
+    );
+    ensure!(config.virtual_nodes > 0, "virtual_nodes must be positive");
+    ensure!(
+        config.operation_timeout_ms > 0 && config.migration_timeout_ms > 0,
+        "timeouts must be positive"
+    );
+    ensure!(
+        config.operation_timeout_ms <= config.receipt_retention_ms,
+        "operation_timeout_ms exceeds the {} ms receipt retention period, which caps every \
+         mutation's retries",
+        config.receipt_retention_ms
+    );
+    if matches!(config.mode, ExperimentMode::Scaling) {
+        ensure!(
+            initial_count <= config.node_count,
+            "initial_nodes exceeds the peak node count"
+        );
+        match config.scaling_scenario {
+            ScalingScenario::Grow => ensure!(
+                initial_count < config.node_count,
+                "a grow run needs fewer initial nodes than the peak"
+            ),
+            ScalingScenario::Shrink => {
+                ensure!(
+                    initial_count == config.node_count,
+                    "a shrink run starts with every peak node"
+                );
+                ensure!(
+                    config.node_count > config.desired_replication_factor as usize,
+                    "a shrink run needs more nodes than the desired replication factor"
+                );
+            }
+            ScalingScenario::RoundTrip => ensure!(
+                initial_count + 1 == config.node_count,
+                "a round trip starts with one fewer node than the peak"
+            ),
+            ScalingScenario::Replace => ensure!(
+                initial_count + 1 == config.node_count,
+                "a replace run starts with one fewer node than the peak so one spare member can \
+                 replace an initial member"
+            ),
+            ScalingScenario::Churn => ensure!(
+                initial_count + 2 <= config.node_count,
+                "a churn run needs at least two more peak nodes than its initial membership"
+            ),
+            ScalingScenario::Control => ensure!(
+                initial_count == config.node_count,
+                "a control run starts with every peak node and changes no membership"
+            ),
+        }
+        // The rates are split into whole operations per second and multiplied
+        // by the pool seconds, so a rate near the integer limit would overflow
+        // those products instead of failing cleanly.
+        ensure!(
+            config.scaling_open_rate <= MAX_SCALING_RATE
+                && config.scaling_write_rate <= MAX_SCALING_RATE,
+            "scaling rates must not exceed {MAX_SCALING_RATE} operations per second"
+        );
+        if config.scaling_load_mode == ScalingLoadMode::Open {
+            ensure!(
+                config.scaling_open_rate > 0,
+                "an open-loop scaling run needs a positive scaling_open_rate"
+            );
+            let minimum = minimum_scaling_rate(3);
+            ensure!(
+                config.scaling_open_rate >= minimum,
+                "an open-loop scaling run needs a rate of at least {minimum} to offer every \
+                 write cohort"
+            );
+            ensure!(
+                config.max_in_flight > 0,
+                "an open-loop scaling run needs a positive max_in_flight"
+            );
+        } else {
+            ensure!(
+                config.scaling_open_rate == 0,
+                "scaling_open_rate only applies to an open-loop scaling run"
+            );
+            // Only the closed loop paces writes with this rate; an open-loop
+            // run takes its write rates from scaling_open_rate.
+            ensure!(
+                config.scaling_write_rate > 0,
+                "scaling_write_rate must be positive"
+            );
+            // Every write cohort gets a share of the rate, and the shares are
+            // whole operations per second. A rate that rounds the smallest
+            // share down to zero would leave the cohort without a key, which
+            // is only noticed when the run builds its plan.
+            let minimum = minimum_scaling_rate(15);
+            ensure!(
+                config.scaling_write_rate >= minimum,
+                "a closed-loop scaling run needs a rate of at least {minimum} to offer every \
+                 write cohort"
+            );
+        }
+        ensure!(
+            config.scaling_pool_seconds > 0,
+            "scaling_pool_seconds must be positive"
+        );
+        // The pool sizes are the cohort rates multiplied by this window.
+        ensure!(
+            config.scaling_pool_seconds <= MAX_SCALING_POOL_SECONDS,
+            "scaling_pool_seconds must not exceed {MAX_SCALING_POOL_SECONDS}"
+        );
+        ensure!(
+            config.scaling_post_seconds > 0,
+            "scaling_post_seconds must be positive"
+        );
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}

+fn write_json(path: &Path, value: &impl Serialize) -> Result<()> {
+    let file = File::create(path)?;
+    // The manifest inlines a multi-megabyte `git diff`. Serializing pretty JSON
+    // emits a few bytes at a time, so an unbuffered handle turns a single write
+    // into tens of thousands of `write` syscalls plus the ext4 metadata churn
+    // that follows them.
+    let mut writer = BufWriter::new(file);
+    serde_json::to_writer_pretty(&mut writer, value)?;
+    // Surface a deferred write error instead of losing it in `Drop`.
+    writer.flush()?;
+    Ok(())
+}

+fn file_digest(path: &Path) -> Result<String> {
+    let mut file = File::open(path)?;
+    let mut hasher = blake3::Hasher::new();
+    let mut buffer = [0_u8; 64 * 1024];
+    loop {
+        let read = file.read(&mut buffer)?;
+        if read == 0 {
+            break;
+        }
+        hasher.update(&buffer[..read]);
+    }
+    Ok(hasher.finalize().to_hex().to_string())
+}
+
+fn source_tree_digest(workspace: &Path) -> Result<String> {
+    let mut files = Vec::new();
+    for path in [
+        "Cargo.toml",
+        "Cargo.lock",
+        "PLAN.md",
+        "README.md",
+        "src",
+        "crates",
+        "tests",
+    ] {
+        collect_files(&workspace.join(path), &mut files)?;
+    }
+    files.sort();
+    let mut hasher = blake3::Hasher::new();
+    hasher.update(b"hashring-rs:source-tree:v1\0");
+    for path in files {
+        let relative = path.strip_prefix(workspace).unwrap_or(&path);
+        let encoded = relative.to_string_lossy();
+        let contents = fs::read(&path)?;
+        hasher.update(&(encoded.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
+        hasher.update(encoded.as_bytes());
+        hasher.update(&(contents.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
+        hasher.update(&contents);
+    }

+fn collect_files(path: &Path, files: &mut Vec<PathBuf>) -> Result<()> {
+    if path.is_file() {
+        files.push(path.to_owned());
+    } else if path.is_dir() {
+        for entry in fs::read_dir(path)? {
+            collect_files(&entry?.path(), files)?;
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(())

-            initial_writes: writes_ok,

-            // completed before it is not the first write after the stop.

-        // the poll catches up with the rejection counter.

-    metrics: Arc<Metrics>,
-    read_pool: Arc<Vec<u64>>,
-    distribution: crate::latency::KeyDistribution,
-    stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,
-    rate: u64,
-) -> Result<OpenSender> {
-    let handle = tokio::runtime::Handle::current();
-    let client = client.clone();
-    let thread_stop = Arc::clone(&stop);
-    let seed = config.hash_seed;
-    let value_bytes = config.value_bytes;
-    let thread = std::thread::Builder::new()
-        .name("scaling-open-reads".to_owned())
-        .spawn(move || {
-            let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed);
-            let mut index = 0_u64;
-            let mut margin = Duration::from_micros(100);
-            let start = Instant::now();
-            while !thread_stop.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
-                let due = start + Duration::from_secs_f64(index as f64 / rate as f64);
-                super::latency::wait_until(due, &mut margin);
-                if thread_stop.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
-                    break;
-                }
-                if metrics.try_begin() {
-                    let key =
-                        read_pool[distribution.sample(&mut rng, read_pool.len() as u64) as usize];
-                    let client = client.clone();
-                    let metrics = Arc::clone(&metrics);
-                    handle.spawn(async move {
-                        let phase = metrics.phase();

-                        let elapsed = Instant::now().saturating_duration_since(due);

-                        metrics.finish();
-                    });
-                } else {
-                    metrics.late();
-                }
-                index += 1;
-            }
-            Ok(())
-        })?;

-        stop,
-        thread: Some(thread),
-    })
-}

-fn start_open_writes(context: OpenWriteContext<'_>) -> Result<Vec<OpenSender>> {
-    let OpenWriteContext {
-        config,
-        client,
-        plan,
-        ledger,
-        metrics,
-        stop,
-        probe_tx,
-    } = context;
-    let rates = cohort_rates(config);
-    let cohorts = [
-        (Cohort::Rewrite, Arc::clone(&plan.rewrite), rates.rewrite),
-        (
-            Cohort::WriteNew,
-            Arc::clone(&plan.write_new),
-            rates.write_new,
-        ),
-        (Cohort::Delete, Arc::clone(&plan.delete), rates.delete),
-    ];
-    let mut senders = Vec::new();
-    let sender_context = OpenSenderContext {
-        client,
-        ledger,
-        metrics,
-        stop,
-        probe_tx,
-        value_bytes: config.value_bytes,
-    };
-    for (cohort, pool, rate) in cohorts {
-        ensure!(rate > 0, "an open-loop write share rounds to zero");
-        senders.push(start_open_writes_for(cohort, rate, pool, &sender_context)?);
-    }
-    Ok(senders)
-}

-fn start_open_writes_for(
-    cohort: Cohort,
-    rate: u64,
-    pool: Arc<KeyPool>,
-    context: &OpenSenderContext<'_>,
-) -> Result<OpenSender> {
-    let value_bytes = context.value_bytes;
-    let probe_tx = context.probe_tx.clone();
-    let handle = tokio::runtime::Handle::current();
-    let client = context.client.clone();
-    let ledger = Arc::clone(context.ledger);
-    let metrics = Arc::clone(context.metrics);
-    let stop = Arc::clone(context.stop);
-    let thread_stop = Arc::clone(&stop);
-    let thread = std::thread::Builder::new()
-        .name(format!("scaling-open-{}", cohort.metric_name()))
-        .spawn(move || {
-            let mut index = 0_u64;
-            let mut margin = Duration::from_micros(100);
-            let start = Instant::now();
-            while !thread_stop.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
-                let due = start + Duration::from_secs_f64(index as f64 / rate as f64);
-                super::latency::wait_until(due, &mut margin);
-                if thread_stop.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
-                    break;
-                }
-                if !metrics.begin_write() {
-                    metrics.late();
-                    index += 1;
-                    continue;
-                }
-                let Some(key) = pool.next() else {
-                    metrics.finish_write();
-                    break;
-                };
-                let client = client.clone();
-                let ledger = Arc::clone(&ledger);
-                let metrics = Arc::clone(&metrics);
-                let probe_tx = probe_tx.clone();
-                handle.spawn(async move {
-                    let phase = metrics.phase();
-                    // Read the rejection count before the write for the same
-                    // reason the closed loop does: only a rejection the client
-                    // already knew when the write started is evidence that the
-                    // write happened after the stop.
-                    let busy_before = client.retry_reason_count(RetryReason::RangeBusy);
-                    let result = match cohort {
-                        Cohort::Rewrite | Cohort::WriteNew => client
-                            .put(
-                                key.to_be_bytes().to_vec(),
-                                deterministic_value(key, 1, value_bytes),
-                            )
-                            .await
-                            .map(|_| ()),
-                        Cohort::Delete => {
-                            client.delete(key.to_be_bytes().to_vec()).await.map(|_| ())
-                        }
-                    };
-                    if result.is_ok() {
-                        metrics.record_write_success(busy_before);
-                    }
-                    let elapsed = Instant::now().saturating_duration_since(due);
-                    ledger.record(key, cohort, &result);
-                    metrics.record(cohort.metric_name(), phase, elapsed, &result);
-                    if result.is_ok() {
-                        let expected = match cohort {
-                            Cohort::Delete => None,
-                            Cohort::Rewrite | Cohort::WriteNew => {
-                                Some(deterministic_value(key, 1, value_bytes))
-                            }
-                        };
-                        let _ = probe_tx.send((key, expected));
-                    }
-                    metrics.finish_write();
-                });
-                index += 1;
-            }
-            Ok(())
-        })?;
-    Ok(OpenSender {
-        stop: Arc::clone(&stop),
-        thread: Some(thread),
-    })
-}

-async fn drain_in_flight(metrics: &Metrics, config: &ExperimentConfig) -> Result<()> {
-    if metrics.in_flight.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 0 {
-        return Ok(());
-    }
-    let deadline = Instant::now()
-        + Duration::from_millis(config.operation_timeout_ms)
-            .saturating_add(Duration::from_secs(10));
-    while metrics.in_flight.load(Ordering::Acquire) > 0 {
-        ensure!(
-            Instant::now() < deadline,
-            "{} open-loop requests were still in flight after the drain deadline",
-            metrics.in_flight.load(Ordering::Acquire)
-        );
-        tokio::time::sleep(PHASE_POLL_INTERVAL).await;
-    }
-    Ok(())
-}

-/// Waits for one transition's writes only. The reads belong to the next

-async fn drain_writes(metrics: &Metrics, config: &ExperimentConfig) -> Result<()> {
-    if metrics.in_flight_writes.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 0 {
-        return Ok(());
-    }
-    let deadline = Instant::now()
-        + Duration::from_millis(config.operation_timeout_ms)
-            .saturating_add(Duration::from_secs(10));
-    while metrics.in_flight_writes.load(Ordering::Acquire) > 0 {
-        ensure!(
-            Instant::now() < deadline,
-            "{} open-loop write requests were still in flight after the drain deadline",
-            metrics.in_flight_writes.load(Ordering::Acquire)
-        );
-        tokio::time::sleep(PHASE_POLL_INTERVAL).await;
-    }
-    Ok(())
-}

-/// rate so it trails the writes instead of competing with them, bounded on
-/// both ends so a tiny or enormous write rate still yields a usable pace.

-/// How long the probe may go without reading a key before it is stuck.
-///
-/// The probe reads its keys one after another, and every read is bounded by
-/// the client's operation timeout, so a probe that is making progress always
-/// finishes a key within that timeout plus the pause between two reads. A
-/// probe that goes longer than that without a key is stuck, and the run must
-/// not wait for it forever.
-///
-/// A budget for the whole probe would have to cover the service time of every
-/// read as well as the pause between them, and the service time is not known
-/// in advance: the probe runs right after a publication, while the cluster is
-/// still repairing replicas. A fixed budget fails a run that is only slow.
-fn after_publish_probe_idle_limit(operation_timeout: Duration, rate: u64) -> Duration {
-    let pause = Duration::from_secs_f64(1.0 / rate as f64);
-    operation_timeout + pause + Duration::from_secs(10)
-}

-/// What a read-after-publish probe is doing.
-///
-/// The probe publishes every key it reads, so the watchdog can tell a probe
-/// that is still working from one that stopped. The last state is the one the
-/// probe leaves behind when it read every key it was given.
-#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
-enum ProbeState {
-    /// The probe read this many keys and is still reading.
-    Reading(u64),

-/// Gives up on a probe that stops reading keys.
-///
-/// The clock starts with the probe rather than with the moment the run waits
-/// for it, so a probe that stopped early is given up on while the run is
-/// still going. Every key the probe reads moves the deadline, so the limit
-/// covers the time between two keys instead of the whole probe.
-async fn watch_after_publish_probe(
-    label: &'static str,
-    mut progress: tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<ProbeState>,
-    abort: tokio::task::AbortHandle,
-    report: Arc<ProbeReport>,
-    idle_limit: Duration,
-    events: EventLog,
-) {
-    let mut read = 0_u64;
-    let mut deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + idle_limit;
-    loop {
-        tokio::select! {
-            update = progress.changed() => {
-                if update.is_err() {
-                    // The probe ended without saying so, so there is nothing
-                    // left to watch.
-                    return;
-                }
-                match *progress.borrow() {
-                    ProbeState::Finished => return,
-                    ProbeState::Reading(count) => {
-                        read = count;
-                        report.verified.store(count, Ordering::Release);
-                        deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + idle_limit;
-                    }
-                }
-            }
-            _ = tokio::time::sleep_until(deadline) => {
-                match *progress.borrow() {
-                    ProbeState::Finished => return,
-                    ProbeState::Reading(count) if count != read => {
-                        // The probe read a key after the deadline was set, so
-                        // it is making progress and the deadline was stale.
-                        read = count;
-                        report.verified.store(count, Ordering::Release);
-                        deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + idle_limit;
-                        continue;
-                    }
-                    ProbeState::Reading(_) => {}
-                }
-                // The store of the count must precede the store of the verdict,
-                // so a reader of the verdict also sees the final count.
-                report.verified.store(read, Ordering::Release);

-                    "scaling_after_publish_probe_stuck",
-                    json!({
-                        "label": label,
-                        "idle_limit_ms": idle_limit.as_millis() as u64,
-                        "verified": read,
-                    }),
-                ) {

-                }

-            }
-        }

-}

-fn build_transition_plan(
-    config: &ExperimentConfig,
-    transition: &Transition,
-    base: &TopologySnapshot,
-    target: &TopologySnapshot,
-    pool_plan: &BuildPlan,
-    index: usize,
-    transitions: usize,

-    let base_ids: BTreeSet<&str> = base
-        .members
-        .iter()
-        .map(|member| member.node_id.as_str())
-        .collect();
-    let target_ids: BTreeSet<&str> = target
-        .members
-        .iter()
-        .map(|member| member.node_id.as_str())
-        .collect();
-    let removed: BTreeSet<String> = base_ids
-        .difference(&target_ids)
-        .map(|id| (*id).to_owned())
-        .collect();
-    let added: BTreeSet<String> = target_ids
-        .difference(&base_ids)
-        .map(|id| (*id).to_owned())
-        .collect();
-
-    let writable = config.key_count - pool_plan.read.len() as u64;
-    let per_transition = writable / transitions as u64;
-    let chunk_start = pool_plan.read.len() as u64 + index as u64 * per_transition;
-    let chunk_end = if index + 1 == transitions {
-        config.key_count
-    } else {
-        chunk_start + per_transition
-    };
-
-    let write_rate = cohort_rates(config);
-    let pool_seconds = config.scaling_pool_seconds;

-    // a u64. Converting them to a usize is still fallible on a platform with a
-    // smaller address space, and a truncated quota would be a wrong plan.
-    let rewrite_quota = usize::try_from(write_rate.rewrite * pool_seconds)
-        .context("the rewrite pool does not fit the platform address space")?;
-    let new_quota = usize::try_from(write_rate.write_new * pool_seconds)
-        .context("the fresh-write pool does not fit the platform address space")?;
-    let delete_quota = usize::try_from(write_rate.delete * pool_seconds)
-        .context("the delete pool does not fit the platform address space")?;

-        rewrite_quota > 0 && new_quota > 0 && delete_quota > 0,
-        "the scaling write rate is too low to give every cohort a key; raise it or raise --scaling-pool-seconds"

-    ensure!(
-        rewrite_quota + delete_quota <= (chunk_end - chunk_start) as usize,
-        "the {} transition needs {} rewrite/delete keys but its chunk has {}; raise --keys or lower --scaling-write-rate/--scaling-pool-seconds",
-        transition.label,
-        rewrite_quota + delete_quota,
-        chunk_end - chunk_start

-    let mut by_stratum = classify_range(base, target, chunk_start..chunk_end, &removed, &added);

-    let delete_keys = take_stratified(&mut by_stratum, delete_quota);

-        !rewrite_keys.is_empty() && !delete_keys.is_empty(),
-        "the {} transition has no rewrite or delete keys",
-        transition.label
-    );
-
-    let fresh_start = config.key_count + index as u64 * new_quota as u64;
-    let fresh_end = fresh_start + new_quota as u64;
-    let mut fresh_by_stratum =
-        classify_range(base, target, fresh_start..fresh_end, &removed, &added);
-    let fresh_present: BTreeSet<Stratum> = fresh_by_stratum.keys().copied().collect();
-    let write_new_keys = take_stratified(&mut fresh_by_stratum, new_quota);

-        !write_new_keys.is_empty(),
-        "the {} transition has no fresh keys",
-        transition.label
-    );
-
-    let mut present_strata = present_strata;

-
-    let mut strata = BTreeMap::new();
-    for key in &rewrite_keys {
-        if let Some(stratum) = classify_key(base, target, *key, &removed, &added) {
-            strata.insert(*key, stratum);
-        }
-    }
-    for key in &delete_keys {
-        if let Some(stratum) = classify_key(base, target, *key, &removed, &added) {
-            strata.insert(*key, stratum);
-        }
-    }
-    for key in &write_new_keys {
-        if let Some(stratum) = classify_key(base, target, *key, &removed, &added) {
-            strata.insert(*key, stratum);
-        }
-    }
-
-    for stratum in &expected_strata {
-        let covered = rewrite_keys
-            .iter()
-            .chain(&delete_keys)
-            .chain(&write_new_keys)
-            .any(|key| strata.get(key) == Some(stratum));

-            covered,
-            "the {} transition has no write or delete key in the {} stratum",
-            transition.label,
-            stratum.name()

-    }

-    Ok(TransitionPlan {
-        rewrite: Arc::new(KeyPool::new(rewrite_keys)),
-        write_new: Arc::new(KeyPool::new(write_new_keys)),
-        delete: Arc::new(KeyPool::new(delete_keys)),

-fn classify_range(
-    base: &TopologySnapshot,
-    target: &TopologySnapshot,
-    range: std::ops::Range<u64>,
-    removed: &BTreeSet<String>,
-    added: &BTreeSet<String>,
-) -> BTreeMap<Stratum, Vec<u64>> {
-    let mut by_stratum: BTreeMap<Stratum, Vec<u64>> = BTreeMap::new();
-    for key in range {
-        if let Some(stratum) = classify_key(base, target, key, removed, added) {
-            by_stratum.entry(stratum).or_default().push(key);
-        }
-    }
-    by_stratum

-fn classify_key(
-    base: &TopologySnapshot,
-    target: &TopologySnapshot,
-    key: u64,
-    removed: &BTreeSet<String>,
-    added: &BTreeSet<String>,
-) -> Option<Stratum> {
-    let encoded = key.to_be_bytes();
-    let token = base.key_token(&encoded);
-    let base_owner = base.owner_for_token(token).ok()?.node_id.as_str();
-    let target_owner = target.owner_for_token(token).ok()?.node_id.as_str();
-    if base_owner != target_owner {
-        if removed.contains(base_owner) {
-            Some(Stratum::RemovedSource)
-        } else if added.contains(target_owner) {
-            Some(Stratum::NewTarget)
-        } else {
-            Some(Stratum::OwnerChanged)
-        }
-    } else {
-        let base_replicas = base.replica_node_ids_for_token(token).ok()?;
-        let target_replicas = target.replica_node_ids_for_token(token).ok()?;
-        if base_replicas != target_replicas {
-            Some(Stratum::ReplicasChanged)
-        } else {
-            Some(Stratum::Unchanged)
-        }
-    }
-}

-fn take_stratified(by_stratum: &mut BTreeMap<Stratum, Vec<u64>>, quota: usize) -> Vec<u64> {
-    let mut selected = Vec::with_capacity(quota);
-    while selected.len() < quota {
-        let mut progressed = false;
-        for keys in by_stratum.values_mut() {
-            if selected.len() == quota {
-                break;
-            }
-            if let Some(key) = keys.pop() {
-                selected.push(key);
-                progressed = true;
-            }
-        }
-        if !progressed {
-            break;
-        }
-    }
-    selected
-}

-    client: &'a HashringClient,

-fn start_writes(context: WriteContext<'_>) {
-    let WriteContext {
-        config,
-        client,
-        plan,
-        ledger,
-        metrics,
-        stop,
-        handles,
-        probe_tx,
-    } = context;
-    let rate = cohort_rates(config);
-    let cohorts = [
-        (Cohort::Rewrite, Arc::clone(&plan.rewrite), rate.rewrite),
-        (
-            Cohort::WriteNew,
-            Arc::clone(&plan.write_new),
-            rate.write_new,
-        ),
-        (Cohort::Delete, Arc::clone(&plan.delete), rate.delete),
-    ];
-    for (cohort, pool, cohort_rate) in cohorts {
-        if cohort_rate == 0 {
-            continue;
-        }
-        let tasks = (cohort_rate / 50).clamp(1, config.concurrency as u64) as usize;
-        let interval = Duration::from_secs_f64(tasks as f64 / cohort_rate as f64);
-        for _ in 0..tasks {
-            let client = client.clone();
-            let pool = Arc::clone(&pool);
-            let ledger = Arc::clone(ledger);
-            let metrics = Arc::clone(metrics);
-            let stop = Arc::clone(stop);
-            let probe_tx = probe_tx.clone();
-            let value_bytes = config.value_bytes;
-            handles.push(tokio::spawn(async move {
-                while !stop.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
-                    let Some(key) = pool.next() else {
-                        break;
-                    };
-                    if !interval.is_zero() {
-                        tokio::time::sleep(interval).await;
-                    }
-                    let phase = metrics.phase();
-                    metrics.issued.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
-                    // The rejection count is read before the write, so the
-                    // success can only claim a rejection the client already
-                    // knew about when it started.
-                    let busy_before = client.retry_reason_count(RetryReason::RangeBusy);
-                    let started = Instant::now();
-                    let result = match cohort {
-                        Cohort::Rewrite | Cohort::WriteNew => client
-                            .put(
-                                key.to_be_bytes().to_vec(),
-                                deterministic_value(key, 1, value_bytes),
-                            )
-                            .await
-                            .map(|_| ()),
-                        Cohort::Delete => {
-                            client.delete(key.to_be_bytes().to_vec()).await.map(|_| ())
-                        }
-                    };
-                    if result.is_ok() {
-                        metrics.record_write_success(busy_before);
-                    }
-                    let elapsed = started.elapsed();
-                    ledger.record(key, cohort, &result);
-                    metrics.record(cohort.metric_name(), phase, elapsed, &result);
-                    if result.is_ok() {
-                        let expected = match cohort {
-                            Cohort::Delete => None,
-                            Cohort::Rewrite | Cohort::WriteNew => {
-                                Some(deterministic_value(key, 1, value_bytes))
-                            }
-                        };
-                        let _ = probe_tx.send((key, expected));
-                    }
-                }
-                Ok(())
-            }));
-        }
-    }
-}

-async fn spawn_after_publish_probe<F, Fut>(
-    mut get: F,
-    metrics: Arc<Metrics>,
-    expected: BTreeMap<u64, Allowed>,
-    rate: u64,
-    progress: tokio::sync::watch::Sender<ProbeState>,
-) -> Result<usize>
-where
-    F: FnMut(u64) -> Fut,
-    Fut: Future<Output = Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>>,
-{
-    let interval = Duration::from_secs_f64(1.0 / rate as f64);
-    let mut read = 0_usize;
-    for (key, allowed) in expected {
-        tokio::time::sleep(interval).await;
-        let phase = metrics.phase();
-        let started = Instant::now();
-        let result = get(key).await;
-        let elapsed = started.elapsed();
-        match result {
-            Ok(value) if allowed.check(Some(&value)) => {
-                metrics.record("probe_read_after_publish", phase, elapsed, &Ok(()));
-            }
-            Err(error) if is_not_found(&error) && allowed.check(None) => {
-                metrics.record("probe_read_after_publish", phase, elapsed, &Ok(()));
-            }
-            Ok(_) => {
-                metrics.record(
-                    "probe_read_after_publish",
-                    phase,
-                    elapsed,
-                    &Err(ClientError::MissingVersion),
-                );
-                metrics.violation(
-                    "probe_after_publish_wrong_value",
-                    format!(
-                        "key {key} expected {} after publication",
-                        allowed.describe()
-                    ),
-                );
-                return Err(anyhow!("key {key} had the wrong value after publication"));
-            }
-            Err(error) if is_not_found(&error) => {
-                metrics.violation(
-                    "probe_after_publish_missing",
-                    format!(
-                        "key {key} expected {} after publication",
-                        allowed.describe()
-                    ),
-                );
-                metrics.record("probe_read_after_publish", phase, elapsed, &Err(error));
-                return Err(anyhow!("key {key} was missing after publication"));
-            }
-            Err(error) => {
-                let detail = format!("key {key} could not be verified after publication: {error}");
-                metrics.record("probe_read_after_publish", phase, elapsed, &Err(error));
-                return Err(anyhow!(detail));
-            }
-        }
-        // Only a checked value or an expected absence is evidence of a read.
-        read += 1;
-        progress.send_replace(ProbeState::Reading(read as u64));
-    }
-    // The probe is done, so the watchdog must not give up on it.
-    progress.send_replace(ProbeState::Finished);
-    Ok(read)
-}

-async fn verify_entries(
-    client: &HashringClient,

-    let violations = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
-    let examples = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
-    let client = client.clone();
-    stream::iter(entries.iter())
-        .for_each_concurrent(Some(concurrency), |(key, allowed)| {
-            let client = client.clone();
-            let violations = Arc::clone(&violations);
-            let examples = Arc::clone(&examples);
-            let key = *key;
-            let allowed = allowed.clone();
-            async move {
-                let result = client.get(key.to_be_bytes().to_vec()).await;
-                let (ok, detail) = match &result {
-                    Ok(output) => (
-                        allowed.check(Some(&output.value)),
-                        format!("key {key} expected {}", allowed.describe()),
-                    ),
-                    Err(ClientError::Operation(failure))
-                        if failure.code == ErrorCode::NotFound && allowed.check(None) =>
-                    {
-                        (true, String::new())
-                    }
-                    Err(error) => (
-                        false,
-                        format!("key {key} expected {}, got {error}", allowed.describe()),
-                    ),

-        .await;
-    let examples = examples
-        .lock()
-        .expect("the example lock is not poisoned")
-        .clone();
-    ensure!(
-        examples.is_empty(),
-        "verification examples: {}",
-        examples.join("; ")

-    Ok(violations.load(Ordering::Acquire))
-}

-async fn wait_for_full_rf_at_epoch(
-    client: &HashringClient,
-    desired_rf: u32,
-    target_epoch: u64,
-    timeout: Duration,
-    processes: &mut ProcessGroup,
-) -> Result<()> {
-    let deadline = Instant::now() + timeout;
-    loop {
-        processes.ensure_running()?;
-        if let Ok(Ok(topology)) =
-            tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(3), client.refresh_topology()).await
-            && topology.epoch >= target_epoch
-            && let Ok(Ok(status)) =
-                tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(3), client.replica_status()).await
-            && !status.ranges.is_empty()
-            && status.ranges.iter().all(|range| {

-        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(250)).await;
-    }
-}
