+            format!("{}_transition", transition.label),
+            measurement(change_operations, change_seconds),
+        );
+        observations.insert(
+            format!("{}_transition", transition.label),
+            json!({
+                "change_seconds": change_seconds.as_secs_f64(),
+                "published_ms": published_ms,
+                "published_ms_source": published_ms_source,
+                "complete_ms": complete_ms,
+                "full_rf_seconds": full_rf_seconds,
+                "post_seconds": config.scaling_post_seconds,
+                "control": completed.is_none(),
+                "direct_merge": completed.as_ref().is_some_and(|change| change.direct_merge),
+                "base_epoch": base_topology.epoch,
+                "target_epoch": target_epoch,
+                "work_steps_ms": completed.as_ref().map(|change| json!(change.timings)),
+                "stop_window": stop_window.as_ref().map(StopWindow::summary),
+                "migration": {
+                    "keys": migration.keys,
+                    "keys_moved": migration.keys_moved,
+                    "rate": migration.rate(),
+                    "ranges": completed.as_ref().map_or(0, |change| change.ranges.len()),
+                    "snapshot_records": completed
+                        .as_ref()
+                        .map_or(0, |change| change.ranges.iter().map(|range| range.snapshot_records).sum::<u64>()),
+                },
+                "retries_by_reason": retry_delta,
+                "rewrite_pool": plan.rewrite.len(),
+                "new_pool": plan.write_new.len(),
+                "delete_pool": plan.delete.len(),
+                "touched_strata": touched.iter().map(|s| s.name()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
+                "verification": verification_status,
+            }),
+        );
+        events.record(
+            "scaling_transition_complete",
+            json!({
+                "label": transition.label,
+                "seconds": change_seconds.as_secs_f64(),
+                "published_ms": published_ms,
+                "published_ms_source": published_ms_source,
+                "complete_ms": complete_ms,
+                "full_rf_seconds": full_rf_seconds,
+                "migration_rate": migration.rate(),
+                "keys_moved": migration.keys_moved,
+                "target_epoch": target_epoch,
+                "retries_by_reason": retry_delta,
+                "work_steps_ms": completed.as_ref().map(|change| json!(change.timings)),
+            }),
+        )?;
+
+        for (key, allowed) in entries {
+            all_entries.insert(key, allowed);
+        }
+        all_fresh.extend(plan.write_new.keys.iter().copied());
+        final_epoch = target_epoch;
+    }
+
+    ensure!(
+        pending_verification.is_none(),
+        "the last transition's cohorts were not verified"
+    );
+    // Every change has to show that its keys could be read after the
+    // publication. A probe that read nothing leaves the run without that
+    // evidence, so it fails the run instead of passing it quietly.
+    let mut probe_results = Vec::new();
+    for probe in re_read_handles {
+        let read = join_after_publish_probe(probe).await?;
+        probe_results.push(read);
+    }
+    ensure!(
+        probe_results.len() == transitions.len() - usize::from(is_control(config)),
+        "the run has {} read-after-publish probes for {} changes; a change whose publish \
+         window held no write to a moved stratum has no read-after-publish evidence",
+        probe_results.len(),
+        transitions.len() - usize::from(is_control(config))
+    );
+    observations.insert(
+        "scaling_after_publish_probes".into(),
+        json!({ "probes": probe_results.len(), "keys_read": probe_results }),
+    );
+    if let Some(sender) = open_reads.take() {
+        sender.join().await?;
+    }
+    drain_in_flight(&metrics, config).await?;
+    read_tasks
+        .stop(
+            Duration::from_millis(config.operation_timeout_ms)
+                .saturating_add(Duration::from_secs(10)),
+        )
+        .await?;
+    sampler.stop().await;
+    let _ = metrics.sample(events);
+
+    // The whole preloaded key space must still be what it was, with the
+    // touched cohorts overlaid. Fresh keys are checked as well.
+    let mut expected: BTreeMap<u64, Allowed> = (0..config.key_count)
+        .map(|key| {
+            (
+                key,
+                Allowed::Value(deterministic_value(key, 0, config.value_bytes)),
+            )
+        })
+        .collect();
+    for (key, allowed) in all_entries {
+        expected.insert(key, allowed);
+    }
+    for key in all_fresh {
+        expected.entry(key).or_insert_with(|| Allowed::Missing);
+    }
+    let violations = verify_entries(workload_client, &expected, config.concurrency).await?;
+    ensure!(
+        violations == 0,
+        "final verification found {violations} violations"
+    );
+    let observed = metrics.violation_count();
+    ensure!(
+        observed == 0,
+        "the load observed {observed} read or probe violations"
+    );
+
+    observations.insert("scaling_metrics".into(), metrics.summary());
+    // An open-loop run takes its write rates from its open rate, so the
+    // closed-loop rate it was also given is not what it wrote at. The plan
+    // reports the rates the run actually used.
+    let rates = cohort_rates(config);
+    observations.insert(
+        "scaling_pool_plan".into(),
+        json!({
+            "read_keys": read_pool.len(),
+            "read_distribution": distribution.name(),
+            "load_mode": config.scaling_load_mode.name(),
+            "open_rate": config.scaling_open_rate,
+            "write_rate": if config.scaling_load_mode == ScalingLoadMode::Open {
+                serde_json::Value::Null
+            } else {
+                json!(config.scaling_write_rate)
+            },
+            "cohort_write_rates": {
+                "rewrite": rates.rewrite,
+                "write_new": rates.write_new,
+                "delete": rates.delete,
+                "total": rates.rewrite + rates.write_new + rates.delete,
+            },
+            "pool_seconds": config.scaling_pool_seconds,
+            "transitions": transitions.iter().map(|t| t.label).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
+        }),
+    );
+    events.record(
+        "scaling_complete",
+        json!({ "epoch": final_epoch, "metrics": metrics.summary() }),
+    )?;
+    super::record_topology(events, admin_client).await?;
+    Ok(final_epoch)
+}
+
+fn transitions(
+    config: &ExperimentConfig,
+    peak_members: &[Member],
+    initial_members: &[Member],
+) -> Vec<Transition> {
+    match config.scaling_scenario {
+        ScalingScenario::Grow => vec![Transition {
+            label: "grow",
+            target_members: peak_members[..config.node_count].to_vec(),
+        }],
+        ScalingScenario::Shrink => vec![Transition {
+            label: "shrink",
+            target_members: initial_members[..initial_members.len().saturating_sub(1)].to_vec(),
+        }],
+        ScalingScenario::RoundTrip | ScalingScenario::Churn => vec![
+            Transition {
+                label: "grow",
+                target_members: peak_members[..config.node_count].to_vec(),
+            },
+            Transition {
+                label: "shrink",
+                target_members: initial_members.to_vec(),
+            },
+        ],
+        ScalingScenario::Replace => {
+            let mut target_members = initial_members.to_vec();
+            target_members.pop();
+            target_members.push(
+                peak_members
+                    .last()
+                    .expect("a replace run has a spare peak member")
+                    .clone(),
+            );
+            vec![Transition {
+                label: "replace",
+                target_members,
+            }]
+        }
+        ScalingScenario::Control => vec![Transition {
+            label: "control",
+            target_members: initial_members.to_vec(),
+        }],
+    }
+}
+
+fn is_control(config: &ExperimentConfig) -> bool {
+    config.scaling_scenario == ScalingScenario::Control
+}
+
+/// The write operations per second each cohort is offered.
+///
+/// The pools and the senders must share one definition. Deriving an open-loop
+/// total from 20% of the offered rate and then splitting it again rounded a
+/// small delete share down to zero in the pool while the sender still offered
+/// deletes.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+struct CohortRates {
+    rewrite: u64,
+    write_new: u64,
+    delete: u64,
+}
+
+/// The per-cohort write rates of the run's load mode.
+///
+/// The shares are whole operations per second, so the cohorts together offer
+/// slightly less than the configured rate when the shares do not divide it.
+fn cohort_rates(config: &ExperimentConfig) -> CohortRates {
+    let (total, rewrite, write_new, delete) = match config.scaling_load_mode {
+        ScalingLoadMode::Closed => (config.scaling_write_rate, 60, 25, 15),
+        ScalingLoadMode::Open => (config.scaling_open_rate, 12, 5, 3),
+    };
+    CohortRates {
+        rewrite: total * rewrite / 100,
+        write_new: total * write_new / 100,
+        delete: total * delete / 100,
+    }
+}
+
+/// The write operations per second of every cohort together.
+fn write_operations_per_second(config: &ExperimentConfig) -> u64 {
+    let rates = cohort_rates(config);
+    rates.rewrite + rates.write_new + rates.delete
+}
+
+/// The paced rate of the read-after-publish probe. It reads at half the write
+/// rate so it trails the writes instead of competing with them, bounded on
+/// both ends so a tiny or enormous write rate still yields a usable pace.
+fn after_publish_probe_rate(config: &ExperimentConfig) -> u64 {
+    (write_operations_per_second(config) / 2).clamp(20, 500)
+}
+
+/// How long the probe may go without reading a key before it is stuck.
+///
+/// The probe reads its keys one after another, and every read is bounded by
+/// the client's operation timeout, so a probe that is making progress always
+/// finishes a key within that timeout plus the pause between two reads. A
+/// probe that goes longer than that without a key is stuck, and the run must
+/// not wait for it forever.
+///
+/// A budget for the whole probe would have to cover the service time of every
+/// read as well as the pause between them, and the service time is not known
+/// in advance: the probe runs right after a publication, while the cluster is
+/// still repairing replicas. A fixed budget fails a run that is only slow.
+fn after_publish_probe_idle_limit(operation_timeout: Duration, rate: u64) -> Duration {
+    let pause = Duration::from_secs_f64(1.0 / rate as f64);
+    operation_timeout + pause + Duration::from_secs(10)
+}
+
+/// The read-after-publish probe of one transition and what it has to show.
+struct AfterPublishProbe {
+    label: &'static str,
+    /// The keys the probe was given to read.
+    expected: usize,
+    /// How long the probe may go without reading a key.
+    idle_limit: Duration,
+    /// What the watchdog saw and how it ended.
+    report: Arc<ProbeReport>,
+    /// The probe's task. It is aborted when the probe is dropped.
+    handle: Option<tokio::task::JoinHandle<Result<usize>>>,
+    /// The watchdog that gives up on a probe which stops reading keys.
+    watchdog: Option<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>,
+}
+
+impl Drop for AfterPublishProbe {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        // A probe that is dropped before it finished would keep reading keys
+        // and writing metrics after the run moved on, so both of its tasks
+        // are aborted here. The joined path consumes the handle first, so an
+        // aborted handle is only ever a task that is still running.
+        if let Some(handle) = self.handle.take() {
+            handle.abort();
+        }
+        if let Some(watchdog) = self.watchdog.take() {
+            watchdog.abort();
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// Starts the read-after-publish probe of one transition.
+///
+/// The probe reads the keys that were written to a moved stratum while the
+/// change was publishing, so a stale read after the publication is caught. A
+/// change whose publish window held no such write has nothing to read, and
+/// that is recorded rather than left to look like a probe that read nothing.
+fn spawn_after_publish_probe_task(
+    config: &ExperimentConfig,
+    workload_client: &HashringClient,
+    metrics: &Arc<Metrics>,
+    ledger: &Ledger,
+    events: &EventLog,
+    label: &'static str,
+) -> Result<Option<AfterPublishProbe>> {
+    let expected = ledger.publish_expected();
+    if expected.is_empty() {
+        events.record(
+            "scaling_after_publish_probe_skipped",
+            json!({
+                "label": label,
+                "reason": "no successful write to a moved stratum landed in the publish window",
+            }),
+        )?;
+        return Ok(None);
+    }
+    let rate = after_publish_probe_rate(config);
+    let idle_limit =
+        after_publish_probe_idle_limit(Duration::from_millis(config.operation_timeout_ms), rate);
+    // Record the start before the tasks exist. An event that cannot be written
+    // must not leave a probe running with no owner left to stop it.
+    events.record(
+        "scaling_after_publish_probe_started",
+        json!({
+            "label": label,
+            "keys": expected.len(),
+            "rate": rate,
+            "idle_limit_ms": idle_limit.as_millis() as u64,
+        }),
+    )?;
+    // The probe reports every key it reads, so the watchdog can tell a probe
+    // that is still working from one that stopped.
+    let (progress, progress_updates) = tokio::sync::watch::channel(ProbeState::Reading(0));
+    let report = Arc::new(ProbeReport::default());
+    let client = workload_client.clone();
+    let handle = tokio::spawn(spawn_after_publish_probe(
+        move |key: u64| {
+            let client = client.clone();
+            async move {
+                client
+                    .get(key.to_be_bytes().to_vec())
+                    .await
+                    .map(|output| output.value)
+            }
+        },
+        Arc::clone(metrics),
+        expected.clone(),
+        rate,
+        progress,
+    ));
+    let watchdog = tokio::spawn(watch_after_publish_probe(
+        label,
+        progress_updates,
+        handle.abort_handle(),
+        Arc::clone(&report),
+        idle_limit,
+        events.clone(),
+    ));
+    Ok(Some(AfterPublishProbe {
+        label,
+        expected: expected.len(),
+        idle_limit,
+        report,
+        handle: Some(handle),
+        watchdog: Some(watchdog),
+    }))
+}
+
+/// What a probe's watchdog saw and how it ended.
+///
+/// The run reads it when the probe is joined: a probe that was given up on can
+/// then say how many keys it verified before it stopped, instead of claiming
+/// that it never read one.
+#[derive(Default)]
+struct ProbeReport {
+    /// The most keys the watchdog saw verified.
+    verified: AtomicU64,
+    /// Whether the watchdog gave up on the probe.
+    stuck: AtomicBool,
+}
+
+/// What a read-after-publish probe is doing.
+///
+/// The probe publishes every key it reads, so the watchdog can tell a probe
+/// that is still working from one that stopped. The last state is the one the
+/// probe leaves behind when it read every key it was given.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+enum ProbeState {
+    /// The probe read this many keys and is still reading.
+    Reading(u64),
+    /// The probe read every key it was given.
+    Finished,
+}
+
+/// Gives up on a probe that stops reading keys.
+///
+/// The clock starts with the probe rather than with the moment the run waits
+/// for it, so a probe that stopped early is given up on while the run is
+/// still going. Every key the probe reads moves the deadline, so the limit
+/// covers the time between two keys instead of the whole probe.
+async fn watch_after_publish_probe(
+    label: &'static str,
+    mut progress: tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<ProbeState>,
+    abort: tokio::task::AbortHandle,
+    report: Arc<ProbeReport>,
+    idle_limit: Duration,
+    events: EventLog,
+) {
+    let mut read = 0_u64;
+    let mut deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + idle_limit;
+    loop {
+        tokio::select! {
+            update = progress.changed() => {
+                if update.is_err() {
+                    // The probe ended without saying so, so there is nothing
+                    // left to watch.
+                    return;
+                }
+                match *progress.borrow() {
+                    ProbeState::Finished => return,
+                    ProbeState::Reading(count) => {
+                        read = count;
+                        report.verified.store(count, Ordering::Release);
+                        deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + idle_limit;
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            _ = tokio::time::sleep_until(deadline) => {
+                match *progress.borrow() {
+                    ProbeState::Finished => return,
+                    ProbeState::Reading(count) if count != read => {
+                        // The probe read a key after the deadline was set, so
+                        // it is making progress and the deadline was stale.
+                        read = count;
+                        report.verified.store(count, Ordering::Release);
+                        deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + idle_limit;
+                        continue;
+                    }
+                    ProbeState::Reading(_) => {}
+                }
+                // The store of the count must precede the store of the verdict,
+                // so a reader of the verdict also sees the final count.
+                report.verified.store(read, Ordering::Release);
+                report.stuck.store(true, Ordering::Release);
+                if let Err(error) = events.record(
+                    "scaling_after_publish_probe_stuck",
+                    json!({
+                        "label": label,
+                        "idle_limit_ms": idle_limit.as_millis() as u64,
+                        "verified": read,
+                    }),
+                ) {
+                    eprintln!("scaling after-publish probe event failed: {error:#}");
+                }
+                abort.abort();
+                return;
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// Waits for the read-after-publish probe and reports how many keys it read.
+///
+/// The probe is given as long as it keeps reading keys. It is given up on
+/// when it stops making progress, because a probe that is not reading will
+/// never finish. A change whose probe read every key it was given passes;
+/// anything else fails the run.
+async fn join_after_publish_probe(mut probe: AfterPublishProbe) -> Result<usize> {
+    let label = probe.label;
+    let expected = probe.expected;
+    let idle_limit = probe.idle_limit;
+    let report = Arc::clone(&probe.report);
+    let handle = probe
+        .handle
+        .take()
+        .expect("a probe always has the task it was started with");
+    let read = match handle.await {
+        Ok(Ok(read)) => read,
+        Ok(Err(error)) => return Err(error.context("the read-after-publish probe failed")),
+        Err(error) if error.is_cancelled() && report.stuck.load(Ordering::Acquire) => {
+            let verified = report.verified.load(Ordering::Acquire);
+            return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(
+                "the {label} read-after-publish probe made no progress for {idle_limit:?} \
+                 after verifying {verified} of its {expected} keys"
+            ));
+        }
+        Err(error) => {
+            return Err(anyhow::Error::new(error).context("joining the read-after-publish probe"));
+        }
+    };
+    ensure!(
+        read == expected && read > 0,
+        "the {label} read-after-publish probe verified {read} of its {expected} keys"
+    );
+    Ok(read)
+}
+
+struct Transition {
+    label: &'static str,
+    target_members: Vec<Member>,
+}
+
+struct BuildPlan {
+    read: Vec<u64>,
+}
+
+/// Splits the preloaded key space into an immutable read pool and one chunk
+/// per transition. The chunks are disjoint, so a key touched in one transition
+/// is never a `v0` input to the next one.
+fn plan_keys(config: &ExperimentConfig, transitions: &[Transition]) -> Result<BuildPlan> {
+    let read_share = if transitions.len() == 1 {
+        60_u64
+    } else {
+        50_u64
+    };
+    let read_count = config.key_count * read_share / 100;
+    ensure!(read_count > 0, "the read pool is empty");
+    let writable = config.key_count.saturating_sub(read_count);
+    let per_transition = writable / transitions.len() as u64;
+    ensure!(
+        per_transition >= 512,
+        "the key space leaves only {per_transition} keys per transition; raise --keys or lower --scaling-write-rate"
+    );
+    let read = (0..read_count).collect();
+    Ok(BuildPlan { read })
+}
+
+fn build_transition_plan(
+    config: &ExperimentConfig,
+    transition: &Transition,
+    base: &TopologySnapshot,
+    target: &TopologySnapshot,
+    pool_plan: &BuildPlan,
+    index: usize,
+    transitions: usize,
+) -> Result<TransitionPlan> {
+    let base_ids: BTreeSet<&str> = base
+        .members
+        .iter()
+        .map(|member| member.node_id.as_str())
+        .collect();
+    let target_ids: BTreeSet<&str> = target
+        .members
+        .iter()
+        .map(|member| member.node_id.as_str())
+        .collect();
+    let removed: BTreeSet<String> = base_ids
+        .difference(&target_ids)
+        .map(|id| (*id).to_owned())
+        .collect();
+    let added: BTreeSet<String> = target_ids
+        .difference(&base_ids)
+        .map(|id| (*id).to_owned())
+        .collect();
+
+    let writable = config.key_count - pool_plan.read.len() as u64;
+    let per_transition = writable / transitions as u64;
+    let chunk_start = pool_plan.read.len() as u64 + index as u64 * per_transition;
+    let chunk_end = if index + 1 == transitions {
+        config.key_count
+    } else {
+        chunk_start + per_transition
+    };
+
+    let write_rate = cohort_rates(config);
+    let pool_seconds = config.scaling_pool_seconds;
+    // The configuration bounds the rate and the window, so these products fit
+    // a u64. Converting them to a usize is still fallible on a platform with a
+    // smaller address space, and a truncated quota would be a wrong plan.
+    let rewrite_quota = usize::try_from(write_rate.rewrite * pool_seconds)
+        .context("the rewrite pool does not fit the platform address space")?;
+    let new_quota = usize::try_from(write_rate.write_new * pool_seconds)
+        .context("the fresh-write pool does not fit the platform address space")?;
+    let delete_quota = usize::try_from(write_rate.delete * pool_seconds)
+        .context("the delete pool does not fit the platform address space")?;
+    ensure!(
+        rewrite_quota > 0 && new_quota > 0 && delete_quota > 0,
+        "the scaling write rate is too low to give every cohort a key; raise it or raise --scaling-pool-seconds"
+    );
+    ensure!(
+        rewrite_quota + delete_quota <= (chunk_end - chunk_start) as usize,
+        "the {} transition needs {} rewrite/delete keys but its chunk has {}; raise --keys or lower --scaling-write-rate/--scaling-pool-seconds",
+        transition.label,
+        rewrite_quota + delete_quota,
+        chunk_end - chunk_start
+    );
+
+    let mut by_stratum = classify_range(base, target, chunk_start..chunk_end, &removed, &added);
+    let present_strata: BTreeSet<Stratum> = by_stratum.keys().copied().collect();
+    let rewrite_keys = take_stratified(&mut by_stratum, rewrite_quota);
+    let delete_keys = take_stratified(&mut by_stratum, delete_quota);
+    ensure!(
+        !rewrite_keys.is_empty() && !delete_keys.is_empty(),
+        "the {} transition has no rewrite or delete keys",
+        transition.label
+    );
+
+    let fresh_start = config.key_count + index as u64 * new_quota as u64;
+    let fresh_end = fresh_start + new_quota as u64;
+    let mut fresh_by_stratum =
+        classify_range(base, target, fresh_start..fresh_end, &removed, &added);
+    let fresh_present: BTreeSet<Stratum> = fresh_by_stratum.keys().copied().collect();
+    let write_new_keys = take_stratified(&mut fresh_by_stratum, new_quota);
+    ensure!(
+        !write_new_keys.is_empty(),
+        "the {} transition has no fresh keys",
+        transition.label
+    );
+
+    let mut present_strata = present_strata;
+    present_strata.extend(fresh_present);
+    let applicable = applicable_strata(config.scaling_scenario, transition.label);
+    let expected_strata: BTreeSet<_> = present_strata.intersection(&applicable).copied().collect();
+
+    let mut strata = BTreeMap::new();
+    for key in &rewrite_keys {
+        if let Some(stratum) = classify_key(base, target, *key, &removed, &added) {
+            strata.insert(*key, stratum);
+        }
+    }
+    for key in &delete_keys {
+        if let Some(stratum) = classify_key(base, target, *key, &removed, &added) {
+            strata.insert(*key, stratum);
+        }
+    }
+    for key in &write_new_keys {
+        if let Some(stratum) = classify_key(base, target, *key, &removed, &added) {
+            strata.insert(*key, stratum);
+        }
+    }
+
+    for stratum in &expected_strata {
+        let covered = rewrite_keys
+            .iter()
+            .chain(&delete_keys)
+            .chain(&write_new_keys)
+            .any(|key| strata.get(key) == Some(stratum));
+        ensure!(
+            covered,
+            "the {} transition has no write or delete key in the {} stratum",
+            transition.label,
+            stratum.name()
+        );
+    }
+
+    Ok(TransitionPlan {
+        rewrite: Arc::new(KeyPool::new(rewrite_keys)),
+        write_new: Arc::new(KeyPool::new(write_new_keys)),
+        delete: Arc::new(KeyPool::new(delete_keys)),
+        strata: Arc::new(strata),
+        expected_strata,
+        present_strata,
+    })
+}
+
+fn classify_range(
+    base: &TopologySnapshot,
+    target: &TopologySnapshot,
+    range: std::ops::Range<u64>,
+    removed: &BTreeSet<String>,
+    added: &BTreeSet<String>,
+) -> BTreeMap<Stratum, Vec<u64>> {
+    let mut by_stratum: BTreeMap<Stratum, Vec<u64>> = BTreeMap::new();
+    for key in range {
+        if let Some(stratum) = classify_key(base, target, key, removed, added) {
+            by_stratum.entry(stratum).or_default().push(key);
+        }
+    }
+    by_stratum
+}
+
+fn classify_key(
+    base: &TopologySnapshot,
+    target: &TopologySnapshot,
+    key: u64,
+    removed: &BTreeSet<String>,
+    added: &BTreeSet<String>,
+) -> Option<Stratum> {
+    let encoded = key.to_be_bytes();
+    let token = base.key_token(&encoded);
+    let base_owner = base.owner_for_token(token).ok()?.node_id.as_str();
+    let target_owner = target.owner_for_token(token).ok()?.node_id.as_str();
+    if base_owner != target_owner {
+        if removed.contains(base_owner) {
+            Some(Stratum::RemovedSource)
+        } else if added.contains(target_owner) {
+            Some(Stratum::NewTarget)
+        } else {
+            Some(Stratum::OwnerChanged)
+        }
+    } else {
+        let base_replicas = base.replica_node_ids_for_token(token).ok()?;
+        let target_replicas = target.replica_node_ids_for_token(token).ok()?;
+        if base_replicas != target_replicas {
+            Some(Stratum::ReplicasChanged)
+        } else {
+            Some(Stratum::Unchanged)
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+fn take_stratified(by_stratum: &mut BTreeMap<Stratum, Vec<u64>>, quota: usize) -> Vec<u64> {
+    let mut selected = Vec::with_capacity(quota);
+    while selected.len() < quota {
+        let mut progressed = false;
+        for keys in by_stratum.values_mut() {
+            if selected.len() == quota {
+                break;
+            }
+            if let Some(key) = keys.pop() {
+                selected.push(key);
+                progressed = true;
+            }
+        }
+        if !progressed {
+            break;
+        }
+    }
+    selected
+}
+
+fn stratum_counts(strata: &BTreeMap<u64, Stratum>) -> BTreeMap<&'static str, u64> {
+    let mut counts = BTreeMap::new();
+    for stratum in strata.values() {
+        *counts.entry(stratum.name()).or_insert(0) += 1;
+    }
+    counts
+}
+
+struct WriteContext<'a> {
+    config: &'a ExperimentConfig,
+    client: &'a HashringClient,
+    plan: &'a TransitionPlan,
+    ledger: &'a Arc<Ledger>,
+    metrics: &'a Arc<Metrics>,
+    stop: &'a Arc<AtomicBool>,
+    handles: &'a mut TaskHandles,
+    probe_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<(u64, Option<Vec<u8>>)>,
+}
+
+fn start_writes(context: WriteContext<'_>) {
+    let WriteContext {
+        config,
+        client,
+        plan,
+        ledger,
+        metrics,
+        stop,
+        handles,
+        probe_tx,
+    } = context;
+    let rate = cohort_rates(config);
+    let cohorts = [
+        (Cohort::Rewrite, Arc::clone(&plan.rewrite), rate.rewrite),
+        (
+            Cohort::WriteNew,
+            Arc::clone(&plan.write_new),
+            rate.write_new,
+        ),
+        (Cohort::Delete, Arc::clone(&plan.delete), rate.delete),
+    ];
+    for (cohort, pool, cohort_rate) in cohorts {
+        if cohort_rate == 0 {
+            continue;
+        }
+        let tasks = (cohort_rate / 50).clamp(1, config.concurrency as u64) as usize;
+        let interval = Duration::from_secs_f64(tasks as f64 / cohort_rate as f64);
+        for _ in 0..tasks {
+            let client = client.clone();
+            let pool = Arc::clone(&pool);
+            let ledger = Arc::clone(ledger);
+            let metrics = Arc::clone(metrics);
+            let stop = Arc::clone(stop);
+            let probe_tx = probe_tx.clone();
+            let value_bytes = config.value_bytes;
+            handles.push(tokio::spawn(async move {
+                while !stop.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
+                    let Some(key) = pool.next() else {
+                        break;
+                    };
+                    if !interval.is_zero() {
+                        tokio::time::sleep(interval).await;
+                    }
+                    let phase = metrics.phase();
+                    metrics.issued.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
+                    // The rejection count is read before the write, so the
+                    // success can only claim a rejection the client already
+                    // knew about when it started.
+                    let busy_before = client.retry_reason_count(RetryReason::RangeBusy);
+                    let started = Instant::now();
+                    let result = match cohort {
+                        Cohort::Rewrite | Cohort::WriteNew => client
+                            .put(
+                                key.to_be_bytes().to_vec(),
+                                deterministic_value(key, 1, value_bytes),
+                            )
+                            .await
+                            .map(|_| ()),
+                        Cohort::Delete => {
+                            client.delete(key.to_be_bytes().to_vec()).await.map(|_| ())
+                        }
+                    };
+                    if result.is_ok() {
+                        metrics.record_write_success(busy_before);
+                    }
+                    let elapsed = started.elapsed();
+                    ledger.record(key, cohort, &result);
+                    metrics.record(cohort.metric_name(), phase, elapsed, &result);
+                    if result.is_ok() {
+                        let expected = match cohort {
+                            Cohort::Delete => None,
+                            Cohort::Rewrite | Cohort::WriteNew => {
+                                Some(deterministic_value(key, 1, value_bytes))
+                            }
+                        };
+                        let _ = probe_tx.send((key, expected));
+                    }
+                }
+                Ok(())
+            }));
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+async fn spawn_after_publish_probe<F, Fut>(
+    mut get: F,
+    metrics: Arc<Metrics>,
+    expected: BTreeMap<u64, Allowed>,
+    rate: u64,
+    progress: tokio::sync::watch::Sender<ProbeState>,
+) -> Result<usize>
+where
+    F: FnMut(u64) -> Fut,
+    Fut: Future<Output = Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>>,
+{
+    let interval = Duration::from_secs_f64(1.0 / rate as f64);
+    let mut read = 0_usize;
+    for (key, allowed) in expected {
+        tokio::time::sleep(interval).await;
+        let phase = metrics.phase();
+        let started = Instant::now();
+        let result = get(key).await;
+        let elapsed = started.elapsed();
+        match result {
+            Ok(value) if allowed.check(Some(&value)) => {
+                metrics.record("probe_read_after_publish", phase, elapsed, &Ok(()));
+            }
+            Err(error) if is_not_found(&error) && allowed.check(None) => {
+                metrics.record("probe_read_after_publish", phase, elapsed, &Ok(()));
+            }
+            Ok(_) => {
+                metrics.record(
+                    "probe_read_after_publish",
+                    phase,
+                    elapsed,
+                    &Err(ClientError::MissingVersion),
+                );
+                metrics.violation(
+                    "probe_after_publish_wrong_value",
+                    format!(
+                        "key {key} expected {} after publication",
+                        allowed.describe()
+                    ),
+                );
+                return Err(anyhow!("key {key} had the wrong value after publication"));
+            }
+            Err(error) if is_not_found(&error) => {
+                metrics.violation(
+                    "probe_after_publish_missing",
+                    format!(
+                        "key {key} expected {} after publication",
+                        allowed.describe()
+                    ),
+                );
+                metrics.record("probe_read_after_publish", phase, elapsed, &Err(error));
+                return Err(anyhow!("key {key} was missing after publication"));
+            }
+            Err(error) => {
+                let detail = format!("key {key} could not be verified after publication: {error}");
+                metrics.record("probe_read_after_publish", phase, elapsed, &Err(error));
+                return Err(anyhow!(detail));
+            }
+        }
+        // Only a checked value or an expected absence is evidence of a read.
+        read += 1;
+        progress.send_replace(ProbeState::Reading(read as u64));
+    }
+    // The probe is done, so the watchdog must not give up on it.
+    progress.send_replace(ProbeState::Finished);
+    Ok(read)
+}
+
+async fn verify_entries(
+    client: &HashringClient,
+    entries: &BTreeMap<u64, Allowed>,
+    concurrency: usize,
+) -> Result<u64> {
+    let violations = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
+    let examples = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
+    let client = client.clone();
+    stream::iter(entries.iter())
+        .for_each_concurrent(Some(concurrency), |(key, allowed)| {
+            let client = client.clone();
+            let violations = Arc::clone(&violations);
+            let examples = Arc::clone(&examples);
+            let key = *key;
+            let allowed = allowed.clone();
+            async move {
+                let result = client.get(key.to_be_bytes().to_vec()).await;
+                let (ok, detail) = match &result {
+                    Ok(output) => (
+                        allowed.check(Some(&output.value)),
+                        format!("key {key} expected {}", allowed.describe()),
+                    ),
+                    Err(ClientError::Operation(failure))
+                        if failure.code == ErrorCode::NotFound && allowed.check(None) =>
+                    {
+                        (true, String::new())
+                    }
+                    Err(error) => (
+                        false,
+                        format!("key {key} expected {}, got {error}", allowed.describe()),
+                    ),
+                };
+                if !ok {
+                    violations.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
+                    let mut examples = examples.lock().expect("the example lock is not poisoned");
+                    if examples.len() < 32 {
+                        examples.push(detail);
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        })
+        .await;
+    let examples = examples
+        .lock()
+        .expect("the example lock is not poisoned")
+        .clone();
+    ensure!(
+        examples.is_empty(),
+        "verification examples: {}",
+        examples.join("; ")
+    );
+    Ok(violations.load(Ordering::Acquire))
+}

+async fn wait_for_full_rf_at_epoch(
+    client: &HashringClient,
+    desired_rf: u32,
+    target_epoch: u64,
+    timeout: Duration,
+    processes: &mut ProcessGroup,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    let deadline = Instant::now() + timeout;
+    loop {
+        processes.ensure_running()?;
+        if let Ok(Ok(topology)) =
+            tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(3), client.refresh_topology()).await
+            && topology.epoch >= target_epoch
+            && let Ok(Ok(status)) =
+                tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(3), client.replica_status()).await
+            && !status.ranges.is_empty()
+            && status.ranges.iter().all(|range| {
+                range.live_rf == desired_rf
+                    && !range.repairing
+                    && range.followers.iter().all(|follower| follower.healthy)
+            })
+        {
+            return Ok(());
+        }
+        ensure!(
+            Instant::now() < deadline,
+            "full RF at epoch {target_epoch} did not converge within {timeout:?}"
+        );
+        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(250)).await;
+    }
+}

+        // The probe reads a key every 10 ms, which is well inside the limit,
+        // and then says that it is done.
+        let probe = tokio::spawn(async move {

+    version: RecordVersion,
+    deleted: bool,
+    expires_at: Instant,
+) {
+    let retained_bytes = dedup_retained_bytes(&mutation_id, key.len(), version.owner_node_id.len());
+    let mutation_id: Arc<str> = mutation_id.into();
+    state
+        .dedup_expirations
+        .push(Reverse((expires_at, mutation_id.clone())));
+    let replaced = state.dedup.insert(
+        mutation_id.clone(),
+        DedupEntry {
+            key: key.clone(),
+            fingerprint,
+            version,
+            deleted,
+            retained_bytes,
+            expires_at,
+            required_acks: Vec::new(),
+        },
+    );
+    // Migration finds a range's receipts through this index, so it has to see
+    // every insert and every removal. A repeated id would otherwise leave two
+    // entries for one receipt.
+    // The replaced entry's bytes, including any ACK state charged to it, leave
+    // the store with it; otherwise each repeat inflates the budget for good.
+    if let Some(previous) = replaced {
+        state.remove_dedup_index(&mutation_id, &previous.key);
+        state.dedup_bytes -= previous.retained_bytes;
+    }
+    state.insert_dedup_index(&mutation_id, &key);
+    state.dedup_bytes += retained_bytes;
+    state.dedup_peak_bytes = state.dedup_peak_bytes.max(state.dedup_bytes);
+}
+
+pub(super) fn dedup_retry_after_millis(state: &NodeState, now: Instant) -> u64 {
+    state
+        .dedup_expirations
+        .peek()
+        .map(|Reverse((expires_at, _))| {
+            remaining_retention_millis(
+                *expires_at,
+                now,
+                state.topology.timings.receipt_retention_millis,
+            )
+            .max(1)
+        })
+        .unwrap_or(1)
+}
+
+pub(super) fn now_unix_millis() -> u64 {
+    SystemTime::now()
+        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
+        .unwrap_or_default()
+        .as_millis()
+        .try_into()
+        .unwrap_or(u64::MAX)
+}

+//! Per-key expiry.
+//!
+//! A record carries an absolute deadline that every replica of it enforces on
+//! read, so an expired key is absent without a delete travelling through the
+//! replication stream and a migration carrying the same value to a new owner.
+//! What is left is memory: the sweep in this module is the only thing that
+//! removes a record once its deadline has passed.
+
+use super::*;
+
+/// How often expired records are reclaimed. Reads already hide them, so the
+/// period only sets how long a value that nobody asks for stays resident.
+pub const EXPIRY_SWEEP_INTERVAL: std::time::Duration = std::time::Duration::from_millis(500);
+
+/// Expiry entries examined per sweep pass, whether they are removed or
+/// deferred. The sweep holds the write lock, so a pass over a node holding
+/// millions of expired keys cannot stall writers; the remainder is picked up by
+/// the next pass.
+pub const EXPIRY_SWEEP_LIMIT: usize = 65_536;
+
+/// Examines up to `limit` records whose deadline has passed at
+/// `now_unix_millis` and returns how many it removed.
+///
+/// A record in a range this node is migrating out is deferred instead of
+/// removed (see `SourceMigration::deferred_expirations`); it stays hidden from reads
+/// either way.
+pub(super) fn sweep_expired_records(
+    state: &mut NodeState,
+    now_unix_millis: u64,
+    limit: usize,
+) -> usize {
+    let mut removed = 0;
+    for _ in 0..limit {
+        let Some((deadline, key)) = state
+            .record_expirations
+            .first()
+            .filter(|(deadline, _)| *deadline <= now_unix_millis)
+            .cloned()
+        else {
+            break;
+        };
+        state.record_expirations.remove(&(deadline, key.clone()));
+        let token = state.token_of(&key);
+        if let Some(source) = state
+            .sources
+            .values_mut()
+            .find(|source| source.range.contains(token))
+        {
+            source.deferred_expirations.insert((deadline, key));
+            continue;
+        }
+        let record = state.remove_record_at(token, &key);
+        debug_assert!(
+            record.is_some_and(|record| record.expires_at_unix_millis == Some(deadline)),
+            "the expiry index named a record that does not carry its deadline",
+        );
+        removed += 1;
+    }
+    removed
+}
+
+pub(super) fn start_expiry_sweep(state: Arc<RwLock<NodeState>>) {
+    tokio::spawn(async move {
+        let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(EXPIRY_SWEEP_INTERVAL);
+        loop {
+            interval.tick().await;
+            let mut guard = state.write().await;
+            sweep_expired_records(&mut guard, now_unix_millis(), EXPIRY_SWEEP_LIMIT);
+        }
+    });
+}

+//! Paging through the keys a node owns, for callers that need the keyspace
+//! rather than one key: `KEYS`, `SCAN`, `DBSIZE` and `RANDOMKEY` at the Redis

+//!
+//! A node also holds follower copies of other owners' ranges, so a page walks
+//! only the token segments this node owns in its current topology and jumps
+//! over the rest. A segment is `(previous assignment, assignment]`, plus the
+//! wrap-around tail past the last assignment, which belongs to the first.
+//!
+//! A page ends only between tokens, never inside one, so where the next page
+//! starts is a token alone. That is what lets `SCAN` hand its cursor to a
+//! Redis client as a plain integer. A token holds more than one key only when
+//! keys' 64-bit hashes collide, which by chance is all but unheard of, but
+//! keys can be built to collide by anyone who knows the hash seed. So an owner
+//! refuses to put more than [`MAX_KEYS_PER_TOKEN`] keys on one token, which
+//! bounds what finishing a token can add to a page.
+
+use super::*;
+
+/// Entries and segments one page may examine, live or not. This bounds how
+/// long a page holds the state read lock, whatever the caller asked for.
+pub(super) const MAX_EXAMINED_PER_PAGE: usize = 10_000;
+pub(super) const MAX_KEYS_PER_PAGE: usize = 10_000;
+pub(super) const MAX_KEY_BYTES_PER_PAGE: usize = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
+/// The most keys one token may hold, deleted or not. Even at the largest key
+/// size, a full token adds a megabyte to a page, which keeps every page well
+/// inside one data message.
+pub(super) const MAX_KEYS_PER_TOKEN: usize = 16;
+
+pub(super) struct PageLimits {
+    pub max_keys: usize,
+    pub max_bytes: usize,
+    pub max_examined: usize,
+    pub count_only: bool,
+    /// Stop at the first segment another node owns, rather than jump over it:
+    /// the page then covers one contiguous stretch of the ring, which is what
+    /// a `SCAN` cursor walks.
+    pub one_stretch: bool,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Default)]
+pub(super) struct KeyPage {
+    pub keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
+    pub count: u64,
+    /// The token the next page starts at, or `None` at the end of the ring.
+    pub next: Option<u64>,
+}
+
+impl NodeState {
+    /// One page of the live keys `node_id` owns in this state's topology, from
+    /// token `start` on, in token order. Deleted records and records past
+    /// their deadline are not keys.
+    pub(super) fn owned_keys_page(
+        &self,
+        node_id: &str,
+        start: u64,
+        now_unix_millis: u64,
+        limits: &PageLimits,
+    ) -> KeyPage {
+        let assignments = &self.topology.assignments;
+        let mut page = KeyPage::default();
+        if assignments.is_empty() {
+            return page;
+        }
+        let mut examined = 0;
+        let mut bytes = 0;
+        let mut position = start;
+        loop {
+            let index = assignments.partition_point(|assignment| assignment.token < position);
+            let (segment_end, owner) = match assignments.get(index) {
+                Some(assignment) => (assignment.token, &assignment.node_id),
+                None => (u64::MAX, &assignments[0].node_id),
+            };
+            examined += 1;
+            if owner != node_id && limits.one_stretch {
+                page.next = Some(position);

+                    // always ends on a token boundary. The first token is
+                    // always taken, which is what keeps every page moving.
+                    if examined >= limits.max_examined
+                        || page.count as usize >= limits.max_keys
+                        || bytes >= limits.max_bytes

+            if examined >= limits.max_examined {
+                page.next = Some(position);

+            }
+        }
+    }

+    fn values(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &T> {
+        let (one, many) = match self {
+            TokenBucket::One(value) => (Some(value), None),
+            TokenBucket::Many(values) => (None, Some(values)),
+        };
+        one.into_iter().chain(many.into_iter().flatten())

+/// Keys or mutation IDs ordered by ring token.

+/// on a 64-bit token, and dropping one would silently lose a record. Records
+/// almost never collide, so a bucket is usually `One` and costs no allocation

+#[derive(Debug)]

+    by_token: std::collections::BTreeMap<u64, TokenBucket<T>>,

+#[derive(Debug)]

+    One(T),
+    Many(std::collections::BTreeSet<T>),
+}
+
+impl<T> Default for TokenIndex<T> {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            by_token: std::collections::BTreeMap::new(),
+        }
+    }
+}

+impl<T: Ord + Clone> TokenIndex<T> {
+    fn insert(&mut self, token: u64, value: T) {
+        use std::collections::btree_map::Entry;
+        match self.by_token.entry(token) {
+            Entry::Vacant(entry) => {
+                entry.insert(TokenBucket::One(value));
+            }
+            Entry::Occupied(mut entry) => {
+                let bucket = entry.get_mut();
+                match bucket {
+                    TokenBucket::One(existing) if *existing == value => {}
+                    TokenBucket::One(existing) => {
+                        *bucket = TokenBucket::Many([existing.clone(), value].into());
+                    }
+                    TokenBucket::Many(values) => {
+                        values.insert(value);
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }

+    /// Removes `value` from `token`'s bucket. Takes any borrowed form, so a
+    /// caller holding `&[u8]` or `&str` need not build an `Arc` to compare.
+    fn remove<Q>(&mut self, token: u64, value: &Q) -> bool
+    where
+        T: std::borrow::Borrow<Q>,
+        Q: Ord + ?Sized,
+    {
+        let Some(bucket) = self.by_token.get_mut(&token) else {
+            return false;
+        };
+        let emptied = match bucket {
+            TokenBucket::One(existing) if existing.borrow() == value => true,
+            TokenBucket::One(_) => return false,
+            TokenBucket::Many(values) => {
+                if !values.remove(value) {
+                    return false;
+                }
+                values.is_empty()
+            }
+        };
+        if emptied {
+            self.by_token.remove(&token);
+        }
+        true
+    }
+
+    /// How many values share `token`.
+    fn len_at(&self, token: u64) -> usize {
+        match self.by_token.get(&token) {
+            None => 0,
+            Some(TokenBucket::One(_)) => 1,
+            Some(TokenBucket::Many(values)) => values.len(),
+        }
+    }
+
+    #[cfg(test)]
+    fn len(&self) -> usize {
+        self.by_token
+            .values()
+            .map(|bucket| match bucket {
+                TokenBucket::One(_) => 1,
+                TokenBucket::Many(values) => values.len(),
+            })
+            .sum()
+    }
+
+    #[cfg(test)]
+    fn contains<Q>(&self, token: u64, value: &Q) -> bool
+    where
+        T: std::borrow::Borrow<Q>,
+        Q: Ord + ?Sized,
+    {
+        match self.by_token.get(&token) {
+            Some(TokenBucket::One(existing)) => existing.borrow() == value,
+            Some(TokenBucket::Many(values)) => values.contains(value),
+            None => false,
+        }
+    }

+    /// order. Equivalent to testing `range.contains` on every value, without
+    /// the hashing.
+    fn in_range(&self, range: &RangeSpec) -> Vec<(u64, T)> {
+        let mut found = Vec::new();

+            for (&token, bucket) in self.by_token.range(bounds) {

+                    }

+    /// `(start_exclusive, end_inclusive]`. The start token belongs to the
+    /// previous range, so excluding it keeps a boundary key in exactly one
+    /// range.
+    fn token_bounds(&self) -> Vec<(std::ops::Bound<&u64>, std::ops::Bound<&u64>)> {
+        use std::ops::Bound;
+        let start = Bound::Excluded(&self.start_exclusive);
+        let end = Bound::Included(&self.end_inclusive);
+        match self.start_exclusive.cmp(&self.end_inclusive) {
+            // A wrapping range crosses the end of the token space, so it is
+            // `[0, end]` plus `(start, MAX]`.
+            Ordering::Greater => vec![(Bound::Unbounded, end), (start, Bound::Unbounded)],
+            // An empty range would be `(Excluded(x), Included(x))`, which matches
+            // nothing; `contains` treats start == end as covering everything.
+            Ordering::Equal => vec![(Bound::Unbounded, Bound::Unbounded)],
+            Ordering::Less => vec![(start, end)],
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn key(&self) -> (String, String) {
+        (self.change_id.clone(), self.range_id.clone())
+    }
+}
+
+impl TryFrom<proto::RangeSpec> for RangeSpec {
+    type Error = Status;
+
+    fn try_from(range: proto::RangeSpec) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
+        if range.change_id.is_empty()
+            || range.range_id.is_empty()
+            || range.source_node_id.is_empty()
+            || range.destination_node_id.is_empty()
+        {
+            return Err(Status::invalid_argument(
+                "range identifiers and node identifiers must not be empty",
+            ));
+        }
+        Ok(Self {
+            change_id: range.change_id,
+            range_id: range.range_id,
+            start_exclusive: range.start_exclusive,
+            end_inclusive: range.end_inclusive,
+            source_node_id: range.source_node_id,
+            destination_node_id: range.destination_node_id,
+        })
+    }
+}

+    /// and the snapshot's hash seed, so this index stays correct across epochs,
+    /// members and virtual-node changes; only a reseed rebuilds it (see
+    /// `set_topology`).

+    /// `(deadline, key)` for every record in `records` that has a deadline
+    /// and is not deferred by a source migration
+    /// (`SourceMigration::deferred_expirations`), ordered by deadline. Reads hide an
+    /// expired record, so this exists only to find those records again without
+    /// scanning every key. A write replaces its key's entry rather than adding
+    /// one, so the index holds one entry per expiring record, however often
+    /// the record is rewritten.

+    /// receipt's key. Holds the same invariant as `records_by_token`.
+    dedup_by_token: TokenIndex<Arc<str>>,
+    dedup_expirations: BinaryHeap<Reverse<(Instant, Arc<str>)>>,

+/// Every mutation of `records` and `dedup` goes through these, so the token
+/// indices cannot drift from the maps they mirror. Reaching into either map
+/// directly is the one way to break that, which is what the tests'
+/// `debug_assert_index` checks.
+impl NodeState {
+    fn token_of(&self, key: &[u8]) -> u64 {
+        self.topology.key_token(key)
+    }
+
+    /// Swaps in a new topology snapshot. The token indices are keyed by
+    /// `TopologySnapshot::key_token`, a function of the key bytes and the hash
+    /// seed. The coordinator reuses the committed seed for every target
+    /// topology (see `hashring_core::migration`), but a recreated coordinator
+    /// picks a fresh one, so a reseed rebuilds both indices rather than leaving
+    /// range queries answering from stale positions.
+    fn set_topology(&mut self, topology: TopologySnapshot) {
+        let reseeded = topology.hash_seed != self.topology.hash_seed;
+        self.topology = topology;
+        if !reseeded {
+            return;
+        }
+        let mut records_by_token = TokenIndex::default();
+        for key in self.records.keys() {
+            records_by_token.insert(self.topology.key_token(key), key.clone());
+        }
+        let mut dedup_by_token = TokenIndex::default();
+        for (id, entry) in &self.dedup {
+            dedup_by_token.insert(self.topology.key_token(&entry.key), id.clone());
+        }
+        self.records_by_token = records_by_token;
+        self.dedup_by_token = dedup_by_token;
+    }
+
+    /// Hashes the key itself rather than trusting a caller's token: a write
+    /// computes its routing token before the write lock, and a reseed in
+    /// between would index the key where no range query looks for it.
+    fn insert_record(&mut self, key: Arc<[u8]>, record: Record) {
+        let deadline = record.expires_at_unix_millis;
+        // Replacing an existing key keeps the map's original `Arc`, which the
+        // token index and the expiry index already hold, so only a new key is
+        // indexed. Indexing the new `Arc` instead would leave the map and the
+        // indices with separate copies.
+        let key = match self.records.get_key_value(&key) {
+            Some((existing, _)) => existing.clone(),
+            None => {
+                let token = self.token_of(&key);
+                self.records_by_token.insert(token, key.clone());
+                key
+            }
+        };
+        if let Some(replaced) = self.records.insert(key.clone(), record) {
+            self.forget_expiration(&key, replaced.expires_at_unix_millis);
+        }
+        if let Some(deadline) = deadline {
+            self.record_expirations.insert((deadline, key));
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Drops the expiry entry a record that is being replaced or removed was
+    /// scheduled under, wherever it is waiting.
+    fn forget_expiration(&mut self, key: &Arc<[u8]>, deadline: Option<u64>) {
+        if let Some(deadline) = deadline {
+            let entry = (deadline, key.clone());
+            if !self.record_expirations.remove(&entry) {
+                for source in self.sources.values_mut() {
+                    if source.deferred_expirations.remove(&entry) {
+                        break;
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Applies a record only when it is newer than the stored one, matching
+    /// [`apply_internal_record`]'s version rule.
+    fn apply_record(&mut self, key: Arc<[u8]>, record: Record) -> bool {
+        if self.records.get(&key).is_some_and(|current| {
+            crate::migration::compare_versions(&record.version, &current.version).is_le()
+        }) {
+            return false;
+        }
+        self.insert_record(key, record);
+        true
+    }
+
+    #[cfg(test)]
+    fn remove_record(&mut self, key: &[u8]) -> Option<Record> {
+        let token = self.token_of(key);
+        self.remove_record_at(token, key)
+    }
+
+    /// [`remove_record`] for a caller that already has the key's token from
+    /// [`record_keys_in_range`] under the same lock, so it matches the index.
+    fn remove_record_at(&mut self, token: u64, key: &[u8]) -> Option<Record> {
+        let (key, removed) = self.records.remove_entry(key)?;
+        let indexed = self.records_by_token.remove(token, &key);
+        debug_assert!(indexed, "removed record was missing from the index");
+        self.forget_expiration(&key, removed.expires_at_unix_millis);
+        Some(removed)
+    }
+
+    /// Ends a source migration, the only way one leaves `sources`, and hands
+    /// the expired records it was holding back to the sweep: only this range's,
+    /// so the work is proportional to the range rather than the node. Another
+    /// active source still covering one defers it again on the next pass.
+    fn remove_source(&mut self, key: &(String, String)) -> Option<SourceMigration> {
+        let mut source = self.sources.remove(key)?;
+        self.journal_bytes_total = self
+            .journal_bytes_total
+            .saturating_sub(source.journal_bytes);
+        // One insertion per released entry: `BTreeSet::append` would merge
+        // through the entries already in the index, which can be the whole
+        // node's backlog.
+        for entry in std::mem::take(&mut source.deferred_expirations) {
+            self.record_expirations.insert(entry);
+        }
+        Some(source)
+    }
+
+    /// Every record key in `range` with its token, in token order.
+    fn record_keys_in_range(&self, range: &RangeSpec) -> Vec<(u64, Arc<[u8]>)> {
+        self.records_by_token.in_range(range)
+    }
+
+    /// Every live receipt id whose key falls in `range`, in token order.
+    fn dedup_ids_in_range(&self, range: &RangeSpec) -> Vec<Arc<str>> {
+        self.dedup_by_token
+            .in_range(range)
+            .into_iter()
+            .map(|(_, id)| id)
+            .collect()
+    }
+
+    /// Test-only reset. The indices cannot be cleared through `records.clear`,
+    /// so the whole reset lives here where the invariant is kept in one place.
+    #[cfg(test)]
+    fn clear_records(&mut self) {
+        self.records.clear();
+        self.records_by_token = TokenIndex::default();
+        self.record_expirations.clear();
+        for source in self.sources.values_mut() {
+            source.deferred_expirations.clear();
+        }
+    }
+
+    #[cfg(test)]
+    fn clear_dedup(&mut self) {
+        self.dedup.clear();
+        self.dedup_by_token = TokenIndex::default();
+    }
+
+    fn insert_dedup_index(&mut self, id: &Arc<str>, key: &[u8]) {
+        let token = self.token_of(key);
+        self.dedup_by_token.insert(token, id.clone());
+    }
+
+    fn remove_dedup_index(&mut self, id: &Arc<str>, key: &[u8]) {
+        let token = self.token_of(key);
+        let removed = self.dedup_by_token.remove(token, &**id);
+        debug_assert!(removed, "removed receipt was missing from the index");
+    }
+
+    /// The indices are load-bearing for migration correctness, so tests check
+    /// them against the maps. Test-only: it rehashes every key on the node, so
+    /// running it under the write lock would bring back the full scan the
+    /// indices exist to avoid.
+    #[cfg(test)]
+    fn debug_assert_index(&self) {
+        debug_assert_eq!(
+            self.records_by_token.len(),
+            self.records.len(),
+            "records and records_by_token disagree",
+        );
+        debug_assert_eq!(
+            self.dedup_by_token.len(),
+            self.dedup.len(),
+            "dedup and dedup_by_token disagree",
+        );
+        for (key, record) in &self.records {
+            debug_assert!(
+                self.records_by_token.contains(self.token_of(key), key),
+                "record is missing from records_by_token",
+            );
+            if let Some(deadline) = record.expires_at_unix_millis {
+                let entry = (deadline, key.clone());
+                let deferred = self
+                    .sources
+                    .values()
+                    .filter(|source| source.deferred_expirations.contains(&entry))
+                    .count();
+                debug_assert_eq!(
+                    usize::from(self.record_expirations.contains(&entry)) + deferred,
+                    1,
+                    "an expiring record is not scheduled exactly once",
+                );
+            }
+        }
+        let deferred: usize = self
+            .sources
+            .values()
+            .map(|source| source.deferred_expirations.len())
+            .sum();
+        debug_assert_eq!(
+            self.record_expirations.len() + deferred,
+            self.records
+                .values()
+                .filter(|record| record.expires_at_unix_millis.is_some())
+                .count(),
+            "the expiry index holds entries for records that are gone",
+        );
+        for (id, entry) in &self.dedup {
+            debug_assert!(
+                self.dedup_by_token.contains(self.token_of(&entry.key), id),
+                "receipt is missing from dedup_by_token",
+            );
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// Per-node resource budgets and timeouts. Nodes in one cluster may use
+/// different values; none of them affects correctness, only when a node
+/// rejects or gives up on work.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
+pub struct NodeSettings {
+    /// Retained deduplication receipts, and separately each migration
+    /// destination's staged receipts.
+    pub max_dedup_bytes: usize,
+    /// The largest value this node accepts. It must fit a replication batch
+    /// and a journaled write, so the two budgets below may not be smaller.
+    pub max_value_bytes: usize,
+    /// Mutations queued for followers, and separately the payload copies held
+    /// by in-flight replication RPCs.
+    pub max_pending_replication_bytes: usize,
+    /// Writes journaled across this node's active migrations.
+    pub max_migration_journal_bytes: usize,
+    /// Mutations queued per follower stream, regardless of their size.
+    pub replication_stream_queue_capacity: usize,
+    /// How long a write waits for its required follower ACKs.
+    pub required_ack_timeout: std::time::Duration,
+    /// Bounds each replication connect and batch RPC.
+    pub replication_rpc_timeout: std::time::Duration,
+    /// How long a follower stream waits for more entries before sending a
+    /// batch that no write is waiting on. Zero sends at once.
+    pub replication_batch_linger: std::time::Duration,
+}
+
+impl Default for NodeSettings {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            max_dedup_bytes: DEFAULT_MAX_DEDUP_BYTES,
+            max_value_bytes: DEFAULT_MAX_VALUE_BYTES,
+            max_pending_replication_bytes: DEFAULT_MAX_PENDING_REPLICATION_BYTES,
+            max_migration_journal_bytes: DEFAULT_MAX_MIGRATION_JOURNAL_BYTES,
+            replication_stream_queue_capacity: DEFAULT_REPLICATION_STREAM_QUEUE_CAPACITY,
+            required_ack_timeout: DEFAULT_REQUIRED_ACK_TIMEOUT,
+            replication_rpc_timeout: DEFAULT_REPLICATION_RPC_TIMEOUT,
+            replication_batch_linger: DEFAULT_REPLICATION_BATCH_LINGER,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+impl NodeSettings {
+    pub fn validate(&self) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
+        anyhow::ensure!(self.max_dedup_bytes > 0, "max_dedup_bytes must be positive");
+        anyhow::ensure!(
+            self.max_value_bytes > 0 && self.max_value_bytes <= MAX_VALUE_BYTES,
+            "max_value_bytes must be positive and at most {}",
+            MAX_VALUE_BYTES
+        );
+        anyhow::ensure!(
+            self.max_pending_replication_bytes > 0
+                && self.max_pending_replication_bytes <= Semaphore::MAX_PERMITS,
+            "max_pending_replication_bytes must be positive and at most {}",
+            Semaphore::MAX_PERMITS
+        );
+        anyhow::ensure!(
+            self.max_pending_replication_bytes >= self.max_value_bytes,
+            "max_pending_replication_bytes ({}) must be at least max_value_bytes ({}), or a \
+             value that size never fits a replication batch",
+            self.max_pending_replication_bytes,
+            self.max_value_bytes
+        );
+        anyhow::ensure!(
+            self.max_migration_journal_bytes > 0,
+            "max_migration_journal_bytes must be positive"
+        );
+        anyhow::ensure!(
+            self.max_migration_journal_bytes >= self.max_value_bytes,
+            "max_migration_journal_bytes ({}) must be at least max_value_bytes ({}), or a \
+             value that size is rejected while a range is moving",
+            self.max_migration_journal_bytes,
+            self.max_value_bytes
+        );
+        anyhow::ensure!(
+            self.replication_stream_queue_capacity > 0,
+            "replication_stream_queue_capacity must be positive"
+        );
+        anyhow::ensure!(
+            !self.required_ack_timeout.is_zero() && !self.replication_rpc_timeout.is_zero(),
+            "timeouts must be positive"
+        );
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}

+fn peer_probe_targets(
+    topology: &TopologySnapshot,
+    node_id: &str,
+) -> Vec<hashring_core::topology::Member> {
+    let Some(index) = topology
+        .members
+        .iter()
+        .position(|member| member.node_id == node_id)
+    else {
+        return Vec::new();
+    };
+    let count = topology.members.len();
+    let mut targets = Vec::new();
+    // Four stable reporters per physical node give each reachable reporter a
+    // one-second cadence independent of cluster size. With three nodes, both
+    // peers report; one broken link alone can never confirm a failure.
+    for offset in [1, 2, count.saturating_sub(1), count.saturating_sub(2)] {
+        let member = &topology.members[(index + offset) % count];
+        if member.node_id != node_id
+            && !targets
+                .iter()
+                .any(|existing: &hashring_core::topology::Member| {
+                    existing.node_id == member.node_id
+                })
+        {
+            targets.push(member.clone());
+        }
+    }
+    targets
+}

+fn clear_replica_repair_staging(state: &mut NodeState) {
+    let keys: Vec<_> = state
+        .sources
+        .keys()
+        .filter(|(change_id, _)| change_id.starts_with("repair-"))
+        .cloned()
+        .collect();
+    for key in keys {
+        state.remove_source(&key);
+    }
+    state
+        .destinations
+        .retain(|(change_id, _), _| !change_id.starts_with("repair-"));
+}

+        unknown_write_outcome: true,
+        ..operation_error(
+            ErrorCode::OutcomeUnknown,
+            "required replica acknowledgement is uncertain",
+            true,
+        )
+    }

+fn range_contains(start: u64, end: u64, token: u64) -> bool {
+    if start < end {
+        token > start && token <= end
+    } else if start > end {
+        token > start || token <= end
+    } else {
+        true
+    }
+}

+impl DataNodeService {
+    fn validate_stop_request(&self, request: &StopRequest) -> Result<(), Status> {
+        if request.node_id != self.node_id
+            || request.process_instance_id != self.process_instance_id
+        {
+            return Err(Status::failed_precondition(
+                "stop request does not match this node process instance",
+            ));
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}
+
+fn operation_error(code: ErrorCode, message: impl Into<String>, retryable: bool) -> OperationError {
+    OperationError {
+        code: code.into(),
+        message: message.into(),
+        retryable,
+        ..Default::default()
+    }
+}
+
+async fn fetch_pending_topology(endpoint: &str) -> anyhow::Result<Option<TopologySnapshot>> {
+    let mut client =
+        configure_coordinator_client(CoordinatorClient::connect(endpoint.to_owned()).await?);
+    let response = client
+        .get_topology_change(proto::Empty {})
+        .await?
+        .into_inner();
+    response
+        .change
+        .filter(|change| {
+            !matches!(
+                proto::MigrationPhase::try_from(change.phase),
+                Ok(proto::MigrationPhase::Complete | proto::MigrationPhase::Aborted)
+            )
+        })
+        .and_then(|change| change.target_topology)
+        .map(TryInto::try_into)
+        .transpose()
+        .map_err(Into::into)
+}
+
+async fn register_node(
+    endpoint: &str,
+    node_id: String,
+    process_instance_id: String,
+) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
+    let mut client =
+        configure_coordinator_client(CoordinatorClient::connect(endpoint.to_owned()).await?);
+    client
+        .register_node(RegisterNodeRequest {
+            node_id,
+            process_instance_id,
+        })
+        .await?;
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+async fn wait_for_durable_stop_confirmation(
+    coordinator_endpoint: String,
+    node_id: String,
+    process_instance_id: String,
+    shutdown: watch::Sender<bool>,
+) {
+    loop {
+        let confirmed = match CoordinatorClient::connect(coordinator_endpoint.clone()).await {
+            Ok(client) => {
+                let mut client = configure_coordinator_client(client);
+                client
+                    .is_stop_confirmed(StopRequest {
+                        node_id: node_id.clone(),
+                        process_instance_id: process_instance_id.clone(),
+                    })
+                    .await
+                    .ok()
+                    .is_some_and(|response| response.into_inner().confirmed)
+            }
+            Err(_) => false,
+        };
+        if confirmed {
+            // Give the coordinator time to issue the final Stop RPC. If its
+            // acknowledgement is lost, this durable-confirmation fallback
+            // still terminates the exact prepared process instance.
+            tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)).await;
+            let _ = shutdown.send(true);
+            return;
+        }
+        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
+    }
+}

+pub(super) fn page_limit(requested: u64, max_value_bytes: usize) -> usize {
+    // Never smaller than one of this node's own largest values, which is the
+    // smallest page that can carry a record it holds; the ceiling is what the

+pub(super) fn migration_record_size(record: &MigrationRecord) -> usize {
+    record.key.len() + record.value.len() + record.mutation_id.len() + 128

+pub(super) fn apply_record(
+    records: &mut HashMap<Vec<u8>, Record>,
+    record: MigrationRecord,

+    let version = record
+        .version
+        .ok_or_else(|| Status::invalid_argument("migration record omitted version"))?;
+    if record.deleted && !record.value.is_empty() {
+        return Err(Status::invalid_argument(
+            "deleted migration record must omit its value",
+        ));
+    }
+    apply_internal_record(
+        records,
+        record.key,
+        Record {
+            value: record.value.into(),
+            version,
+            deleted: record.deleted,
+            expires_at_unix_millis: stored_deadline(record.expires_at_unix_millis),

+pub(super) fn apply_internal_record(
+    records: &mut HashMap<Vec<u8>, Record>,
+    key: Vec<u8>,
+    record: Record,
+) {

+        .get(&key)
+        .is_none_or(|current| compare_versions(&record.version, &current.version).is_gt())
+    {
+        records.insert(key, record);
+    }

+
+pub(super) fn compare_versions(left: &RecordVersion, right: &RecordVersion) -> Ordering {
+    (
+        left.topology_epoch,
+        left.owner_sequence,
+        &left.owner_node_id,
+    )
+        .cmp(&(
+            right.topology_epoch,
+            right.owner_sequence,
+            &right.owner_node_id,
+        ))
+}

+/// Sorts `(token, key, _)` entries into the order [`range_digest`] requires.
+///
+/// The key comparison runs only when two tokens are equal, which for distinct
+/// keys means a 64-bit hash collision, so the sort still compares integers.
+pub(super) fn sort_into_token_order<T>(entries: &mut [(u64, &[u8], T)]) {
+    entries.sort_unstable_by(|(left_token, left_key, _), (right_token, right_key, _)| {
+        left_token
+            .cmp(right_token)
+            .then_with(|| left_key.cmp(right_key))
+    });

+
+/// Digest of one range's records, taken in the order the caller supplies.
+///
+/// The caller must supply **token order, ties broken by key bytes**, and that
+/// is part of this function's contract rather than an implementation detail:
+/// `RangeDigestResponse` is compared between a source and a destination, so
+/// both sides have to agree on the byte stream. Token order is the one ordering
+/// both sides can produce without re-sorting keys, because a token depends only
+/// on the key bytes and the committed seed, which the two nodes share. The tie
+/// break is what the source's `TokenIndex` yields for keys whose tokens
+/// collide, and [`sort_into_token_order`] reproduces it on the destination.
+///
+/// The previous version took a `HashMap`, sorted it by key bytes, and hashed
+/// the result. Two costs are gone now. `source_range_digest` no longer builds a
+/// `HashMap` of cloned keys and records just to iterate it, and neither side
+/// sorts byte slices. In a 1,000,000-key migration that sort and clone were the
+/// two largest items under `source_range_digest` and
+/// `destination_range_digest` (21.3% and 8.2% of the migration phase in
+/// results/flamegraph-correctness-20261015-005607).
+///
+/// The digest bytes differ from v2 because the order differs, so the domain
+/// separator is bumped: a digest from a node running the old code must never be
+/// compared against one from a node running this.
+///
+/// Records now carry an expiry, so the digest covers it as well: a source and a
+/// destination that disagreed about a deadline would hand over keys that stop
+/// being readable at different times. The digest bytes change again, hence the
+/// new domain separator.
+pub(super) fn range_digest<'a>(
+    records: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'a [u8], &'a Record)>,
+    watermark: u64,
+) -> RangeDigestResponse {
+    let mut digest = blake3::Hasher::new();
+    digest.update(b"hashring-rs:records:v4\0");
+    let mut count = 0u64;
+    for (key, record) in records {
+        count += 1;
+        digest.update(&(key.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
+        digest.update(key);
+        digest.update(&record.version.topology_epoch.to_be_bytes());
+        digest.update(&record.version.owner_sequence.to_be_bytes());
+        digest.update(&(record.version.owner_node_id.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
+        digest.update(record.version.owner_node_id.as_bytes());
+        digest.update(&(record.value.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
+        digest.update(record.value.as_ref());
+        digest.update(&[u8::from(record.deleted)]);
+        match record.expires_at_unix_millis {
+            Some(expires_at) => {
+                digest.update(&[1]);
+                let deadline = expires_at.to_be_bytes();
+                digest.update(&deadline);
+            }
+            None => {
+                digest.update(&[0]);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    RangeDigestResponse {
+        record_count: count,
+        digest: digest.finalize().to_hex().to_string(),
+        changelog_watermark: watermark,
+    }
+}

+    topology: &TopologySnapshot,
+    token: u64,
+    status: Option<&proto::ReplicaStatusResponse>,
