+    async fn apply_migration_batch(
+        &self,
+        request: Request<ApplyMigrationBatchRequest>,
+    ) -> Result<Response<proto::Empty>, Status> {
+        let request = request.into_inner();
+        let mut state = self.state.write().await;
+        let topology = state.topology.clone();
+        let destination = state
+            .destinations
+            .get_mut(&(request.change_id, request.range_id))
+            .ok_or_else(|| Status::not_found("destination migration not prepared"))?;
+        if destination.committed {
+            return Err(Status::failed_precondition(
+                "destination range is already committed",
+            ));
+        }
+        purge_staged_dedup(destination, Instant::now());
+        for record in request.snapshot_records {
+            if !destination.range.contains(topology.key_token(&record.key)) {
+                return Err(Status::invalid_argument(
+                    "snapshot record is outside the prepared range",
+                ));
+            }
+            apply_record(&mut destination.records, record)?;
+        }
+        for entry in request.journal_records {
+            if entry.watermark <= destination.watermark {
+                continue;
+            }
+            if entry.watermark != destination.watermark + 1 {
+                return Err(Status::failed_precondition(format!(
+                    "non-contiguous changelog: expected {}, received {}",
+                    destination.watermark + 1,
+                    entry.watermark
+                )));
+            }
+            let record = entry
+                .record
+                .ok_or_else(|| Status::invalid_argument("journal entry omitted record"))?;
+            if !destination.range.contains(topology.key_token(&record.key)) {
+                return Err(Status::invalid_argument(
+                    "journal record is outside the prepared range",
+                ));
+            }
+            if !record.mutation_id.is_empty() {
+                let dedup = DeduplicationRecord {
+                    mutation_id: record.mutation_id.clone(),
+                    key: record.key.clone(),
+                    fingerprint: record.request_fingerprint.clone(),
+                    version: record.version.clone(),
+                    deleted: record.deleted,
+                    remaining_retention_millis: record.remaining_retention_millis,
+                };
+                stage_dedup(
+                    destination,
+                    dedup,
+                    self.max_dedup_bytes,
+                    topology.timings.receipt_retention_millis,
+                )?;
+            }
+            apply_record(&mut destination.records, record)?;
+            destination.watermark = entry.watermark;
+        }
+        Ok(Response::new(proto::Empty {}))
+    }

+    async fn source_range_digest(
+        &self,
+        request: Request<RangeControlRequest>,
+    ) -> Result<Response<RangeDigestResponse>, Status> {
+        let request = request.into_inner();
+        let state = self.state.read().await;
+        let (range, watermark) = {
+            let source = state
+                .sources
+                .get(&(request.change_id, request.range_id))
+                .ok_or_else(|| Status::not_found("source migration not prepared"))?;
+            (source.range.clone(), source.watermark)
+        };
+        // `record_keys_in_range` is already in token order, which is the order
+        // `range_digest` requires, so no sort is needed. Only handles are taken
+        // under the read lock -- each key's `Arc` and a record whose value is an
+        // `Arc` too -- and the hashing, which reads every value byte, runs after
+        // the lock is released. Hashing under the lock stalled writers to every
+        // range on this node for time proportional to the range's bytes.
+        let in_token_order: Vec<_> = state
+            .record_keys_in_range(&range)
+            .into_iter()
+            .filter_map(|(_, key)| {
+                let record = state.records.get(&key)?.clone();
+                Some((key, record))
+            })
+            .collect();
+        drop(state);
+        let response = range_digest(
+            in_token_order
+                .iter()
+                .map(|(key, record)| (key.as_ref(), record)),
+            watermark,
+        );
+        Ok(Response::new(response))
+    }
+
+    async fn destination_range_digest(
+        &self,
+        request: Request<RangeControlRequest>,
+    ) -> Result<Response<RangeDigestResponse>, Status> {
+        let request = request.into_inner();
+        let state = self.state.read().await;
+        let destination = state
+            .destinations
+            .get(&(request.change_id, request.range_id))
+            .ok_or_else(|| Status::not_found("destination migration not prepared"))?;
+        let watermark = destination.watermark;
+        // `DestinationMigration::records` is a plain map, so token order has to
+        // be established here rather than read off an index. The read lock is
+        // held only to copy the records out; tokens, the sort and the hash all
+        // run after it is released, so writers to other ranges wait for the
+        // copy and not for a pass over every value byte. Sorting by the u64
+        // token still compares integers where the old path compared key bytes.
+        let hash_seed = state.topology.hash_seed;
+        let records: Vec<_> = destination
+            .records
+            .iter()
+            .map(|(key, record)| (key.clone(), record.clone()))
+            .collect();
+        drop(state);
+        let mut by_token: Vec<_> = records
+            .iter()
+            .map(|(key, record)| (key_token(key, hash_seed), key.as_slice(), record))
+            .collect();
+        sort_into_token_order(&mut by_token);
+        let response = range_digest(
+            by_token.iter().map(|(_, key, record)| (*key, *record)),
+            watermark,
+        );
+        Ok(Response::new(response))
+    }

+    async fn commit_destination_range(
+        &self,
+        request: Request<RangeControlRequest>,
+    ) -> Result<Response<proto::Empty>, Status> {
+        let request = request.into_inner();
+        let mut state = self.state.write().await;
+        let key = (request.change_id, request.range_id);
+        let (range, records, dedup) = {
+            let destination = state
+                .destinations
+                .get(&key)
+                .ok_or_else(|| Status::not_found("destination migration not prepared"))?;
+            if destination.committed {
+                return Ok(Response::new(proto::Empty {}));
+            }
+            (
+                destination.range.clone(),
+                destination.records.clone(),
+                destination
+                    .dedup
+                    .iter()
+                    .filter(|(_, entry)| entry.expires_at > Instant::now())
+                    .map(|(id, entry)| (id.clone(), entry.clone()))
+                    .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>(),
+            )
+        };
+        purge_expired_dedup(&mut state, Instant::now());
+        let mut added_bytes = 0usize;
+        for staged in dedup.values() {
+            let record = &staged.record;
+            if let Some(existing) = state.dedup.get(record.mutation_id.as_str()) {
+                if existing.fingerprint.as_slice() != record.fingerprint
+                    || Some(&existing.version) != record.version.as_ref()
+                    || existing.deleted != record.deleted
+                {
+                    return Err(Status::failed_precondition(
+                        "destination mutation ID conflicts with existing deduplication receipt",
+                    ));
+                }
+            } else {
+                let version = record
+                    .version
+                    .as_ref()
+                    .expect("staged dedup version was validated");
+                added_bytes = added_bytes.saturating_add(dedup_retained_bytes(
+                    &record.mutation_id,
+                    record.key.len(),
+                    version.owner_node_id.len(),
+                ));
+            }
+        }
+        if state.dedup_bytes.saturating_add(added_bytes) > self.max_dedup_bytes {
+            return Err(Status::resource_exhausted(
+                "destination deduplication receipt store is full",
+            ));
+        }
+        // Only the range's own records leave this node, taken from the token
+        // index. The previous `records.retain` hashed every key on the node while
+        // holding this write lock.
+        for (token, record_key) in state.record_keys_in_range(&range) {
+            state.remove_record_at(token, &record_key);
+        }
+        for (key, record) in records {
+            state.apply_record(Arc::from(key.as_slice()), record);
+        }
+        for (id, staged) in dedup {
+            if state.dedup.contains_key(id.as_str()) {
+                continue;
+            }
+            let record = staged.record;
+            insert_dedup_until(
+                &mut state,
+                id,
+                Arc::from(record.key),
+                record
+                    .fingerprint
+                    .try_into()
+                    .expect("staged fingerprint was validated"),
+                record.version.expect("staged version was validated"),
+                record.deleted,
+                staged.expires_at,
+            );
+        }
+        state
+            .destinations
+            .get_mut(&key)
+            .expect("destination was checked above")
+            .committed = true;
+        Ok(Response::new(proto::Empty {}))
+    }
+

+    async fn cleanup_source_range(
+        &self,
+        request: Request<RangeControlRequest>,
+    ) -> Result<Response<proto::Empty>, Status> {
+        let request = request.into_inner();
+        let mut state = self.state.write().await;
+        let key = (request.change_id, request.range_id);
+        let Some(range) = state.sources.get(&key).map(|source| source.range.clone()) else {
+            return Ok(Response::new(proto::Empty {}));
+        };
+        // The replica check now runs on the range's keys instead of on every
+        // key this node holds.
+        let keys: Vec<_> = state
+            .record_keys_in_range(&range)
+            .into_iter()
+            .filter(|(token, _)| {
+                state
+                    .topology
+                    .replica_node_ids_for_token(*token)
+                    .is_ok_and(|replicas| !replicas.contains(&self.node_id.as_str()))
+            })
+            .collect();
+        for (token, record_key) in keys {
+            state.remove_record_at(token, &record_key);
+        }
+        state.remove_source(&key);
+        Ok(Response::new(proto::Empty {}))
+    }

+    async fn install_topology(
+        &self,
+        request: Request<InstallTopologyRequest>,
+    ) -> Result<Response<proto::Empty>, Status> {
+        let request = request.into_inner();
+        let topology: TopologySnapshot = request
+            .topology
+            .ok_or_else(|| Status::invalid_argument("missing topology"))?
+            .try_into()
+            .map_err(|error: hashring_core::topology::TopologyError| {
+                Status::invalid_argument(error.to_string())
+            })?;
+        let mut state = self.state.write().await;
+        if topology.epoch < state.topology.epoch {
+            return Err(Status::failed_precondition(
+                "cannot install an older topology",
+            ));
+        }
+        let epoch = topology.epoch;
+        if epoch != state.topology.epoch {
+            state.lease = None;
+            state.admitted_followers.clear();
+            clear_replica_repair_staging(&mut state);
+        }
+        state.set_topology(topology);
+        state
+            .owner_stream_sequences
+            .retain(|(stream_epoch, _), _| *stream_epoch == epoch);
+        state
+            .owner_stream_unacked
+            .retain(|(stream_epoch, _), _| *stream_epoch == epoch);
+        state
+            .follower_streams
+            .retain(|(stream_epoch, _), _| *stream_epoch == epoch);
+        prune_ack_progress(&mut state);
+        self.replication_dispatch.prune_epoch(epoch);
+        drop(state);
+        if request.require_lease
+            && self
+                .state
+                .read()
+                .await
+                .topology
+                .members
+                .iter()
+                .any(|member| member.node_id == self.node_id)
+        {

+                Status::unavailable(format!("new-epoch lease is unavailable: {error}"))

+    async fn pause_policy_writes(
+        &self,
+        request: Request<PolicyWriteFenceRequest>,
+    ) -> Result<Response<proto::Empty>, Status> {
+        let request = request.into_inner();
+        if request.change_id.is_empty() {
+            return Err(Status::invalid_argument("policy change ID is empty"));
+        }
+        let mut state = self.state.write().await;
+        if state.topology.epoch != request.base_epoch {
+            return Err(Status::failed_precondition(
+                "policy fence base epoch does not match installed topology",
+            ));
+        }
+        match &state.policy_write_fence {
+            Some((change_id, epoch))
+                if change_id != &request.change_id || *epoch != request.base_epoch =>
+            {
+                return Err(Status::failed_precondition(
+                    "another policy change has fenced writes",
+                ));
+            }
+            _ => state.policy_write_fence = Some((request.change_id, request.base_epoch)),
+        }
+        Ok(Response::new(proto::Empty {}))
+    }

+    async fn resume_policy_writes(
+        &self,
+        request: Request<PolicyWriteFenceRequest>,
+    ) -> Result<Response<proto::Empty>, Status> {
+        let request = request.into_inner();
+        let mut state = self.state.write().await;
+        if state.policy_write_fence.as_ref() == Some(&(request.change_id, request.base_epoch)) {
+            state.policy_write_fence = None;
+        }
+        Ok(Response::new(proto::Empty {}))
+    }

+    async fn stop(&self, request: Request<StopRequest>) -> Result<Response<proto::Empty>, Status> {
+        let request = request.into_inner();
+        self.validate_stop_request(&request)?;
+        if !self.stop_prepared.load(AtomicOrdering::Acquire) {
+            return Err(Status::failed_precondition(
+                "stop must be prepared before finalization",
+            ));
+        }
+        let shutdown = self.shutdown.clone();
+        tokio::spawn(async move {
+            // Let the acknowledged response reach the coordinator so it can
+            // durably record shutdown progress before the server exits.
+            tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
+            let _ = shutdown.send(true);
+        });
+        if !self.stop_response_delay.is_zero() {
+            tokio::time::sleep(self.stop_response_delay).await;
+        }
+        Ok(Response::new(proto::Empty {}))
+    }
+
+    async fn prepare_stop(
+        &self,
+        request: Request<StopRequest>,
+    ) -> Result<Response<proto::Empty>, Status> {
+        let request = request.into_inner();
+        self.validate_stop_request(&request)?;
+        if !self.stop_prepared.swap(true, AtomicOrdering::AcqRel) {
+            let coordinator_endpoint = self.coordinator_endpoint.clone();
+            let node_id = self.node_id.clone();
+            let process_instance_id = self.process_instance_id.clone();
+            let shutdown = self.shutdown.clone();
+            tokio::spawn(async move {
+                wait_for_durable_stop_confirmation(
+                    coordinator_endpoint,
+                    node_id,
+                    process_instance_id,
+                    shutdown,
+                )
+                .await;
+            });
+        }
+        Ok(Response::new(proto::Empty {}))
+    }
+}

+    pub(super) fn owner_dedup_full_error(&self, state: &NodeState) -> OperationError {
+        let count = self
+            .pressure
+            .owner_dedup_rejections
+            .fetch_add(1, AtomicOrdering::Relaxed)
+            + 1;
+        let retry_after_millis = dedup_retry_after_millis(state, Instant::now());
+        if count.is_power_of_two() {
+            tracing::info!(
+                node = %self.node_id,
+                count,
+                dedup_bytes = state.dedup_bytes,
+                capacity_bytes = self.max_dedup_bytes,
+                retry_after_millis,
+                "owner deduplication receipt store is full"
+            );
+        }
+        OperationError {
+            current_epoch: state.topology.epoch,
+            retry_after_millis,
+            ..operation_error(
+                ErrorCode::ResourceExhausted,
+                "owner deduplication receipt store is full; retry after capacity returns",
+                true,
+            )
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn record_follower_dedup_rejection(&self, state: &NodeState) {
+        let count = self
+            .pressure
+            .follower_dedup_rejections
+            .fetch_add(1, AtomicOrdering::Relaxed)
+            + 1;
+        if count.is_power_of_two() {
+            tracing::info!(
+                node = %self.node_id,
+                count,
+                dedup_bytes = state.dedup_bytes,
+                capacity_bytes = self.max_dedup_bytes,
+                retry_after_millis = dedup_retry_after_millis(state, Instant::now()),
+                "follower deduplication receipt store is full"
+            );
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub(super) async fn ready_followers(
+        &self,
+        token: u64,
+    ) -> Result<(u64, Vec<String>), OperationError> {
+        let state = self.state.read().await;
+        let topology = &state.topology;
+        let guard = &topology.write_availability_guard;
+        let needs_status = guard.minimum_admitted_copies > 1
+            || guard.minimum_healthy_followers > 0
+            || topology.write_ack_policy != WriteAckPolicy::OwnerOnly;
+        // The lease carries policy-required admissions bound to follower process
+        // identities. Actual mutation ACKs validate those identities below.
+        if guard.minimum_admitted_copies <= 1 && guard.minimum_healthy_followers == 0 {
+            let replicas = topology
+                .replica_node_ids_for_token(token)
+                .map_err(|error| temporarily_unavailable(topology.epoch, error.to_string()))?;
+            let count = match topology.write_ack_policy {
+                WriteAckPolicy::OwnerOnly => 0,
+                WriteAckPolicy::FirstSuccessor => 1,
+                WriteAckPolicy::AllReplicas => topology.desired_replication_factor as usize - 1,
+            };
+            if replicas.len() < count + 1 {
+                return Err(temporarily_unavailable(
+                    topology.epoch,
+                    "required replica placement is unavailable",
+                ));
+            }
+            let followers = replicas.iter().skip(1).take(count);
+            if followers
+                .clone()
+                .any(|node_id| !state.admitted_followers.contains_key(*node_id))
+            {
+                return Err(temporarily_unavailable(
+                    topology.epoch,
+                    "required follower admission is unavailable",
+                ));
+            }
+            let now = now_unix_millis();
+            if followers.clone().any(|node_id| {
+                state
+                    .owner_stream_unacked
+                    .get(&(topology.epoch, (*node_id).to_owned()))
+                    .and_then(|queue| queue.front())
+                    .is_some_and(|(_, sent_at)| {
+                        now.saturating_sub(*sent_at) > guard.max_replica_lag_millis
+                    })
+            }) {
+                return Err(temporarily_unavailable(
+                    topology.epoch,
+                    "required follower exceeds the replication lag bound",
+                ));
+            }
+            return Ok((
+                topology.epoch,
+                followers.map(|node_id| (*node_id).to_owned()).collect(),
+            ));
+        }
+        let topology = topology.clone();
+        drop(state);
+        let status = if needs_status {
+            let result = tokio::time::timeout(COORDINATOR_RPC_TIMEOUT, async {
+                let mut client = configure_coordinator_client(CoordinatorClient::new(
+                    self.coordinator_channel.clone(),
+                ));
+                client
+                    .get_replica_status(proto::Empty {})
+                    .await
+                    .map(Response::into_inner)
+                    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())
+            })
+            .await;
+            // Transport and RPC failures are deliberately indistinguishable at the
+            // write gate: neither proves that a required copy is ready.
+            match result {
+                Ok(Ok(status)) => Some(status),
+                _ => {
+                    return Err(temporarily_unavailable(
+                        topology.epoch,
+                        "replica readiness could not be verified",
+                    ));
+                }
+            }
+        } else {
+            None
+        };
+        let followers = required_followers(&topology, token, status.as_ref(), &self.node_id)?;
+        Ok((topology.epoch, followers))
+    }
+
+    pub(super) async fn wait_required_acks(
+        &self,
+        required: &[RequiredAck],
+        epoch: u64,
+        mutation_id: &str,
+        version: &RecordVersion,
+    ) -> Result<(), OperationError> {
+        if !required.is_empty() {
+            let mut receivers = {
+                let state = self.state.read().await;
+                required
+                    .iter()
+                    .map(|(stream_epoch, node_id, sequence)| {
+                        state
+                            .ack_progress
+                            .get(&(*stream_epoch, node_id.clone()))
+                            .map(|sender| (sender.subscribe(), *sequence))
+                    })
+                    .collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()
+            }
+            .ok_or_else(|| outcome_unknown(epoch))?;
+            let wait = async {
+                for (receiver, sequence) in &mut receivers {
+                    while *receiver.borrow_and_update() < *sequence {
+                        receiver
+                            .changed()
+                            .await
+                            .map_err(|_| outcome_unknown(epoch))?;
+                    }
+                }
+                Ok(())
+            };
+            tokio::time::timeout(self.required_ack_timeout, wait)
+                .await
+                .unwrap_or_else(|_| Err(outcome_unknown(epoch)))?;
+        }
+        if required.is_empty() {
+            let state = self.state.read().await;
+            if state.lease.is_none_or(|(lease_epoch, expires_at)| {
+                lease_epoch != epoch
+                    || state.topology.epoch != epoch
+                    || Instant::now() >= expires_at
+            }) {
+                return Err(outcome_unknown(epoch));
+            }
+            return Ok(());
+        }
+        let mut state =
+            diagnostics::write(&self.state, &self.pressure.ack_completion_write_timing).await;
+        if state.lease.is_none_or(|(lease_epoch, expires_at)| {
+            lease_epoch != epoch || state.topology.epoch != epoch || Instant::now() >= expires_at
+        }) {
+            return Err(outcome_unknown(epoch));
+        }
+        for (stream_epoch, node_id, sequence) in required {
+            let stream = (*stream_epoch, node_id.clone());
+            let admitted = state.admitted_followers.get(node_id);
+            if admitted.is_none()
+                || state.ack_process_instances.get(&stream) != admitted
+                || state
+                    .ack_progress
+                    .get(&stream)
+                    .is_none_or(|progress| *progress.borrow() < *sequence)
+            {
+                return Err(outcome_unknown(epoch));
+            }
+        }
+        complete_required_acks(&mut state, mutation_id, version);
+        Ok(())
+    }
+
+    pub async fn connect(
+        node_id: String,
+        coordinator_endpoint: String,
+        settings: NodeSettings,
+    ) -> anyhow::Result<Self> {
+        settings.validate()?;
+        let process_instance_id = uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
+        let topology = fetch_topology(&coordinator_endpoint).await?;
+        let is_committed_member = topology
+            .members
+            .iter()
+            .any(|member| member.node_id == node_id);
+        let is_pending_member = if is_committed_member {
+            false
+        } else {
+            fetch_pending_topology(&coordinator_endpoint)
+                .await?
+                .is_some_and(|target| {
+                    target
+                        .members
+                        .iter()
+                        .any(|member| member.node_id == node_id)
+                })
+        };
+        if !is_committed_member && !is_pending_member {
+            anyhow::bail!("node {node_id:?} is not present in coordinator topology");
+        }
+        register_node(
+            &coordinator_endpoint,
+            node_id.clone(),
+            process_instance_id.clone(),
+        )
+        .await?;
+        // A Channel reconnects on demand and is cheap to clone. Guarded writes
+        // must not create a fresh TCP connection for every readiness check.
+        let coordinator_channel =
+            Endpoint::from_shared(coordinator_endpoint.clone())?.connect_lazy();
+        let (shutdown, _) = watch::channel(false);
+        let state = Arc::new(RwLock::new(NodeState {
+            topology,
+            records: HashMap::new(),
+            records_by_token: TokenIndex::default(),
+            record_expirations: BTreeSet::new(),
+            next_sequence: 0,
+            owner_stream_sequences: HashMap::new(),
+            owner_stream_unacked: HashMap::new(),
+            ack_progress: HashMap::new(),
+            ack_process_instances: HashMap::new(),
+            admitted_followers: HashMap::new(),
+            follower_streams: HashMap::new(),
+            sources: HashMap::new(),
+            destinations: HashMap::new(),
+            journal_bytes_total: 0,
+            lease: None,
+            policy_write_fence: None,
+            dedup: HashMap::new(),
+            dedup_by_token: TokenIndex::default(),
+            dedup_expirations: BinaryHeap::new(),
+            dedup_bytes: 0,
+            dedup_peak_bytes: 0,
+            ack_progress_needs_prune: false,
+            next_ack_prune_at: Instant::now(),
+            cleanup_timing: proto::ReceiptCleanupTiming::default(),
+        }));
+        let pressure = Arc::new(NodePressureStats::default());
+        let replication_dispatch =
+            start_replication_dispatch(state.clone(), pressure.clone(), &settings);
+        start_expiry_sweep(state.clone());
+        let service = Self {
+            node_id,
+            process_instance_id,
+            coordinator_endpoint,
+            coordinator_channel,
+            state,
+            replication_dispatch,
+            pressure,
+            refresh_lock: Arc::new(Mutex::new(())),
+            max_key_bytes: DEFAULT_MAX_KEY_BYTES,
+            max_value_bytes: settings.max_value_bytes,
+            max_journal_bytes: settings.max_migration_journal_bytes,
+            max_dedup_bytes: settings.max_dedup_bytes,
+            required_ack_timeout: settings.required_ack_timeout,
+            stop_response_delay: std::time::Duration::ZERO,
+            stop_prepared: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
+            shutdown,
+        };
+        if is_committed_member {
+            service.renew_lease_once().await?;
+        }
+        service.start_lease_renewal();
+        service.start_peer_probes();
+        Ok(service)
+    }
+
+    pub(super) async fn renew_lease_once(&self) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
+        let (epoch, lease_duration) = {
+            let state = self.state.read().await;
+            (
+                state.topology.epoch,
+                state.topology.timings.lease_duration(),
+            )
+        };
+        // Discount the entire RPC round trip from the granted lifetime. This
+        // makes local authority expire no later than the coordinator's grant.
+        let sent_at = Instant::now();
+        let response = tokio::time::timeout(lease_renewal_timeout(lease_duration), async {
+            let mut client = configure_coordinator_client(CoordinatorClient::new(
+                self.coordinator_channel.clone(),
+            ));
+            Ok::<_, anyhow::Error>(
+                client
+                    .renew_node_lease(proto::RenewNodeLeaseRequest {
+                        node_id: self.node_id.clone(),
+                        process_instance_id: self.process_instance_id.clone(),
+                        topology_epoch: epoch,
+                    })
+                    .await?
+                    .into_inner(),
+            )
+        })
+        .await??;
+        if response.topology_epoch == epoch && response.lease_duration_millis > 0 {
+            let mut state = self.state.write().await;
+            if state.topology.epoch == epoch {
+                state.admitted_followers = response
+                    .admitted_followers
+                    .into_iter()
+                    .map(|follower| (follower.node_id, follower.process_instance_id))
+                    .collect();
+                state.lease = Some((
+                    epoch,
+                    sent_at + std::time::Duration::from_millis(response.lease_duration_millis),
+                ));
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn start_lease_renewal(&self) {
+        let service = self.clone();
+        let mut shutdown = self.shutdown.subscribe();
+        tokio::spawn(async move {
+            // The cluster's lease duration never changes, so the cadence is
+            // fixed for the process.
+            let lease_duration = service.state.read().await.topology.timings.lease_duration();
+            let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(lease_renewal_interval(lease_duration));
+            interval.set_missed_tick_behavior(tokio::time::MissedTickBehavior::Skip);
+            loop {
+                tokio::select! {
+                    _ = interval.tick() => {
+                        if service.renew_lease_once().await.is_err() {
+                            // The coordinator may have published a new epoch.
+                            let _ = service.refresh_topology().await;
+                        }
+                    }
+                    _ = shutdown.changed() => {
+                        if *shutdown.borrow() { break; }
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        });
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn start_peer_probes(&self) {
+        let service = self.clone();
+        let mut shutdown = self.shutdown.subscribe();
+        tokio::spawn(async move {
+            let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(std::time::Duration::from_secs(1));
+            interval.set_missed_tick_behavior(tokio::time::MissedTickBehavior::Skip);
+            loop {
+                tokio::select! {
+                    _ = interval.tick() => service.probe_peers().await,
+                    _ = shutdown.changed() => {
+                        if *shutdown.borrow() { break; }
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        });
+    }
+
+    pub(super) async fn probe_peers(&self) {
+        let (topology, leased) = {
+            let state = self.state.read().await;
+            let leased = state.lease.is_some_and(|(epoch, expires_at)| {
+                epoch == state.topology.epoch && Instant::now() < expires_at
+            });
+            (state.topology.clone(), leased)
+        };
+        if !leased {
+            return;
+        }
+        let selected = peer_probe_targets(&topology, &self.node_id);
+        if selected.is_empty() {
+            return;
+        }
+        let coordinator =
+            configure_coordinator_client(CoordinatorClient::new(self.coordinator_channel.clone()));
+        let mut probes = tokio::task::JoinSet::new();
+        for member in selected {
+            let mut coordinator = coordinator.clone();
+            let reporter_node_id = self.node_id.clone();
+            let reporter_process_instance_id = self.process_instance_id.clone();
+            let topology_epoch = topology.epoch;
+            probes.spawn(async move {
+                let reachable = tokio::time::timeout(PEER_PROBE_TIMEOUT, async {
+                    let mut client = configure_data_node_client(
+                        DataNodeClient::connect(member.endpoint.clone())
+                            .await
+                            .ok()?,
+                    );
+                    let info = client
+                        .get_process_info(proto::Empty {})
+                        .await
+                        .ok()?
+                        .into_inner();
+                    Some(info.node_id == member.node_id)
+                })
+                .await
+                .ok()
+                .flatten()
+                .unwrap_or(false);
+                let report = proto::ReportPeerHealthRequest {
+                    reporter_node_id,
+                    reporter_process_instance_id,
+                    peer_node_id: member.node_id.clone(),
+                    topology_epoch,
+                    reachable,
+                };
+                let _ = tokio::time::timeout(
+                    PEER_PROBE_TIMEOUT,
+                    coordinator.report_peer_health(report),
+                )
+                .await;
+            });
+        }
+        while probes.join_next().await.is_some() {}
+    }
+
+    pub fn with_stop_response_delay(mut self, delay: std::time::Duration) -> Self {
+        self.stop_response_delay = delay;
+        self
+    }
+
+    pub fn shutdown_receiver(&self) -> watch::Receiver<bool> {
+        self.shutdown.subscribe()
+    }
+
+    pub fn process_instance_id(&self) -> &str {
+        &self.process_instance_id
+    }
+
+    pub(super) async fn refresh_if_newer(&self, request_epoch: u64) -> Result<(), Status> {
+        if self.state.read().await.topology.epoch >= request_epoch {
+            return Ok(());
+        }
+        let _guard = self.refresh_lock.lock().await;
+        if self.state.read().await.topology.epoch >= request_epoch {
+            return Ok(());
+        }
+        self.refresh_topology().await
+    }
+
+    pub(super) async fn refresh_topology(&self) -> Result<(), Status> {
+        let topology = fetch_topology(&self.coordinator_endpoint)
+            .await
+            .map_err(|error| Status::unavailable(error.to_string()))?;
+        let mut state = self.state.write().await;
+        if topology.epoch >= state.topology.epoch {
+            let epoch = topology.epoch;
+            if epoch != state.topology.epoch {
+                state.lease = None;
+                state.admitted_followers.clear();
+                clear_replica_repair_staging(&mut state);
+            }
+            state.set_topology(topology);
+            state
+                .owner_stream_sequences
+                .retain(|(stream_epoch, _), _| *stream_epoch == epoch);
+            state
+                .owner_stream_unacked
+                .retain(|(stream_epoch, _), _| *stream_epoch == epoch);
+            state
+                .follower_streams
+                .retain(|(stream_epoch, _), _| *stream_epoch == epoch);
+            prune_ack_progress(&mut state);
+            self.replication_dispatch.prune_epoch(epoch);
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn validate_key(&self, key: &[u8]) -> Option<OperationError> {
+        if key.is_empty() {
+            return Some(operation_error(
+                ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
+                "key must not be empty",
+                false,
+            ));
+        }
+        if key.len() > self.max_key_bytes {
+            return Some(operation_error(
+                ErrorCode::TooLarge,
+                format!("key exceeds {} bytes", self.max_key_bytes),
+                false,
+            ));
+        }
+        None
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn owner_error(
+        &self,
+        state: &NodeState,
+        token: u64,
+    ) -> Result<Option<OperationError>, Status> {
+        let owner = state
+            .topology
+            .owner_for_token(token)
+            .map_err(|error| Status::internal(error.to_string()))?;
+        if owner.node_id == self.node_id {
+            return Ok(lease_error(state));
+        }
+        Ok(Some(OperationError {
+            code: ErrorCode::Moved.into(),
+            message: format!("key is owned by {}", owner.node_id),
+            current_epoch: state.topology.epoch,
+            owner_endpoint: owner.endpoint.clone(),
+            retryable: true,
+            unknown_write_outcome: false,
+            retry_after_millis: 0,
+        }))
+    }
+}
+
+/// Refuses an owner's answer once its lease for the current epoch has run out:
+/// by then the coordinator may have handed its ranges to another node.
+pub(super) fn lease_error(state: &NodeState) -> Option<OperationError> {
+    state
+        .lease
+        .is_none_or(|(epoch, expires_at)| {
+            epoch != state.topology.epoch || Instant::now() >= expires_at
+        })
+        .then(|| OperationError {
+            current_epoch: state.topology.epoch,
+            ..operation_error(ErrorCode::LeaseExpired, "owner lease has expired", true)
+        })
+}
+
+/// A node renews five times per lease, so a lease survives a lost renewal
+/// or one that times out.
+pub(super) fn lease_renewal_interval(lease_duration: std::time::Duration) -> std::time::Duration {
+    lease_duration / 5
+}
+
+pub(super) fn lease_renewal_timeout(lease_duration: std::time::Duration) -> std::time::Duration {
+    lease_renewal_interval(lease_duration) * 2
+}

+//! Writes the owner applies only if a precondition holds.
+//!
+//! The check runs under the write lock that applies the mutation, which is the
+//! whole point: a caller that read a version and computes a new value from it
+//! must not overwrite a write that landed in between.
+
+use super::*;
+use proto::{Precondition, precondition::Expect};
+
+fn absent() -> Option<Precondition> {
+    Some(Precondition {
+        expect: Some(Expect::Absent(proto::Empty {})),
+    })
+}
+
+fn at_version(version: &RecordVersion) -> Option<Precondition> {
+    Some(Precondition {
+        expect: Some(Expect::Version(version.clone())),
+    })
+}
+
+fn put(
+    key: &[u8],
+    value: &[u8],
+    request_id: &str,
+    precondition: Option<Precondition>,
+) -> PutRequest {
+    PutRequest {
+        key: key.to_vec(),
+        value: value.to_vec(),
+        topology_epoch: 1,
+        request_id: request_id.into(),
+        precondition,
+        ..Default::default()
+    }
+}
+
+async fn write(service: &DataNodeService, request: PutRequest) -> PutResponse {
+    service
+        .put(Request::new(request))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner()
+}
+
+async fn delete(
+    service: &DataNodeService,
+    key: &[u8],
+    request_id: &str,
+    precondition: Option<Precondition>,
+) -> DeleteResponse {
+    service
+        .delete(Request::new(DeleteRequest {
+            key: key.to_vec(),
+            topology_epoch: 1,
+            request_id: request_id.into(),
+            precondition,
+        }))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner()
+}
+
+async fn read(service: &DataNodeService, key: &[u8]) -> GetResponse {
+    service
+        .get(Request::new(GetRequest {
+            key: key.to_vec(),
+            topology_epoch: 1,
+            request_id: "read".into(),
+        }))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner()
+}
+
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn an_absent_condition_creates_a_key_once() {
+    let service = service();
+    let first = write(&service, put(b"key", b"one", "first", absent())).await;
+    assert!(first.error.is_none() && !first.condition_failed);
+    assert!(first.version.is_some());
+
+    let second = write(&service, put(b"key", b"two", "second", absent())).await;
+    assert!(second.condition_failed);
+    assert!(second.error.is_none() && second.version.is_none());
+    assert_eq!(read(&service, b"key").await.value, b"one");
+    // A failed condition writes nothing, receipt included, so the same ID can
+    // be sent again once the caller has recomputed.
+    assert!(!service.state.read().await.dedup.contains_key("second"));
+}
+
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn a_version_condition_rejects_a_write_based_on_a_stale_read() {
+    let service = service();
+    let created = write(&service, put(b"key", b"0", "create", None)).await;
+    let read_version = created.version.unwrap();
+
+    // Two writers read the same version; only the first one's write lands.
+    let winner = write(
+        &service,
+        put(b"key", b"1", "winner", at_version(&read_version)),
+    )
+    .await;
+    assert!(winner.version.is_some());
+    let loser = write(
+        &service,
+        put(b"key", b"1", "loser", at_version(&read_version)),
+    )
+    .await;
+    assert!(loser.condition_failed);
+    assert_eq!(read(&service, b"key").await.value, b"1");
+}

+#[tokio::test]
+async fn a_record_past_its_deadline_is_absent_to_a_condition() {
+    let service = service();
+    let expired = write(
+        &service,
+        PutRequest {
+            expires_at_unix_millis: Some(now_unix_millis()),
+            ..put(b"key", b"old", "expired", None)
+        },
+    )
+    .await;
+    let expired_version = expired.version.unwrap();
+
+    let stale = write(
+        &service,
+        put(b"key", b"new", "stale", at_version(&expired_version)),
+    )
+    .await;
+    assert!(
+        stale.condition_failed,
+        "a version that reads as absent matched"
+    );
+    let created = write(&service, put(b"key", b"new", "created", absent())).await;
+    assert!(created.version.is_some());
+}
+
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn a_retry_is_answered_from_its_receipt_before_the_condition() {
+    let service = service();
+    let first = write(&service, put(b"key", b"one", "first", absent())).await;
+    // The key now exists, so the condition no longer holds, but this is the
+    // same write retried and it already happened.
+    let retried = write(&service, put(b"key", b"one", "first", absent())).await;
+    assert!(!retried.condition_failed);
+    assert_eq!(retried.version, first.version);
+
+    let reused = write(&service, put(b"key", b"one", "first", None)).await;
+    assert_eq!(
+        reused.error.map(|error| ErrorCode::try_from(error.code)),
+        Some(Ok(ErrorCode::MutationIdConflict)),
+        "a different condition is a different write"
+    );
+}

+#[tokio::test]
+async fn a_conditional_delete_removes_only_the_version_it_read() {
+    let service = service();
+    let first = write(&service, put(b"key", b"one", "first", None)).await;
+    let first_version = first.version.unwrap();
+    write(&service, put(b"key", b"two", "second", None)).await;
+
+    let stale = delete(&service, b"key", "stale", at_version(&first_version)).await;
+    assert!(stale.condition_failed);
+    assert_eq!(read(&service, b"key").await.value, b"two");
+
+    let current = read(&service, b"key").await.version;
+    let removed = delete(&service, b"key", "current", at_version(&current.unwrap())).await;
+    assert!(!removed.condition_failed && removed.error.is_none());
+    assert!(read(&service, b"key").await.error.is_some());
+
+    let again = delete(&service, b"key", "absent", absent()).await;
+    assert!(!again.condition_failed, "a deleted key is absent");
+}
+
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn a_precondition_must_say_what_it_expects() {
+    let service = service();
+    let response = write(
+        &service,
+        put(
+            b"key",
+            b"value",
+            "empty",
+            Some(Precondition { expect: None }),
+        ),
+    )
+    .await;
+    assert_eq!(
+        response.error.map(|error| ErrorCode::try_from(error.code)),
+        Some(Ok(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument))
+    );
+}

+//! The end-to-end experiment cannot resolve this change. Four repetitions of one
+//! unchanged binary spanned 79s to 109s in a single session, and the negative
+//! control makes the reason plain: `initial_put` moved 75.7% between runs even
+//! though `range_digest` never executes during the put phase. Against that, the
+//! digest is at most ~3% of a run, so only a measurement of the operation itself
+//! says anything.
+//!
+//! Four paths are timed over one set of records, because the change did not only
+//! remove work:
+//!
+//! | | before | now |
+//! |---|---|---|
+//! | source | copy the range into a `HashMap`, sort key bytes, hash | copy handles off the token index, hash |
+//! | destination | clone the map, sort key bytes, hash | copy the records, token every key, sort `u64`s, hash |
+//!
+//! The destination gained a pass of `xxh3`, so timing it separately is the only
+//! way to see whether the bytes sorted as integers give back more than that pass
+//! costs. The copies on both sides are what the handlers take under the state
+//! lock before releasing it; `digest_stall_bench.rs` measures that lock hold.
+//!
+//! ```sh
+//! cargo test --release -p hashring-node range_digest -- --ignored --nocapture
+//! ```

+use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

+use super::*;

+/// What both sides did before: order the records by key byte and hash. Kept as
+/// it was, except for the `v3` domain separator, so the comparison measures the
+/// code it replaced rather than a paraphrase of it and the two orders can be
+/// compared digest for digest.
+fn sorted_by_key(records: &HashMap<Vec<u8>, Record>, watermark: u64) -> RangeDigestResponse {
+    let mut ordered: Vec<_> = records.iter().collect();
+    ordered.sort_by_key(|(key, _)| *key);
+    let mut digest = blake3::Hasher::new();
+    digest.update(b"hashring-rs:records:v3\0");
+    for (key, record) in &ordered {
+        digest.update(&(key.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
+        digest.update(key);
+        digest.update(&record.version.topology_epoch.to_be_bytes());
+        digest.update(&record.version.owner_sequence.to_be_bytes());
+        digest.update(&(record.version.owner_node_id.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
+        digest.update(record.version.owner_node_id.as_bytes());
+        digest.update(&(record.value.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());
+        digest.update(record.value.as_ref());
+        digest.update(&[u8::from(record.deleted)]);
+    }
+    RangeDigestResponse {
+        record_count: ordered.len() as u64,
+        digest: digest.finalize().to_hex().to_string(),
+        changelog_watermark: watermark,
+    }

+    let copied: HashMap<Vec<u8>, Record> = index

+            records
+                .get(key.as_ref())
+                .map(|record| (key.to_vec(), record.clone()))
+        })
+        .collect();
+    sorted_by_key(&copied, 0)
+}
+
+/// The source path now: `record_keys_in_range` already yields token order, so
+/// the handler copies `Arc` handles off the index under the lock and hashes them
+/// after releasing it.
+fn source_now(index: &[Arc<[u8]>], records: &HashMap<Vec<u8>, Record>) -> RangeDigestResponse {
+    let collected: Vec<_> = index
+        .iter()
+        .filter_map(|key| {
+            let record = records.get(key.as_ref())?.clone();
+            Some((key.clone(), record))
+        })
+        .collect();
+    range_digest(
+        collected.iter().map(|(key, record)| (key.as_ref(), record)),
+        0,
+    )
+}
+
+/// The destination path before: clone the map and sort the copy by key byte.
+fn destination_before(records: &HashMap<Vec<u8>, Record>) -> RangeDigestResponse {
+    sorted_by_key(&records.clone(), 0)
+}
+
+/// The destination path now: the records live in a plain map, so the handler
+/// copies them under the lock, then outside it computes one `xxh3` per key and
+/// sorts `u64`s.
+fn destination_now(
+    records: &HashMap<Vec<u8>, Record>,
+    topology: &TopologySnapshot,
+) -> RangeDigestResponse {
+    let copied: Vec<_> = records
+        .iter()
+        .map(|(key, record)| (key.clone(), record.clone()))
+        .collect();
+    let mut by_token: Vec<_> = copied
+        .iter()
+        .map(|(key, record)| (topology.key_token(key), key.as_slice(), record))
+        .collect();
+    sort_into_token_order(&mut by_token);
+    range_digest(by_token.iter().map(|(_, key, record)| (*key, *record)), 0)
+}
+
+/// Same shape as the test helper in `mod.rs`: one member, replication factor 1,
+/// so the seed is the only thing that distinguishes tokens from key bytes.
+fn bench_topology() -> TopologySnapshot {
+    TopologySnapshot::new_with_config(
+        1,
+        0x5e3d_1234,
+        8,
+        vec![Member {
+            node_id: "node-1".into(),
+            endpoint: "http://127.0.0.1:5001".into(),
+        }],
+        TopologyConfig {
+            desired_replication_factor: 1,
+            write_availability_guard: WriteAvailabilityGuard {
+                minimum_admitted_copies: 1,
+                minimum_healthy_followers: 0,
+                ..WriteAvailabilityGuard::default()
+            },
+            ..TopologyConfig::default()
+        },
+    )
+    .unwrap()
+}
+
+/// The source's view of a range: its keys, in token order.
+type TokenOrderedKeys = Vec<Arc<[u8]>>;
+
+/// Counter keys, whose byte order is their numeric order, plus their token
+/// order. `xxh3` is not monotonic, so the two are genuinely different
+/// permutations — without that the sort being removed would not have been work.
+fn bench_records(
+    count: usize,
+    topology: &TopologySnapshot,
+) -> (TokenOrderedKeys, HashMap<Vec<u8>, Record>) {
+    let mut records = HashMap::with_capacity(count);
+    let mut index = Vec::with_capacity(count);
+    for counter in 0..count {
+        let key: Arc<[u8]> = counter.to_be_bytes().to_vec().into();
+        let deleted = counter % 17 == 0;
+        records.insert(
+            key.to_vec(),
+            Record {
+                value: if deleted {
+                    Vec::new().into()
+                } else {
+                    format!("value-{counter}").into_bytes().into()
+                },
+                version: RecordVersion {
+                    topology_epoch: 1,
+                    owner_sequence: counter as u64,
+                    owner_node_id: format!("node-{}", counter % 4),
+                },
+                deleted,
+                expires_at_unix_millis: None,
+            },
+        );
+        index.push(key);
+    }
+    // `records_by_token` is a `BTreeMap`, so the source's view of a range is
+    // already in token order. Leaving `index` in key order would have made
+    // `source_now` hash the wrong stream and quietly measured the old path.
+    index.sort_by_key(|key| topology.key_token(key));
+    (index, records)
+}
+
+/// Generic over the closure's return so the `black_box` value stays live through
+/// the call instead of being discarded before it is produced.
+fn time<T>(rounds: u32, mut body: impl FnMut() -> T) -> Duration {
+    body();
+    let started = Instant::now();
+    for _ in 0..rounds {
+        drop(body());
+    }
+    started.elapsed() / rounds
+}
+
+fn milliseconds(duration: Duration) -> f64 {
+    duration.as_secs_f64() * 1e3
+}
+
+#[test]
+#[ignore = "micro-benchmark; run with --ignored --nocapture"]
+fn range_digest_pays_for_the_order_it_is_given() {
+    const RECORDS: usize = 20_000;
+    const ROUNDS: u32 = 30;
+
+    let topology = bench_topology();
+    let (index, records) = bench_records(RECORDS, &topology);
+
+    // The setup has to be non-trivial, or a timing result proves nothing about
+    // the sort that was removed.
+    let mut by_key = index.clone();
+    by_key.sort();
+    let mut by_token = index.clone();
+    by_token.sort_by_key(|key| topology.key_token(key));
+    assert_ne!(
+        by_key, by_token,
+        "test keys are already in token order, so no sort was ever needed"
+    );
+
+    let old_src = source_before(&index, &records);
+    let old_dst = destination_before(&records);
+    let new_src = source_now(&index, &records);
+    let new_dst = destination_now(&records, &topology);
+
+    for response in [&old_src, &old_dst, &new_src, &new_dst] {
+        assert_eq!(response.record_count as usize, RECORDS);
+    }
+    // Both contracts, each over the order its side is supposed to use.
+    assert_eq!(
+        old_src.digest, old_dst.digest,
+        "key-byte order agreed on both sides before"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        new_src.digest, new_dst.digest,
+        "token order must agree on both sides now, or a range would fail verification"
+    );
+    assert_ne!(
+        new_src.digest, old_src.digest,
+        "the orders differ, so the inputs really did exercise the removed sort"
+    );
+
+    let old_source = time(ROUNDS, || {
+        std::hint::black_box(source_before(&index, &records))
+    });
+    let new_source = time(ROUNDS, || {
+        std::hint::black_box(source_now(&index, &records))
+    });
+    let old_dest = time(ROUNDS, || {
+        std::hint::black_box(destination_before(&records))
+    });
+    let new_dest = time(ROUNDS, || {
+        std::hint::black_box(destination_now(&records, &topology))
+    });
+
+    println!("range_digest over {RECORDS} records, {ROUNDS} rounds each:");
+    println!(
+        "  source      before {ms1:.3} ms   now {ms2:.3} ms   ({speed:.2}x)",
+        ms1 = milliseconds(old_source),
+        ms2 = milliseconds(new_source),
+        speed = old_source.as_secs_f64() / new_source.as_secs_f64()
+    );
+    println!(
+        "  destination before {ms1:.3} ms   now {ms2:.3} ms   ({speed:.2}x)",
+        ms1 = milliseconds(old_dest),
+        ms2 = milliseconds(new_dest),
+        speed = old_dest.as_secs_f64() / new_dest.as_secs_f64()
+    );
+}

+//! How long a range digest stalls writers to the rest of the node.
+//!
+//! A digest reads the node's state under its `RwLock`, and every `put` takes
+//! that lock for writing, so whatever a digest does before releasing the lock
+//! is added to the latency of writes to every other range. This times the real
+//! `source_range_digest` and `destination_range_digest` handlers against a
+//! concurrent writer and reports the writer's latency next to a run with no
+//! digest at all. It uses only the RPC surface and test helpers, so it can be
+//! dropped into an older tree to compare against the code it replaced.
+//!
+//! ```sh
+//! cargo test --release -p hashring-node range_digest_writer_stall -- --ignored --nocapture
+//! ```
+
+use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
+
+use super::*;
+
+fn milliseconds(duration: Duration) -> f64 {
+    duration.as_secs_f64() * 1e3
+}
+
+/// Half the token ring: the migrating range is `(0, HALF]`, and the writer's keys
+/// sit above it, so the writer is never fenced by the paused range and only waits
+/// on the node's state lock.
+const HALF: u64 = 1 << 63;
+
+fn bench_record(counter: usize, value_bytes: usize) -> Record {
+    Record {
+        value: vec![(counter % 251) as u8; value_bytes].into(),
+        version: RecordVersion {
+            topology_epoch: 1,
+            owner_sequence: counter as u64,
+            owner_node_id: "node-1".into(),
+        },
+        deleted: false,
+        expires_at_unix_millis: None,
+    }
+}
+
+/// `count` counter keys whose tokens fall on the chosen side of `HALF`.
+fn keys_on_side(topology: &TopologySnapshot, count: usize, in_range: bool) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {
+    (0u64..)
+        .map(|counter| counter.to_be_bytes().to_vec())
+        .filter(|key| {
+            let token = topology.key_token(key);
+            (token != 0 && token <= HALF) == in_range
+        })
+        .take(count)
+        .collect()
+}
+
+fn percentile(sorted: &[Duration], fraction: f64) -> Duration {
+    sorted[((sorted.len() - 1) as f64 * fraction).round() as usize]
+}
+
+/// Writer latency, sorted ascending. `stall` is the mean of the `stalls`
+/// slowest puts: each digest delays the one put waiting when it takes the lock,
+/// so with one digest per round that is the per-digest stall.
+fn summary(sorted: &[Duration], stalls: usize) -> String {
+    let slowest = &sorted[sorted.len().saturating_sub(stalls)..];
+    let stall = slowest.iter().sum::<Duration>() / slowest.len() as u32;
+    format!(
+        "puts {:>5}  p50 {:>7.3} ms  p99 {:>7.3} ms  stall {:>7.3} ms  max {:>7.3} ms",
+        sorted.len(),
+        milliseconds(percentile(sorted, 0.50)),
+        milliseconds(percentile(sorted, 0.99)),
+        milliseconds(stall),
+        milliseconds(*sorted.last().unwrap()),
+    )
+}
+
+/// Issues one put per millisecond to keys outside the migrating range until
+/// `stop`, and returns
+/// each put's latency. A put takes the node's state lock for writing, so its
+/// latency is exactly what a digest holding the read lock costs other ranges.
+fn spawn_writer(
+    service: DataNodeService,
+    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
+    stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,
+) -> tokio::task::JoinHandle<Vec<Duration>> {
+    tokio::spawn(async move {
+        let mut latencies = Vec::new();
+        let mut sequence = 0usize;
+        while !stop.load(AtomicOrdering::Relaxed) {
+            let key = keys[sequence % keys.len()].clone();
+            let started = Instant::now();
+            let response = service
+                .put(Request::new(PutRequest {
+                    key,
+                    value: vec![7; 128],
+                    topology_epoch: 1,
+                    request_id: format!("writer-{sequence}"),
+                    expires_at_unix_millis: None,
+                    preserve_value: false,
+                    ..Default::default()
+                }))
+                .await
+                .unwrap()
+                .into_inner();
+            assert!(response.error.is_none(), "writer put failed");
+            latencies.push(started.elapsed());
+            sequence += 1;
+            // Paced so the receipts it leaves stay far inside the dedup budget;
+            // a stall still lands on whichever put is waiting when it starts.
+            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1)).await;
+        }
+        latencies
+    })
+}
+
+/// Runs `digest` `rounds` times against a concurrent writer and prints the
+/// digest's own time next to the writer's latency while it ran.
+async fn measure_writer_stall<F, Fut>(
+    label: &str,
+    service: &DataNodeService,
+    writer_keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
+    rounds: u32,
+    mut digest: F,
+) where
+    F: FnMut() -> Fut,
+    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = RangeDigestResponse>,
+{
+    let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
+    let writer = spawn_writer(service.clone(), writer_keys, stop.clone());
+    // Let the writer reach a steady state before the first digest.
+    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
+    let started = Instant::now();
+    let mut count = 0;
+    for _ in 0..rounds {
+        count = std::hint::black_box(digest().await).record_count;
+    }
+    let digest_time = started.elapsed() / rounds;
+    stop.store(true, AtomicOrdering::Relaxed);
+    let mut latencies = writer.await.unwrap();
+    latencies.sort();
+    println!(
+        "  {label:<12} {count:>6} records  digest {:>8.3} ms   {}",
+        milliseconds(digest_time),
+        summary(&latencies, rounds as usize),
+    );
+}
+

+            .unwrap();
+        destination.node_id = "node-1".into();
+        {
+            let mut state = destination.state.write().await;
+            let staged = state
+                .destinations
+                .get_mut(&("change-1".to_string(), "range-1".to_string()))
+                .unwrap();
+            for (counter, key) in range_keys.iter().enumerate() {
+                staged
+                    .records
+                    .insert(key.clone(), bench_record(counter, value_bytes));
+            }
+        }
+        measure_writer_stall("destination", &destination, writer_keys, ROUNDS, || {
+            let destination = destination.clone();
+            let control = control.clone();
+            async move {
+                destination
+                    .destination_range_digest(Request::new(control))
+                    .await
+                    .unwrap()
+                    .into_inner()
+            }
+        })
+        .await;

+        // The same writer with no digest running, as the floor to compare against.
+        let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
+        let writer = spawn_writer(service(), keys_on_side(&topology, 64, false), stop.clone());
+        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1000)).await;
+        stop.store(true, AtomicOrdering::Relaxed);
+        let mut latencies = writer.await.unwrap();
+        latencies.sort();
+        println!(
+            "  {:<12} {:>6}          {:>18}   {}",
+            "no digest",
+            "",
+            "",
+            summary(&latencies, ROUNDS as usize),
+        );
+    }

+//! Per-key expiry on a node.
+//!
+//! The properties these check are the ones a promoted replica and a migration
+//! destination have to agree on: a record past its deadline reads as absent
+//! wherever it lives, and nothing about it depends on a delete having travelled
+//! through the cluster.
+
+use super::*;
+
+/// A migration range that contains one key's token, whatever it is.
+fn range_covering(token: u64) -> proto::RangeSpec {
+    proto::RangeSpec {
+        start_exclusive: token.saturating_sub(1),
+        end_inclusive: token,
+        change_id: "change-1".into(),
+        range_id: "range-1".into(),
+        source_node_id: "node-1".into(),
+        destination_node_id: "node-2".into(),
+    }
+}
+
+/// A deadline a little way ahead, in the form the wire carries.
+fn deadline_in(secs: u64) -> u64 {
+    now_unix_millis() + secs * 1000
+}
+
+fn put(key: &[u8], value: &[u8], request_id: &str) -> PutRequest {
+    PutRequest {
+        key: key.to_vec(),
+        value: value.to_vec(),
+        topology_epoch: 1,
+        request_id: request_id.into(),
+        expires_at_unix_millis: None,
+        preserve_value: false,
+        ..Default::default()
+    }
+}
+
+async fn get(service: &DataNodeService, key: &[u8]) -> GetResponse {
+    service
+        .get(Request::new(GetRequest {
+            key: key.to_vec(),
+            topology_epoch: 1,
+            request_id: "read".into(),
+        }))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner()
+}
+
+async fn write(service: &DataNodeService, request: PutRequest) -> PutResponse {
+    service
+        .put(Request::new(request))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner()
+}

+        &service,

+            key: b"key".to_vec(),

+        &service,
+        PutRequest {

+async fn the_sweep_reclaims_deadlines_nobody_asks_about() {
+    let service = service();
+    {
+        let mut state = service.state.write().await;
+        for index in 0..16_u32 {
+            seed_record(
+                &mut state,
+                format!("key-{index}").as_bytes(),
+                Record {
+                    value: Arc::from(b"value".as_slice()),
+                    version: RecordVersion {
+                        topology_epoch: 1,
+                        owner_sequence: u64::from(index) + 1,
+                        owner_node_id: "node-1".into(),
+                    },
+                    deleted: false,
+                    expires_at_unix_millis: Some(now_unix_millis() - index as u64 - 1),
+                },
+            );
+        }
+        // A key whose deadline is still ahead is left alone.
+        seed_record(
+            &mut state,
+            b"kept",
+            Record {
+                value: Arc::from(b"value".as_slice()),
+                version: RecordVersion {
+                    topology_epoch: 1,
+                    owner_sequence: 1,
+                    owner_node_id: "node-1".into(),
+                },
+                deleted: false,
+                expires_at_unix_millis: Some(now_unix_millis() + 3_600_000),
+            },
+        );
+    }
+    assert_eq!(service.state.read().await.records.len(), 17);
+
+    // Every key but `kept` is already past its deadline.
+    let removed = {
+        let mut state = service.state.write().await;
+        sweep_expired_records(&mut state, now_unix_millis(), EXPIRY_SWEEP_LIMIT)
+    };
+    assert_eq!(removed, 16);
+    {
+        let state = service.state.read().await;
+        assert_eq!(state.records.len(), 1);
+        assert!(state.records.contains_key(b"kept".as_slice()));
+        state.debug_assert_index();
+    }
+
+    // The index is drained of expired entries, so the next pass costs nothing.
+    let mut state = service.state.write().await;
+    assert_eq!(
+        sweep_expired_records(&mut state, now_unix_millis(), EXPIRY_SWEEP_LIMIT),
+        0
+    );
+    drop(state);
+}

+async fn a_deadline_reaches_a_follower_and_a_replica_read_agrees() {
+    let topology = replication_topology(2);
+    let owner = service_for("node-1", topology.clone());
+    let follower = service_for("node-2", topology.clone());
+    let key = key_with_placement(&topology, |replicas| {
+        replicas[0] == "node-1" && replicas[1] == "node-2"
+    });
+
+    let expires_at = deadline_in(600);
+    let stored = write(
+        &owner,
+        PutRequest {
+            expires_at_unix_millis: Some(expires_at),
+            ..put(&key, b"value", "first")
+        },
+    )
+    .await;
+    let version = stored.version.expect("the write was applied");
+
+    let applied = follower
+        .replicate_mutation(Request::new(replication_entry(
+            &topology,
+            key.to_vec(),
+            (1, 1),
+            b"value",
+            false,
+            Some(expires_at),
+        )))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner();
+    assert_eq!(applied.applied_stream_sequence, 1);
+
+    // The follower stores the deadline the owner sent, so both read the key the
+    // same way and both would agree if one of them were promoted.
+    {
+        let state = follower.state.read().await;
+        let record = state.records.get(key.as_slice()).unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(record.expires_at_unix_millis, Some(expires_at));
+        assert_eq!(record.version, version);
+    }
+
+    // A record that arrives already expired is not readable either.
+    let expired = write(
+        &owner,
+        PutRequest {
+            expires_at_unix_millis: Some(now_unix_millis()),
+            ..put(&key, b"second", "second")
+        },
+    )
+    .await;
+    assert!(expired.error.is_none());
+    follower
+        .replicate_mutation(Request::new(replication_entry(
+            &topology,
+            key.clone(),
+            (2, 2),
+            b"second",
+            false,
+            Some(now_unix_millis()),
+        )))
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    let read = get(&follower, &key).await;
+    assert!(read.error.is_some(), "the follower read an expired record");

+        .await
+        .unwrap();

+    // resolve the same way the owner did, so the journal must carry the result.
+    let kept = write(&source, put(&key, b"second", "second")).await;
+    assert!(kept.error.is_none());

+use super::*;
+use hashring_core::topology::{Member, TopologyConfig, WriteAvailabilityGuard};
+
+/// The index is only worth having if it answers exactly what hashing every key
+/// would have answered, including for the wrapping range that spans the end of
+/// the token space.
+fn ranges() -> Vec<RangeSpec> {
+    vec![
+        spec(0, 0),
+        spec(0, u64::MAX / 3),
+        spec(u64::MAX / 3, u64::MAX / 2),
+        // Wraps past the end of the token space.
+        spec(u64::MAX / 2, u64::MAX / 3),
+        spec(u64::MAX - 1, 0),
+        spec(u64::MAX, 1),
+        // start == end means every token.
+        spec(42, 42),
+    ]
+}
+
+fn spec(start_exclusive: u64, end_inclusive: u64) -> RangeSpec {
+    RangeSpec {
+        change_id: "change-1".into(),
+        range_id: "range-1".into(),
+        start_exclusive,
+        end_inclusive,
+        source_node_id: "node-1".into(),
+        destination_node_id: "node-2".into(),
+    }
+}
+
+fn keys(count: u32) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {
+    (0..count)
+        .map(|index| format!("key-{index:04}").into_bytes())
+        .collect()
+}
+
+fn record(owner_sequence: u64) -> Record {
+    Record {
+        expires_at_unix_millis: None,
+        value: Arc::from(format!("value-{owner_sequence}").as_bytes()),
+        version: RecordVersion {
+            topology_epoch: 1,
+            owner_sequence,
+            owner_node_id: "node-1".into(),
+        },
+        deleted: false,
+    }
+}
+
+/// What the previous implementation produced: hash every key on the node and
+/// keep the ones whose token the range claims.
+fn brute_force(state: &NodeState, range: &RangeSpec) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {
+    let mut found: Vec<Vec<u8>> = state
+        .records
+        .keys()
+        .filter(|key| range.contains(state.topology.key_token(key)))
+        .map(|key| key.to_vec())
+        .collect();
+    found.sort();
+    found
+}
+
+fn indexed(state: &NodeState, range: &RangeSpec) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {
+    let mut found: Vec<Vec<u8>> = state
+        .record_keys_in_range(range)
+        .into_iter()
+        .map(|(_, key)| key.to_vec())
+        .collect();
+    found.sort();
+    found
+}

+#[tokio::test]
+async fn record_index_matches_hashing_every_key() {
+    let service = service();
+    let mut state = service.state.write().await;
+    for (index, key) in keys(64).into_iter().enumerate() {
+        seed_record(&mut state, key.as_slice(), record(index as u64 + 1));
+    }
+    state.debug_assert_index();
+    assert_eq!(state.records_by_token.len(), 64);
+
+    for range in ranges() {
+        assert_eq!(
+            indexed(&state, &range),
+            brute_force(&state, &range),
+            "range {}..= disagrees with a full scan",
+            range.start_exclusive,
+        );
+    }
+}

+fn epoch_two(hash_seed: u64) -> TopologySnapshot {
+    TopologySnapshot::new_with_config(
+        2,
+        hash_seed,
+        16,
+        (0..4)
+            .map(|index| Member {
+                node_id: format!("node-{index}"),
+                endpoint: format!("http://127.0.0.1:500{}", index + 1),
+            })
+            .collect(),
+        TopologyConfig {
+            desired_replication_factor: 1,
+            write_availability_guard: WriteAvailabilityGuard {
+                minimum_admitted_copies: 1,
+                minimum_healthy_followers: 0,
+                ..WriteAvailabilityGuard::default()

+            ..TopologyConfig::default()

+    let service = service();
+    let mut state = service.state.write().await;
+    for (index, key) in keys(48).into_iter().enumerate() {
+        seed_record(&mut state, key.as_slice(), record(index as u64 + 1));
+    }
+    let before: Vec<Vec<Vec<u8>>> = ranges()
+        .iter()
+        .map(|range| indexed(&state, range))
+        .collect();
+
+    // A topology change carries the committed hash seed forward, so no key
+    // moves: the index must keep answering the same ranges without a rebuild.
+    let seed = state.topology.hash_seed;
+    state.set_topology(epoch_two(seed));
+    state.debug_assert_index();

+    for (index, range) in ranges().iter().enumerate() {
+        assert_eq!(
+            indexed(&state, range),
+            before[index],
+            "range {}..= changed across an epoch bump",
+            range.start_exclusive,
+        );
+        assert_eq!(indexed(&state, range), brute_force(&state, range));
+    }
+
+    // Writes at the new epoch still index correctly.
+    seed_record(&mut state, b"at-epoch-2", record(100));
+    state.debug_assert_index();
+    let mut at_epoch_two = brute_force(&state, &spec(0, u64::MAX));
+    assert_eq!(at_epoch_two.len(), 49);
+    at_epoch_two.sort();
+    assert_eq!(indexed(&state, &spec(0, u64::MAX)), at_epoch_two);

+//! Paging through the keys a node owns.
+//!
+//! A walk over every owner has to see each live key exactly once: the node
+//! must skip its follower copies, deleted and expired records, and end every
+//! page between tokens so the next one can start from a token alone.
+
+use super::*;
+
+fn record(deleted: bool, expires_at_unix_millis: Option<u64>) -> Record {
+    Record {
+        value: Arc::from(b"value".as_slice()),
+        version: RecordVersion {
+            topology_epoch: 1,
+            owner_sequence: 1,
+            owner_node_id: "node-1".into(),
+        },
+        deleted,
+        expires_at_unix_millis,
+    }
+}
+
+fn limits(max_keys: usize, count_only: bool) -> crate::keyspace::PageLimits {
+    crate::keyspace::PageLimits {
+        max_keys,
+        max_bytes: usize::MAX,
+        max_examined: crate::keyspace::MAX_EXAMINED_PER_PAGE,
+        count_only,
+        one_stretch: false,
+    }
+}
+
+/// Every page from the start until the node says it is done.
+fn walk(
+    state: &NodeState,
+    node_id: &str,
+    limits: &crate::keyspace::PageLimits,
+) -> (Vec<Vec<u8>>, u64) {
+    let mut cursor = 0;
+    let (mut keys, mut count) = (Vec::new(), 0);
+    for _ in 0..10_000 {
+        let page = state.owned_keys_page(node_id, cursor, now_unix_millis(), limits);
+        keys.extend(page.keys);
+        count += page.count;
+        match page.next {
+            Some(next) => cursor = next,
+            None => return (keys, count),
+        }
+    }
+    panic!("the walk did not finish");
+}
+
+fn list_request(epoch: u64) -> ListKeysRequest {
+    ListKeysRequest {
+        topology_epoch: epoch,
+        max_keys: 100,
+        max_bytes: 1 << 20,
+        ..Default::default()
+    }
+}
+
+/// A state holding every key, under a three-node topology, so that each node's
+/// pages can be taken from it as that node would take them from its own.
+async fn three_owners_with_keys(count: usize) -> (TopologySnapshot, DataNodeService, Vec<Vec<u8>>) {
+    let topology = replication_topology(3);
+    let service = service_for("node-1", topology.clone());
+    let keys: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (0..count)
+        .map(|index| format!("key-{index}").into_bytes())
+        .collect();
+    {
+        let mut state = service.state.write().await;
+        for key in &keys {
+            seed_record(&mut state, key, record(false, None));
+        }
+    }
+    (topology, service, keys)
+}
+
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn a_page_lists_live_keys_only() {
+    let service = service();
+    let mut state = service.state.write().await;
+    seed_record(&mut state, b"live", record(false, None));
+    seed_record(
+        &mut state,
+        b"expiring",
+        record(false, Some(now_unix_millis() + 3_600_000)),
+    );
+    seed_record(&mut state, b"deleted", record(true, None));
+    seed_record(
+        &mut state,
+        b"expired",
+        record(false, Some(now_unix_millis() - 1)),
+    );
+
+    let (mut keys, count) = walk(&state, "node-1", &limits(100, false));
+    keys.sort();
+    assert_eq!(keys, [b"expiring".to_vec(), b"live".to_vec()]);
+    assert_eq!(count, 2);
+
+    let (keys, count) = walk(&state, "node-1", &limits(100, true));
+    assert!(keys.is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(count, 2);
+}
+
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn single_key_pages_visit_every_key_once_and_never_split_a_token() {
+    let service = service();
+    let mut state = service.state.write().await;
+    for index in 0..50 {
+        seed_record(
+            &mut state,
+            format!("key-{index}").as_bytes(),
+            record(false, None),
+        );
+    }
+    // Two keys that land on the same token share a bucket. A page takes both,
+    // even past its key limit, so that the next page can start at a token.
+    for key in [b"twin-a".as_slice(), b"twin-b"] {
+        state.records.insert(Arc::from(key), record(false, None));
+        state.records_by_token.insert(7, Arc::from(key));
+    }
+    let twins = state.owned_keys_page("node-1", 7, now_unix_millis(), &limits(1, false));
+    assert_eq!(twins.keys, [b"twin-a".to_vec(), b"twin-b".to_vec()]);
+    assert!(twins.next.is_some_and(|next| next > 7));
+
+    let (keys, count) = walk(&state, "node-1", &limits(1, false));
+    assert_eq!(count, 52);
+    let unique: HashSet<_> = keys.iter().collect();
+    assert_eq!(unique.len(), 52);
+}
