+#[tokio::test]
+async fn an_owner_refuses_one_key_too_many_on_a_token() {
+    let service = service();
+    let key = b"newcomer";
+    let token = service.state.read().await.token_of(key);
+    {
+        // Keys built to collide with `newcomer`, as anyone who knows the
+        // hash seed could build them.
+        let mut state = service.state.write().await;
+        for index in 0..crate::keyspace::MAX_KEYS_PER_TOKEN {
+            let colliding: Arc<[u8]> = Arc::from(format!("colliding-{index}").as_bytes());
+            state.records.insert(colliding.clone(), record(false, None));
+            state.records_by_token.insert(token, colliding);
+        }
+    }
+    let put = |key: &[u8], request_id: &str| PutRequest {
+        key: key.to_vec(),
+        value: b"value".to_vec(),
+        topology_epoch: 1,
+        request_id: request_id.into(),
+        ..Default::default()
+    };
+    let refused = service
+        .put(Request::new(put(key, "new")))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner();
+    assert_eq!(
+        refused.error.map(|error| error.code),
+        Some(ErrorCode::ResourceExhausted as i32)
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        service.state.read().await.records_by_token.len_at(token),
+        crate::keyspace::MAX_KEYS_PER_TOKEN
+    );
+
+    // A key already on the token is still written.
+    let rewritten = service
+        .put(Request::new(put(b"colliding-0", "rewrite")))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner();
+    assert!(rewritten.error.is_none(), "{:?}", rewritten.error);
+}

+#[tokio::test]
+async fn a_page_skips_the_follower_copies_a_node_holds() {
+    let (topology, service, keys) = three_owners_with_keys(300).await;
+    let state = service.state.read().await;
+    for node in ["node-1", "node-2", "node-3"] {
+        let (listed, _) = walk(&state, node, &limits(7, false));
+        let mut expected: Vec<_> = keys
+            .iter()
+            .filter(|key| topology.owner(key).unwrap().node_id == node)
+            .cloned()
+            .collect();
+        let mut listed = listed;
+        expected.sort();
+        listed.sort();
+        assert!(!expected.is_empty());
+        assert_eq!(listed, expected, "{node}");
+    }
+}
+
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn one_stretch_at_a_time_round_the_ring_visits_every_key_once() {
+    let (topology, service, keys) = three_owners_with_keys(300).await;
+    let state = service.state.read().await;
+    let one_stretch = crate::keyspace::PageLimits {
+        one_stretch: true,
+        ..limits(5, false)
+    };
+    // What a scan does: ask whoever owns the cursor's token, and carry on
+    // from where its stretch ended.
+    let mut position = 0;
+    let mut seen = Vec::new();
+    for _ in 0..10_000 {
+        let owner = topology.owner_for_token(position).unwrap().node_id.clone();
+        let page = state.owned_keys_page(&owner, position, now_unix_millis(), &one_stretch);
+        for key in &page.keys {
+            assert_eq!(topology.owner(key).unwrap().node_id, owner);
+            assert!(topology.key_token(key) >= position);
+        }
+        seen.extend(page.keys);
+        match page.next {
+            Some(next) => {
+                assert!(next > position, "a stretch made no progress");
+                position = next;
+            }
+            None => break,
+        }
+    }
+    let mut expected = keys;
+    expected.sort();
+    seen.sort();
+    assert_eq!(seen, expected);
+}
+
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn a_page_stops_at_its_examination_budget() {
+    let service = service();
+    let mut state = service.state.write().await;
+    for index in 0..20 {
+        seed_record(
+            &mut state,
+            format!("gone-{index}").as_bytes(),
+            record(true, None),
+        );
+    }
+    seed_record(&mut state, b"live", record(false, None));
+
+    let tight = crate::keyspace::PageLimits {
+        max_examined: 5,
+        ..limits(100, false)
+    };
+    let first = state.owned_keys_page("node-1", 0, now_unix_millis(), &tight);
+    assert!(
+        first.next.is_some(),
+        "twenty dead entries do not fit in five"
+    );
+    let (keys, _) = walk(&state, "node-1", &tight);
+    assert_eq!(keys, [b"live".to_vec()]);
+}
+
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn a_walk_from_an_older_epoch_is_told_to_start_over() {
+    let service = service();
+    let stale = service
+        .list_keys(Request::new(list_request(0)))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner();
+    let error = stale.error.expect("an older epoch is refused");
+    assert_eq!(error.code, ErrorCode::Moved as i32);
+    assert_eq!(error.current_epoch, 1);
+}
+
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn a_stretch_is_held_to_ownership_rather_than_to_the_callers_epoch() {
+    let (topology, service, _) = three_owners_with_keys(30).await;
+    let owned = topology
+        .assignments
+        .iter()
+        .find(|assignment| assignment.node_id == "node-1")
+        .unwrap()
+        .token;
+    let foreign = topology
+        .assignments
+        .iter()
+        .find(|assignment| assignment.node_id != "node-1")
+        .unwrap();
+    let stretch = |start_token| ListKeysRequest {
+        start_token,
+        one_stretch: true,
+        ..list_request(0)
+    };
+
+    // A cursor from an older epoch is still answered by the token's owner.
+    let answered = service
+        .list_keys(Request::new(stretch(owned)))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner();
+    assert!(answered.error.is_none(), "{:?}", answered.error);
+
+    // A token another node owns is sent there.
+    let moved = service
+        .list_keys(Request::new(stretch(foreign.token)))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner()
+        .error
+        .expect("a token owned elsewhere is refused");
+    assert_eq!(moved.code, ErrorCode::Moved as i32);
+    let endpoint = &topology
+        .members
+        .iter()
+        .find(|member| member.node_id == foreign.node_id)
+        .unwrap()
+        .endpoint;
+    assert_eq!(&moved.owner_endpoint, endpoint);
+}
+
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn an_owner_whose_lease_ran_out_does_not_answer() {
+    let service = service();
+    service.state.write().await.lease = None;
+    for one_stretch in [false, true] {
+        let response = service
+            .list_keys(Request::new(ListKeysRequest {
+                one_stretch,
+                ..list_request(1)
+            }))
+            .await
+            .unwrap()
+            .into_inner();
+        assert_eq!(
+            response.error.map(|error| error.code),
+            Some(ErrorCode::LeaseExpired as i32),
+            "one_stretch={one_stretch}"
+        );
+    }
+}

-/// Pairs of distinct 16-byte keys whose tokens collide under `seed`.
-///
-/// XXH3 is invertible for 9-16 byte inputs: with `lo` and `hi` the two input
-/// words XORed with seed-dependent constants of the default secret, the hash is
-/// `avalanche(len + swap_bytes(lo) + hi + fold(lo * hi))`. A key with `lo == 0`
-/// reaches any accumulator through `hi` alone, so it can be aimed at any other
-/// key's accumulator.
-fn colliding_key_pairs(seed: u64, pairs: u64) -> Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)> {
-    let flip_lo = 0x6782_737b_ea42_39b9_u64.wrapping_add(seed);
-    let flip_hi = 0xaf56_bc3b_0996_523a_u64.wrapping_sub(seed);
-    let fold = |left: u64, right: u64| {
-        let product = u128::from(left) * u128::from(right);
-        (product as u64) ^ ((product >> 64) as u64)
-    };
-    let key = |lo: u64, hi: u64| {
-        let mut key = (lo ^ flip_lo).to_le_bytes().to_vec();
-        key.extend_from_slice(&(hi ^ flip_hi).to_le_bytes());
-        key
-    };
-    (1..=pairs)
-        .map(|pair| {
-            let lo = pair << 56;
-            let hi = pair.wrapping_mul(0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15);
-            let aimed = lo.swap_bytes().wrapping_add(hi).wrapping_add(fold(lo, hi));
-            (key(0, aimed), key(lo, hi))
-        })
-        .collect()
-}

+/// Pairs of distinct 16-byte keys whose tokens collide under `seed`.
+///
+/// XXH3 is invertible for 9-16 byte inputs: with `lo` and `hi` the two input
+/// words XORed with seed-dependent constants of the default secret, the hash is
+/// `avalanche(len + swap_bytes(lo) + hi + fold(lo * hi))`. A key with `lo == 0`
+/// reaches any accumulator through `hi` alone, so it can be aimed at any other
+/// key's accumulator.
+fn colliding_key_pairs(seed: u64, pairs: u64) -> Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)> {
+    let flip_lo = 0x6782_737b_ea42_39b9_u64.wrapping_add(seed);
+    let flip_hi = 0xaf56_bc3b_0996_523a_u64.wrapping_sub(seed);
+    let fold = |left: u64, right: u64| {
+        let product = u128::from(left) * u128::from(right);
+        (product as u64) ^ ((product >> 64) as u64)
+    };
+    let key = |lo: u64, hi: u64| {
+        let mut key = (lo ^ flip_lo).to_le_bytes().to_vec();
+        key.extend_from_slice(&(hi ^ flip_hi).to_le_bytes());
+        key
+    };
+    (1..=pairs)
+        .map(|pair| {
+            let lo = pair << 56;
+            let hi = pair.wrapping_mul(0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15);
+            let aimed = lo.swap_bytes().wrapping_add(hi).wrapping_add(fold(lo, hi));
+            (key(0, aimed), key(lo, hi))
+        })
+        .collect()
+}

+/// Source and destination must digest a range to the same value.
+///
+/// The earlier test compared digests over a single record, where both sides
+/// agree whichever order they walk in, so it could not catch one side walking
+/// key bytes while the other walked tokens. That is now the whole risk:
+/// `range_digest` takes records in the order its caller supplies, the source
+/// reads that order off the token index, and the destination sorts by token.
+/// Here the range is large enough that token order and key-byte order are
+/// different permutations, so a side using the wrong one cannot match by luck.
+#[tokio::test]
+async fn source_and_destination_digest_a_range_whose_orders_differ() {
+    const RECORDS: usize = 256;
+
+    let source = service();
+
+    // Records first: `prepare_source_range` captures the range's keys into
+    // `snapshot_keys`, so seeding afterwards would leave an empty snapshot even
+    // though the token index already has them.
+    let keys: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (0..RECORDS)
+        .map(|index| format!("key-{index:04}").into_bytes())
+        .collect();
+    {
+        let mut state = source.state.write().await;
+        for (index, key) in keys.iter().enumerate() {
+            let deleted = index % 7 == 0;
+            let value: Arc<[u8]> = if deleted {
+                Vec::new().into()
+            } else {
+                format!("value-{index}").into_bytes().into()
+            };
+            seed_record(
+                &mut state,
+                key.as_slice(),
+                Record {
+                    value,
+                    version: RecordVersion {
+                        topology_epoch: 1,
+                        owner_sequence: index as u64 + 1,
+                        owner_node_id: "node-1".into(),
+                    },
+                    deleted,
+                    expires_at_unix_millis: None,
+                },
+            );
+        }
+        // The setup has to genuinely differ, or the comparison below proves
+        // nothing: if these keys were already in token order, a destination
+        // walking key bytes would match by accident.
+        let mut by_key = keys.clone();
+        by_key.sort();
+        let mut by_token = keys.clone();
+        by_token.sort_by_key(|key| state.topology.key_token(key));
+        assert_ne!(
+            by_key, by_token,
+            "test keys are already in token order, so the test cannot distinguish the two"
+        );
+    }
+
+    source
+        .prepare_source_range(Request::new(PrepareRangeRequest {
+            range: Some(range(0)),
+        }))
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+
+    let digest = source
+        .source_range_digest(Request::new(RangeControlRequest {
+            change_id: "change-1".into(),
+            range_id: "range-1".into(),
+        }))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner();
+    assert_eq!(digest.record_count, RECORDS as u64);
+
+    let snapshot = source
+        .read_snapshot_page(Request::new(SnapshotPageRequest {
+            change_id: "change-1".into(),
+            range_id: "range-1".into(),
+            cursor: 0,
+            max_bytes: MAX_MIGRATION_PAGE_BYTES as u64,
+        }))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner();
+    assert!(
+        snapshot.done,
+        "the whole range must fit one page for this comparison"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(snapshot.records.len(), RECORDS);
+
+    let mut destination = service();
+    destination.node_id = "node-2".into();
+    destination
+        .prepare_destination_range(Request::new(PrepareRangeRequest {
+            range: Some(range(0)),
+        }))
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    destination
+        .apply_migration_batch(Request::new(ApplyMigrationBatchRequest {
+            change_id: "change-1".into(),
+            range_id: "range-1".into(),
+            snapshot_records: snapshot.records,
+            journal_records: Vec::new(),
+        }))
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    let destination_digest = destination
+        .destination_range_digest(Request::new(RangeControlRequest {
+            change_id: "change-1".into(),
+            range_id: "range-1".into(),
+        }))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner();
+
+    assert_eq!(destination_digest.record_count, RECORDS as u64);
+    assert_eq!(
+        destination_digest.digest, digest.digest,
+        "the source walks its token index and the destination sorts by token; \
+         both must hash the same bytes in the same order"
+    );
+}

+#[test]
+fn a_page_carries_at_least_one_of_the_largest_values_the_node_holds() {
+    use crate::migration::page_limit;
+
+    // What a coordinator asks for is what a default cluster needs; a node
+    // holding larger values still has to be able to move one of them.
+    let asked = hashring_core::limits::DEFAULT_MIGRATION_PAGE_BYTES as u64;
+    assert_eq!(
+        page_limit(asked, DEFAULT_MAX_VALUE_BYTES),
+        hashring_core::limits::DEFAULT_MIGRATION_PAGE_BYTES
+    );
+    assert_eq!(page_limit(asked, 64 * 1024 * 1024), 64 * 1024 * 1024);
+
+    // The request may not take a page past what the transport carries, nor
+    // below a page that can hold something.
+    assert_eq!(
+        page_limit(u64::MAX, DEFAULT_MAX_VALUE_BYTES),
+        MAX_MIGRATION_PAGE_BYTES
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        page_limit(0, DEFAULT_MAX_VALUE_BYTES),
+        DEFAULT_MAX_VALUE_BYTES
+    );
+}

+async fn unavailable_follower_backpressures_before_unbounded_queue_growth() {
+    let topology = TopologySnapshot::new_with_config(
+        1,
+        42,
+        8,
+        vec![
+            Member {
+                node_id: "node-1".into(),
+                endpoint: "http://127.0.0.1:1".into(),
+            },
+            Member {
+                node_id: "node-2".into(),
+                endpoint: "http://127.0.0.1:2".into(),
+            },
+        ],
+        TopologyConfig {
+            desired_replication_factor: 2,
+            write_availability_guard: WriteAvailabilityGuard {
+                minimum_admitted_copies: 1,
+                minimum_healthy_followers: 0,
+                ..WriteAvailabilityGuard::default()
+            },
+            ..TopologyConfig::default()
+        },
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    let owner = service_for("node-1", topology.clone());
+    let key = key_with_placement(&topology, |replicas| replicas[0] == "node-1");
+    let mut successful = 0;
+    let rejected = loop {
+        let response = owner
+            .put(Request::new(PutRequest {
+                key: key.clone(),
+                value: vec![successful as u8],
+                topology_epoch: 1,
+                request_id: format!("put-{successful}"),
+                expires_at_unix_millis: None,
+                preserve_value: false,
+                ..Default::default()
+            }))
+            .await
+            .unwrap()
+            .into_inner();
+        if let Some(error) = response.error {
+            break error;
+        }
+        successful += 1;
+        // Backpressure is bounded by the per-stream channel plus at most one
+        // in-flight replication batch that the delivery task drained before
+        // blocking on the unavailable follower.
+        assert!(
+            successful <= DEFAULT_REPLICATION_STREAM_QUEUE_CAPACITY + REPLICATION_BATCH_MAX_ENTRIES
+        );
+    };
+
+    assert_eq!(rejected.code, ErrorCode::ResourceExhausted as i32);
+    let pressure = owner
+        .get_process_info(Request::new(proto::Empty {}))
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner();
+    assert_eq!(pressure.replication_reservation_rejections, 1);
+    assert_eq!(
+        pressure.replication_stream_peak_pending,
+        DEFAULT_REPLICATION_STREAM_QUEUE_CAPACITY as u64
+    );
+    let state = owner.state.read().await;
+    assert_eq!(state.next_sequence, successful as u64);
+    assert_eq!(
+        state.records[key.as_slice()].version.owner_sequence,
+        successful as u64
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        state.owner_stream_sequences.values().copied().next(),
+        Some(successful as u64)
+    );
+}

+#[tokio::test]

+    let service = service();

+    let old = (0, "old-follower".to_owned());
+    let orphan = (0, "orphan-instance".to_owned());
+    let current = (current_epoch, "current-follower".to_owned());
+    for stream in [&old, &current] {
+        state
+            .ack_progress
+            .insert(stream.clone(), watch::channel(1).0);
+        state
+            .ack_process_instances
+            .insert(stream.clone(), "process".into());
+    }
+    // An identity can require retirement even without a corresponding sender.
+    state
+        .ack_process_instances
+        .insert(orphan.clone(), "process".into());
+    let version = RecordVersion {
+        topology_epoch: 0,
+        owner_sequence: 1,
+        owner_node_id: "node-1".into(),
+    };
+    insert_dedup_until(
+        &mut state,
+        "live".into(),
+        Arc::from(&b"key"[..]),
+        [0; 32],
+        version,
+        false,
+        Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(60),
+    );
+    state.dedup.get_mut("live").unwrap().required_acks = vec![(0, old.1.clone(), 1)];
+    prune_ack_progress(&mut state);
+    assert!(state.ack_progress.contains_key(&old));
+    assert!(state.ack_process_instances.contains_key(&old));
+    assert!(!state.ack_process_instances.contains_key(&orphan));
+    assert!(state.ack_progress.contains_key(&current));

+    state.dedup.get_mut("live").unwrap().required_acks.clear();
+    prune_ack_progress(&mut state);
+    assert!(!state.ack_progress.contains_key(&old));

+// Run alone: RSS is process-wide and requires the Unix `ps` utility.
+#[tokio::test]
+#[ignore = "isolated RSS regression check; run with --ignored --nocapture"]
+async fn unreachable_streams_do_not_copy_unbudgeted_payloads() {
+    fn rss_kib() -> usize {
+        let output = std::process::Command::new("ps")
+            .args(["-o", "rss=", "-p", &std::process::id().to_string()])
+            .output()
+            .unwrap();
+        assert!(output.status.success());
+        String::from_utf8(output.stdout)
+            .unwrap()
+            .trim()
+            .parse()
+            .unwrap()
+    }
+    let service = service_for("node-1", replication_topology(3));
+    let mutation = Arc::new(ReplicationMutation {
+        topology_epoch: 1,
+        owner_node_id: "node-1".into(),
+        key: Arc::from(b"memory-reproduction".as_slice()),
+        value: Arc::from(vec![7_u8; 8 * 1024 * 1024]),
+        deleted: false,
+        version: RecordVersion {
+            topology_epoch: 1,
+            owner_sequence: 1,
+            owner_node_id: "node-1".into(),
+        },
+        mutation_id: "memory-reproduction".into(),
+        expires_at_unix_millis: None,
+        request_fingerprint: [0; 32],
+    });
+    let bytes = replication_mutation_bytes(&mutation);
+    let retained = Arc::new(Semaphore::new(DEFAULT_MAX_PENDING_REPLICATION_BYTES));
+    let budget = Arc::new(ReplicationBudget {
+        _permit: retained
+            .clone()
+            .acquire_many_owned(bytes as u32)
+            .await
+            .unwrap(),
+    });
+    let active = Arc::new(Semaphore::new(DEFAULT_MAX_PENDING_REPLICATION_BYTES));
+    let failed = Arc::new(StdMutex::new(HashSet::new()));
+    let before = rss_kib();
+    let mut tasks = Vec::new();
+    for index in 0..32 {
+        let follower = format!("follower-{index}");
+        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::channel(1);
+        sender
+            .send(PendingReplication {
+                prepared: PreparedReplication {
+                    follower_node_id: follower.clone(),
+                    follower_endpoint: "http://127.0.0.1:1".into(),
+                    stream_sequence: 1,
+                    mutation: mutation.clone(),
+                    ack_awaited: false,
+                },
+                _budget: budget.clone(),
+            })
+            .await
+            .unwrap();
+        tasks.push(tokio::spawn(deliver_replication_stream(
+            ReplicationStream {
+                state: service.state.clone(),
+                failed_streams: failed.clone(),
+                active_rpc_budget: active.clone(),
+                rpc_timeout: DEFAULT_REPLICATION_RPC_TIMEOUT,
+                batch_linger: std::time::Duration::ZERO,
+                pressure: service.pressure.clone(),
+                stream_key: (1, "node-1".into(), follower),
+                entries: receiver,
+            },
+        )));
+    }
+    tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(500)).await;
+    let growth = rss_kib().saturating_sub(before);
+    eprintln!(
+        "32 unreachable streams, shared 8 MiB payload: RSS growth {growth} KiB; active permits {}",
+        active.available_permits()
+    );
+    for task in tasks {
+        task.abort();
+        let _ = task.await;
+    }
+    assert_eq!(
+        active.available_permits(),
+        DEFAULT_MAX_PENDING_REPLICATION_BYTES
+    );
+    assert!(
+        growth < DEFAULT_MAX_PENDING_REPLICATION_BYTES / 1024,
+        "unbudgeted payload growth: {growth} KiB"
+    );
+}

+#[tokio::test]
+async fn delivery_publishes_partial_ack_and_retries_suffix_after_capacity_returns() {
+    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
+    let mut topology = replication_topology(2);
+    topology
+        .members
+        .iter_mut()
+        .find(|member| member.node_id == "node-2")
+        .unwrap()
+        .endpoint = format!("http://{}", listener.local_addr().unwrap());
+    let key = key_with_placement(&topology, |replicas| {
+        replicas[0] == "node-1" && replicas[1] == "node-2"
+    });
+    let mut follower = service_for("node-2", topology.clone());
+    follower.max_dedup_bytes = dedup_retained_bytes("mutation-1", key.len(), "node-1".len());
+    let follower_state = follower.state.clone();
+    let server = tokio::spawn(
+        tonic::transport::Server::builder()
+            .add_service(proto::data_node_server::DataNodeServer::new(follower))
+            .serve_with_incoming(tokio_stream::wrappers::TcpListenerStream::new(listener)),
+    );
+    let owner = service_for("node-1", topology.clone());
+    let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::channel(2);
+    let retained = Arc::new(Semaphore::new(DEFAULT_MAX_PENDING_REPLICATION_BYTES));
+    let mut state = owner.state.write().await;
+    for sequence in 1..=2 {
+        let version = RecordVersion {
+            topology_epoch: topology.epoch,
+            owner_sequence: sequence,
+            owner_node_id: "node-1".into(),
+        };
+        let token = topology.key_token(&key);
+        let prepared = prepare_replication_entries(
+            &mut state,
+            ReplicationWrite {
+                key: &key,
+                record: &value_record(&[sequence as u8], &version),
+                request_fingerprint: [sequence as u8; 32],
+                mutation_id: format!("mutation-{sequence}"),
+                token,
+                max_pending_bytes: DEFAULT_MAX_PENDING_REPLICATION_BYTES,
+                ack_awaited_followers: &[],
+            },
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+        .pop()
+        .unwrap();
+        let bytes = replication_mutation_bytes(&prepared.mutation);
+        sender
+            .send(PendingReplication {
+                prepared,
+                _budget: Arc::new(ReplicationBudget {
+                    _permit: retained
+                        .clone()
+                        .acquire_many_owned(bytes as u32)
+                        .await
+                        .unwrap(),
+                }),
+            })
+            .await
+            .unwrap();
+    }
+    let stream = (topology.epoch, "node-2".to_owned());
+    state
+        .owner_stream_unacked
+        .insert(stream.clone(), [(1, 0), (2, 0)].into());
+    let mut progress = state.ack_progress[&stream].subscribe();
+    drop(state);
+    drop(sender);
+    let failed = Arc::new(StdMutex::new(HashSet::new()));
+    let active = Arc::new(Semaphore::new(DEFAULT_MAX_PENDING_REPLICATION_BYTES));
+    let delivery = tokio::spawn(deliver_replication_stream(ReplicationStream {
+        state: owner.state.clone(),
+        failed_streams: failed.clone(),
+        active_rpc_budget: active.clone(),
+        rpc_timeout: DEFAULT_REPLICATION_RPC_TIMEOUT,
+        batch_linger: std::time::Duration::ZERO,
+        pressure: owner.pressure.clone(),
+        stream_key: (topology.epoch, "node-1".into(), "node-2".into()),
+        entries: receiver,
+    }));
+    tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(3), async {
+        loop {
+            if *progress.borrow_and_update() == 1 {
+                break;
+            }
+            progress.changed().await.unwrap();
+        }
+        while owner
+            .pressure
+            .replication_rpc_retries
+            .load(AtomicOrdering::Relaxed)
+            == 0
+        {
+            tokio::task::yield_now().await;
+        }
+    })
+    .await
+    .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(
+        owner.state.read().await.owner_stream_unacked[&stream]
+            .front()
+            .unwrap()
+            .0,
+        2
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        follower_state.read().await.records[key.as_slice()]
+            .value
+            .as_ref(),
+        &[1]
+    );
+    // Model receipt expiry freeing capacity while the failed suffix is pending.
+    {
+        let mut state = follower_state.write().await;
+        state.clear_dedup();
+        state.dedup_expirations.clear();
+        state.dedup_bytes = 0;
+    }
+    tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(3), delivery)
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(*progress.borrow(), 2);
+    assert!(owner.state.read().await.owner_stream_unacked[&stream].is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(
+        follower_state.read().await.records[key.as_slice()]
+            .value
+            .as_ref(),
+        &[2]
+    );
+    assert!(failed.lock().unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(
+        active.available_permits(),
+        DEFAULT_MAX_PENDING_REPLICATION_BYTES
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        retained.available_permits(),
+        DEFAULT_MAX_PENDING_REPLICATION_BYTES
+    );
+    server.abort();
+}

+async fn linger_test_entry(sequence: u64, ack_awaited: bool) -> PendingReplication {
+    let mutation = Arc::new(ReplicationMutation {
+        topology_epoch: 1,
+        owner_node_id: "node-1".into(),
+        key: Arc::from(format!("key-{sequence}").into_bytes()),
+        value: Arc::from(b"value".as_slice()),
+        deleted: false,
+        version: RecordVersion {
+            topology_epoch: 1,
+            owner_sequence: sequence,
+            owner_node_id: "node-1".into(),
+        },
+        mutation_id: format!("mutation-{sequence}"),
+        expires_at_unix_millis: None,
+        request_fingerprint: [0; 32],
+    });
+    let budget = Arc::new(Semaphore::new(1 << 20))
+        .acquire_many_owned(replication_mutation_bytes(&mutation) as u32)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    PendingReplication {
+        prepared: PreparedReplication {
+            follower_node_id: "node-2".into(),
+            follower_endpoint: "http://127.0.0.1:1".into(),
+            stream_sequence: sequence,
+            mutation,
+            ack_awaited,
+        },
+        _budget: Arc::new(ReplicationBudget { _permit: budget }),
+    }
+}

+/// Collects one batch whose first entry is queued at once and whose later
+/// entries arrive 1 ms after the start, returning the batch's sequences and
+/// how long collection took.
+async fn collect_with_late_entries(
+    linger_ms: u64,
+    first_awaited: bool,
+    late: &[(u64, bool)],
+) -> (Vec<u64>, std::time::Duration) {
+    let (sender, mut receiver) = mpsc::channel(8);
+    let first = linger_test_entry(1, first_awaited).await;
+    let late = late.to_vec();
+    tokio::spawn(async move {
+        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(1)).await;
+        for (sequence, awaited) in late {
+            sender
+                .send(linger_test_entry(sequence, awaited).await)
+                .await
+                .unwrap();
+        }
+        // Keep the stream open past any linger so closing never ends a batch.
+        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(1)).await;
+    });
+    let started = tokio::time::Instant::now();
+    let (batch, _, carry) = collect_replication_batch(
+        first,
+        &mut receiver,
+        std::time::Duration::from_millis(linger_ms),
+    )
+    .await;
+    assert!(carry.is_none());
+    let sequences = batch
+        .iter()
+        .map(|pending| pending.prepared.stream_sequence)
+        .collect();
+    (sequences, started.elapsed())
+}

+#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]
+async fn batch_linger_collects_entries_that_arrive_while_waiting() {
+    let ms = std::time::Duration::from_millis;
+    assert_eq!(
+        collect_with_late_entries(0, false, &[(2, false), (3, false)]).await,
+        (vec![1], ms(0))
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        collect_with_late_entries(5, false, &[(2, false), (3, false)]).await,
+        (vec![1, 2, 3], ms(5))
+    );
+}

+#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]
+async fn batch_linger_never_delays_an_acknowledged_write() {
+    let ms = std::time::Duration::from_millis;
+    // A first entry with a waiting write is sent at once.
+    assert_eq!(
+        collect_with_late_entries(5, true, &[(2, false)]).await,
+        (vec![1], ms(0))
+    );
+    // An awaited entry that arrives during the linger ends the wait; entries
+    // already queued behind it still join the batch.
+    assert_eq!(
+        collect_with_late_entries(5, false, &[(2, true), (3, false)]).await,
+        (vec![1, 2, 3], ms(1))
+    );
+}

+fn value_record(value: &[u8], version: &RecordVersion) -> Record {

+        value: Arc::from(value),
+        version: version.clone(),
+        deleted: false,
+        expires_at_unix_millis: None,
+    }

-/// How many scripts a gateway keeps for `EVALSHA`. A client's scripts are its

-/// Virtual-machine instructions a script may execute before it is stopped. A

-/// One attempt's private view of its declared key. The original version is

-            inner: Mutex::new(Snapshot {
-                expected: current.as_ref().map(|value| value.version.clone()),
-                current,
-                dirty: false,

-    fn check_key(&self, key: &[u8]) -> RedisResult<()> {

-/// `SCRIPT LOAD`, `SCRIPT EXISTS` and `SCRIPT FLUSH`.
-pub fn script_command(scripts: &Scripts, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
-    let subcommand = args.next_keyword().ok_or_else(RedisError::syntax)?;
-    let mut cache = scripts.cache();
-    match subcommand.as_str() {
-        "load" => {
-            let source = args.next_owned()?;
-            args.finish()?;
-            let hash = script::hash_hex(&source);
-            cache.remember(hash_of(&hash)?, &source);
-            Ok(Reply::bulk(hash))
-        }
-        "exists" => Ok(Reply::Array(
-            args.remaining()
-                .iter()
-                .map(|hash| match digest(hash) {
-                    Ok(hash) => Reply::Integer(i64::from(cache.knows(hash))),
-                    Err(error) => error.to_reply(),
-                })
-                .collect(),
-        )),
-        "flush" => {
-            args.finish()?;
-            cache.clear();
-            Ok(Reply::status())
-        }
-        other => Err(RedisError::new(
-            "ERR",
-            format!("Unknown subcommand or wrong number of arguments for 'SCRIPT {other}'"),
-        )),
-    }
-}

-/// Run a private single-key attempt and publish its final state once.
-async fn run(
-    scripts: &Scripts,
-    dispatcher: &Dispatcher,
-    connection: &Connection,
-    source: &[u8],
-    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
-    argv: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
-) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
-    if keys.len() > 1 {
-        return Err(RedisError::new(
-            "ERR",
-            "a script may declare at most one key",
-        ));
-    }
-    let _running = scripts.running.lock().await;
-
-    let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + dispatcher.command_timeout();
-    loop {
-        let client = match keys.first() {
-            Some(_) => Some(dispatcher.client.get().await?),
-            None => None,
-        };
-        let current = match keys.first() {
-            Some(key) => match client
-                .as_ref()
-                .expect("a declared key has a client")
-                .get(key.clone())
-                .await
-            {
-                Ok(value) => Some(Current {
-                    value: value.value,
-                    deadline: value.expires_at_unix_millis,
-                    version: value.version,
-                }),
-                Err(hashring_client::ClientError::Operation(failure))
-                    if failure.code == ErrorCode::NotFound =>
-                {
-                    None
-                }
-                Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
-            },
-            None => None,
-        };
-        let state = Arc::new(State::new(keys.first().cloned(), current));
-        let host = Host {
-            dispatcher: dispatcher.clone(),
-            connection: Connection {
-                authenticated: true,
-                ..connection.clone()
-            },
-            state: state.clone(),
-        };
-        let limits = Limits {
-            max_steps: MAX_STEPS,
-            timeout: deadline.saturating_duration_since(tokio::time::Instant::now()),
-        };
-        let mut runtime = scripts.take_runtime();
-        let answer = runtime
-            .run(host, source, keys.clone(), argv.clone(), limits)
-            .await;
-        scripts.put_runtime(runtime);
-        // Like Redis, an error after successful commands does not roll those
-        // commands back. Their staged effects still publish in one commit.
-        if let Some(client) = client
-            && !state.commit(&client).await?
-        {
-            tokio::task::yield_now().await;
-            continue;
-        }
-        return answer;
-    }
-}

-/// The bridge from the interpreter to the gateway: one command at a time,
-/// through the same dispatcher a connection uses.
-///
-/// The interpreter has already checked the command against the script's `KEYS`
-/// and against the command table, so what is left here is the gateway's own
-/// policy: commands that change the connection or bypass the private snapshot
-/// are refused.
-struct Host {
-    dispatcher: Dispatcher,
-    /// The connection a script sees, which is a copy of the client's rather
-    /// than the client's itself: nothing a script may run changes a connection,
-    /// so it has no business holding the real one while it runs.
-    connection: Connection,
-    state: Arc<State>,
-}
-
-impl script::Host for Host {
-    fn call(&mut self, command: &[Vec<u8>]) -> impl Future<Output = RedisResult<Reply>> + Send {
-        let dispatcher = self.dispatcher.clone();
-        let state = self.state.clone();
-        // The connection is copied rather than borrowed, so the future owns what
-        // it needs and nothing is held across the call but the copy.
-        let mut connection = self.connection.clone();
-        async move {
-            let name = command
-                .first()
-                .map(|name| keyword(name))
-                .unwrap_or_default();
-            if REFUSED.contains(&name.as_str()) {
-                return Err(RedisError::new(
-                    "ERR",
-                    format!("This command is not allowed from a script: {name}"),
-                ));
-            }
-            dispatcher
-                .execute_with_store(&mut connection, command, Some(state.as_ref()))
-                .await
-                .reply
-        }
-    }
-}

-/// The SHA-1 of a script as forty hex characters, read back into the twenty
-/// bytes it names.
-fn digest(hash: &[u8]) -> RedisResult<[u8; 20]> {
-    let hash = std::str::from_utf8(hash).map_err(|_| malformed_hash())?;
-    hash_of(hash)
-}
-
-fn hash_of(hash: &str) -> RedisResult<[u8; 20]> {
-    let malformed = || malformed_hash();
-    if hash.len() != 40 {
-        return Err(malformed());
-    }
-    let mut digest = [0_u8; 20];
-    for (index, byte) in digest.iter_mut().enumerate() {
-        *byte = u8::from_str_radix(&hash[index * 2..index * 2 + 2], 16).map_err(|_| malformed())?;
-    }
-    Ok(digest)
-}

-fn malformed_hash() -> RedisError {
-    RedisError::new(
-        "ERR",

+        flags: &["write"],
+        first_key: 0,
+        last_key: 0,
+        step: 0,
+        declined: false,
+        keyspace: false,
+    },
+    CommandInfo {
+        name: "script",
+        arity: -2,
+        flags: &["admin"],
+        first_key: 0,
+        last_key: 0,
+        step: 0,
+        declined: false,
+        keyspace: false,
+    },
+];
+
+impl CommandExtension for Scripts {
+    fn commands(&self) -> &'static [CommandInfo] {
+        COMMANDS
+    }
+
+    fn execute<'a>(
+        &'a self,
+        dispatcher: &'a Dispatcher,
+        connection: &'a mut Connection,
+        command: &'a CommandInfo,
+        arguments: &'a [Vec<u8>],
+    ) -> BoxFuture<'a, RedisResult<Reply>> {
+        Box::pin(async move {
+            let args = Args::new(command.name, arguments);
+            match command.name {
+                "script" => script_command(self, args),
+                _ => eval(self, dispatcher, connection, command, args).await,
+            }
+        })
+    }
+}
+
+/// How many scripts a gateway keeps for `EVALSHA`. A client's scripts are its
+/// own few texts, so the cache is small; it is bounded so that a client loading
+/// scripts it never runs again cannot grow it without limit.
+const CACHED_SCRIPTS: usize = 512;
+
+/// Virtual-machine instructions a script may execute before it is stopped. A
+/// cache key claim is two statements and a rate limiter's `INCR` with its
+/// deadline is four more, so this is orders of magnitude above anything a
+/// client library sends.
+const MAX_STEPS: usize = 10_000_000;
+
+/// The scripts this gateway has seen, and the lock that runs one at a time.
+#[derive(Default)]
+pub struct Scripts {
+    /// One script at a time per extension. Cross-gateway exclusion is supplied
+    /// by the final conditional commit, rather than a local key lock.
+    running: AsyncMutex<()>,
+    sources: Mutex<Cached>,
+    /// The Lua state every script runs in, taken out for the length of a run
+    /// rather than borrowed, so holding it never waits on a lock that is held
+    /// across a `.await`.
+    runtime: Mutex<Option<script::Runtime>>,
+}
+
+#[derive(Default)]
+pub(crate) struct Cached {
+    by_hash: HashMap<[u8; 20], Arc<[u8]>>,
+    /// The order scripts arrived in, so the oldest is the one to drop.
+    order: VecDeque<[u8; 20]>,
+}
+
+impl Scripts {
+    /// The scripts seen so far, which is what `SCRIPT EXISTS` and `SCRIPT
+    /// FLUSH` read and write.
+    pub(crate) fn cache(&self) -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, Cached> {
+        self.sources.lock().expect("a script's own lock")
+    }
+
+    /// Keeps a script's source under the hash `EVALSHA` will ask for.
+    pub fn remember(&self, source: &[u8]) -> Arc<[u8]> {
+        self.sources
+            .lock()
+            .expect("a script's own lock")
+            .remember(script::digest(source), source);
+        Arc::from(source)
+    }
+
+    pub fn cached(&self, hash: [u8; 20]) -> Option<Arc<[u8]>> {
+        self.sources
+            .lock()
+            .expect("a script's own lock")
+            .source(hash)
+    }
+
+    /// The Lua state for the length of one run. It is taken out rather than
+    /// borrowed so that no lock is held while the script runs.
+    pub(crate) fn take_runtime(&self) -> script::Runtime {
+        self.runtime
+            .lock()
+            .expect("a script's own lock")
+            .take()
+            .unwrap_or_default()
+    }
+
+    pub(crate) fn put_runtime(&self, runtime: script::Runtime) {
+        *self.runtime.lock().expect("a script's own lock") = Some(runtime);
+    }
+}
+
+impl Cached {
+    /// Keeps a script's source under the hash `EVALSHA` will ask for, which is
+    /// what Redis does with `EVAL` as well as with `SCRIPT LOAD`.
+    fn remember(&mut self, hash: [u8; 20], source: &[u8]) {
+        if self.by_hash.insert(hash, Arc::from(source)).is_none() {
+            self.order.push_back(hash);
+        }
+        while self.order.len() > CACHED_SCRIPTS {
+            if let Some(oldest) = self.order.pop_front() {
+                self.by_hash.remove(&oldest);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn source(&self, hash: [u8; 20]) -> Option<Arc<[u8]>> {
+        self.by_hash.get(&hash).cloned()
+    }
+
+    fn knows(&self, hash: [u8; 20]) -> bool {
+        self.by_hash.contains_key(&hash)
+    }
+
+    fn clear(&mut self) {
+        self.by_hash.clear();
+        self.order.clear();
+    }
+}
+
+/// One attempt's private view of its declared key. The original version is
+/// immutable; staged writes only replace `current`.
+pub struct State {
+    key: Option<Vec<u8>>,
+    inner: Mutex<Snapshot>,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone)]
+struct Snapshot {
+    expected: Option<RecordVersion>,
+    current: Option<Current>,
+    dirty: bool,
+}
+
+impl State {
+    fn new(key: Option<Vec<u8>>, current: Option<Current>) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            key,
+            inner: Mutex::new(Snapshot {
+                expected: current.as_ref().map(|value| value.version.clone()),
+                current,
+                dirty: false,
+            }),
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn check_key(&self, key: &[u8]) -> RedisResult<()> {
+        if self.key.as_deref() != Some(key) {
+            return Err(RedisError::new(
+                "ERR",
+                "a script may only touch its declared key",
+            ));
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+
+    pub fn read(&self, key: &[u8]) -> RedisResult<Option<Current>> {
+        self.check_key(key)?;
+        Ok(self
+            .inner
+            .lock()
+            .expect("a script's own lock")
+            .current
+            .clone())
+    }
+
+    /// Only this operation can publish a script's changes. A failed condition
+    /// writes nothing, so the complete attempt can safely be repeated.
+    async fn commit(&self, client: &HashringClient) -> RedisResult<bool> {
+        let snapshot = self.inner.lock().expect("a script's own lock").clone();
+        if !snapshot.dirty {
+            return Ok(true);
+        }
+        let key = self.key.clone().expect("a staged write has a declared key");
+        let expected = snapshot
+            .expected
+            .map_or(Precondition::Absent, Precondition::Version);
+        Ok(match snapshot.current {
+            Some(current) => client
+                .put_if(key, current.value, expiry(current.deadline), expected)
+                .await?
+                .is_some(),
+            None => client.delete_if(key, expected).await?.is_some(),
+        })
+    }
+}
+
+impl Overlay for State {
+    fn read(&self, key: &[u8]) -> RedisResult<Option<Current>> {
+        State::read(self, key)
+    }
+
+    fn write(&self, key: &[u8], value: Option<Current>) -> RedisResult<()> {
+        self.check_key(key)?;
+        if value
+            .as_ref()
+            .is_some_and(|current| current.value.len() > MAX_VALUE_BYTES)
+        {
+            return Err(RedisError::new("ERR", "value exceeds the cluster ceiling"));
+        }
+        let mut snapshot = self.inner.lock().expect("a script's own lock");
+        snapshot.current = value;
+        snapshot.dirty = true;
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}
+
+/// `EVAL script numkeys key... arg...`, and `EVALSHA` with the hash in place of
+/// the script.
+pub async fn eval(
+    scripts: &Scripts,
+    dispatcher: &Dispatcher,
+    connection: &mut Connection,
+    command: &CommandInfo,
+    args: Args<'_>,
+) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let rest = args.remaining();
+    let Some((script, tail)) = rest.split_first() else {
+        return Err(RedisError::syntax());
+    };
+    let source = match command.name {
+        "evalsha" => {
+            let source = scripts.cached(digest(script)?).ok_or_else(no_such_script)?;
+            scripts.remember(&source);
+            source
+        }
+        _ => scripts.remember(script),
+    };
+    let (keys, argv) = keys_and_arguments(tail)?;
+    run(scripts, dispatcher, connection, &source, keys, argv).await
+}
+
+/// `SCRIPT LOAD`, `SCRIPT EXISTS` and `SCRIPT FLUSH`.
+pub fn script_command(scripts: &Scripts, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let subcommand = args.next_keyword().ok_or_else(RedisError::syntax)?;
+    let mut cache = scripts.cache();
+    match subcommand.as_str() {
+        "load" => {
+            let source = args.next_owned()?;
+            args.finish()?;
+            let hash = script::hash_hex(&source);
+            cache.remember(hash_of(&hash)?, &source);
+            Ok(Reply::bulk(hash))
+        }
+        "exists" => Ok(Reply::Array(
+            args.remaining()
+                .iter()
+                .map(|hash| match digest(hash) {
+                    Ok(hash) => Reply::Integer(i64::from(cache.knows(hash))),
+                    Err(error) => error.to_reply(),
+                })
+                .collect(),
+        )),
+        "flush" => {
+            args.finish()?;
+            cache.clear();
+            Ok(Reply::status())
+        }
+        other => Err(RedisError::new(
+            "ERR",
+            format!("Unknown subcommand or wrong number of arguments for 'SCRIPT {other}'"),
+        )),
+    }
+}
+
+/// Run a private single-key attempt and publish its final state once.
+async fn run(
+    scripts: &Scripts,
+    dispatcher: &Dispatcher,
+    connection: &Connection,
+    source: &[u8],
+    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
+    argv: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
+) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    if keys.len() > 1 {
+        return Err(RedisError::new(
+            "ERR",
+            "a script may declare at most one key",
+        ));
+    }
+    let _running = scripts.running.lock().await;
+
+    let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + dispatcher.command_timeout();
+    loop {
+        let client = match keys.first() {
+            Some(_) => Some(dispatcher.client.get().await?),
+            None => None,
+        };
+        let current = match keys.first() {
+            Some(key) => match client
+                .as_ref()
+                .expect("a declared key has a client")
+                .get(key.clone())
+                .await
+            {
+                Ok(value) => Some(Current {
+                    value: value.value,
+                    deadline: value.expires_at_unix_millis,
+                    version: value.version,
+                }),
+                Err(hashring_client::ClientError::Operation(failure))
+                    if failure.code == ErrorCode::NotFound =>
+                {
+                    None
+                }
+                Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
+            },
+            None => None,
+        };
+        let state = Arc::new(State::new(keys.first().cloned(), current));
+        let host = Host {
+            dispatcher: dispatcher.clone(),
+            connection: Connection {
+                authenticated: true,
+                ..connection.clone()
+            },
+            state: state.clone(),
+        };
+        let limits = Limits {
+            max_steps: MAX_STEPS,
+            timeout: deadline.saturating_duration_since(tokio::time::Instant::now()),
+        };
+        let mut runtime = scripts.take_runtime();
+        let answer = runtime
+            .run(host, source, keys.clone(), argv.clone(), limits)
+            .await;
+        scripts.put_runtime(runtime);
+        // Like Redis, an error after successful commands does not roll those
+        // commands back. Their staged effects still publish in one commit.
+        if let Some(client) = client
+            && !state.commit(&client).await?
+        {
+            tokio::task::yield_now().await;
+            continue;
+        }
+        return answer;
+    }
+}
+
+/// The keys a script declared and the arguments it was given.
+type Split = (Vec<Vec<u8>>, Vec<Vec<u8>>);
+
+/// The keys and the arguments of `numkeys key... arg...`.
+fn keys_and_arguments(tail: &[Vec<u8>]) -> RedisResult<Split> {
+    let Some(count) = tail.first().and_then(|value| parse_integer(value)) else {
+        return Err(RedisError::syntax());
+    };
+    if !(0..=(tail.len() as i64 - 1)).contains(&count) {
+        return Err(RedisError::new(
+            "ERR",
+            "Number of keys can't be greater than number of args passed",
+        ));
+    }
+    let count = count as usize;
+    Ok((tail[1..1 + count].to_vec(), tail[1 + count..].to_vec()))
+}
+
+/// The bridge from the interpreter to the gateway: one command at a time,
+/// through the same dispatcher a connection uses.
+///
+/// The interpreter has already checked the command against the script's `KEYS`
+/// and against the command table, so what is left here is the gateway's own
+/// policy: commands that change the connection or bypass the private snapshot
+/// are refused.
+struct Host {
+    dispatcher: Dispatcher,
+    /// The connection a script sees, which is a copy of the client's rather
+    /// than the client's itself: nothing a script may run changes a connection,
+    /// so it has no business holding the real one while it runs.
+    connection: Connection,
+    state: Arc<State>,
+}
+
+impl script::Host for Host {
+    fn call(&mut self, command: &[Vec<u8>]) -> impl Future<Output = RedisResult<Reply>> + Send {
+        let dispatcher = self.dispatcher.clone();
+        let state = self.state.clone();
+        // The connection is copied rather than borrowed, so the future owns what
+        // it needs and nothing is held across the call but the copy.
+        let mut connection = self.connection.clone();
+        async move {
+            let name = command
+                .first()
+                .map(|name| keyword(name))
+                .unwrap_or_default();
+            if REFUSED.contains(&name.as_str()) {
+                return Err(RedisError::new(
+                    "ERR",
+                    format!("This command is not allowed from a script: {name}"),
+                ));
+            }
+            dispatcher
+                .execute_with_store(&mut connection, command, Some(state.as_ref()))
+                .await
+                .reply
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// The SHA-1 of a script as forty hex characters, read back into the twenty
+/// bytes it names.
+fn digest(hash: &[u8]) -> RedisResult<[u8; 20]> {
+    let hash = std::str::from_utf8(hash).map_err(|_| malformed_hash())?;
+    hash_of(hash)
+}
+
+fn hash_of(hash: &str) -> RedisResult<[u8; 20]> {
+    let malformed = || malformed_hash();
+    if hash.len() != 40 {
+        return Err(malformed());
+    }
+    let mut digest = [0_u8; 20];
+    for (index, byte) in digest.iter_mut().enumerate() {
+        *byte = u8::from_str_radix(&hash[index * 2..index * 2 + 2], 16).map_err(|_| malformed())?;
+    }
+    Ok(digest)
+}
+
+fn malformed_hash() -> RedisError {
+    RedisError::new(
+        "ERR",
+        "SCRIPT LOAD and EVALSHA need the script's SHA-1 as forty hexadecimal characters",
+    )
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+
+    #[test]
+    fn the_keys_come_before_the_arguments() {
+        let tail: Vec<Vec<u8>> = ["2", "a", "b", "one", "two"]
+            .iter()
+            .map(|part| part.as_bytes().to_vec())
+            .collect();
+        let (keys, argv) = keys_and_arguments(&tail).unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(keys, vec![b"a".to_vec(), b"b".to_vec()]);
+        assert_eq!(argv, vec![b"one".to_vec(), b"two".to_vec()]);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_script_with_no_keys_may_carry_only_arguments() {
+        let tail: Vec<Vec<u8>> = ["0", "one"].iter().map(|p| p.as_bytes().to_vec()).collect();
+        let (keys, argv) = keys_and_arguments(&tail).unwrap();
+        assert!(keys.is_empty());
+        assert_eq!(argv, vec![b"one".to_vec()]);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_key_count_the_arguments_do_not_cover_is_an_error() {
+        for tail in [vec!["3"], vec!["-1"], vec!["x"], vec!["2", "a"]] {
+            let tail: Vec<Vec<u8>> = tail.iter().map(|p| p.as_bytes().to_vec()).collect();
+            assert!(keys_and_arguments(&tail).is_err(), "{tail:?}");
+        }
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_hash_is_read_the_way_a_client_sends_it() {
+        let source = b"return 1";
+        let hex = script::hash_hex(source);
+        assert_eq!(hash_of(&hex).unwrap(), script::digest(source));
+        assert!(hash_of("too short").is_err());
+        assert!(hash_of(&"z".repeat(40)).is_err());
+        // Redis reads either case, and so does this.
+        assert_eq!(
+            hash_of(&hex.to_uppercase()).unwrap(),
+            hash_of(&hex).unwrap()
+        );
+    }
+}

-async fn run<H: Host + Send + 'static>(
-    lua: &Lua,
-    host: H,
-    source: &[u8],
-    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
-    argv: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
-    limits: Limits,
-) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
-    let program = lua.load(source).set_name("user_script");
-    let budget = Budget::new(limits);
-    let watched = budget.clone();
-    // The script runs on its own coroutine, and the hook is set on that
-    // coroutine rather than the main thread: a hook on the main thread never
-    // fires while a coroutine runs, which is what let a runaway script loop
-    // forever under the old hand-written interpreter.
-    let function = execute(lua, program, host, keys, argv)?;
-    let thread = lua
-        .create_thread(function)
-        .map_err(|error| internal(format!("the script could not be watched: {error}")))?;
-    thread
-        .set_hook(
-            HookTriggers::new()
-                .every_nth_instruction(u32::try_from(CHECK_INTERVAL).unwrap_or(1_000)),
-            move |_, _| watched.check(),
-        )
-        .map_err(|error| internal(format!("the script could not be watched: {error}")))?;
-    let keep = thread.clone();
-    let answer = match thread.into_async::<MultiValue>(()) {
-        Ok(pending) => pending.await.map_err(script_failure),
-        Err(error) => Err(script_failure(error)),
-    };
-    keep.remove_hook();
-    match answer {
-        Ok(values) => reply_of(values),
-        Err(error) => Err(error),
-    }
-}

-/// What a script is allowed to compute, and for how long.
-#[derive(Clone)]
-struct Budget {
-    /// Instructions the run has left.
-    left: Arc<AtomicU64>,
-    timeout: Duration,
-    until: Instant,
-}
-
-impl Budget {
-    fn new(limits: Limits) -> Self {
-        Self {
-            left: Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(limits.max_steps as u64)),
-            timeout: limits.timeout,
-            until: Instant::now() + limits.timeout,
-        }
-    }
-
-    /// Runs on every instruction the hook sees. Returning an error from a Lua
-    /// hook is what aborts the script, with this message.
-    fn check(&self) -> mlua::Result<VmState> {
-        let spent = self.left.fetch_sub(CHECK_INTERVAL, Ordering::Relaxed);
-        if spent <= CHECK_INTERVAL {
-            return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(
-                "this script exceeded its maximum number of steps",
-            ));
-        }
-        if Instant::now() >= self.until {
-            return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(format!(
-                "this script was stopped after {}ms, which is longer than the deadline its \
-                 command was given",
-                self.timeout.as_millis()
-            )));
-        }
-        Ok(VmState::Continue)
-    }
-}

-/// Builds the environment one script runs in, and answers with the function
-/// that runs there. The coroutine it runs on is made by the caller, which is
-/// also what watches it.
-fn execute<H: Host + Send + 'static>(
-    lua: &Lua,
-    program: mlua::chunk::Chunk<'_>,
-    host: H,
-    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
-    argv: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
-) -> Result<mlua::Function, RedisError> {
-    // Every command this script may run goes through here, and the handle is
-    // what lets Lua's own call be `async`: the virtual machine suspends at
-    // `redis.call` while the cluster is asked.
-    let host = Arc::new(Mutex::new(host));
-    let declared = Arc::new(keys.clone());
-
-    let globals = lua.globals();
-    let environment = lua.create_table().map_err(setup_failure)?;
-    // A script reads the standard library through the globals, and keeps
-    // whatever it writes to itself, so nothing it defines outlives the run.
-    let metatable = lua.create_table().map_err(setup_failure)?;
-    metatable.set("__index", globals).map_err(setup_failure)?;
-    environment
-        .set_metatable(Some(metatable))
-        .map_err(setup_failure)?;
-    environment
-        .set("KEYS", list(lua, &keys).map_err(setup_failure)?)
-        .map_err(setup_failure)?;
-    environment
-        .set("ARGV", list(lua, &argv).map_err(setup_failure)?)
-        .map_err(setup_failure)?;
-    environment
-        .set(
-            "redis",
-            commands(lua, &host, &declared).map_err(setup_failure)?,
-        )
-        .map_err(setup_failure)?;
-
-    program
-        .set_environment(environment)
-        .into_function()
-        .map_err(script_failure)
-}

-/// The `redis` table: what a script may ask of the cluster.
-fn commands<H: Host + Send + 'static>(
-    lua: &Lua,
-    host: &Arc<Mutex<H>>,
-    declared: &Arc<Vec<Vec<u8>>>,
-) -> mlua::Result<Table> {
-    let table = lua.create_table().map_err(lua_failure)?;
-
-    let raising = host.clone();
-    let keys = declared.clone();
-    let call = lua
-        .create_async_function(move |lua, arguments: MultiValue| {
-            let host = raising.clone();
-            let declared = keys.clone();
-            async move {
-                // A command that answers with an error is an error to the
-                // script, the way `redis.call` treats it.
-                match run_command(&host, &declared, arguments).await {
-                    Err(error) => Err(mlua::Error::external(error)),
-                    Ok(Reply::Error(message)) => {
-                        Err(mlua::Error::runtime(script_error(message).message))
-                    }
-                    Ok(reply) => into_lua(&lua, reply),
-                }
-            }
-        })
-        .map_err(lua_failure)?;
-    table.set("call", call).map_err(lua_failure)?;
-
-    let catching = host.clone();
-    let keys = declared.clone();
-    let pcall = lua
-        .create_async_function(move |lua, arguments: MultiValue| {
-            let host = catching.clone();
-            let declared = keys.clone();
-            async move {
-                let answer = match run_command(&host, &declared, arguments).await {
-                    Ok(Reply::Error(message)) => Err(message),
-                    Ok(reply) => into_lua(&lua, reply).map_err(|error| error.to_string()),
-                    Err(error) => Err(error.message),
-                };
-                Ok::<MultiValue, mlua::Error>(match answer {
-                    Ok(value) => MultiValue::from_iter([value]),
-                    // `redis.pcall` answers with the error rather than raising
-                    // it, which is what a script that wants to try twice needs.
-                    Err(message) => MultiValue::from_iter([failed(&lua, message)?]),
-                })
-            }
-        })
-        .map_err(lua_failure)?;
-    table.set("pcall", pcall).map_err(lua_failure)?;
-
-    let error_reply = lua
-        .create_function(|lua, message: String| failed(lua, message))
-        .map_err(lua_failure)?;
-    table.set("error_reply", error_reply).map_err(lua_failure)?;
-
-    let status_reply = lua
-        .create_function(|lua, message: String| {
-            let table = lua.create_table()?;
-            table.set("ok", message)?;
-            Ok(Value::Table(table))
-        })
-        .map_err(lua_failure)?;
-    table
-        .set("status_reply", status_reply)
-        .map_err(lua_failure)?;
-
-    let sha1hex = lua
-        .create_function(|_, argument: mlua::LuaString| Ok(hash_hex(argument.as_bytes().as_ref())))
-        .map_err(lua_failure)?;
-    table.set("sha1hex", sha1hex).map_err(lua_failure)?;
-
-    Ok(table)
-}

-/// One command from a script, checked against the keys it declared and then run
-/// against the cluster.
-async fn run_command<H: Host + Send + 'static>(
-    host: &Arc<Mutex<H>>,
-    declared: &Arc<Vec<Vec<u8>>>,
-    arguments: MultiValue,
-) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
-    let command = command_line(arguments).map_err(script_failure)?;
-    check_declared(declared, &command)?;
-    let mut host = host.lock().await;
-    host.call(&command).await
-}
-
-/// Every key the command will touch must be one the script declared.
-///
-/// The positions come from the command table, which already says where the
-/// keys are for `COMMAND`, so this reads the same table rather than keeping a
-/// second list that could disagree with it.
-fn check_declared(declared: &[Vec<u8>], command: &[Vec<u8>]) -> RedisResult<()> {
-    let Some(name) = command.first() else {
-        return Ok(());
-    };
-    let spelled = String::from_utf8_lossy(name);
-    let Some(info) = crate::table::lookup(&spelled.to_ascii_lowercase()) else {
-        return Err(script_error(format!("unknown command '{spelled}'")));
-    };
-    let name = spelled.to_ascii_lowercase();
-    for key in info.keys(command) {
-        if !declared.iter().any(|one| one.as_slice() == key) {
-            return Err(script_error(format!(
-                "the command '{name}' touches '{}', which this script did not \
-                 declare in KEYS; a script here may only touch the keys it \
-                 declares",
-                String::from_utf8_lossy(key)
-            )));
-        }
-    }
-    Ok(())
-}

-/// The arguments a script passed, as a command line. A table is expanded into
-/// the several arguments it holds, as Redis expands it.
-fn command_line(arguments: MultiValue) -> mlua::Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>> {
-    let mut line = Vec::with_capacity(arguments.len());
-    for argument in arguments {
-        match argument {
-            Value::String(text) => line.push(text.as_bytes().as_ref().to_vec()),
-            Value::Integer(number) => line.push(number.to_string().into_bytes()),
-            Value::Number(number) => line.push(number_text(number).into_bytes()),
-            Value::Table(table) => {
-                for index in 1..=table.raw_len() {
-                    line.push(argument_text(table.raw_get::<Value>(index)?)?);
-                }
-            }
-            other => {
-                return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(format!(
-                    "Lua redis lib command arguments must be strings or integers (got {})",
-                    other.type_name()
-                )));
-            }
-        }
-    }
-    Ok(line)
-}
-
-fn argument_text(value: Value) -> mlua::Result<Vec<u8>> {
-    match value {
-        Value::String(text) => Ok(text.as_bytes().as_ref().to_vec()),
-        Value::Integer(number) => Ok(number.to_string().into_bytes()),
-        Value::Number(number) => Ok(number_text(number).into_bytes()),
-        Value::Table(table) => {
-            let mut joined = Vec::new();
-            for index in 1..=table.raw_len() {
-                joined.push(argument_text(table.raw_get::<Value>(index)?)?);
-            }
-            Ok(joined.join(&b" "[..]))
-        }
-        other => Err(mlua::Error::runtime(format!(
-            "Lua redis lib command arguments must be strings or integers (got {})",
-            other.type_name()
-        ))),
-    }
-}
-
-/// A Lua number as its shortest exact text, which is what a client means when
-/// it passes one.
-fn number_text(number: f64) -> String {
-    if number.is_finite() && number.fract() == 0.0 && number.abs() < 9.007_199_254_740_992e15 {
-        format!("{}", number as i64)
-    } else {
-        format!("{number}")
-    }
-}
-
-/// `KEYS` and `ARGV` as Lua sees them: byte strings, indexed from one.
-fn list(lua: &Lua, values: &[Vec<u8>]) -> mlua::Result<Table> {
-    let table = lua.create_table().map_err(lua_failure)?;
-    for (index, value) in values.iter().enumerate() {
-        table
-            .set(
-                index + 1,
-                Value::String(lua.create_string(value).map_err(lua_failure)?),
-            )
-            .map_err(lua_failure)?;
-    }
-    Ok(table)
-}
-
-/// The `err` table `redis.pcall` and `redis.error_reply` answer with.
-fn failed(lua: &Lua, message: String) -> mlua::Result<Value> {
-    let table = lua.create_table()?;
-    table.set("err", message)?;
-    Ok(Value::Table(table))
-}
-
-/// What the cluster answered, as Lua sees it. A missing value is `false`,
-/// which is what a script tests for.
-fn into_lua(lua: &Lua, reply: Reply) -> mlua::Result<Value> {
-    Ok(match reply {
-        Reply::Nil | Reply::Bulk(None) => Value::Boolean(false),
-        Reply::Bulk(Some(bytes)) => Value::String(lua.create_string(bytes).map_err(lua_failure)?),
-        Reply::Integer(number) => Value::Integer(number),
-        Reply::Double(number) => Value::Number(number),
-        Reply::Boolean(yes) => Value::Boolean(yes),
-        Reply::Array(items) => {
-            let table = lua.create_table().map_err(lua_failure)?;
-            for (index, item) in items.into_iter().enumerate() {
-                let item = into_lua(lua, item)?;
-                table.set(index + 1, item).map_err(lua_failure)?;
-            }
-            Value::Table(table)
-        }
-        Reply::Set(items) => {
-            let table = lua.create_table().map_err(lua_failure)?;
-            for (index, item) in items.into_iter().enumerate() {
-                table
-                    .set(
-                        index + 1,
-                        Value::String(lua.create_string(item).map_err(lua_failure)?),
-                    )
-                    .map_err(lua_failure)?;
-            }
-            Value::Table(table)
-        }
-        Reply::Map(entries) => {
-            let table = lua.create_table().map_err(lua_failure)?;
-            for (key, value) in entries {
-                let value = into_lua(lua, value)?;
-                table
-                    .set(
-                        Value::String(lua.create_string(key).map_err(lua_failure)?),
-                        value,
-                    )
-                    .map_err(lua_failure)?;
-            }
-            Value::Table(table)
-        }
-        Reply::Simple(status) => {
-            let table = lua.create_table().map_err(lua_failure)?;
-            table.set("ok", status).map_err(lua_failure)?;
-            Value::Table(table)
-        }
-        Reply::Error(message) => {
-            return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(script_error(message).message));
-        }
-    })
-}

-/// What a script returned, converted the way Redis converts it: one value is
-/// itself, several are an array, and a table is the array it holds.
-fn reply_of(values: MultiValue) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
-    match values.len() {
-        0 => Ok(Reply::Nil),
-        1 => value_of(values.into_iter().next().expect("one value was counted")),
-        _ => values
-            .into_iter()
-            .map(value_of)
-            .collect::<RedisResult<Vec<_>>>()
-            .map(Reply::Array),
-    }
-}
-
-fn value_of(value: Value) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
-    match value {
-        Value::Nil => Ok(Reply::Nil),
-        Value::Boolean(yes) => Ok(Reply::Integer(i64::from(yes))),
-        Value::Integer(number) => Ok(Reply::Integer(number)),
-        Value::Number(number) => Ok(number_reply(number)),
-        Value::String(text) => Ok(Reply::Bulk(Some(text.as_bytes().as_ref().to_vec()))),
-        Value::Table(table) => table_reply(&table),
-        other => Err(script_error(format!(
-            "a script may only return nil, a boolean, a number, a string or a table (got {})",
-            other.type_name()
-        ))),
-    }
-}
-
-/// A whole number answers as an integer, as it does in Redis; anything else
-/// answers as its text.
-fn number_reply(number: f64) -> Reply {
-    if number.is_finite() && number.fract() == 0.0 && number.abs() < 9.007_199_254_740_992e15 {
-        Reply::Integer(number as i64)
-    } else {
-        Reply::Bulk(Some(number_text(number).into_bytes()))
-    }
-}

-/// A table answers as the array it holds. A table that carries an `err` or an
-/// `ok` answers as that instead, which is what `redis.error_reply`,
-/// `redis.status_reply` and `redis.pcall` hand back. Both fields are read by
-/// name, as Redis reads them, and neither needs an array part: a table built
-/// out of `err` alone has no numbered entries at all, so counting them would
-/// miss the one field that matters.
-fn table_reply(table: &Table) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
-    if let Ok(Value::String(message)) = table.raw_get::<Value>("err") {
-        return Err(script_error(text(message)));
-    }
-    if let Ok(Value::String(status)) = table.raw_get::<Value>("ok") {
-        return Ok(Reply::Simple(text(status)));
-    }
-    let mut items = Vec::with_capacity(table.raw_len());
-    for index in 1..=table.raw_len() {
-        match table.raw_get::<Value>(index) {
-            Ok(value) if !value.is_nil() => items.push(value_of(value)?),
-            // A hole ends the array, as it does everywhere in Redis.
-            _ => break,
-        }
-    }
-    Ok(Reply::Array(items))
-}

-/// A Lua string as text. A script's own text is text; a value it built out of
-/// bytes that are not is reported as it reads rather than refused.
-fn text(value: mlua::LuaString) -> String {
-    String::from_utf8_lossy(value.as_bytes().as_ref()).into_owned()

-/// A failure inside the script, as Redis words it. The chunk is named
-/// `user_script`, so Lua's own errors already start that way and are passed
-/// through rather than named twice.
-fn script_failure(error: mlua::Error) -> RedisError {
-    // A failure the cluster reported crosses into Lua as itself and comes back
-    // out unchanged, including whether a write may have applied. Only a
-    // failure that began in Lua is given the script's own wording.
-    if let Some(inner) = error.downcast_ref::<RedisError>() {
-        return inner.clone();
-    }
-    match error {
-        mlua::Error::RuntimeError(message) if message.contains("user_script") => {
-            script_error(message)
-        }
-        other => script_error(other.to_string()),
-    }
-}

-/// A failure while building a script's world, as the error Lua carries.
-fn lua_failure(error: mlua::Error) -> mlua::Error {
-    mlua::Error::external(script_error(error.to_string()))
-}
-
-/// The same failure, as the error the gateway answers a client with.
-fn setup_failure(error: mlua::Error) -> RedisError {
-    script_error(error.to_string())
-}

-/// A script's failure, as the client is told it. Lua words an error with the
-/// script's own message first and a traceback after it, and only the first is
-/// an answer: the traceback describes the interpreter to whoever runs the
-/// gateway, not the failure to the client, and Redis leaves it out too. What
-/// remains is one line, since RESP ends an error at a line break, so a message
-/// carrying one of its own would otherwise end early and leave the client
-/// reading the rest as the next reply.
-fn script_error(message: impl Into<String>) -> RedisError {
-    let message = message.into();
-    let message = match message.find("\nstack traceback") {
-        Some(end) => &message[..end],
-        None => &message[..],
-    };
-    RedisError::new("ERR", format!("user_script: {}", one_line(message)))
-}
-
-/// Text as one line: every line break is a space.
-fn one_line(message: &str) -> String {
-    let mut line = String::with_capacity(message.len());
-    let mut broke = false;
-    for character in message.chars() {
-        match character {
-            '\r' | '\n' => broke = true,
-            ' ' if broke && line.ends_with(' ') => {}
-            _ => {
-                if broke {
-                    line.push(' ');
-                    broke = false;
-                }
-                line.push(character);
-            }
-        }
-    }
-    line.trim_end().to_owned()
-}
-
-fn internal(message: impl Into<String>) -> RedisError {
-    RedisError::new("ERR", message.into())
-}
