+//! Running a client's Lua script against the cluster.
+//!
+//! The language is Lua itself, embedded as [`mlua`] with a vendored Lua 5.4,
+//! rather than a subset of it: what a client library sends is ordinary Lua, so
+//! a script gets the whole grammar and the `string`, `table`, `math`, `utf8`
+//! and `coroutine` libraries. What it does not get is anything a cache has no
+//! business doing. There is no `io`, `os`, `debug` or `package`, so a script
+//! cannot reach the filesystem, the clock, the environment or the process, and
+//! there is no `load`, `dofile`, `loadfile` or `require`, so it cannot pull in
+//! code it was not sent. The host enforces access to its one declared key and
+//! commits private state conditionally. Resource isolation and Redis Lua
+//! compatibility are incomplete; see `docs/experimental-redis.md`.
+
+use std::{
+    sync::{
+        Arc,
+        atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering},
+    },
+    time::{Duration, Instant},
+};
+
+use futures::Future;
+use mlua::{HookTriggers, Lua, LuaOptions, MultiValue, StdLib, Table, Value, VmState};
+use sha1::Digest;
+use tokio::sync::Mutex;
+
+use crate::{
+    error::{RedisError, RedisResult},
+    resp::Reply,
+};
+
+/// The SHA-1 that names a script, as the twenty bytes it is.
+pub fn digest(source: &[u8]) -> [u8; 20] {
+    sha1::Sha1::digest(source).into()
+}
+
+/// The same hash as the forty hex characters `SCRIPT LOAD` answers with, and
+/// the name `EVALSHA` asks for.
+pub fn hash_hex(source: &[u8]) -> String {
+    hex::encode(digest(source))
+}
+
+/// What a script may ask the cluster to do: run one command, as a client would.
+pub trait Host {
+    fn call(&mut self, command: &[Vec<u8>]) -> impl Future<Output = RedisResult<Reply>> + Send;
+}
+
+/// How long a script may run, and how much it may compute.
+#[derive(Clone)]
+pub struct Limits {
+    /// Lua virtual-machine instructions, counted by a hook, so the bound holds
+    /// on any machine rather than on how fast one is. This is the deterministic
+    /// half of the budget: a script that computes rather than calls is stopped
+    /// at exactly this many instructions.
+    pub max_steps: usize,
+    /// Wall-clock time, checked by the same hook. Redis' equivalent is
+    /// `lua-time-limit`; the gateway has no background thread watching for a
+    /// busy script, so a running script checks itself.
+    pub timeout: Duration,
+}
+
+impl Default for Limits {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            // A claim is two statements and a rate limiter's `INCR` with its
+            // deadline is four more, each a handful of instructions, so this is
+            // orders of magnitude above anything a client library sends.
+            max_steps: 10_000_000,
+            timeout: Duration::from_secs(5),
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// How many instructions pass between two checks of the budget. Small enough
+/// that a stopped script stops promptly, large enough that the hook costs
+/// nothing next to the work it watches.
+const CHECK_INTERVAL: u64 = 1_000;
+
+/// One Lua state, reused by every script this gateway runs.
+///
+/// Creating a state and loading its libraries is the expensive part, and a
+/// gateway runs one script at a time, so there is nothing to contend. Each run
+/// gets its own environment table, but nested library tables are shared in
+/// this experimental implementation. The state also keeps the memory
+/// its largest script needed, which is the same thing Redis keeps.
+#[derive(Default)]
+pub struct Runtime {
+    state: Option<Lua>,
+}
+
+impl Runtime {
+    /// Runs `source` once, against `keys` and `argv`, and answers with whatever
+    /// the script returned, converted the way Redis converts it.
+    pub async fn run<H: Host + Send + 'static>(
+        &mut self,
+        host: H,
+        source: &[u8],
+        keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
+        argv: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
+        limits: Limits,
+    ) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+        if self.state.is_none() {
+            self.state = Some(new_state()?);
+        }
+        let lua = self.state.as_ref().expect("the state was just made");
+        run(lua, host, source, keys, argv, limits).await
+    }
+}
+
+/// A state with only the libraries a script may have: no `io`, `os`, `package`
+/// or `debug`, and so no way to touch the machine it runs on. The base library
+/// comes with every state, and its doors to more code are closed here, as they
+/// are in Redis: a script is text that was already read, not a way to read more.
+fn new_state() -> RedisResult<Lua> {
+    let libraries =
+        StdLib::STRING | StdLib::TABLE | StdLib::MATH | StdLib::UTF8 | StdLib::COROUTINE;
+    let lua = Lua::new_with(libraries, LuaOptions::default())
+        .map_err(|error| internal(format!("the script state could not be made: {error}")))?;
+    let globals = lua.globals();
+    for door in ["load", "loadfile", "dofile", "require"] {
+        globals
+            .set(door, mlua::Value::Nil)
+            .map_err(|error| internal(format!("the script state could not be made: {error}")))?;
+    }
+    Ok(lua)
+}
+
+async fn run<H: Host + Send + 'static>(
+    lua: &Lua,
+    host: H,
+    source: &[u8],
+    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
+    argv: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
+    limits: Limits,
+) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let program = lua.load(source).set_name("user_script");
+    let budget = Budget::new(limits);
+    let watched = budget.clone();
+    // The script runs on its own coroutine, and the hook is set on that
+    // coroutine rather than the main thread: a hook on the main thread never
+    // fires while a coroutine runs, which is what let a runaway script loop
+    // forever under the old hand-written interpreter.
+    let function = execute(lua, program, host, keys, argv)?;
+    let thread = lua
+        .create_thread(function)
+        .map_err(|error| internal(format!("the script could not be watched: {error}")))?;
+    thread
+        .set_hook(
+            HookTriggers::new()
+                .every_nth_instruction(u32::try_from(CHECK_INTERVAL).unwrap_or(1_000)),
+            move |_, _| watched.check(),
+        )
+        .map_err(|error| internal(format!("the script could not be watched: {error}")))?;
+    let keep = thread.clone();
+    let answer = match thread.into_async::<MultiValue>(()) {
+        Ok(pending) => pending.await.map_err(script_failure),
+        Err(error) => Err(script_failure(error)),
+    };
+    keep.remove_hook();
+    match answer {
+        Ok(values) => reply_of(values),
+        Err(error) => Err(error),
+    }
+}
+
+/// What a script is allowed to compute, and for how long.
+#[derive(Clone)]
+struct Budget {
+    /// Instructions the run has left.
+    left: Arc<AtomicU64>,
+    timeout: Duration,
+    until: Instant,
+}
+
+impl Budget {
+    fn new(limits: Limits) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            left: Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(limits.max_steps as u64)),
+            timeout: limits.timeout,
+            until: Instant::now() + limits.timeout,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Runs on every instruction the hook sees. Returning an error from a Lua
+    /// hook is what aborts the script, with this message.
+    fn check(&self) -> mlua::Result<VmState> {
+        let spent = self.left.fetch_sub(CHECK_INTERVAL, Ordering::Relaxed);
+        if spent <= CHECK_INTERVAL {
+            return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(
+                "this script exceeded its maximum number of steps",
+            ));
+        }
+        if Instant::now() >= self.until {
+            return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(format!(
+                "this script was stopped after {}ms, which is longer than the deadline its \
+                 command was given",
+                self.timeout.as_millis()
+            )));
+        }
+        Ok(VmState::Continue)
+    }
+}
+
+/// Builds the environment one script runs in, and answers with the function
+/// that runs there. The coroutine it runs on is made by the caller, which is
+/// also what watches it.
+fn execute<H: Host + Send + 'static>(
+    lua: &Lua,
+    program: mlua::chunk::Chunk<'_>,
+    host: H,
+    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
+    argv: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
+) -> Result<mlua::Function, RedisError> {
+    // Every command this script may run goes through here, and the handle is
+    // what lets Lua's own call be `async`: the virtual machine suspends at
+    // `redis.call` while the cluster is asked.
+    let host = Arc::new(Mutex::new(host));
+    let declared = Arc::new(keys.clone());
+
+    let globals = lua.globals();
+    let environment = lua.create_table().map_err(setup_failure)?;
+    // A script reads the standard library through the globals, and keeps
+    // whatever it writes to itself, so nothing it defines outlives the run.
+    let metatable = lua.create_table().map_err(setup_failure)?;
+    metatable.set("__index", globals).map_err(setup_failure)?;
+    environment
+        .set_metatable(Some(metatable))
+        .map_err(setup_failure)?;
+    environment
+        .set("KEYS", list(lua, &keys).map_err(setup_failure)?)
+        .map_err(setup_failure)?;
+    environment
+        .set("ARGV", list(lua, &argv).map_err(setup_failure)?)
+        .map_err(setup_failure)?;
+    environment
+        .set(
+            "redis",
+            commands(lua, &host, &declared).map_err(setup_failure)?,
+        )
+        .map_err(setup_failure)?;
+
+    program
+        .set_environment(environment)
+        .into_function()
+        .map_err(script_failure)
+}
+
+/// The `redis` table: what a script may ask of the cluster.
+fn commands<H: Host + Send + 'static>(
+    lua: &Lua,
+    host: &Arc<Mutex<H>>,
+    declared: &Arc<Vec<Vec<u8>>>,
+) -> mlua::Result<Table> {
+    let table = lua.create_table().map_err(lua_failure)?;
+
+    let raising = host.clone();
+    let keys = declared.clone();
+    let call = lua
+        .create_async_function(move |lua, arguments: MultiValue| {
+            let host = raising.clone();
+            let declared = keys.clone();
+            async move {
+                // A command that answers with an error is an error to the
+                // script, the way `redis.call` treats it.
+                match run_command(&host, &declared, arguments).await {
+                    Err(error) => Err(mlua::Error::external(error)),
+                    Ok(Reply::Error(message)) => {
+                        Err(mlua::Error::runtime(script_error(message).message))
+                    }
+                    Ok(reply) => into_lua(&lua, reply),
+                }
+            }
+        })
+        .map_err(lua_failure)?;
+    table.set("call", call).map_err(lua_failure)?;
+
+    let catching = host.clone();
+    let keys = declared.clone();
+    let pcall = lua
+        .create_async_function(move |lua, arguments: MultiValue| {
+            let host = catching.clone();
+            let declared = keys.clone();
+            async move {
+                let answer = match run_command(&host, &declared, arguments).await {
+                    Ok(Reply::Error(message)) => Err(message),
+                    Ok(reply) => into_lua(&lua, reply).map_err(|error| error.to_string()),
+                    Err(error) => Err(error.message),
+                };
+                Ok::<MultiValue, mlua::Error>(match answer {
+                    Ok(value) => MultiValue::from_iter([value]),
+                    // `redis.pcall` answers with the error rather than raising
+                    // it, which is what a script that wants to try twice needs.
+                    Err(message) => MultiValue::from_iter([failed(&lua, message)?]),
+                })
+            }
+        })
+        .map_err(lua_failure)?;
+    table.set("pcall", pcall).map_err(lua_failure)?;
+
+    let error_reply = lua
+        .create_function(|lua, message: String| failed(lua, message))
+        .map_err(lua_failure)?;
+    table.set("error_reply", error_reply).map_err(lua_failure)?;
+
+    let status_reply = lua
+        .create_function(|lua, message: String| {
+            let table = lua.create_table()?;
+            table.set("ok", message)?;
+            Ok(Value::Table(table))
+        })
+        .map_err(lua_failure)?;
+    table
+        .set("status_reply", status_reply)
+        .map_err(lua_failure)?;
+
+    let sha1hex = lua
+        .create_function(|_, argument: mlua::LuaString| Ok(hash_hex(argument.as_bytes().as_ref())))
+        .map_err(lua_failure)?;
+    table.set("sha1hex", sha1hex).map_err(lua_failure)?;
+
+    Ok(table)
+}
+
+/// One command from a script, checked against the keys it declared and then run
+/// against the cluster.
+async fn run_command<H: Host + Send + 'static>(
+    host: &Arc<Mutex<H>>,
+    declared: &Arc<Vec<Vec<u8>>>,
+    arguments: MultiValue,
+) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let command = command_line(arguments).map_err(script_failure)?;
+    check_declared(declared, &command)?;
+    let mut host = host.lock().await;
+    host.call(&command).await
+}
+
+/// Every key the command will touch must be one the script declared.
+///
+/// The positions come from the command table, which already says where the
+/// keys are for `COMMAND`, so this reads the same table rather than keeping a
+/// second list that could disagree with it.
+fn check_declared(declared: &[Vec<u8>], command: &[Vec<u8>]) -> RedisResult<()> {
+    let Some(name) = command.first() else {
+        return Ok(());
+    };
+    let spelled = String::from_utf8_lossy(name);
+    let Some(info) = crate::table::lookup(&spelled.to_ascii_lowercase()) else {
+        return Err(script_error(format!("unknown command '{spelled}'")));
+    };
+    let name = spelled.to_ascii_lowercase();
+    for key in info.keys(command) {
+        if !declared.iter().any(|one| one.as_slice() == key) {
+            return Err(script_error(format!(
+                "the command '{name}' touches '{}', which this script did not \
+                 declare in KEYS; a script here may only touch the keys it \
+                 declares",
+                String::from_utf8_lossy(key)
+            )));
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+/// The arguments a script passed, as a command line. A table is expanded into
+/// the several arguments it holds, as Redis expands it.
+fn command_line(arguments: MultiValue) -> mlua::Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>> {
+    let mut line = Vec::with_capacity(arguments.len());
+    for argument in arguments {
+        match argument {
+            Value::String(text) => line.push(text.as_bytes().as_ref().to_vec()),
+            Value::Integer(number) => line.push(number.to_string().into_bytes()),
+            Value::Number(number) => line.push(number_text(number).into_bytes()),
+            Value::Table(table) => {
+                for index in 1..=table.raw_len() {
+                    line.push(argument_text(table.raw_get::<Value>(index)?)?);
+                }
+            }
+            other => {
+                return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(format!(
+                    "Lua redis lib command arguments must be strings or integers (got {})",
+                    other.type_name()
+                )));
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(line)
+}
+
+fn argument_text(value: Value) -> mlua::Result<Vec<u8>> {
+    match value {
+        Value::String(text) => Ok(text.as_bytes().as_ref().to_vec()),
+        Value::Integer(number) => Ok(number.to_string().into_bytes()),
+        Value::Number(number) => Ok(number_text(number).into_bytes()),
+        Value::Table(table) => {
+            let mut joined = Vec::new();
+            for index in 1..=table.raw_len() {
+                joined.push(argument_text(table.raw_get::<Value>(index)?)?);
+            }
+            Ok(joined.join(&b" "[..]))
+        }
+        other => Err(mlua::Error::runtime(format!(
+            "Lua redis lib command arguments must be strings or integers (got {})",
+            other.type_name()
+        ))),
+    }
+}
+
+/// A Lua number as its shortest exact text, which is what a client means when
+/// it passes one.
+fn number_text(number: f64) -> String {
+    if number.is_finite() && number.fract() == 0.0 && number.abs() < 9.007_199_254_740_992e15 {
+        format!("{}", number as i64)
+    } else {
+        format!("{number}")
+    }
+}
+
+/// `KEYS` and `ARGV` as Lua sees them: byte strings, indexed from one.
+fn list(lua: &Lua, values: &[Vec<u8>]) -> mlua::Result<Table> {
+    let table = lua.create_table().map_err(lua_failure)?;
+    for (index, value) in values.iter().enumerate() {
+        table
+            .set(
+                index + 1,
+                Value::String(lua.create_string(value).map_err(lua_failure)?),
+            )
+            .map_err(lua_failure)?;
+    }
+    Ok(table)
+}
+
+/// The `err` table `redis.pcall` and `redis.error_reply` answer with.
+fn failed(lua: &Lua, message: String) -> mlua::Result<Value> {
+    let table = lua.create_table()?;
+    table.set("err", message)?;
+    Ok(Value::Table(table))
+}
+
+/// What the cluster answered, as Lua sees it. A missing value is `false`,
+/// which is what a script tests for.
+fn into_lua(lua: &Lua, reply: Reply) -> mlua::Result<Value> {
+    Ok(match reply {
+        Reply::Nil | Reply::Bulk(None) => Value::Boolean(false),
+        Reply::Bulk(Some(bytes)) => Value::String(lua.create_string(bytes).map_err(lua_failure)?),
+        Reply::Integer(number) => Value::Integer(number),
+        Reply::Double(number) => Value::Number(number),
+        Reply::Boolean(yes) => Value::Boolean(yes),
+        Reply::Array(items) => {
+            let table = lua.create_table().map_err(lua_failure)?;
+            for (index, item) in items.into_iter().enumerate() {
+                let item = into_lua(lua, item)?;
+                table.set(index + 1, item).map_err(lua_failure)?;
+            }
+            Value::Table(table)
+        }
+        Reply::Set(items) => {
+            let table = lua.create_table().map_err(lua_failure)?;
+            for (index, item) in items.into_iter().enumerate() {
+                table
+                    .set(
+                        index + 1,
+                        Value::String(lua.create_string(item).map_err(lua_failure)?),
+                    )
+                    .map_err(lua_failure)?;
+            }
+            Value::Table(table)
+        }
+        Reply::Map(entries) => {
+            let table = lua.create_table().map_err(lua_failure)?;
+            for (key, value) in entries {
+                let value = into_lua(lua, value)?;
+                table
+                    .set(
+                        Value::String(lua.create_string(key).map_err(lua_failure)?),
+                        value,
+                    )
+                    .map_err(lua_failure)?;
+            }
+            Value::Table(table)
+        }
+        Reply::Simple(status) => {
+            let table = lua.create_table().map_err(lua_failure)?;
+            table.set("ok", status).map_err(lua_failure)?;
+            Value::Table(table)
+        }
+        Reply::Error(message) => {
+            return Err(mlua::Error::runtime(script_error(message).message));
+        }
+    })
+}
+
+/// What a script returned, converted the way Redis converts it: one value is
+/// itself, several are an array, and a table is the array it holds.
+fn reply_of(values: MultiValue) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    match values.len() {
+        0 => Ok(Reply::Nil),
+        1 => value_of(values.into_iter().next().expect("one value was counted")),
+        _ => values
+            .into_iter()
+            .map(value_of)
+            .collect::<RedisResult<Vec<_>>>()
+            .map(Reply::Array),
+    }
+}
+
+fn value_of(value: Value) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    match value {
+        Value::Nil => Ok(Reply::Nil),
+        Value::Boolean(yes) => Ok(Reply::Integer(i64::from(yes))),
+        Value::Integer(number) => Ok(Reply::Integer(number)),
+        Value::Number(number) => Ok(number_reply(number)),
+        Value::String(text) => Ok(Reply::Bulk(Some(text.as_bytes().as_ref().to_vec()))),
+        Value::Table(table) => table_reply(&table),
+        other => Err(script_error(format!(
+            "a script may only return nil, a boolean, a number, a string or a table (got {})",
+            other.type_name()
+        ))),
+    }
+}
+
+/// A whole number answers as an integer, as it does in Redis; anything else
+/// answers as its text.
+fn number_reply(number: f64) -> Reply {
+    if number.is_finite() && number.fract() == 0.0 && number.abs() < 9.007_199_254_740_992e15 {
+        Reply::Integer(number as i64)
+    } else {
+        Reply::Bulk(Some(number_text(number).into_bytes()))
+    }
+}
+
+/// A table answers as the array it holds. A table that carries an `err` or an
+/// `ok` answers as that instead, which is what `redis.error_reply`,
+/// `redis.status_reply` and `redis.pcall` hand back. Both fields are read by
+/// name, as Redis reads them, and neither needs an array part: a table built
+/// out of `err` alone has no numbered entries at all, so counting them would
+/// miss the one field that matters.
+fn table_reply(table: &Table) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    if let Ok(Value::String(message)) = table.raw_get::<Value>("err") {
+        return Err(script_error(text(message)));
+    }
+    if let Ok(Value::String(status)) = table.raw_get::<Value>("ok") {
+        return Ok(Reply::Simple(text(status)));
+    }
+    let mut items = Vec::with_capacity(table.raw_len());
+    for index in 1..=table.raw_len() {
+        match table.raw_get::<Value>(index) {
+            Ok(value) if !value.is_nil() => items.push(value_of(value)?),
+            // A hole ends the array, as it does everywhere in Redis.
+            _ => break,
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(Reply::Array(items))
+}
+
+/// A Lua string as text. A script's own text is text; a value it built out of
+/// bytes that are not is reported as it reads rather than refused.
+fn text(value: mlua::LuaString) -> String {
+    String::from_utf8_lossy(value.as_bytes().as_ref()).into_owned()
+}
+
+/// A failure inside the script, as Redis words it. The chunk is named
+/// `user_script`, so Lua's own errors already start that way and are passed
+/// through rather than named twice.
+fn script_failure(error: mlua::Error) -> RedisError {
+    // A failure the cluster reported crosses into Lua as itself and comes back
+    // out unchanged, including whether a write may have applied. Only a
+    // failure that began in Lua is given the script's own wording.
+    if let Some(inner) = error.downcast_ref::<RedisError>() {
+        return inner.clone();
+    }
+    match error {
+        mlua::Error::RuntimeError(message) if message.contains("user_script") => {
+            script_error(message)
+        }
+        other => script_error(other.to_string()),
+    }
+}
+
+/// A failure while building a script's world, as the error Lua carries.
+fn lua_failure(error: mlua::Error) -> mlua::Error {
+    mlua::Error::external(script_error(error.to_string()))
+}
+
+/// The same failure, as the error the gateway answers a client with.
+fn setup_failure(error: mlua::Error) -> RedisError {
+    script_error(error.to_string())
+}
+
+/// A script's failure, as the client is told it. Lua words an error with the
+/// script's own message first and a traceback after it, and only the first is
+/// an answer: the traceback describes the interpreter to whoever runs the
+/// gateway, not the failure to the client, and Redis leaves it out too. What
+/// remains is one line, since RESP ends an error at a line break, so a message
+/// carrying one of its own would otherwise end early and leave the client
+/// reading the rest as the next reply.
+fn script_error(message: impl Into<String>) -> RedisError {
+    let message = message.into();
+    let message = match message.find("\nstack traceback") {
+        Some(end) => &message[..end],
+        None => &message[..],
+    };
+    RedisError::new("ERR", format!("user_script: {}", one_line(message)))
+}
+
+/// Text as one line: every line break is a space.
+fn one_line(message: &str) -> String {
+    let mut line = String::with_capacity(message.len());
+    let mut broke = false;
+    for character in message.chars() {
+        match character {
+            '\r' | '\n' => broke = true,
+            ' ' if broke && line.ends_with(' ') => {}
+            _ => {
+                if broke {
+                    line.push(' ');
+                    broke = false;
+                }
+                line.push(character);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    line.trim_end().to_owned()
+}
+
+fn internal(message: impl Into<String>) -> RedisError {
+    RedisError::new("ERR", message.into())
+}

+    async fn a_named_reply_comes_back_as_what_it_named() {
+        let error = evaluate(
+            Canned::default(),
+            "return redis.error_reply('WRONGTYPE fake')",
+            Vec::new(),
+            Limits::default(),
+        )
+        .await
+        .unwrap_err();
+        assert!(
+            error.message.contains("user_script: WRONGTYPE fake"),
+            "{error:?}"
+        );
+
+        let status = evaluate(
+            Canned::default(),
+            "return redis.status_reply('QUEUED')",
+            Vec::new(),
+            Limits::default(),
+        )
+        .await
+        .unwrap();

+        let mut host = Canned::default();
+        host.answers.insert(
+            "get".into(),
+            Reply::Error("WRONGTYPE Operation against a key".into()),
+        );
+        let raised = evaluate(
+            host,
+            "return redis.pcall('GET', KEYS[1])",
+            vec![b"alpha".to_vec()],
+            Limits::default(),
+        )

+        .unwrap_err();

+            raised.message.contains("WRONGTYPE Operation against a key"),
+            "{raised:?}"
+        );

+    /// a traceback after it, and RESP ends a simple error at the line break, so
+    /// sending the traceback whole would leave the client reading the rest of it
+    /// as the next reply. The first line is the error itself.
+    #[tokio::test]
+    async fn a_failure_reaches_a_client_as_one_line() {
+        let error = evaluate(
+            Canned::default(),
+            "return os.time()",
+            Vec::new(),
+            Limits::default(),
+        )
+        .await
+        .unwrap_err();
+        assert!(
+            !error.message.contains(['\r', '\n']),
+            "the error was more than one line: {error:?}"
+        );
+        assert!(error.message.contains("'os'"), "{error:?}");

+            Canned::default(),
+            "error('first\\nsecond')",

+        .unwrap_err();

+            !error.message.contains(['\r', '\n']),
+            "the error was more than one line: {error:?}"
+        );

+    }

+        let error = evaluate(
+            Canned::default(),
+            "local t = nil return t.field",
+            keys(),
+            Limits::default(),
+        )
+        .await
+        .unwrap_err();
+        assert!(error.message.contains("user_script"), "{error:?}");
+        let error = evaluate(Canned::default(), "return (", keys(), Limits::default())
+            .await
+            .unwrap_err();
+        assert!(error.message.contains("user_script"), "{error:?}");
+    }
+
+    #[tokio::test]
+    async fn one_state_serves_many_scripts_and_keeps_nothing() {
+        let mut runtime = Runtime::default();
+        runtime
+            .run(
+                Canned::default(),
+                b"leaked = 42",

+                Vec::new(),
+                Limits::default(),
+            )
+            .await
+            .unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(answer, Reply::bulk("nil"));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_script_is_named_by_the_hash_of_its_text() {
+        assert_eq!(hash_hex(b"abc"), "a9993e364706816aba3e25717850c26c9cd0d89d");
+    }
+}

+//! The cluster connection a connection's commands share, and the locks that
+//! keep read-modify-write commands within one gateway from colliding.
+
+use std::sync::{
+    Arc,
+    atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering},
+};
+
+use hashring_client::{ClientConfig, ClientError, HashringClient};
+use tokio::sync::{Mutex, OwnedMutexGuard, RwLock};
+
+use crate::error::{RedisError, RedisResult};
+
+/// One cluster client per gateway rather than per connection.
+///
+/// `HashringClient` caches a topology and a channel per data node, both of
+/// which are worth sharing: every connection to the same gateway would
+/// otherwise hold its own copy and poll the coordinator separately. The client
+/// is built on first use and dropped when it stops working, so a gateway that
+/// starts before its coordinator still answers clients once the coordinator is
+/// up.
+pub struct SharedClient {
+    endpoint: String,
+    config: ClientConfig,
+    client: RwLock<Option<HashringClient>>,
+    connecting: Mutex<()>,
+    failures: AtomicU64,
+}
+
+impl SharedClient {
+    pub fn new(endpoint: String, operation_timeout: std::time::Duration) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            endpoint,
+            config: ClientConfig::new(operation_timeout),
+            client: RwLock::new(None),
+            connecting: Mutex::new(()),
+            failures: AtomicU64::new(0),
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub async fn get(&self) -> RedisResult<HashringClient> {
+        if let Some(client) = self.client.read().await.clone() {
+            return Ok(client);
+        }
+        // One connection attempt at a time, so a burst of commands after a
+        // gateway restart does not open a burst of coordinator connections.
+        let _guard = self.connecting.lock().await;
+        if let Some(client) = self.client.read().await.clone() {
+            return Ok(client);
+        }
+        let client = self.connect().await?;
+        *self.client.write().await = Some(client.clone());
+        self.failures.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
+        Ok(client)
+    }
+
+    async fn connect(&self) -> RedisResult<HashringClient> {
+        let attempt = self.failures.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) + 1;
+        match HashringClient::connect_with_config(self.endpoint.clone(), self.config.clone()).await
+        {
+            Ok(client) => {
+                tracing::info!(endpoint = %self.endpoint, "connected to the cluster coordinator");
+                Ok(client)
+            }
+            Err(error) => {
+                tracing::debug!(endpoint = %self.endpoint, attempt, %error, "coordinator connection failed");
+                Err(connect_error(error))
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Drops the cached client so the next command reconnects. Called when a
+    /// command fails in a way that means the cached topology or channels are no
+    /// longer usable; a later command rebuilds them.
+    pub async fn invalidate(&self) {
+        self.client.write().await.take();
+    }
+}
+
+/// A gateway that cannot reach the coordinator is not down: the cluster may be
+/// starting, or migrating. `TRYAGAIN` is the code clients already back off on.
+fn connect_error(error: ClientError) -> RedisError {
+    let message = error.to_string();
+    tracing::debug!(%error, "gateway could not reach the coordinator");
+    RedisError::new("TRYAGAIN", format!("cluster is unavailable: {message}"))
+}
+
+/// Keeps two read-modify-write commands on one key from the same gateway from
+/// running at once.
+///
+/// Correctness does not depend on it: every such command writes on condition
+/// that the key is still the version it read, and the owner enforces that
+/// against every writer. What the lock saves is the retry. Without it, eight
+/// clients incrementing one hot key would each read the same version and all
+/// but one would have to read again; with it they take turns within this
+/// gateway and only collide with writers elsewhere.
+pub struct KeyLocks {
+    stripes: Vec<Arc<Mutex<()>>>,
+}
+
+/// Stripe count. Two keys landing on one stripe wait for each other, so this
+/// trades a little concurrency for a fixed-size table; 4096 stripes make a
+/// collision between two hot keys unlikely while costing 4096 tiny allocations.
+const STRIPES: usize = 4096;
+
+impl KeyLocks {
+    pub fn new() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            stripes: (0..STRIPES).map(|_| Arc::new(Mutex::new(()))).collect(),
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn stripe(&self, key: &[u8]) -> usize {
+        // FNV-1a: cheap, and the same for a key every time.
+        let mut hash = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325_u64;
+        for byte in key {
+            hash ^= u64::from(*byte);
+            hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01b3);
+        }
+        (hash % self.stripes.len() as u64) as usize
+    }
+
+    /// Locks every key's stripe, in ascending stripe order so two commands that
+    /// name the same keys in opposite orders cannot deadlock. Repeated keys
+    /// lock once.
+    pub async fn lock(&self, keys: &[&[u8]]) -> Vec<OwnedMutexGuard<()>> {
+        let mut stripes: Vec<usize> = keys.iter().map(|key| self.stripe(key)).collect();
+        stripes.sort_unstable();
+        stripes.dedup();
+        let mut guards = Vec::with_capacity(stripes.len());
+        for stripe in stripes {
+            guards.push(self.stripes[stripe].clone().lock_owned().await);
+        }
+        guards
+    }
+}
+
+impl Default for KeyLocks {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        Self::new()
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_key_always_lands_on_the_same_stripe() {
+        let locks = KeyLocks::new();
+        assert_eq!(locks.stripe(b"key"), locks.stripe(b"key"));
+    }
+
+    #[tokio::test]
+    async fn two_holders_of_one_key_wait_for_each_other() {
+        let locks = Arc::new(KeyLocks::new());
+        let held = locks.lock(&[b"key"]).await;
+        let other = {
+            let locks = locks.clone();
+            tokio::spawn(async move {
+                let _guard = locks.lock(&[b"key"]).await;
+                true
+            })
+        };
+        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
+        assert!(!other.is_finished(), "the second holder did not wait");
+        drop(held);
+        assert!(other.await.unwrap());
+    }
+
+    #[tokio::test]
+    async fn one_key_in_a_set_locks_its_stripe_once() {
+        let locks = KeyLocks::new();
+        let guards = locks.lock(&[b"key", b"key"]).await;
+        assert_eq!(guards.len(), 1);
+    }
+}

+//! Reading a command's arguments.
+//!
+//! Every handler reads its arguments through [`Args`], which never indexes past
+//! the end: an option whose operand is missing is a syntax error rather than a
+//! panic, and an argument left over after a command has read everything it
+//! takes is one too. The dispatcher has already checked the command's arity
+//! against [`crate::table`], so a handler only reads what that arity
+//! guarantees, or asks for optional arguments and handles their absence.
+
+use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
+
+use crate::error::{RedisError, RedisResult};
+
+/// The arguments after the command name, read front to back.
+pub struct Args<'a> {
+    name: &'static str,
+    rest: &'a [Vec<u8>],
+}
+
+impl<'a> Args<'a> {
+    /// `rest` excludes the command name; `name` is what errors call the
+    /// command.
+    pub fn new(name: &'static str, rest: &'a [Vec<u8>]) -> Self {
+        Self { name, rest }
+    }
+
+    pub fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
+        self.name
+    }
+
+    /// Everything not read yet.
+    pub fn remaining(&self) -> &'a [Vec<u8>] {
+        self.rest
+    }
+
+    /// The next argument, or a syntax error when there is none.
+    ///
+    /// Unlike [`Iterator::next`], a missing required argument is a protocol
+    /// error rather than the end of the argument list.
+    pub fn next_required(&mut self) -> RedisResult<&'a [u8]> {
+        self.next_optional().ok_or_else(RedisError::syntax)
+    }
+
+    pub fn next_optional(&mut self) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
+        let (first, rest) = self.rest.split_first()?;
+        self.rest = rest;
+        Some(first)
+    }
+
+    pub fn next_owned(&mut self) -> RedisResult<Vec<u8>> {
+        self.next_required().map(<[u8]>::to_vec)
+    }
+
+    /// The next argument as an option keyword, lower case.
+    pub fn next_keyword(&mut self) -> Option<String> {
+        self.next_optional().map(keyword)
+    }
+
+    pub fn next_integer(&mut self) -> RedisResult<i64> {
+        let value = self.next_required()?;
+        integer(value, self.name)
+    }
+
+    pub fn next_float(&mut self) -> RedisResult<f64> {
+        float(self.next_required()?)
+    }
+
+    /// Ends the command: anything left is a syntax error.
+    pub fn finish(self) -> RedisResult<()> {
+        match self.rest.is_empty() {
+            true => Ok(()),
+            false => Err(RedisError::syntax()),
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// A command word in lower case, for comparing against `NX`, `EX` and friends.
+pub fn keyword(value: &[u8]) -> String {
+    String::from_utf8_lossy(value).to_lowercase()
+}
+
+pub fn parse_integer(value: &[u8]) -> Option<i64> {
+    let text = std::str::from_utf8(value).ok()?;
+    text.trim().parse::<i64>().ok()
+}
+
+pub fn integer(value: &[u8], command: &str) -> RedisResult<i64> {
+    parse_integer(value).ok_or_else(|| {
+        RedisError::new(
+            "ERR",
+            format!("value is not an integer or out of range ({command})"),
+        )
+    })
+}
+
+pub fn float(value: &[u8]) -> RedisResult<f64> {
+    let text = std::str::from_utf8(value).unwrap_or_default();
+    match text.trim().parse::<f64>() {
+        Ok(parsed) if parsed.is_finite() => Ok(parsed),
+        _ => Err(RedisError::not_a_float()),
+    }
+}
+
+pub fn now_millis() -> u64 {
+    SystemTime::now()
+        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
+        .unwrap_or_default()
+        .as_millis()
+        .try_into()
+        .unwrap_or(u64::MAX)
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
+pub enum TimeUnit {
+    Seconds,
+    Milliseconds,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
+pub enum DeadlineMode {
+    /// A timeout from now: `EX`, `PX`, `EXPIRE`, `PEXPIRE`.
+    Relative,
+    /// A Unix timestamp: `EXAT`, `PXAT`, `EXPIREAT`, `PEXPIREAT`.
+    Absolute,
+}
+
+/// How a command states a deadline: the unit and whether it counts from now.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
+pub struct TtlForm {
+    pub unit: TimeUnit,
+    pub mode: DeadlineMode,
+}
+
+impl TtlForm {
+    pub const fn new(unit: TimeUnit, mode: DeadlineMode) -> Self {
+        Self { unit, mode }
+    }
+
+    /// The expiry option a keyword names, for the commands that take one.
+    pub fn from_option(keyword: &str) -> Option<Self> {
+        use DeadlineMode::*;
+        use TimeUnit::*;
+        Some(match keyword {
+            "ex" => Self::new(Seconds, Relative),
+            "px" => Self::new(Milliseconds, Relative),
+            "exat" => Self::new(Seconds, Absolute),
+            "pxat" => Self::new(Milliseconds, Absolute),
+            _ => return None,
+        })
+    }
+
+    /// The absolute deadline, in Unix milliseconds, that `amount` names at
+    /// `now`. Signed and wide, because `EXPIRE key -10` names a deadline in the
+    /// past, which a command treats as a delete rather than as a far future.
+    /// `None` when it overflows what a deadline can hold, which Redis reports
+    /// as an invalid expire time.
+    pub fn deadline(self, amount: i64, now: u64) -> Option<i128> {
+        let millis = match self.unit {
+            TimeUnit::Seconds => i128::from(amount) * 1000,
+            TimeUnit::Milliseconds => i128::from(amount),
+        };
+        let deadline = match self.mode {
+            DeadlineMode::Relative => i128::from(now) + millis,
+            DeadlineMode::Absolute => millis,
+        };
+        (deadline <= i128::from(i64::MAX)).then_some(deadline)
+    }
+}
+
+pub fn invalid_expire_time(command: &str) -> RedisError {
+    RedisError::new("ERR", format!("invalid expire time in '{command}' command"))
+}
+
+/// A deadline set by `SET`, `SETEX`, `PSETEX` or `GETEX`. Unlike `EXPIRE`,
+/// these refuse a zero or negative amount instead of deleting the key.
+pub fn positive_deadline(form: TtlForm, amount: i64, command: &str) -> RedisResult<u64> {
+    if amount <= 0 {
+        return Err(invalid_expire_time(command));
+    }
+    form.deadline(amount, now_millis())
+        .and_then(|deadline| u64::try_from(deadline).ok())
+        .ok_or_else(|| invalid_expire_time(command))
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+
+    fn owned(args: &[&[u8]]) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {
+        args.iter().map(|arg| arg.to_vec()).collect()
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_missing_operand_is_a_syntax_error_not_a_panic() {
+        let rest = owned(&[b"EX"]);
+        let mut args = Args::new("set", &rest);
+        assert_eq!(args.next_keyword().as_deref(), Some("ex"));
+        assert_eq!(args.next_integer().unwrap_err().message, "syntax error");
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_leftover_argument_is_a_syntax_error() {
+        let rest = owned(&[b"a", b"b"]);
+        let mut args = Args::new("echo", &rest);
+        args.next_required().unwrap();
+        assert!(args.finish().is_err());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn each_expiry_option_has_its_own_unit() {
+        let now = 1_000_000;
+        let deadline = |option: &str, amount| {
+            TtlForm::from_option(option)
+                .unwrap()
+                .deadline(amount, now)
+                .unwrap()
+        };
+        assert_eq!(deadline("ex", 10), 1_010_000);
+        assert_eq!(deadline("px", 10), 1_000_010);
+        assert_eq!(deadline("exat", 1_800_000_000), 1_800_000_000_000);
+        assert_eq!(deadline("pxat", 1_800_000_000_000), 1_800_000_000_000);
+        assert_eq!(TtlForm::from_option("persist"), None);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_negative_timeout_is_a_deadline_in_the_past() {
+        let form = TtlForm::new(TimeUnit::Seconds, DeadlineMode::Relative);
+        assert_eq!(form.deadline(-1, 5_000), Some(4_000));
+        assert_eq!(form.deadline(i64::MAX, 5_000), None);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn set_style_deadlines_refuse_zero_and_overflow() {
+        let ex = TtlForm::new(TimeUnit::Seconds, DeadlineMode::Relative);
+        assert!(positive_deadline(ex, 0, "set").is_err());
+        assert!(positive_deadline(ex, -5, "set").is_err());
+        assert!(positive_deadline(ex, i64::MAX, "set").is_err());
+        assert!(positive_deadline(ex, 10, "set").unwrap() > now_millis());
+    }
+}

+//! Commands the gateway answers itself: the handshake, connection settings and
+//! the introspection clients run on connect. None of them reaches the cluster.
+
+use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
+
+use super::{
+    Connection, Dispatcher, Effect, ReplyMode, Response,
+    args::{Args, keyword, parse_integer},
+};
+use crate::{
+    error::{RedisError, RedisResult},
+    resp::{Protocol, Reply},
+    table::CommandInfo,
+};
+
+impl Dispatcher {
+    pub(super) fn local(
+        &self,
+        command: &CommandInfo,
+        connection: &mut Connection,
+        args: Args<'_>,
+    ) -> Response {
+        let reply = match command.name {
+            // Redis ignores anything after `QUIT`.
+            "quit" => {
+                return Response {
+                    reply: Ok(Reply::status()),
+                    effect: Effect::Close,
+                };
+            }
+            "client" => return self.client_command(connection, args),
+            "ping" => ping(args),
+            "echo" => echo(args),
+            "hello" => self.hello(connection, args),
+            "auth" => self.auth(connection, args),
+            "select" => select(args),
+            "reset" => self.reset(connection, args),
+            "command" => command_command(self, args),
+            "info" => self.info(args),
+            "config" => config(args),
+            other => Err(RedisError::unsupported(&other.to_ascii_uppercase())),
+        };
+        Response::reply(reply)
+    }
+
+    /// `HELLO [protover [AUTH username password] [SETNAME name]]`.
+    ///
+    /// Everything is parsed and checked before anything is applied, so a
+    /// request that fails part-way, on a bad option or a wrong password,
+    /// leaves the connection exactly as it was.
+    fn hello(&self, connection: &mut Connection, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+        let mut protocol = connection.protocol;
+        if let Some(version) = args
+            .remaining()
+            .first()
+            .and_then(|value| parse_integer(value))
+        {
+            args.next_required()?;
+            protocol = match version {
+                2 => Protocol::Resp2,
+                3 => Protocol::Resp3,
+                other => {
+                    return Err(RedisError::new(
+                        "NOPROTO",
+                        format!("unsupported protocol version {other}"),
+                    ));
+                }
+            };
+        }
+        let mut credentials = None;
+        let mut name = None;
+        while let Some(option) = args.next_keyword() {
+            match option.as_str() {
+                "auth" => credentials = Some((args.next_required()?, args.next_required()?)),
+                "setname" => name = Some(args.next_owned()?),
+                _ => return Err(RedisError::syntax()),
+            }
+        }
+        if let Some((user, password)) = credentials {
+            self.check_credentials(Some(user), password)?;
+            connection.authenticated = true;
+        }
+        if name.is_some() {
+            connection.name = name;
+        }
+        connection.protocol = protocol;
+        Ok(Reply::Map(vec![
+            (b"server".to_vec(), Reply::bulk("hashring-rs")),
+            (b"version".to_vec(), Reply::bulk(crate::VERSION)),
+            (
+                b"proto".to_vec(),
+                Reply::Integer(i64::from(protocol.version())),
+            ),
+            (b"id".to_vec(), Reply::Integer(connection.id as i64)),
+            (b"mode".to_vec(), Reply::bulk("standalone")),
+            (b"role".to_vec(), Reply::bulk("master")),
+            (b"modules".to_vec(), Reply::Array(Vec::new())),
+        ]))
+    }
+
+    /// `AUTH password` and `AUTH user password` are both accepted; the gateway
+    /// has one password and one user, `default`.
+    fn auth(&self, connection: &mut Connection, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+        let first = args.next_required()?;
+        let credentials = match args.next_optional() {
+            Some(password) => (Some(first), password),
+            None => (None, first),
+        };
+        args.finish()?;
+        self.check_credentials(credentials.0, credentials.1)?;
+        connection.authenticated = true;
+        Ok(Reply::status())
+    }
+
+    fn check_credentials(&self, user: Option<&[u8]>, password: &[u8]) -> RedisResult<()> {
+        let Some(expected) = &self.password else {
+            return Err(RedisError::new(
+                "ERR",
+                "Client sent AUTH, but no password is set. Did you mean AUTH <username> <password>?",
+            ));
+        };
+        let user_ok = user.is_none_or(|user| keyword(user) == "default");
+        if user_ok && expected.as_bytes() == password {
+            Ok(())
+        } else {
+            Err(RedisError::wrong_pass())
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn client_command(&self, connection: &mut Connection, mut args: Args<'_>) -> Response {
+        let Some(subcommand) = args.next_keyword() else {
+            return Response::error(RedisError::wrong_arity("client"));
+        };
+        if subcommand == "reply" {
+            let mode = match args.next_keyword().as_deref() {
+                Some("on") => ReplyMode::On,
+                Some("off") => ReplyMode::Off,
+                Some("skip") => ReplyMode::Skip,
+                _ => return Response::error(RedisError::syntax()),
+            };
+            return match args.finish() {
+                Ok(()) => Response {
+                    reply: Ok(Reply::status()),
+                    effect: Effect::ReplyMode(mode),
+                },
+                Err(error) => Response::error(error),
+            };
+        }
+        Response::reply(client_subcommand(connection, &subcommand, args))
+    }
+
+    fn reset(&self, connection: &mut Connection, args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+        args.finish()?;
+        connection.protocol = Protocol::Resp2;
+        connection.name = None;
+        connection.authenticated = self.password.is_none();
+        connection.reply_mode = ReplyMode::On;
+        Ok(Reply::Simple("RESET".into()))
+    }
+
+    fn info(&self, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+        let section = args.next_keyword();
+        args.finish().map_err(|_| RedisError::wrong_arity("info"))?;
+        let uptime = self.started_at.elapsed().as_secs();
+        let mut body = match section.as_deref() {
+            Some("server") | None => format!(
+                "# Server\r\n\
+                 redis_version:{version}\r\n\
+                 redis_mode:standalone\r\n\
+                 os:{os}\r\n\
+                 arch_bits:64\r\n\
+                 process_id:{pid}\r\n\
+                 run_id:{run_id}\r\n\
+                 tcp_port:{port}\r\n\
+                 uptime_in_seconds:{uptime}\r\n\
+                 uptime_in_days:{days}\r\n\
+                 executable:hashring-rs redis-gateway\r\n\
+                 config_file:\r\n",
+                version = crate::VERSION,
+                os = std::env::consts::OS,
+                pid = std::process::id(),
+                run_id = gateway_instance_id(),
+                port = 0,
+                uptime = uptime,
+                days = uptime / 86_400,
+            ),
+            _ => String::new(),
+        };
+        if matches!(section.as_deref(), None | Some("clients")) {
+            body.push_str("# Clients\r\nconnected_clients:0\r\nblocked_clients:0\r\n");
+        }
+        if matches!(section.as_deref(), None | Some("memory")) {
+            body.push_str(
+                "# Memory\r\n\
+                 used_memory:0\r\n\
+                 used_memory_human:0B\r\n\
+                 maxmemory:0\r\n\
+                 maxmemory_policy:noeviction\r\n",
+            );
+        }
+        if matches!(section.as_deref(), None | Some("persistence")) {
+            body.push_str(
+                "# Persistence\r\nloading:0\r\naof_enabled:0\r\nrdb_changes_since_last_save:0\r\n",
+            );
+        }
+        if matches!(section.as_deref(), None | Some("stats")) {
+            body.push_str(&format!(
+                "# Stats\r\n\
+                 total_connections_received:0\r\n\
+                 total_commands_processed:0\r\n\
+                 uptime_in_seconds:{uptime}\r\n",
+                uptime = uptime,
+            ));
+        }
+        if matches!(section.as_deref(), None | Some("replication")) {
+            // There is no Redis replica to promote and no Redis master to
+            // follow; the cluster has one owner per key, which `cluster`
+            // describes instead.
+            body.push_str("# Replication\r\nrole:master\r\nconnected_slaves:0\r\n");
+        }
+        if matches!(section.as_deref(), None | Some("cluster")) {
+            body.push_str(
+                "# Cluster\r\n\
+                 cluster_enabled:0\r\n\
+                 cluster_state:ok\r\n\
+                 cluster_slots_assigned:0\r\n",
+            );
+        }
+        if matches!(section.as_deref(), None | Some("keyspace")) {
+            // Counting keys would mean asking every owner, and the answer would
+            // be a snapshot no two callers could agree on. It is left out
+            // rather than wrong.
+            body.push_str("# Keyspace\r\n");
+        }
+        Ok(Reply::bulk(body))
+    }
+}

+fn ping(mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let message = args.next_optional();
+    args.finish().map_err(|_| RedisError::wrong_arity("ping"))?;
+    Ok(match message {
+        None => Reply::Simple("PONG".into()),
+        Some(message) => Reply::bulk(message.to_vec()),
+    })
+}
+
+fn echo(mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    Ok(Reply::bulk(args.next_owned()?))
+}
+
+fn select(mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    // Every key lives in one flat namespace, so only database 0 exists.
+    match parse_integer(args.next_required()?) {
+        Some(0) => Ok(Reply::status()),
+        _ => Err(RedisError::new(
+            "ERR",
+            "DB index is out of range. This gateway serves one database, 0",
+        )),
+    }
+}
+
+fn client_subcommand(
+    connection: &mut Connection,
+    subcommand: &str,
+    mut args: Args<'_>,
+) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    match subcommand {
+        "id" => Ok(Reply::Integer(connection.id as i64)),
+        "setname" => {
+            let name = args.next_owned()?;
+            args.finish()?;
+            connection.name = Some(name);
+            Ok(Reply::status())
+        }
+        "getname" => Ok(match &connection.name {
+            Some(name) => Reply::bulk(name.clone()),
+            None => Reply::Nil,
+        }),
+        // Clients send `CLIENT SETINFO lib-name ...` on connect and expect a
+        // plain OK; nothing is recorded.
+        "setinfo" => {
+            args.next_required()?;
+            args.next_required()?;
+            args.finish()?;
+            Ok(Reply::status())
+        }
+        "no-evict" | "no-touch" | "no-evict-on-expiry" | "unpause" | "tracking" => {
+            Ok(Reply::status())
+        }
+        "info" => Ok(Reply::bulk(client_info(connection).into_bytes())),
+        "list" => Ok(Reply::bulk("")),
+        "getredir" => Ok(Reply::Integer(-1)),
+        other => Err(RedisError::new(
+            "ERR",
+            format!("Unknown subcommand or wrong number of arguments for '{other}'"),
+        )),
+    }
+}
+
+fn command_command(dispatcher: &Dispatcher, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    match args.next_keyword().as_deref() {
+        None => Ok(Reply::Array(
+            dispatcher.commands().map(CommandInfo::to_reply).collect(),
+        )),
+        Some("count") => Ok(Reply::Array(vec![Reply::Integer(
+            dispatcher.commands().count() as i64,
+        )])),
+        // Documentation is for commands this gateway does not implement, so
+        // there is none to send.
+        Some("docs") => Ok(Reply::Array(Vec::new())),
+        Some("info") => Ok(Reply::Array(
+            args.remaining()
+                .iter()
+                .map(
+                    |name| match dispatcher.command(&String::from_utf8_lossy(name)) {
+                        Some(command) => command.to_reply(),
+                        None => Reply::Nil,
+                    },
+                )
+                .collect(),
+        )),
+        Some("getkeys") | Some("getkeysandflags") => {
+            Err(RedisError::unsupported("COMMAND GETKEYS"))
+        }
+        Some(other) => Err(RedisError::new(
+            "ERR",
+            format!("Unknown subcommand or wrong number of arguments for '{other}'"),
+        )),
+    }
+}
+
+fn config(mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    match args.next_keyword().as_deref() {
+        Some("get") => {
+            let pattern = super::glob::Pattern::new(keyword(args.next_required()?).as_bytes());
+            Ok(Reply::Map(
+                config_entries()
+                    .into_iter()
+                    .filter(|(name, _)| pattern.matches(name.as_bytes()))
+                    .map(|(name, value)| (name.as_bytes().to_vec(), Reply::bulk(value)))
+                    .collect(),
+            ))
+        }
+        Some("set") => {
+            let pairs = args.remaining();
+            if pairs.is_empty() || !pairs.len().is_multiple_of(2) {
+                return Err(RedisError::syntax());
+            }
+            for name in pairs.iter().step_by(2) {
+                let name = keyword(name);
+                if !config_entries().into_iter().any(|(known, _)| known == name) {
+                    return Err(RedisError::new(
+                        "ERR",
+                        format!("Unknown option or number of arguments for CONFIG SET - '{name}'"),
+                    ));
+                }
+            }
+            // Nothing is stored: every parameter is either already the only
+            // value that can hold, or names a feature this gateway does not
+            // have. Redis answers OK for a parameter it accepts.
+            Ok(Reply::status())
+        }
+        Some("resetstat") | Some("rewrite") => Ok(Reply::status()),
+        Some(other) => Err(RedisError::new(
+            "ERR",
+            format!("Unknown CONFIG subcommand '{other}'"),
+        )),
+        None => Err(RedisError::wrong_arity("config")),
+    }
+}

+/// The `CONFIG GET` parameters this gateway reports, and accepts unchanged.
+fn config_entries() -> Vec<(&'static str, &'static str)> {
+    vec![
+        ("maxmemory", "0"),
+        ("maxmemory-policy", "noeviction"),
+        ("appendonly", "no"),

+//! Redis' glob patterns, for `KEYS` and `CONFIG GET`: `*`, `?`, character
+//! classes such as `[a-z]` and `[^x]`, and a backslash escape. Classes parse
+//! exactly as Redis' `stringmatchlen` parses them, edge cases included.
+//!
+//! A pattern is compiled once, so a character class is a bit lookup rather
+//! than a reparse each time a `*` retries. Compiling costs a bounded amount
+//! per pattern byte, ranges included, since it too runs where no deadline can
+//! interrupt it. Matching is over bytes, since keys
+//! are, and takes at most one step per pattern element per key byte. `KEYS`
+//! applies one client-chosen pattern to every key in the cluster
+//! synchronously, where no deadline can interrupt it, so it matches within a
+//! step budget and gives up when the budget runs out.
+
+use hashring_core::limits::DEFAULT_MAX_KEY_BYTES;
+
+/// Every element but `*` consumes exactly one byte, so a pattern with more of
+/// them than the longest key can hold matches nothing, and compiling it any
+/// further would only spend the gateway's memory.
+const MAX_FIXED_ELEMENTS: usize = DEFAULT_MAX_KEY_BYTES;
+
+enum Element {
+    /// `*`, any run of bytes. Consecutive stars are one.
+    Star,
+    /// `?`, exactly one byte.
+    AnyByte,
+    Byte(u8),
+    /// The bytes a class accepts, one bit each.
+    Class([u64; 4]),
+}
+
+pub struct Pattern {
+    elements: Vec<Element>,
+    /// Longer than any key could match.
+    impossible: bool,
+}
+
+impl Pattern {
+    pub fn new(pattern: &[u8]) -> Self {
+        let mut elements = Vec::new();
+        let mut fixed = 0;
+        let mut p = 0;
+        while p < pattern.len() {
+            let element = match pattern[p] {
+                b'*' => {
+                    p += 1;
+                    if matches!(elements.last(), Some(Element::Star)) {
+                        continue;
+                    }
+                    elements.push(Element::Star);
+                    continue;
+                }
+                b'?' => {
+                    p += 1;
+                    Element::AnyByte
+                }
+                b'[' => {
+                    let (class, next) = class(pattern, p + 1);
+                    p = next;
+                    Element::Class(class)
+                }
+                b'\\' if p + 1 < pattern.len() => {
+                    p += 2;
+                    Element::Byte(pattern[p - 1])
+                }
+                literal => {
+                    p += 1;
+                    Element::Byte(literal)
+                }
+            };
+            fixed += 1;
+            if fixed > MAX_FIXED_ELEMENTS {
+                return Self {
+                    elements: Vec::new(),
+                    impossible: true,
+                };
+            }
+            elements.push(element);
+        }
+        Self {
+            elements,
+            impossible: false,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Whether `text` matches all of the pattern.
+    pub fn matches(&self, text: &[u8]) -> bool {
+        let mut unlimited = u64::MAX;
+        self.matches_within(text, &mut unlimited)
+            .expect("an unlimited budget does not run out")
+    }
+
+    /// Whether `text` matches, spending one unit of `budget` per step; `None`
+    /// if the budget ran out first.
+    pub fn matches_within(&self, text: &[u8], budget: &mut u64) -> Option<bool> {
+        if self.impossible {
+            return Some(false);
+        }
+        let elements = &self.elements;
+        let (mut p, mut t) = (0, 0);
+        // The element just past the last `*`, and the text position that `*`
+        // has consumed up to. On a mismatch the `*` takes one more byte.
+        let mut star: Option<(usize, usize)> = None;
+        while t < text.len() {
+            *budget = budget.checked_sub(1)?;
+            let matched = match elements.get(p) {
+                Some(Element::Star) => {
+                    p += 1;
+                    star = Some((p, t));
+                    continue;
+                }
+                Some(Element::AnyByte) => true,
+                Some(Element::Byte(byte)) => *byte == text[t],
+                Some(Element::Class(accepts)) => accepts_byte(accepts, text[t]),
+                None => false,
+            };
+            if matched {
+                p += 1;
+                t += 1;
+                continue;
+            }
+            let Some((after_star, consumed)) = star else {
+                return Some(false);
+            };
+            p = after_star;
+            t = consumed + 1;
+            star = Some((after_star, t));
+        }
+        Some(
+            elements[p..]
+                .iter()
+                .all(|element| matches!(element, Element::Star)),
+        )
+    }
+}
+
+fn accepts_byte(class: &[u64; 4], byte: u8) -> bool {
+    class[usize::from(byte / 64)] & (1 << (byte % 64)) != 0
+}
+
+fn accept(class: &mut [u64; 4], byte: u8) {
+    class[usize::from(byte / 64)] |= 1 << (byte % 64);
+}
+
+/// Accepts every byte from `low` to `high`, a word at a time, so a range costs
+/// the same however many bytes it spans.
+fn accept_range(class: &mut [u64; 4], low: u8, high: u8) {
+    for (index, word) in class.iter_mut().enumerate() {
+        let base = index * 64;
+        let from = usize::from(low).max(base);
+        let to = usize::from(high).min(base + 63);
+        if from > to {
+            continue;
+        }
+        let width = to - from + 1;
+        let bits = if width == 64 {
+            u64::MAX
+        } else {
+            (1_u64 << width) - 1
+        };
+        *word |= bits << (from - base);
+    }
+}
+
+/// A range as Redis reads it. `stringmatchlen` compares C `char`s, which are
+/// signed on x86-64, the platform Redis is overwhelmingly deployed on: so
+/// `a-\xff` spans -1 to 97 and leaves `b` out. In unsigned terms a range that
+/// crosses zero is two stretches, from 0 up and from 0x80 up to 0xff.
+fn accept_redis_range(class: &mut [u64; 4], first: u8, second: u8) {
+    let (first, second) = (first as i8, second as i8);
+    let (low, high) = (first.min(second), first.max(second));
+    if low >= 0 || high < 0 {
+        accept_range(class, low as u8, high as u8);
+    } else {
+        accept_range(class, 0, high as u8);
+        accept_range(class, low as u8, u8::MAX);
+    }
+}
+
+/// Compiles the class whose body starts at `p`: the bytes it accepts, and
+/// where the pattern continues after it. In the order Redis checks them: an
+/// escape, the closing `]`, the end of the pattern (which closes the class
+/// too), a range `x-y` (whose `y` may be `]`), and a literal.
+fn class(pattern: &[u8], mut p: usize) -> ([u64; 4], usize) {
+    let mut accepts = [0_u64; 4];
+    // Only `^` negates, as in Redis: `[!a]` is a class of `!` and `a`.
+    let negated = pattern.get(p) == Some(&b'^');
+    if negated {
+        p += 1;
+    }
+    let next = loop {
+        match pattern.get(p) {
+            Some(b'\\') if p + 1 < pattern.len() => {
+                accept(&mut accepts, pattern[p + 1]);
+                p += 2;
+            }
+            Some(b']') => break p + 1,
+            None => break p,
+            Some(&first) if pattern.get(p + 1) == Some(&b'-') && p + 2 < pattern.len() => {
+                // Redis accepts a range written backwards.
+                accept_redis_range(&mut accepts, first, pattern[p + 2]);
+                p += 3;
+            }
+            Some(&literal) => {
+                accept(&mut accepts, literal);
+                p += 1;
+            }
+        }
+    };
+    if negated {
+        for word in accepts.iter_mut() {
+            *word = !*word;
+        }
+    }
+    (accepts, next)
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::Pattern;
+
+    fn m(pattern: &str, text: &str) -> bool {
+        Pattern::new(pattern.as_bytes()).matches(text.as_bytes())
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn wildcards_match_the_way_redis_documents_them() {
+        assert!(m("*", ""));
+        assert!(m("*", "anything"));
+        assert!(m("h?llo", "hello") && m("h?llo", "hallo") && !m("h?llo", "hllo"));
+        assert!(m("h*llo", "hllo") && m("h*llo", "heeeello"));
+        assert!(m("h[ae]llo", "hello") && m("h[ae]llo", "hallo") && !m("h[ae]llo", "hillo"));
+        assert!(m("h[^e]llo", "hallo") && !m("h[^e]llo", "hello"));
+        assert!(m("h[a-b]llo", "hbllo") && !m("h[a-b]llo", "hcllo"));
+        assert!(m("h[b-a]llo", "hallo"), "a backwards range still matches");
+        assert!(m("user:*:name", "user:42:name") && !m("user:*:name", "user:42:email"));
+        assert!(!m("abc", "ab") && !m("ab", "abc"));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn only_a_caret_negates_a_class() {
+        assert!(m("[!a]", "a") && m("[!a]", "!") && !m("[!a]", "b"));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_backslash_escapes_a_special_character() {
+        assert!(m(r"a\*b", "a*b") && !m(r"a\*b", "axb"));
+        assert!(m(r"[\]]", "]"));
+        assert!(m("a\\", "a\\"), "a trailing backslash is literal");
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn classes_parse_their_edge_cases_as_redis_does() {
+        // A range may end in `]`; written backwards, `a-]` spans `]` to `a`.
+        assert!(m("[a-]]", "_") && !m("[a-]]", "b"));
+        // The end of the pattern closes a class and keeps what it gathered.
+        assert!(m("[abc", "a") && !m("[abc", "x"));
+        assert!(m("[^abc", "x") && !m("[^abc", "a"));
+        // `[]` closes at once: an empty class, which matches nothing.
+        assert!(!m("[]", "]") && !m("[]", ""));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_binary_range_orders_its_ends_as_redis_on_x86_64_does() {
+        let matches = |pattern: &[u8], text: &[u8]| Pattern::new(pattern).matches(text);
+        // `a-\xff` is 97 to -1, so -1 to 97: every ASCII byte up to `a`, and
+        // 0xff, but not `b` and not the rest of the high half.
+        assert!(matches(b"[a-\xff]", b"a") && matches(b"[a-\xff]", b"\xff"));
+        assert!(matches(b"[a-\xff]", b"\0"));
+        assert!(!matches(b"[a-\xff]", b"b") && !matches(b"[a-\xfe]", b"\x80"));
+        // Within the high half the order is the usual one.
+        assert!(matches(b"[\x80-\xff]", b"\x90") && !matches(b"[\x80-\xff]", b"a"));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_range_mask_covers_exactly_its_span() {
+        for (low, high) in [(0, 255), (0, 63), (63, 64), (5, 5), (100, 200), (192, 255)] {
+            let mut class = [0_u64; 4];
+            super::accept_range(&mut class, low, high);
+            for byte in 0..=255_u8 {
+                assert_eq!(
+                    super::accepts_byte(&class, byte),
+                    (low..=high).contains(&byte),
+                    "{low}-{high} at {byte}"
+                );
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn many_stars_do_not_backtrack_exponentially() {
+        let text = "a".repeat(10_000);
+        assert!(!m("*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*b", &text));
+        assert!(m("*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*", &text));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_large_class_costs_one_step_per_byte() {
+        // Compiled once, a class of a million bytes is one bit lookup.
+        let pattern = format!("*[{}]", "a".repeat(1 << 20));
+        let pattern = Pattern::new(pattern.as_bytes());
+        let mut budget = 1_000_000;
+        assert_eq!(
+            pattern.matches_within(&[b'x'; 1024], &mut budget),
+            Some(false)
+        );
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_pattern_longer_than_any_key_is_not_compiled_out() {
+        // Eight million empty classes would be gigabytes of tables; the
+        // pattern stops compiling once it outgrows the longest key.
+        let pattern = Pattern::new("[]".repeat(1 << 23).as_bytes());
+        assert!(pattern.impossible && pattern.elements.is_empty());
+        assert!(!pattern.matches(b"anything"));
+        // Stars consume nothing, so any number of them still compiles.
+        let stars = Pattern::new(&[b'*'; 1 << 20]);
+        assert!(!stars.impossible && stars.matches(b"anything"));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn matching_stops_when_the_budget_runs_out() {
+        let pattern = Pattern::new(b"*a*a*a*b");
+        let mut budget = 100;
+        assert_eq!(pattern.matches_within(&[b'a'; 10_000], &mut budget), None);
+    }
+}

+//! Commands about keys rather than values: existence, deletion, renaming and
+//! deadlines.
+
+use hashring_client::Precondition;
+
+use super::{
+    args::{Args, TimeUnit, TtlForm, invalid_expire_time, now_millis},
+    store::{Change, Store, expiry},
+};
+use crate::{
+    error::{RedisError, RedisResult},
+    resp::Reply,
+};
+
+/// `DEL` counts the keys that existed and were removed. The cluster's delete
+/// is idempotent and reports success either way, so each key is read and then
+/// deleted on condition that it is still the version read; a key that changed
+/// in between is read again.
+pub async fn delete(store: &Store<'_>, args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let removed = store
+        .each_write(args.remaining(), |key| async move {
+            store
+                .update(key, |current| {
+                    Ok(match current {
+                        Some(_) => Change::Delete { reply: 1 },
+                        None => Change::Nothing(0),
+                    })
+                })
+                .await
+        })
+        .await?;
+    Ok(Reply::Integer(removed.into_iter().sum()))
+}
+
+/// `EXISTS` and `TOUCH`. A key named twice counts twice, as in Redis.
+pub async fn exists(store: &Store<'_>, args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let found = store
+        .each(args.remaining(), |key| async move {
+            Ok(i64::from(store.read(key).await?.is_some()))
+        })
+        .await?;
+    Ok(Reply::Integer(found.into_iter().sum()))
+}
+
+pub async fn key_type(store: &Store<'_>, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    Ok(match store.read(key).await? {
+        // Every value this gateway stores is a byte string.
+        Some(_) => Reply::Simple("string".into()),
+        None => Reply::Simple("none".into()),
+    })
+}
+
+/// The value and its deadline move together. The two keys may live on
+/// different owners, so the copy and the delete are two writes: the
+/// destination is written first, and the source is then deleted only if it is
+/// still the version that was copied. A source rewritten in between is left
+/// in place and reported, since the destination now holds its earlier value.
+pub async fn rename(
+    store: &Store<'_>,
+    mut args: Args<'_>,
+    only_if_absent: bool,
+) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let from = args.next_required()?;
+    let to = args.next_required()?;
+    let Some(source) = store.read(from).await? else {
+        return Err(RedisError::no_such_key());
+    };
+    let done = || match only_if_absent {
+        true => Reply::Integer(1),
+        false => Reply::status(),
+    };
+    if from == to {
+        return Ok(match only_if_absent {
+            true => Reply::Integer(0),
+            false => done(),
+        });
+    }
+    let client = store.client().await?;
+    let value = source.value.clone();
+    if only_if_absent {
+        let written = client
+            .put_if(
+                to.to_vec(),
+                value,
+                expiry(source.deadline),
+                Precondition::Absent,
+            )
+            .await?;
+        if written.is_none() {
+            return Ok(Reply::Integer(0));
+        }
+    } else {
+        store.put(to, value, expiry(source.deadline)).await?;
+    }
+    let deleted = client
+        .delete_if(from.to_vec(), Precondition::Version(source.version))
+        .await?;
+    match deleted {
+        Some(_) => Ok(done()),
+        None => Err(RedisError::new(
+            "ERR",
+            "the source key changed during RENAME; the destination holds its earlier value",
+        )),
+    }
+}
+
+/// The `NX`, `XX`, `GT` and `LT` conditions `EXPIRE` accepts.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
+enum ExpiryGuard {
+    Always,
+    OnlyWithout,
+    OnlyWith,
+    OnlyGreater,
+    OnlyLess,
+}
+
+impl ExpiryGuard {
+    fn parse(args: &mut Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Self> {
+        let guard = match args.next_keyword().as_deref() {
+            None => Self::Always,
+            Some("nx") => Self::OnlyWithout,
+            Some("xx") => Self::OnlyWith,
+            Some("gt") => Self::OnlyGreater,
+            Some("lt") => Self::OnlyLess,
+            Some(_) => return Err(RedisError::syntax()),
+        };
+        args.next_optional()
+            .map_or(Ok(guard), |_| Err(RedisError::syntax()))
+    }
+
+    /// `current` is the deadline the key has now, and `requested` the one
+    /// being asked for, both absolute. A key without a deadline never expires,
+    /// so for `GT` and `LT` it compares as infinitely far away: no deadline is
+    /// greater, and every deadline is less.
+    fn allows(self, current: Option<u64>, requested: i128) -> bool {
+        match self {
+            Self::Always => true,
+            Self::OnlyWithout => current.is_none(),
+            Self::OnlyWith => current.is_some(),
+            Self::OnlyGreater => current.is_some_and(|current| requested > i128::from(current)),
+            Self::OnlyLess => current.is_none_or(|current| requested < i128::from(current)),
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// `EXPIRE`, `PEXPIRE`, `EXPIREAT` and `PEXPIREAT`. A deadline that is not in
+/// the future deletes the key, as Redis does, whichever form named it.
+pub async fn expire(store: &Store<'_>, mut args: Args<'_>, form: TtlForm) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    let amount = args.next_integer()?;
+    let guard = ExpiryGuard::parse(&mut args)?;
+    let requested = form
+        .deadline(amount, now_millis())
+        .ok_or_else(|| invalid_expire_time(args.name()))?;
+    store
+        .update(key, |current| {
+            let Some(current) = current else {
+                return Ok(Change::Nothing(Reply::Integer(0)));
+            };
+            if !guard.allows(current.deadline, requested) {
+                return Ok(Change::Nothing(Reply::Integer(0)));
+            }
+            let reply = Reply::Integer(1);
+            Ok(match u64::try_from(requested) {
+                Ok(deadline) if deadline > now_millis() => Change::Expire {
+                    deadline: Some(deadline),
+                    reply,
+                },
+                _ => Change::Delete { reply },
+            })
+        })
+        .await
+}
+
+pub async fn persist(store: &Store<'_>, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    store
+        .update(key, |current| {
+            Ok(match current {
+                Some(current) if current.deadline.is_some() => Change::Expire {
+                    deadline: None,
+                    reply: Reply::Integer(1),
+                },
+                _ => Change::Nothing(Reply::Integer(0)),
+            })
+        })
+        .await
+}
+
+pub async fn ttl(store: &Store<'_>, mut args: Args<'_>, unit: TimeUnit) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    Ok(match store.read(key).await? {
+        // -2 is no key at all, -1 a key with no deadline.
+        None => Reply::Integer(-2),
+        Some(current) => match current.deadline {
+            None => Reply::Integer(-1),
+            Some(deadline) => {
+                let remaining = deadline.saturating_sub(now_millis());
+                let value = match unit {
+                    // Redis rounds a remaining TTL up to whole seconds.
+                    TimeUnit::Seconds => remaining.div_ceil(1000),
+                    TimeUnit::Milliseconds => remaining,
+                };

+            }
+        },
+    })
