+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+
+    #[test]
+    fn the_expiry_conditions_compare_the_deadline() {
+        let now = i128::from(now_millis());
+        let at = |offset: i128| u64::try_from(now + offset).unwrap();
+        assert!(ExpiryGuard::Always.allows(None, now));
+        assert!(ExpiryGuard::OnlyWithout.allows(None, now));
+        assert!(!ExpiryGuard::OnlyWithout.allows(Some(at(1)), now));
+        assert!(ExpiryGuard::OnlyWith.allows(Some(at(1)), now));
+        assert!(ExpiryGuard::OnlyGreater.allows(Some(at(0)), now + 1));
+        assert!(!ExpiryGuard::OnlyGreater.allows(Some(at(1)), now));
+        assert!(ExpiryGuard::OnlyLess.allows(Some(at(1)), now));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_key_without_a_deadline_compares_as_never_expiring() {
+        let now = i128::from(now_millis());
+        assert!(ExpiryGuard::OnlyLess.allows(None, now + 10_000));
+        assert!(!ExpiryGuard::OnlyGreater.allows(None, now + 10_000));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn expire_takes_at_most_one_condition() {
+        let rest: Vec<Vec<u8>> = vec![b"NX".to_vec(), b"GT".to_vec()];
+        assert!(ExpiryGuard::parse(&mut Args::new("expire", &rest)).is_err());
+    }
+}

+//! Commands over the whole keyspace rather than named keys: `KEYS`, `SCAN`,
+//! `DBSIZE` and `RANDOMKEY`.
+//!
+//! `KEYS` and `DBSIZE` walk every owner through the client (see
+//! `hashring_client::HashringClient::keys`), which starts over if the topology
+//! changes underneath it. So an answer covers every key that was live for the
+//! whole command; a key written or deleted while it ran may or may not count.
+//!
+//! `SCAN` goes round the ring in token order instead, a stretch at a time (see
+//! `hashring_client::HashringClient::scan`), and its cursor is the token to
+//! continue from. A token means the same thing in every epoch and at every
+//! gateway, so a scan survives membership changes and may be continued
+//! through any gateway, and returns a key that was live throughout exactly
+//! once, where Redis promises only at least once.
+
+use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, Ordering};
+
+use hashring_client::ClientError;
+use hashring_core::proto::ErrorCode;
+
+use super::{
+    args::{Args, keyword, parse_integer},
+    glob,
+    store::Store,
+};
+use crate::{
+    error::{RedisError, RedisResult},
+    resp::Reply,
+};
+
+/// The most `KEYS` or one `SCAN` gathers before giving up, counting each key's
+/// bytes plus the client's per-key overhead. Redis has no such limit, but it
+/// answers from memory it already holds; a gateway would have to buffer every
+/// node's keys, so `KEYS *` on a large cluster could exhaust it for every
+/// other client.
+pub const MAX_KEYS_REPLY_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
+
+/// Pattern steps one `KEYS` or `SCAN` may spend matching, across every key it
+/// sees. Matching runs synchronously as pages arrive, where the command
+/// deadline cannot interrupt it, so a pattern built to be slow has to be cut
+/// off here. At a few nanoseconds a step this is well under a second.
+pub const MAX_KEYS_MATCH_STEPS: u64 = 100_000_000;
+
+/// `SCAN`'s `COUNT` when none is given, as in Redis.
+const DEFAULT_SCAN_COUNT: usize = 10;
+
+/// A `MATCH` pattern and the matching budget of the command that applies it.
+struct Matcher {
+    pattern: Option<glob::Pattern>,
+    remaining: AtomicU64,
+    exhausted: AtomicBool,
+}
+
+impl Matcher {
+    fn new(pattern: Option<&[u8]>) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            pattern: pattern.map(glob::Pattern::new),
+            remaining: AtomicU64::new(MAX_KEYS_MATCH_STEPS),
+            exhausted: AtomicBool::new(false),
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn keep(&self, key: &[u8]) -> bool {
+        let Some(pattern) = &self.pattern else {
+            return true;
+        };
+        let before = self.remaining.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
+        let mut budget = before;
+        let matched = pattern.matches_within(key, &mut budget);
+        // Owners' pages are matched concurrently, so another may have spent
+        // from the same budget since it was read.
+        let spent = before - budget;
+        let _ = self
+            .remaining
+            .try_update(Ordering::Relaxed, Ordering::Relaxed, |left| {
+                Some(left.saturating_sub(spent))
+            });
+        matched.unwrap_or_else(|| {
+            self.exhausted.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
+            false
+        })
+    }
+
+    /// An error if the budget ran out, so some keys went unmatched.
+    fn finish(&self, command: &str) -> RedisResult<()> {
+        if self.exhausted.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
+            return Err(RedisError::new(
+                "ERR",
+                format!("the {command} pattern takes too much work to match; simplify it"),
+            ));
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}
+
+/// The client's `TooLarge` for a gathering that passed its byte limit, as an
+/// error that says which command and what to do about it.
+fn too_many_keys(
+    command: &'static str,
+    advice: &'static str,
+) -> impl Fn(ClientError) -> RedisError {
+    move |error| match error {
+        ClientError::Operation(failure) if failure.code == ErrorCode::TooLarge => RedisError::new(
+            "ERR",
+            format!("{command} gathered more than {MAX_KEYS_REPLY_BYTES} bytes of keys; {advice}"),
+        ),
+        other => other.into(),
+    }
+}
+
+pub async fn keys(store: &Store<'_>, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let matcher = Matcher::new(Some(args.next_required()?));
+    let keys = store
+        .client()
+        .await?
+        .keys(|key| matcher.keep(key), MAX_KEYS_REPLY_BYTES)
+        .await
+        .map_err(too_many_keys("KEYS", "narrow the pattern"))?;
+    matcher.finish("KEYS")?;
+    Ok(Reply::Array(keys.into_iter().map(Reply::bulk).collect()))
+}
+
+/// `SCAN cursor [MATCH pattern] [COUNT count] [TYPE type]`.
+pub async fn scan(store: &Store<'_>, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let cursor = std::str::from_utf8(args.next_required()?)
+        .ok()
+        .and_then(|cursor| cursor.parse::<u64>().ok())
+        .ok_or_else(|| RedisError::new("ERR", "invalid cursor"))?;
+    let mut pattern = None;
+    let mut count = DEFAULT_SCAN_COUNT;
+    let mut strings_only = true;
+    while let Some(option) = args.next_keyword() {
+        match option.as_str() {
+            "match" => pattern = Some(args.next_required()?),
+            "count" => {
+                count = parse_integer(args.next_required()?)
+                    .ok_or_else(RedisError::not_an_integer)?
+                    .try_into()
+                    .ok()
+                    .filter(|count| *count >= 1)
+                    .ok_or_else(RedisError::syntax)?;
+            }
+            // Every key here is a string, so naming any other type, one Redis
+            // knows or not, selects nothing. Redis too accepts any name.
+            "type" => strings_only = keyword(args.next_required()?) == "string",
+            _ => return Err(RedisError::syntax()),
+        }
+    }
+    // No key is of another type, so the scan is complete before it starts.
+    if !strings_only {
+        return Ok(scan_reply(0, Vec::new()));
+    }
+    let matcher = Matcher::new(pattern);
+    let (keys, next) = store
+        .client()
+        .await?
+        .scan(cursor, count, |key| matcher.keep(key), MAX_KEYS_REPLY_BYTES)
+        .await
+        .map_err(too_many_keys("SCAN", "use a smaller COUNT"))?;
+    matcher.finish("SCAN")?;
+    Ok(scan_reply(next.unwrap_or(0), keys))
+}
+
+/// A cursor is the decimal integer clients expect, `0` once the scan is done.
+fn scan_reply(cursor: u64, keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>) -> Reply {
+    Reply::Array(vec![
+        Reply::bulk(cursor.to_string()),
+        Reply::Array(keys.into_iter().map(Reply::bulk).collect()),
+    ])
+}
+
+pub async fn dbsize(store: &Store<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let count = store.client().await?.key_count().await?;
+    Ok(Reply::Integer(i64::try_from(count).unwrap_or(i64::MAX)))
+}
+
+pub async fn randomkey(store: &Store<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = store.client().await?.random_key().await?;
+    Ok(Reply::Bulk(key))
+}

+//! Command dispatch: a Redis command in, a Redis reply out.
+//!
+//! Every request is checked against [`crate::table`] before a handler sees it:
+//! the command must exist and not be declined, its arity must match, and the
+//! connection must have authenticated unless the command is part of the
+//! handshake. A handler then reads its arguments through [`args::Args`].
+//!
+//! Commands that answer from the gateway live in `connection`; the ones that
+//! reach the cluster live in `strings`, `keys` and `keyspace` and go
+//! through [`store::Store`], which routes each key to its owner through
+//! [`hashring_client`] and makes every read-modify-write conditional on the
+//! version it read. See docs/redis-compatibility.md for the semantics this
+//! reproduces and the ones it deliberately does not.
+
+mod args;
+mod connection;
+mod glob;
+mod keys;
+mod keyspace;
+pub mod store;
+mod strings;
+
+use std::{sync::Arc, time::Duration};
+
+use crate::{
+    client::{KeyLocks, SharedClient},
+    error::{RedisError, RedisResult},
+    resp::{Limits, Protocol, Reply},
+    table::{self, CommandInfo},
+};
+
+pub use args::{Args, keyword, now_millis, parse_integer};
+use futures::future::BoxFuture;
+
+/// Registers additional commands without changing the gateway's transport.
+/// The dispatcher applies metadata validation, authentication and the deadline
+/// before invoking an extension. Ordinary commands use the existing handlers.
+pub trait CommandExtension: Send + Sync {
+    fn commands(&self) -> &'static [CommandInfo];
+    fn execute<'a>(
+        &'a self,
+        dispatcher: &'a Dispatcher,
+        connection: &'a mut Connection,
+        command: &'a CommandInfo,
+        arguments: &'a [Vec<u8>],
+    ) -> BoxFuture<'a, RedisResult<Reply>>;
+}
+
+/// The gateway, shared by every connection it serves.
+#[derive(Clone)]
+pub struct Dispatcher {
+    pub client: Arc<SharedClient>,
+    locks: Arc<KeyLocks>,
+    password: Option<Arc<str>>,
+    limits: Limits,
+    /// How long one command that reaches the cluster may take, from its first
+    /// lock wait or request to its last.
+    command_timeout: Duration,
+    started_at: std::time::Instant,
+    extension: Option<Arc<dyn CommandExtension>>,
+}
+
+/// What one command produced: the reply, and what it does to the connection
+/// once that reply is settled. An effect applies only when the command
+/// succeeded, so `CLIENT REPLY BOGUS` changes nothing.
+pub struct Response {
+    pub reply: RedisResult<Reply>,
+    pub effect: Effect,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
+pub enum Effect {
+    None,
+    /// `QUIT`: answer, then close.
+    Close,
+    /// `CLIENT REPLY`: switch the reply mode. Redis answers `ON` with `OK` and
+    /// the other two with nothing at all.
+    ReplyMode(ReplyMode),
+}
+
+impl Response {
+    fn reply(reply: RedisResult<Reply>) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            reply,
+            effect: Effect::None,
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn error(error: RedisError) -> Self {
+        Self::reply(Err(error))
+    }
+}
+
+impl Dispatcher {
+    pub fn new(
+        client: Arc<SharedClient>,
+        password: Option<Arc<str>>,
+        limits: Limits,
+        command_timeout: Duration,
+    ) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            client,
+            locks: Arc::new(KeyLocks::new()),
+            password,
+            limits,
+            command_timeout,
+            started_at: std::time::Instant::now(),
+            extension: None,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Install additional command handlers before sharing the dispatcher.
+    pub fn with_extension(mut self, extension: Arc<dyn CommandExtension>) -> Self {
+        self.extension = Some(extension);
+        self
+    }
+
+    pub fn command_timeout(&self) -> Duration {
+        self.command_timeout
+    }
+
+    /// Registered commands take precedence over the built-in metadata.
+    pub fn command(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&'static CommandInfo> {
+        self.extension
+            .as_ref()
+            .and_then(|extension| {
+                extension
+                    .commands()
+                    .iter()
+                    .find(|command| command.name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
+            })
+            .or_else(|| table::lookup(name))
+    }
+
+    pub fn commands(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static CommandInfo> + '_ {
+        let extra = self
+            .extension
+            .as_ref()
+            .map_or(&[][..], |extension| extension.commands());
+        table::COMMANDS
+            .iter()
+            .filter(move |command| !extra.iter().any(|item| item.name == command.name))
+            .chain(extra.iter())
+    }
+
+    pub fn limits(&self) -> Limits {
+        self.limits
+    }
+
+    /// Whether a connection has to authenticate before it may read or write.
+    pub fn requires_auth(&self) -> bool {
+        self.password.is_some()
+    }
+
+    /// Runs one command. `connection` carries everything specific to the
+    /// socket: the negotiated protocol, the name the client gave itself, and
+    /// whether it has authenticated.
+    pub async fn execute(&self, connection: &mut Connection, args: &[Vec<u8>]) -> Response {
+        self.execute_with_store(connection, args, None).await
+    }
+
+    /// Execute existing handlers against an optional private store. Extensions
+    /// can compose ordinary commands without publishing intermediate changes.
+    pub async fn execute_with_store(
+        &self,
+        connection: &mut Connection,
+        args: &[Vec<u8>],
+        overlay: Option<&dyn store::Overlay>,
+    ) -> Response {
+        let Some((name, rest)) = args.split_first() else {
+            return Response::error(RedisError::new("ERR", "empty multibulk"));
+        };
+        let name = keyword(name);
+        let Some(command) = self.command(&name) else {
+            return Response::error(RedisError::new(
+                "ERR",
+                format!("unknown command '{name}', with args beginning with: "),
+            ));
+        };
+        // A declined command is refused by name however it was called, so a
+        // client learns it is unsupported rather than that it miscounted.
+        if !command.declined && !command.accepts(args.len()) {
+            return Response::error(RedisError::wrong_arity(command.name));
+        }
+        if self.password.is_some() && !connection.authenticated && !command.pre_auth() {
+            return Response::error(RedisError::no_auth());
+        }
+        if command.declined {
+            return Response::error(RedisError::unsupported(&command.name.to_ascii_uppercase()));
+        }
+        if let Some(extension) = &self.extension
+            && extension
+                .commands()
+                .iter()
+                .any(|item| item.name == command.name)
+        {
+            return match tokio::time::timeout(
+                self.command_timeout,
+                extension.execute(self, connection, command, rest),
+            )
+            .await
+            {
+                Ok(reply) => Response::reply(reply),
+                Err(_) => Response::error(RedisError::deadline(command.writes())),
+            };
+        }
+        if overlay.is_some() && command.keyspace {
+            return Response::error(RedisError::new(
+                "ERR",
+                "keyspace commands cannot use a private store",
+            ));
+        }
+        let args = args::Args::new(command.name, rest);
+        if !command.reaches_cluster() {
+            return self.local(command, connection, args);
+        }
+        match tokio::time::timeout(self.command_timeout, self.cluster(command, args, overlay)).await
+        {
+            Ok(reply) => Response::reply(reply),
+            Err(_) => Response::error(RedisError::deadline(command.writes())),
+        }
+    }
+
+    async fn cluster(
+        &self,
+        command: &CommandInfo,
+        args: args::Args<'_>,
+        overlay: Option<&dyn store::Overlay>,
+    ) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+        let store = store::Store::new(&self.client, &self.locks).with_overlay(overlay);
+        let max_value = self.limits.max_bulk_bytes;
+        use args::{DeadlineMode::*, TimeUnit::*, TtlForm};
+        match command.name {
+            "get" => strings::get(&store, args).await,
+            "getdel" => strings::getdel(&store, args).await,
+            "getex" => strings::getex(&store, args).await,
+            "getrange" => strings::getrange(&store, args).await,
+            "set" => strings::set(&store, args).await,
+            "setex" => strings::set_with_ttl(&store, args, Seconds).await,
+            "psetex" => strings::set_with_ttl(&store, args, Milliseconds).await,
+            "setnx" => strings::setnx(&store, args).await,
+            "setrange" => strings::setrange(&store, args, max_value).await,
+            "mset" => strings::mset(&store, args).await,
+            "msetnx" => strings::msetnx(&store, args).await,
+            "mget" => strings::mget(&store, args).await,
+            "getset" => strings::getset(&store, args).await,
+            "append" => strings::append(&store, args, max_value).await,
+            "strlen" => strings::strlen(&store, args).await,
+            "incr" => strings::incr_by(&store, args, Some(1)).await,
+            "decr" => strings::incr_by(&store, args, Some(-1)).await,
+            "incrby" | "decrby" => strings::incr_by(&store, args, None).await,
+            "incrbyfloat" => strings::incrbyfloat(&store, args).await,
+            "del" | "unlink" => keys::delete(&store, args).await,
+            "exists" | "touch" => keys::exists(&store, args).await,
+            "type" => keys::key_type(&store, args).await,
+            "rename" => keys::rename(&store, args, false).await,
+            "renamenx" => keys::rename(&store, args, true).await,
+            "expire" => keys::expire(&store, args, TtlForm::new(Seconds, Relative)).await,
+            "pexpire" => keys::expire(&store, args, TtlForm::new(Milliseconds, Relative)).await,
+            "expireat" => keys::expire(&store, args, TtlForm::new(Seconds, Absolute)).await,
+            "pexpireat" => keys::expire(&store, args, TtlForm::new(Milliseconds, Absolute)).await,
+            "persist" => keys::persist(&store, args).await,
+            "ttl" => keys::ttl(&store, args, Seconds).await,
+            "pttl" => keys::ttl(&store, args, Milliseconds).await,
+            "keys" => keyspace::keys(&store, args).await,
+            "scan" => keyspace::scan(&store, args).await,
+            "dbsize" => keyspace::dbsize(&store).await,
+            "randomkey" => keyspace::randomkey(&store).await,
+            other => Err(RedisError::unsupported(&other.to_ascii_uppercase())),
+        }
+    }

+    /// Absolute Unix milliseconds, or `None` for a key that never expires.
+    pub deadline: Option<u64>,
+    pub version: RecordVersion,
+}
+
+/// What a command decided to do with a key, given what it read, and what it
+/// answers once that is done.
+pub enum Change<T> {
+    /// Store this value with this deadline (`None` for no deadline).
+    Put {
+        value: Vec<u8>,
+        deadline: Option<u64>,
+        reply: T,
+    },
+    /// Keep the value, store this deadline. Only for a key that exists.
+    Expire { deadline: Option<u64>, reply: T },
+    /// Delete the key. Only for a key that exists.
+    Delete { reply: T },
+    /// Write nothing.
+    Nothing(T),
+}
+
+/// A private command store supplied by an extension. Implementations keep
+/// writes local and decide separately when to publish them. No remote client
+/// is exposed to a handler while an overlay is active.
+pub trait Overlay: Send + Sync {
+    fn read(&self, key: &[u8]) -> RedisResult<Option<Current>>;
+    fn write(&self, key: &[u8], value: Option<Current>) -> RedisResult<()>;
+}
+
+pub struct Store<'a> {
+    client: &'a SharedClient,
+    locks: &'a KeyLocks,
+    overlay: Option<&'a dyn Overlay>,
+}
+
+impl<'a> Store<'a> {
+    pub fn new(client: &'a SharedClient, locks: &'a KeyLocks) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            client,
+            locks,
+            overlay: None,
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub fn with_overlay(mut self, overlay: Option<&'a dyn Overlay>) -> Self {
+        self.overlay = overlay;
+        self
+    }
+
+    pub async fn client(&self) -> RedisResult<HashringClient> {
+        if self.overlay.is_some() {
+            return Err(RedisError::new(
+                "ERR",
+                "this command requires direct cluster access",
+            ));
+        }
+        self.client.get().await
+    }
+
+    pub async fn read(&self, key: &[u8]) -> RedisResult<Option<Current>> {
+        match self.overlay {
+            Some(overlay) => overlay.read(key),
+            None => read_with(&self.client().await?, key).await,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// An unconditional write, for commands whose result does not depend on
+    /// what the key held: `SET`, `SETEX`, `MSET`.
+    pub async fn put(&self, key: &[u8], value: Vec<u8>, expiry: Expiry) -> RedisResult<()> {
+        if let Some(overlay) = self.overlay {
+            let current = overlay.read(key)?;
+            let deadline = match expiry {
+                Expiry::Keep => current.as_ref().and_then(|value| value.deadline),
+                Expiry::At(deadline) => Some(deadline),
+                Expiry::Clear => None,
+            };
+            return overlay.write(
+                key,
+                Some(Current {
+                    value,
+                    deadline,
+                    version: current.map(|value| value.version).unwrap_or_default(),
+                }),
+            );
+        }
+        self.client()
+            .await?
+            .put_with_expiry(key.to_vec(), value, expiry)
+            .await?;
+        Ok(())
+    }
+
+    /// Preserve the direct conditional-write path for ordinary commands,
+    /// while private stores evaluate the same condition locally.
+    pub async fn put_if_absent(&self, key: &[u8], value: &[u8]) -> RedisResult<bool> {
+        if self.overlay.is_some() {
+            return self
+                .update(key, |current| {
+                    Ok(match current {
+                        Some(_) => Change::Nothing(false),
+                        None => Change::Put {
+                            value: value.to_vec(),
+                            deadline: None,
+                            reply: true,
+                        },
+                    })
+                })
+                .await;
+        }
+        Ok(self
+            .client()
+            .await?
+            .put_if(
+                key.to_vec(),
+                value.to_vec(),
+                Expiry::Clear,
+                Precondition::Absent,
+            )
+            .await?
+            .is_some())
+    }
+
+    /// Reads `key`, asks `decide` what to do, and applies that only if the key
+    /// is still as read; otherwise reads again. `decide` may run more than
+    /// once, so it computes from its argument and nothing else.
+    ///
+    /// The loop ends when a write lands or `decide` writes nothing. Contention
+    /// keeps it going, which the command deadline bounds.
+    pub async fn update<T>(
+        &self,
+        key: &[u8],
+        mut decide: impl FnMut(Option<&Current>) -> RedisResult<Change<T>>,
+    ) -> RedisResult<T> {
+        if let Some(overlay) = self.overlay {
+            let current = overlay.read(key)?;
+            let (next, reply) = match decide(current.as_ref())? {
+                Change::Nothing(reply) => return Ok(reply),
+                Change::Put {
+                    value,
+                    deadline,
+                    reply,
+                } => (
+                    Some(Current {
+                        value,
+                        deadline,
+                        version: current.map(|value| value.version).unwrap_or_default(),
+                    }),
+                    reply,
+                ),
+                Change::Expire { deadline, reply } => {
+                    let mut current = current.expect("expiry needs a key");
+                    current.deadline = deadline;
+                    (Some(current), reply)
+                }
+                Change::Delete { reply } => (None, reply),
+            };
+            overlay.write(key, next)?;
+            return Ok(reply);
+        }
+        let _guard = self.locks.lock(&[key]).await;
+        let client = self.client().await?;
+        loop {
+            let current = read_with(&client, key).await?;
+            let expected = match &current {
+                Some(current) => Precondition::Version(current.version.clone()),
+                None => Precondition::Absent,
+            };
+            let key = key.to_vec();
+            let (applied, reply) = match decide(current.as_ref())? {
+                Change::Nothing(reply) => return Ok(reply),
+                Change::Put {
+                    value,
+                    deadline,
+                    reply,
+                } => {
+                    let applied = client
+                        .put_if(key, value, expiry(deadline), expected)
+                        .await?;
+                    (applied.is_some(), reply)
+                }
+                Change::Expire { deadline, reply } => {
+                    debug_assert!(current.is_some(), "an expiry change needs a key");
+                    let applied = client.set_expiry_if(key, deadline, expected).await?;
+                    (applied.is_some(), reply)
+                }
+                Change::Delete { reply } => {
+                    debug_assert!(current.is_some(), "a delete change needs a key");
+                    let applied = client.delete_if(key, expected).await?;
+                    (applied.is_some(), reply)
+                }
+            };
+            if applied {
+                return Ok(reply);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Runs `operation` on every key, at most `FAN_OUT` at a time, and
+    /// returns the answers in argument order. Any key's failure fails the
+    /// command, reported for the first failing key in argument order: a count
+    /// or a value list built from the keys that happened to answer would be a
+    /// wrong answer that looks like a right one.
+    pub async fn each<'k, T, F, Fut>(
+        &self,
+        keys: &'k [Vec<u8>],
+        operation: F,
+    ) -> RedisResult<Vec<T>>
+    where
+        F: Fn(&'k [u8]) -> Fut,
+        Fut: Future<Output = RedisResult<T>>,
+    {
+        // The futures are built before the stream runs them, which keeps the
+        // closure out of the state held across `.await`; a future built inside
+        // the stream does not prove `Send` for every key lifetime.
+        let operations: Vec<Fut> = keys.iter().map(|key| operation(key)).collect();
+        let results: Vec<RedisResult<T>> =
+            stream::iter(operations).buffered(FAN_OUT).collect().await;
+        results.into_iter().collect()
+    }
+
+    /// [`Store::each`] for an operation that writes. A key that failed after
+    /// another key's write landed leaves the command partly applied, which a
+    /// retryable error would hide: a client that sent it again could, say,
+    /// delete a key someone recreated in between. So the command fails with an
+    /// error that says its writes may have been applied whenever any key
+    /// succeeded or any failure may itself have applied, and with the first
+    /// key's own error only when nothing was written.
+    pub async fn each_write<'k, T, F, Fut>(
+        &self,
+        keys: &'k [Vec<u8>],
+        operation: F,
+    ) -> RedisResult<Vec<T>>
+    where
+        F: Fn(&'k [u8]) -> Fut,
+        Fut: Future<Output = RedisResult<T>>,
+    {
+        let operations: Vec<Fut> = keys.iter().map(|key| operation(key)).collect();
+        let results: Vec<RedisResult<T>> =
+            stream::iter(operations).buffered(FAN_OUT).collect().await;
+        partial_write_outcome(results)
+    }
+}
+
+fn partial_write_outcome<T>(results: Vec<RedisResult<T>>) -> RedisResult<Vec<T>> {
+    let wrote = results.iter().any(Result::is_ok);
+    let mut first = None;
+    let mut ambiguous = false;
+    for error in results.iter().filter_map(|result| result.as_ref().err()) {
+        ambiguous |= error.may_have_applied;
+        first.get_or_insert_with(|| error.clone());
+    }
+    match first {
+        None => Ok(results
+            .into_iter()
+            .map(|result| result.ok().unwrap())
+            .collect()),
+        Some(error) if !wrote && !ambiguous => Err(error),
+        Some(error) => Err(RedisError::outcome_unknown(&format!(
+            "the command failed on some of its keys after others were written ({} {})",
+            error.code, error.message
+        ))),
+    }
+}
+
+async fn read_with(client: &HashringClient, key: &[u8]) -> RedisResult<Option<Current>> {
+    match client.get(key.to_vec()).await {
+        Ok(output) => Ok(Some(Current {
+            value: output.value,
+            deadline: output.expires_at_unix_millis,
+            version: output.version,
+        })),
+        Err(ClientError::Operation(failure)) if failure.code == ErrorCode::NotFound => Ok(None),
+        Err(error) => Err(error.into()),
+    }
+}
+
+/// A conditional write states the deadline it computed from what it read, so
+/// the node never resolves "keep" against a record other than that one.
+pub fn expiry(deadline: Option<u64>) -> Expiry {
+    deadline.map_or(Expiry::Clear, Expiry::At)
+}
+
+/// The deadline a write that keeps the key's deadline stores.
+pub fn kept(current: Option<&Current>) -> Option<u64> {
+    current.and_then(|current| current.deadline)
+}
+
+pub fn value_of(current: Option<&Current>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
+    current.map(|current| current.value.clone())
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_partly_applied_write_is_never_a_plain_retry() {
+        let busy = || RedisError::new("TRYAGAIN", "range is moving");
+        let none_written: Vec<RedisResult<()>> = vec![Err(busy()), Err(busy())];
+        assert_eq!(
+            partial_write_outcome(none_written).unwrap_err().code,
+            "TRYAGAIN"
+        );
+
+        let one_written: Vec<RedisResult<()>> = vec![Ok(()), Err(busy())];
+        let error = partial_write_outcome(one_written).unwrap_err();
+        assert!(error.may_have_applied && error.code == "ERR", "{error}");
+
+        let unknown: Vec<RedisResult<()>> =
+            vec![Err(busy()), Err(RedisError::outcome_unknown("timed out"))];
+        assert!(partial_write_outcome(unknown).unwrap_err().may_have_applied);
+
+        let all: Vec<RedisResult<u8>> = vec![Ok(1), Ok(2)];
+        assert_eq!(partial_write_outcome(all).unwrap(), vec![1, 2]);
+    }
+}

+use std::collections::HashMap;

+use hashring_client::Expiry;

+fn bulk_or_nil(value: Option<Vec<u8>>) -> Reply {
+    match value {
+        Some(value) => Reply::bulk(value),
+        None => Reply::Nil,
+    }
+}
+
+fn too_large() -> RedisError {
+    RedisError::new(
+        "ERR",
+        "string exceeds maximum allowed size (proto-max-bulk-len)",
+    )
+}

+pub async fn get(store: &Store<'_>, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    Ok(bulk_or_nil(
+        store.read(key).await?.map(|current| current.value),
+    ))
+}

+pub async fn strlen(store: &Store<'_>, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    let length = store
+        .read(key)
+        .await?
+        .map_or(0, |current| current.value.len());
+    Ok(Reply::Integer(length as i64))
+}

+pub async fn getrange(store: &Store<'_>, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    let start = args.next_integer()?;
+    let end = args.next_integer()?;
+    let value = store
+        .read(key)
+        .await?
+        .map(|current| current.value)
+        .unwrap_or_default();
+    Ok(Reply::bulk(slice_range(&value, start, end)))
+}

+pub async fn getdel(store: &Store<'_>, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    store
+        .update(key, |current| {
+            Ok(match current {
+                None => Change::Nothing(Reply::Nil),
+                Some(current) => Change::Delete {
+                    reply: Reply::bulk(current.value.clone()),
+                },
+            })
+        })
+        .await
+}

+/// `GETEX key [EX s | PX ms | EXAT ts | PXAT ts | PERSIST]`. Without an option
+/// it is a `GET`; with one it changes only the deadline.
+pub async fn getex(store: &Store<'_>, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    let mut change: Option<Option<u64>> = None;
+    while let Some(option) = args.next_keyword() {
+        if change.is_some() {
+            return Err(RedisError::syntax());
+        }
+        change = Some(match TtlForm::from_option(&option) {
+            Some(form) => Some(positive_deadline(form, args.next_integer()?, "getex")?),
+            None if option == "persist" => None,
+            None => return Err(RedisError::syntax()),
+        });
+    }
+    store
+        .update(key, |current| {
+            let Some(current) = current else {
+                return Ok(Change::Nothing(Reply::Nil));
+            };
+            let reply = Reply::bulk(current.value.clone());
+            Ok(match change {
+                Some(deadline) if deadline != current.deadline => {
+                    Change::Expire { deadline, reply }
+                }
+                _ => Change::Nothing(reply),
+            })
+        })
+        .await
+}

+/// The options `SET` accepts.
+#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
+struct SetOptions {
+    condition: Option<SetCondition>,
+    get: bool,
+    ttl: SetTtl,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
+enum SetCondition {
+    /// `NX`: only if the key does not exist.
+    Absent,
+    /// `XX`: only if it does.
+    Present,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
+enum SetTtl {
+    /// A plain `SET` drops the deadline the key had, as in Redis.
+    Clear,
+    /// `KEEPTTL`.
+    Keep,
+    At(u64),
+}
+
+impl SetOptions {
+    fn parse(args: &mut Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Self> {
+        let mut options = Self {
+            condition: None,
+            get: false,
+            ttl: SetTtl::Clear,
+        };
+        let mut ttl_given = false;
+        while let Some(option) = args.next_keyword() {
+            let mut set_ttl = |ttl| {
+                if std::mem::replace(&mut ttl_given, true) {
+                    return Err(RedisError::syntax());
+                }
+                options.ttl = ttl;
+                Ok(())
+            };
+            match option.as_str() {
+                "nx" | "xx" => {
+                    if options.condition.is_some() {
+                        return Err(RedisError::syntax());
+                    }
+                    options.condition = Some(match option.as_str() {
+                        "nx" => SetCondition::Absent,
+                        _ => SetCondition::Present,
+                    });
+                }
+                "get" => options.get = true,
+                "keepttl" => set_ttl(SetTtl::Keep)?,
+                other => match TtlForm::from_option(other) {
+                    Some(form) => {
+                        let deadline = positive_deadline(form, args.next_integer()?, "set")?;
+                        set_ttl(SetTtl::At(deadline))?;
+                    }
+                    None => return Err(RedisError::syntax()),
+                },
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(options)
+    }
+
+    fn allows(&self, current: Option<&Current>) -> bool {
+        match self.condition {
+            None => true,
+            Some(SetCondition::Absent) => current.is_none(),
+            Some(SetCondition::Present) => current.is_some(),
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn deadline(&self, current: Option<&Current>) -> Option<u64> {
+        match self.ttl {
+            SetTtl::Clear => None,
+            SetTtl::Keep => kept(current),
+            SetTtl::At(deadline) => Some(deadline),
+        }
+    }
+}

+pub async fn set(store: &Store<'_>, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    let value = args.next_owned()?;
+    let options = SetOptions::parse(&mut args)?;
+    if options.condition.is_none() && !options.get {
+        // Nothing the reply or the write depends on is read, so the owner
+        // resolves even `KEEPTTL` itself, under the lock that applies it.
+        let expiry = match options.ttl {
+            SetTtl::Clear => Expiry::Clear,
+            SetTtl::Keep => Expiry::Keep,
+            SetTtl::At(deadline) => Expiry::At(deadline),
+        };
+        store.put(key, value, expiry).await?;
+        return Ok(Reply::status());
+    }
+    store
+        .update(key, |current| {
+            // `GET` answers with what the key held whether or not the
+            // condition let the write through.
+            let reply = match options.get {
+                true => bulk_or_nil(value_of(current)),
+                false => Reply::status(),
+            };
+            if !options.allows(current) {
+                return Ok(Change::Nothing(match options.get {
+                    true => reply,
+                    false => Reply::Nil,
+                }));
+            }
+            Ok(Change::Put {
+                value: value.clone(),
+                deadline: options.deadline(current),
+                reply,
+            })
+        })
+        .await
+}

+pub async fn set_with_ttl(
+    store: &Store<'_>,
+    mut args: Args<'_>,
+    unit: TimeUnit,
+) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    let amount = args.next_integer()?;
+    let value = args.next_owned()?;
+    let deadline = positive_deadline(
+        TtlForm::new(unit, DeadlineMode::Relative),
+        amount,
+        args.name(),
+    )?;
+    store.put(key, value, Expiry::At(deadline)).await?;
+    Ok(Reply::status())

+                reply: bulk_or_nil(value_of(current)),
+            })

+pub async fn setrange(
+    store: &Store<'_>,
+    mut args: Args<'_>,
+    max_value: usize,
+) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    let offset = args.next_integer()?;
+    let patch = args.next_required()?;
+    let offset = usize::try_from(offset).map_err(|_| RedisError::out_of_range())?;
+    if patch.is_empty() {
+        // Redis neither creates nor pads a key for an empty patch; it only
+        // reports the length.
+        let length = store
+            .read(key)
+            .await?
+            .map_or(0, |current| current.value.len());
+        return Ok(Reply::Integer(length as i64));
+    }
+    if offset.saturating_add(patch.len()) > max_value {
+        return Err(too_large());
+    }
+    store
+        .update(key, |current| {
+            let mut value = value_of(current).unwrap_or_default();
+            if offset > value.len() {
+                value.resize(offset, 0);
+            }
+            let end = (offset + patch.len()).min(value.len());
+            value.splice(offset..end, patch.iter().copied());
+            let length = value.len() as i64;
+            Ok(Change::Put {
+                value,
+                deadline: kept(current),
+                reply: Reply::Integer(length),
+            })
+        })
+        .await
+}

+pub async fn append(store: &Store<'_>, mut args: Args<'_>, max_value: usize) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    let suffix = args.next_required()?;
+    store
+        .update(key, |current| {
+            let mut value = value_of(current).unwrap_or_default();
+            if value.len() + suffix.len() > max_value {
+                return Err(too_large());
+            }
+            value.extend_from_slice(suffix);
+            let length = value.len() as i64;
+            // Redis keeps the deadline an `APPEND` finds.
+            Ok(Change::Put {
+                value,
+                deadline: kept(current),
+                reply: Reply::Integer(length),
+            })
+        })
+        .await
+}

+/// `INCR` and `DECR` pass their fixed step; `INCRBY` and `DECRBY` read theirs.
+pub async fn incr_by(
+    store: &Store<'_>,
+    mut args: Args<'_>,
+    step: Option<i64>,
+) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    let delta = match step {
+        Some(step) => step,
+        None => {
+            let amount = args.next_integer()?;
+            match args.name() {
+                "decrby" => amount
+                    .checked_neg()
+                    .ok_or_else(|| RedisError::new("ERR", "decrement would overflow"))?,
+                _ => amount,
+            }
+        }
+    };
+    store
+        .update(key, |current| {
+            // An absent key counts as zero; a key that exists but is not an
+            // integer is an error rather than a reset, which is what Redis
+            // reports.
+            let base = match current {
+                Some(current) => {
+                    parse_integer(&current.value).ok_or_else(RedisError::not_an_integer)?
+                }
+                None => 0,
+            };
+            let updated = base.checked_add(delta).ok_or_else(RedisError::overflow)?;
+            Ok(Change::Put {
+                value: updated.to_string().into_bytes(),
+                deadline: kept(current),
+                reply: Reply::Integer(updated),
+            })
+        })
+        .await
+}

+pub async fn incrbyfloat(store: &Store<'_>, mut args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let key = args.next_required()?;
+    let delta = args.next_float()?;
+    store
+        .update(key, |current| {
+            let base = match current {
+                Some(current) if current.value.is_empty() => 0.0,
+                Some(current) => float(&current.value)?,
+                None => 0.0,
+            };
+            let updated = base + delta;
+            if !updated.is_finite() {
+                return Err(RedisError::new(
+                    "ERR",
+                    "increment would produce NaN or Infinity",
+                ));
+            }
+            let formatted = format_number(updated);
+            // `INCRBYFLOAT` is a rewrite of the value, and Redis keeps the
+            // deadline it finds.
+            Ok(Change::Put {
+                value: formatted.clone().into_bytes(),
+                deadline: kept(current),
+                reply: Reply::bulk(formatted),
+            })
+        })
+        .await
+}

+pub async fn mget(store: &Store<'_>, args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let values = store
+        .each(args.remaining(), |key| async move {
+            Ok(bulk_or_nil(
+                store.read(key).await?.map(|current| current.value),
+            ))
+        })

+    Ok(Reply::Array(values))
+}
+
+/// The pairs of `MSET` or `MSETNX`, one per key. A key named twice takes the
+/// later value, as it would when Redis applies the pairs in order; the writes
+/// here run concurrently, so that order has to be settled before they start.
+fn pairs<'a>(args: &Args<'a>) -> RedisResult<Vec<(&'a [u8], &'a [u8])>> {
+    let rest = args.remaining();
+    if !rest.len().is_multiple_of(2) {
+        return Err(RedisError::wrong_arity(args.name()));
+    }
+    let mut latest: HashMap<&[u8], usize> = HashMap::new();
+    let pairs: Vec<_> = rest
+        .as_chunks::<2>()
+        .0
+        .iter()
+        .map(|pair| (pair[0].as_slice(), pair[1].as_slice()))
+        .collect();
+    for (index, (key, _)) in pairs.iter().enumerate() {
+        latest.insert(key, index);
+    }
+    Ok(pairs
+        .iter()
+        .enumerate()
+        .filter(|(index, (key, _))| latest[key] == *index)
+        .map(|(_, pair)| *pair)
+        .collect())
+}
+
+/// Redis makes `MSET` atomic across keys. It cannot be here: the keys may live
+/// on different owners, and no node offers a write that spans two of them.
+pub async fn mset(store: &Store<'_>, args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let pairs = pairs(&args)?;
+    let keys: Vec<Vec<u8>> = pairs.iter().map(|(key, _)| key.to_vec()).collect();
+    let values: HashMap<&[u8], &[u8]> = pairs.into_iter().collect();
+    store
+        .each_write(&keys, |key| {
+            let value = values[key].to_vec();
+            async move { store.put(key, value, Expiry::Clear).await }
+        })
+        .await?;
+    Ok(Reply::status())
+}
+
+/// `MSETNX` exists to set several keys as one: all of them or none. The keys may
+/// live on different owners and no node offers a write that spans two, so
+/// that promise cannot be kept, and a version that sometimes leaves part of
+/// the keys set would break the callers that use it to claim keys together.
+/// It is declined unless it names one key, where it is `SETNX`.
+pub async fn msetnx(store: &Store<'_>, args: Args<'_>) -> RedisResult<Reply> {
+    let pairs = pairs(&args)?;
+    let [(key, value)] = pairs[..] else {
+        return Err(RedisError::new(
+            "ERR",
+            "MSETNX with more than one key is not supported by the hashring-rs \
+             Redis gateway: the keys cannot be set atomically; see \
+             docs/redis-compatibility.md",
+        ));
+    };
+    Ok(Reply::Integer(i64::from(
+        store.put_if_absent(key, value).await?,
+    )))
+}
+
+/// Redis's `GETRANGE` index rules: a negative index counts from the end, and
+/// both ends are clamped into the value before they are compared.
+fn slice_range(value: &[u8], start: i64, end: i64) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let length = value.len() as i64;
+    if length == 0 {
+        return Vec::new();
+    }
+    let mut start = if start < 0 { length + start } else { start };
+    let mut end = if end < 0 { length + end } else { end };
+    if start < 0 {
+        start = 0;
+    }
+    if end < 0 {
+        end = 0;
+    }
+    if end >= length {
+        end = length - 1;
+    }
+    if start > end || start >= length {
+        return Vec::new();
+    }
+    value[start as usize..=end as usize].to_vec()
+}
+
+/// Redis prints a computed float in the shortest form that reads back as the
+/// same number, and always with a point or an exponent so a client parsing it
+/// as a double is not left guessing.
+fn format_number(value: f64) -> String {
+    let text = format!("{value}");
+    if text.contains(['.', 'e', 'E']) {
+        text
+    } else {
+        format!("{text}.0")
+    }
+}

+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+    use crate::commands::args::now_millis;
+
+    fn parse(parts: &[&[u8]]) -> RedisResult<SetOptions> {
+        let rest: Vec<Vec<u8>> = parts.iter().map(|part| part.to_vec()).collect();
+        SetOptions::parse(&mut Args::new("set", &rest))
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn getrange_follows_the_redis_index_rules() {
+        assert_eq!(slice_range(b"Hello", 0, 4), b"Hello");
+        assert_eq!(slice_range(b"Hello", 1, 3), b"ell");
+        assert_eq!(slice_range(b"Hello", -3, -1), b"llo");
+        assert_eq!(slice_range(b"Hello", 0, 100), b"Hello");
+        // A start far below the beginning clamps to 0 and leaves the end alone.
+        assert_eq!(slice_range(b"Hello", -100, 2), b"Hel");
+        assert_eq!(slice_range(b"Hello", 3, 1), b"");
+        assert_eq!(slice_range(b"Hello", 5, 6), b"");
+        assert_eq!(slice_range(b"", 0, -1), b"");
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn set_options_are_parsed_the_way_redis_documents_them() {
+        assert_eq!(
+            parse(&[b"NX"]).unwrap().condition,
+            Some(SetCondition::Absent)
+        );
+        let SetTtl::At(deadline) = parse(&[b"EX", b"10"]).unwrap().ttl else {
+            panic!("EX did not set a deadline");
+        };
+        assert!(deadline.abs_diff(now_millis() + 10_000) < 1_000);
+        let SetTtl::At(deadline) = parse(&[b"PX", b"500"]).unwrap().ttl else {
+            panic!("PX did not set a deadline");
+        };
+        assert!(
+            deadline.abs_diff(now_millis() + 500) < 100,
+            "PX is milliseconds"
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            parse(&[b"EXAT", b"1800000000"]).unwrap().ttl,
+            SetTtl::At(1_800_000_000_000),
+            "EXAT is seconds"
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            parse(&[b"PXAT", b"1800000000000"]).unwrap().ttl,
+            SetTtl::At(1_800_000_000_000)
+        );
+        // NX and XX together, and two expiry options, are both syntax errors.
+        assert!(parse(&[b"NX", b"XX"]).is_err());
+        assert!(parse(&[b"EX", b"10", b"PX", b"10"]).is_err());
+        assert!(parse(&[b"KEEPTTL", b"EX", b"10"]).is_err());
+        assert!(parse(&[b"EX", b"0"]).is_err());
+        // An option with its operand missing is an error, not a panic.
+        assert!(parse(&[b"EX"]).is_err());
+        assert!(parse(&[b"NX", b"PXAT"]).is_err());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_plain_set_drops_the_deadline_and_keepttl_keeps_it() {
+        assert_eq!(parse(&[]).unwrap().ttl, SetTtl::Clear);
+        assert_eq!(parse(&[b"KEEPTTL"]).unwrap().ttl, SetTtl::Keep);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_key_named_twice_takes_its_later_value() {
+        let rest: Vec<Vec<u8>> = [b"a", b"1", b"b", b"2", b"a", b"3"]
+            .iter()
+            .map(|part| part.to_vec())
+            .collect();
+        let args = Args::new("mset", &rest);
+        let pairs = pairs(&args).unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(
+            pairs,
+            vec![(b"b".as_slice(), b"2".as_slice()), (b"a", b"3")]
+        );
+        let odd: Vec<Vec<u8>> = vec![b"a".to_vec()];
+        assert!(pairs_of(&odd).is_err());
+    }
+
+    fn pairs_of(rest: &[Vec<u8>]) -> RedisResult<Vec<(&[u8], &[u8])>> {
+        pairs(&Args::new("mset", rest))
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_computed_float_always_reads_back_as_a_double() {
+        for value in [1.0_f64, 1.5, -0.25, 1e17, 3.0e-7] {

+                "{text} would be read back as an integer"
+            );
+            assert_eq!(text.parse::<f64>().unwrap(), value);
+        }
+    }

+//! Errors as a Redis client sees them.
+
+use hashring_client::{ClientError, MutationOutcome, OperationFailure};
+use hashring_core::proto::ErrorCode;
+
+/// A failure with the error code in front of the message, which is the part
+/// clients branch on: `redis-py` matches the code, `redis-cli` only prints it.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, thiserror::Error)]
+#[error("{code} {message}")]
+pub struct RedisError {
+    pub code: &'static str,
+    pub message: String,
+    /// A write may have been applied before this was returned, so the command
+    /// is not safe to send again as if nothing happened.
+    pub may_have_applied: bool,
+}
+
+pub type RedisResult<T> = Result<T, RedisError>;
+
+impl RedisError {
+    pub fn new(code: &'static str, message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            code,
+            message: message.into(),
+            may_have_applied: false,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The code for a request this gateway cannot answer at all. Naming the
+    /// command keeps the message useful without the client having to know what
+    /// the gateway does support.
+    pub fn unsupported(command: &str) -> Self {
+        Self::new(
+            "ERR",
+            format!(
+                "{command} is not supported by the hashring-rs Redis gateway; \
+                 see docs/redis-compatibility.md"
+            ),
+        )
+    }
+
+    pub fn wrong_arity(command: &str) -> Self {
+        Self::new(
+            "ERR",
+            format!("wrong number of arguments for '{command}' command"),
+        )
+    }
+
+    pub fn syntax() -> Self {
+        Self::new("ERR", "syntax error")
+    }
+
+    pub fn wrong_type() -> Self {
+        Self::new(
+            "WRONGTYPE",
+            "Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value",
+        )
+    }
+
+    pub fn not_an_integer() -> Self {
+        Self::new("ERR", "value is not an integer or out of range")
+    }
+
+    pub fn not_a_float() -> Self {
+        Self::new("ERR", "value is not a valid float")
+    }
+
+    pub fn wrong_length(expected: usize) -> Self {
+        Self::new(
+            "WRONGTYPE",
+            format!("Expected {expected} arguments, but got a different number of arguments"),
+        )
+    }
+
+    pub fn no_such_key() -> Self {
+        Self::new("ERR", "no such key")
+    }
+
+    pub fn out_of_range() -> Self {
+        Self::new("ERR", "value is out of range, must be positive")
+    }
+
+    pub fn overflow() -> Self {
+        Self::new("ERR", "increment or decrement would overflow")
+    }
+
+    pub fn no_auth() -> Self {
+        Self::new("NOAUTH", "Authentication required.")
+    }
+
+    pub fn wrong_pass() -> Self {
+        Self::new(
+            "WRONGPASS",
+            "invalid username-password pair or user is disabled.",
+        )
+    }
+
+    /// A command that ran out of time. A read can simply be sent again; a
+    /// write may have been applied before the deadline cut it off, which
+    /// `TRYAGAIN` would hide.
+    pub fn deadline(writes: bool) -> Self {
+        match writes {
+            false => Self::new("TRYAGAIN", "the command did not finish before its deadline"),
+            true => Self::outcome_unknown("the command did not finish before its deadline"),
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub fn outcome_unknown(detail: &str) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            may_have_applied: true,
+            ..Self::new(
+                "ERR",
+                format!("{detail}; its writes may or may not have been applied"),
+            )
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub fn protocol(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
+        Self::new("ERR", message)
+    }
+
+    pub fn to_reply(&self) -> crate::resp::Reply {
+        crate::resp::Reply::Error(format!("{} {}", self.code, self.message))
+    }
+}
+
+impl From<ClientError> for RedisError {
+    /// A retryable cluster condition becomes `TRYAGAIN`, which is the code
+    /// clients already treat as "back off and send it again". A permanent
+    /// condition becomes `ERR`, and so does any failure after which a write
+    /// may have been applied: retrying that blindly is not safe.
+    fn from(error: ClientError) -> Self {
+        match error {
+            ClientError::DeadlineExceeded {
+                outcome: MutationOutcome::MayHaveApplied,
+            }
+            | ClientError::TopologyRefresh {
+                outcome: MutationOutcome::MayHaveApplied,
+                ..
+            }
+            | ClientError::Rpc {
+                outcome: MutationOutcome::MayHaveApplied,
+                ..
+            } => Self::outcome_unknown(&error.to_string()),
+            ClientError::Operation(failure) => Self::from(failure),
+            ClientError::TopologyRefresh { source, .. } => Self::new(
+                "TRYAGAIN",
+                format!("cluster topology is unavailable: {source}"),
+            ),
+            ClientError::Topology(source) => Self::new(
+                "CLUSTERDOWN",
+                format!("cluster topology is unavailable: {source}"),
+            ),
+            ClientError::DeadlineExceeded { .. } => Self::new(
+                "TRYAGAIN",
+                "the operation did not finish before its deadline",
+            ),
+            ClientError::MissingVersion => {
+                Self::new("ERR", "the cluster returned a record without a version")
+            }
+            ClientError::Rpc { code, message, .. } => {
+                if code == tonic::Code::Unavailable {
+                    Self::new(
+                        "TRYAGAIN",
+                        format!("cluster node is unavailable: {message}"),
+                    )
+                } else {
+                    Self::new("ERR", message)
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+impl From<OperationFailure> for RedisError {
+    fn from(failure: OperationFailure) -> Self {
+        let message = failure.message.trim().to_owned();
+        if failure.outcome == MutationOutcome::MayHaveApplied {
+            return Self::outcome_unknown(&message);
+        }
+        match failure.code {
+            ErrorCode::NotFound => Self::new(
+                "ERR",
+                if message.is_empty() {
+                    "key not found".into()
+                } else {
+                    message
+                },
+            ),
+            ErrorCode::TooLarge => Self::new("OOM", message),
+            ErrorCode::Moved
+            | ErrorCode::RangeBusy
+            | ErrorCode::Unavailable
+            | ErrorCode::TemporarilyUnavailable
+            | ErrorCode::ResourceExhausted
+            | ErrorCode::ReplicaNotReady
+            | ErrorCode::LeaseExpired => Self::new("TRYAGAIN", message),
+            // A write whose outcome is unknown is reported as an error rather

+        assert_eq!(

+            "TRYAGAIN"

+            "TRYAGAIN"

+    #[test]
+    fn a_permanent_condition_is_an_error_not_a_retry() {
+        assert_eq!(

+            "ERR"

+            RedisError::from(failure(ErrorCode::TooLarge, false)).code,
+            "OOM"

+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn an_unknown_write_outcome_is_reported_as_an_error() {
+        assert_eq!(
+            RedisError::from(failure(ErrorCode::OutcomeUnknown, true)).code,
+            "ERR"
+        );
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn the_reply_carries_the_code_the_client_matches_on() {
+        assert_eq!(
+            RedisError::wrong_arity("get").to_reply(),
+            crate::resp::Reply::Error("ERR wrong number of arguments for 'get' command".into())
+        );
+    }
+}

+//! A Redis-protocol front end for a hashring-rs cluster.
+//!
+//! The gateway speaks RESP on a TCP port and reaches the cluster through
+//! [`hashring_client`], so a Redis client connects to it the way it would to a
+//! Redis server: `redis-cli`, `redis-py`, Jedis, Lettuce and go-redis all work
+//! against it in single-node mode, and none of them has to know that the data
+//! lives on ten nodes behind a consistent hash ring.
+//!
+//! What it is not: Redis Cluster. There is no slot table, no `MOVED`, and no
+//! gossip, because the cluster already has one owner per key and a coordinator
+//! that hands out the whole topology. Routing stays in the client, where it
+//! already was.
+//!
+//! The commands it answers, the ones it declines, and the places where its
+//! semantics differ from a single-threaded Redis server are all in
+//! `docs/redis-compatibility.md`.
+
+use std::{net::SocketAddr, sync::Arc, time::Duration};
+
+pub mod client;
+pub mod commands;
+pub mod error;
+pub mod resp;
+pub mod server;
+pub mod table;
+
+use client::SharedClient;
+use commands::Dispatcher;
+
+/// The version this gateway reports in `HELLO` and `INFO`. It is the
+/// hashring-rs version, not a Redis version, so a client that checks for Redis
+/// 7 features does not find them claimed.
+pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
+
+/// How the gateway is set up. Every field has a default a deployment can
+/// override, and none of them changes what a command means.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
+pub struct GatewayConfig {
+    /// The coordinator the cluster's topology comes from.
+    pub coordinator: String,
+    /// The port Redis clients connect to.
+    pub listen: SocketAddr,
+    /// How long one command may take against the cluster before it is reported
+    /// as not finished. Redis has no such deadline; a proxy does, because the
+    /// cluster can be mid-migration and slow to answer.
+    pub operation_timeout: Duration,
+    /// When set, a connection must send `AUTH` before it may read or write.
+    pub password: Option<Arc<str>>,
+    pub limits: resp::Limits,
+    /// Connections open at once; one more is answered with Redis's
+    /// `max number of clients reached` and closed. Redis's `maxclients`.
+    pub max_connections: usize,
+}
+
+impl Default for GatewayConfig {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            coordinator: "http://127.0.0.1:50050".into(),
+            listen: SocketAddr::from(([127, 0, 0, 1], 6379)),
+            operation_timeout: Duration::from_secs(5),
+            password: None,
+            limits: resp::Limits::default(),
+            max_connections: 10_000,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// Binds the port and serves clients until `shutdown` is set.
+///
+/// The coordinator is contacted on the first command rather than before the
+/// port is opened, so a gateway may start before, alongside, or instead of the
+/// coordinator being up; clients get `-TRYAGAIN` until the cluster answers.
+pub async fn serve(
+    config: GatewayConfig,
+    shutdown: tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<bool>,
+) -> std::io::Result<()> {
+    serve_inner(config, shutdown, None).await
+}
+
+/// Serve the same protocol and connection handling with additional commands.
+pub async fn serve_with_extension(
+    config: GatewayConfig,
+    shutdown: tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<bool>,
+    extension: Arc<dyn commands::CommandExtension>,
+) -> std::io::Result<()> {
+    serve_inner(config, shutdown, Some(extension)).await
+}
+
+async fn serve_inner(
+    config: GatewayConfig,
+    shutdown: tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<bool>,
+    extension: Option<Arc<dyn commands::CommandExtension>>,
+) -> std::io::Result<()> {
+    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(config.listen).await?;
+    let local = listener.local_addr()?;
+    let client = Arc::new(SharedClient::new(
+        config.coordinator.clone(),
+        config.operation_timeout,
+    ));
+    let mut dispatcher = Dispatcher::new(
+        client,
+        config.password.clone(),
+        config.limits,
+        config.operation_timeout,
+    );
+    if let Some(extension) = extension {
+        dispatcher = dispatcher.with_extension(extension);
+    }
+    let dispatcher = Arc::new(dispatcher);
+    tracing::info!(
+        listen = %local,
+        coordinator = %config.coordinator,
+        operation_timeout_ms = config.operation_timeout.as_millis(),
+        authentication = config.password.is_some(),
+        max_connections = config.max_connections,
+        "redis gateway ready"
+    );
+    server::Gateway::new(dispatcher, shutdown, config.max_connections)
+        .serve(listener)
+        .await
+}

+//! The Redis serialization protocol, as much of it as this gateway speaks.
+//!
+//! Requests arrive as RESP arrays of bulk strings, which is the only framing
+//! real clients use, plus the inline form `telnet` and `redis-cli` fall back to
+//! when a command is typed by hand. Replies are written for whichever protocol
+//! version the connection negotiated: the same logical answer, encoded as a
+//! null bulk under RESP2 and as the RESP3 null under RESP3, for instance, or as
+//! a map instead of a flat array.
+
+/// Which dialect a connection speaks. Everything else about a reply is the
+/// same; only the encoding of null, maps and sets differs.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
+pub enum Protocol {
+    Resp2,
+    Resp3,
+}
+
+impl Protocol {
+    pub fn version(self) -> u8 {
+        match self {
+            Self::Resp2 => 2,
+            Self::Resp3 => 3,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// Bounds on what a connection may send, so a client cannot make the gateway
+/// allocate without limit before a single command runs.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+pub struct Limits {
+    /// Largest accepted bulk string. The largest value a node accepts is 8
+    /// MiB, and a key is 64 KiB, so nothing a node would store is refused here.
+    pub max_bulk_bytes: usize,
+    pub max_arguments: usize,
+    /// Longest line without a newline: an inline command, or a `*` or `$`
+    /// header. Redis's own bound, so a stream of bytes that never ends a line
+    /// is refused instead of buffered.
+    pub max_line_bytes: usize,
+    /// Bytes a connection may have received and not yet run, across however
+    /// many requests they hold. Redis's `client-query-buffer-limit`.
+    pub max_query_buffer_bytes: usize,
+}
+
+impl Default for Limits {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            max_bulk_bytes: 16 * 1024 * 1024,
+            max_arguments: 1 << 17,
+            max_line_bytes: 64 * 1024,
+            max_query_buffer_bytes: 1024 * 1024 * 1024,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+impl Limits {
+    /// What a connection that has not authenticated may send. The handshake
+    /// needs a handful of short arguments; anything larger is someone without
+    /// the password asking the gateway to hold memory for them. Redis uses the
+    /// same two numbers.
+    pub fn unauthenticated(self) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            max_bulk_bytes: self.max_bulk_bytes.min(16 * 1024),
+            max_arguments: self.max_arguments.min(10),
+            ..self
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// What a request frame parsed off the buffer turned out to be.
+#[derive(Debug)]
+pub enum Frame {
+    /// A complete command: its arguments, first one the command name.
+    Command {
+        args: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
+        /// Bytes consumed from the front of the buffer.
+        length: usize,
+    },
+    /// The buffer holds a prefix of a request; read more and try again.
+    Incomplete,
+    /// The bytes cannot be a request in any protocol version. The connection
+    /// cannot resynchronize after this, so it is answered and closed.
+    Invalid(String),
+}
+
+/// One parsed request.
+pub fn parse(buffer: &[u8], limits: &Limits) -> Frame {
+    match buffer.first() {
+        // A newline before anything else is a blank line between pipelined
+        // commands, which Redis skips.
+        Some(b'\r') | Some(b'\n') => match find_line_end(buffer, 1) {
+            Some(end) => Frame::Command {
+                args: Vec::new(),
+                length: end,
+            },
+            None => Frame::Incomplete,
+        },
+        Some(b'*') => parse_multibulk(buffer, limits),
+        Some(_) => parse_inline(buffer, limits),
+        None => Frame::Incomplete,
+    }
+}
+
+/// `*<count>\r\n` followed by that many `$<length>\r\n<bytes>\r\n` elements.
+fn parse_multibulk(buffer: &[u8], limits: &Limits) -> Frame {
+    let count = match read_header(buffer, 0, b'*', limits) {
+        Header::Incomplete => return Frame::Incomplete,
+        Header::Invalid(error) => return Frame::Invalid(error),
+        Header::Found { value, next } => (value, next),
+    };
+    if count.0 > limits.max_arguments {
+        return Frame::Invalid(format!(
+            "invalid multibulk length, the command has too many arguments (at most {})",
+            limits.max_arguments
+        ));
+    }
+    let mut args = Vec::with_capacity(count.0.min(1024));
+    let mut cursor = count.1;
+    for _ in 0..count.0 {
+        let (length, start) = match read_header(buffer, cursor, b'$', limits) {
+            Header::Incomplete => return Frame::Incomplete,
+            Header::Invalid(error) => return Frame::Invalid(error),
+            Header::Found { value, next } => (value, next),
+        };
+        if length > limits.max_bulk_bytes {
+            return Frame::Invalid(format!(
+                "invalid bulk length, a single argument is at most {} bytes",
+                limits.max_bulk_bytes
+            ));
+        }
+        // The bytes, then the CRLF that ends the element.
+        let Some(end) = start
+            .checked_add(length)
+            .and_then(|at| at.checked_add(2))
+            .filter(|end| *end <= buffer.len())
+        else {
+            return Frame::Incomplete;
+        };
+        if &buffer[end - 2..end] != b"\r\n" {
+            return Frame::Invalid("invalid bulk length, missing CRLF after argument".into());
+        }
+        args.push(buffer[start..start + length].to_vec());
+        cursor = end;
+    }
+    Frame::Command {
+        args,
+        length: cursor,
+    }
+}
+
+/// A `<prefix><digits><CRLF>` header at one offset: the number it holds and the
+/// offset of the first byte after the line.
+enum Header {
+    Found { value: usize, next: usize },
+    Incomplete,
+    Invalid(String),
+}
+
+fn read_header(buffer: &[u8], index: usize, expected: u8, limits: &Limits) -> Header {
+    let Some(byte) = buffer.get(index) else {
+        return Header::Incomplete;
+    };
+    if *byte != expected {
+        return Header::Invalid(format!(
+            "expected '{}', but got something else",
+            expected as char
+        ));
+    }
+    let digits_start = index + 1;
+    let Some(end) = find_line_end(buffer, digits_start) else {
+        if buffer.len() - index > limits.max_line_bytes {
+            return Header::Invalid(match expected {
+                b'*' => "too big mbulk count string".into(),
+                _ => "too big bulk count string".into(),
+            });
+        }
+        return Header::Incomplete;
+    };
+    // `end` is past the line ending, so drop the LF and a CR if the client sent
+    // one; a bare LF ends a line here too.
+    let mut digits = &buffer[digits_start..end - 1];
+    if digits.last() == Some(&b'\r') {
+        digits = &digits[..digits.len() - 1];
+    }
+    let Ok(text) = std::str::from_utf8(digits) else {
+        return Header::Invalid("invalid multibulk length".into());
+    };
+    match text.parse::<usize>() {
+        Ok(value) => Header::Found { value, next: end },
+        Err(_) => Header::Invalid(if expected == b'*' {
+            "invalid multibulk length".into()
+        } else {
+            "invalid bulk length".into()
+        }),
+    }
+}
+
+/// The `PING\r\n` form, with arguments separated by spaces.
+fn parse_inline(buffer: &[u8], limits: &Limits) -> Frame {
+    let Some(end) = find_line_end(buffer, 0) else {
+        if buffer.len() > limits.max_line_bytes {
+            return Frame::Invalid("too big inline request".into());
+        }
+        return Frame::Incomplete;
+    };
+    let line = &buffer[..end];
+    let mut args = Vec::new();
+    for argument in line.split(|byte| byte.is_ascii_whitespace()) {
+        if argument.is_empty() {
+            continue;
+        }
+        if argument.len() > limits.max_bulk_bytes {
+            return Frame::Invalid(format!(
+                "invalid bulk length, a single argument is at most {} bytes",
+                limits.max_bulk_bytes
+            ));
+        }
+        args.push(argument.to_vec());
+    }
+    if args.len() > limits.max_arguments {
+        return Frame::Invalid(format!(
+            "invalid multibulk length, the command has too many arguments (at most {})",
+            limits.max_arguments
+        ));
+    }
+    Frame::Command { args, length: end }
+}
+
+/// Reads a `<prefix><number>\r\n` header that starts at `start`, returning the
+/// number and leaving the cursor on the first byte after the line.
+/// The offset just past the line ending at or after `start`. A bare LF ends a
+/// line as well as CRLF, so a hand-typed line through `nc` is not a protocol
+/// error.
+fn find_line_end(buffer: &[u8], start: usize) -> Option<usize> {
+    buffer[start..]
+        .iter()
+        .position(|byte| *byte == b'\n')
+        .map(|offset| start + offset + 1)
+}
+
+/// Everything a command can answer with. A reply is built without knowing how
+/// it will be encoded, so a handler does not have to know the connection's
+/// protocol version.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub enum Reply {
+    /// A one-word status such as `OK`.
+    Simple(String),
+    Error(String),
+    Integer(i64),
+    /// A byte string, or `None` for a missing one.
+    Bulk(Option<Vec<u8>>),
+    Array(Vec<Reply>),
+    /// Bulk-keyed pairs. RESP2 has no map, so this encodes as a flat array.
+    Map(Vec<(Vec<u8>, Reply)>),
+    Set(Vec<Vec<u8>>),
+    Double(f64),
+    Boolean(bool),
+    /// A missing value, in whichever spelling the protocol has for one.
+    Nil,
+}
+
+impl Reply {
+    pub fn bulk(value: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) -> Self {
+        Self::Bulk(Some(value.into()))
+    }
+
+    pub fn status() -> Self {
+        Self::Simple("OK".into())
+    }
+
+    pub fn is_error(&self) -> bool {
+        matches!(self, Self::Error(_))
+    }
+}
+
+pub fn encode(reply: &Reply, protocol: Protocol, out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
+    match reply {
+        Reply::Simple(text) => {
+            out.push(b'+');
+            out.extend_from_slice(text.as_bytes());
+            out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
+        }
+        Reply::Error(message) => {
+            out.push(b'-');
+            out.extend_from_slice(message.as_bytes());
+            out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
+        }
+        Reply::Integer(value) => {
+            out.push(b':');
+            out.extend_from_slice(value.to_string().as_bytes());
+            out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
+        }
+        Reply::Bulk(Some(value)) => {
+            out.push(b'$');
+            out.extend_from_slice(value.len().to_string().as_bytes());
+            out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
+            out.extend_from_slice(value);
+            out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
+        }
+        Reply::Bulk(None) | Reply::Nil => match protocol {
+            // RESP2 spells an absent value as a bulk of length -1.
+            Protocol::Resp2 => out.extend_from_slice(b"$-1\r\n"),
+            Protocol::Resp3 => out.extend_from_slice(b"_\r\n"),
+        },
+        Reply::Array(items) => {
+            out.push(b'*');
+            out.extend_from_slice(items.len().to_string().as_bytes());
+            out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
+            for item in items {
+                encode(item, protocol, out);
+            }
+        }
+        Reply::Set(items) => match protocol {
+            Protocol::Resp2 => {
+                out.push(b'*');
+                out.extend_from_slice(items.len().to_string().as_bytes());
+                out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
+                for item in items {
+                    encode(&Reply::bulk(item.clone()), protocol, out);
+                }
+            }
+            Protocol::Resp3 => {
+                out.push(b'~');
+                out.extend_from_slice(items.len().to_string().as_bytes());
+                out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
+                for item in items {
+                    encode(&Reply::bulk(item.clone()), protocol, out);
+                }
+            }
+        },
+        Reply::Map(entries) => match protocol {
+            Protocol::Resp2 => {
+                out.push(b'*');
+                out.extend_from_slice((entries.len() * 2).to_string().as_bytes());
+                out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
+                for (key, value) in entries {
+                    encode(&Reply::bulk(key.clone()), protocol, out);
+                    encode(value, protocol, out);
+                }
+            }
+            Protocol::Resp3 => {
+                out.push(b'%');
+                out.extend_from_slice(entries.len().to_string().as_bytes());
+                out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
+                for (key, value) in entries {
+                    encode(&Reply::bulk(key.clone()), protocol, out);
+                    encode(value, protocol, out);
+                }
+            }
+        },
+        Reply::Double(value) => {
+            out.push(b',');
+            out.extend_from_slice(format_double(*value).as_bytes());
+            out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
+        }
+        Reply::Boolean(value) => {
+            out.push(b'#');
+            out.extend_from_slice(if *value { b"t" } else { b"f" });
+            out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// RESP3 doubles reject the shapes Redis never emits, and `inf` and `nan` are
+/// rejected outright because they are not valid RESP3 doubles.
+fn format_double(value: f64) -> String {
+    if !value.is_finite() {
+        return "0".into();
+    }
+    let text = format!("{value}");
+    if text.contains(['.', 'e', 'E', 'n', 'i']) {
+        text
+    } else {
+        format!("{text}.0")
+    }
+}

+        assert!(matches!(parse(request, &limits()), Frame::Incomplete));
+    }

+    fn parses_an_inline_command() {
+        let Frame::Command { args, length } = parse(b"PING hello\r\n", &limits()) else {
+            panic!("expected a command");
+        };

+        assert_eq!(args, vec![b"PING".to_vec(), b"hello".to_vec()]);

+            panic!("expected a command");
+        };

+    }

+    fn rejects_a_bulk_longer_than_the_limit() {
+        let limits = Limits {

+        assert!(matches!(parse(request, &limits), Frame::Invalid(_)));
+    }
+

+    fn a_line_that_never_ends_is_refused_instead_of_buffered() {
+        let limits = Limits {
+            max_line_bytes: 16,

+            panic!("expected a command");
+        };

+    }
+
+    fn encoded(reply: &Reply, protocol: Protocol) -> String {
+        let mut out = Vec::new();
+        encode(reply, protocol, &mut out);
+        String::from_utf8(out).unwrap()
+    }
+

+    fn a_missing_value_uses_the_protocol_null() {
+        assert_eq!(encoded(&Reply::Nil, Protocol::Resp2), "$-1\r\n");
+        assert_eq!(encoded(&Reply::Nil, Protocol::Resp3), "_\r\n");
+    }

+        let reply = Reply::Map(vec![

+        );

+            "%2\r\n$9\r\nmaxmemory\r\n$1\r\n0\r\n$4\r\nsave\r\n$0\r\n\r\n"
+        );
+    }
