+    fn a_set_is_an_array_in_resp2() {
+        let reply = Reply::Set(vec![b"a".to_vec(), b"b".to_vec()]);

+            "*2\r\n$1\r\na\r\n$1\r\nb\r\n"
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            encoded(&reply, Protocol::Resp3),
+            "~2\r\n$1\r\na\r\n$1\r\nb\r\n"
+        );
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_double_always_carries_a_point_or_an_exponent() {
+        assert_eq!(encoded(&Reply::Double(2.0), Protocol::Resp3), ",2.0\r\n");
+        assert_eq!(encoded(&Reply::Double(2.5), Protocol::Resp3), ",2.5\r\n");
+        assert_eq!(encoded(&Reply::Double(f64::NAN), Protocol::Resp3), ",0\r\n");
+    }

+//! Accepting connections and running each one's commands in order.
+//!
+//! One connection is one task. Commands on a connection are answered in the
+//! order they arrive, which is what a Redis client expects and what lets a
+//! pipelined burst be written back as one reply stream.
+//!
+//! This module owns what a command does to its connection: a command returns
+//! its reply and an [`Effect`], and only here are replies suppressed, the
+//! reply mode switched, or the connection closed. It also owns the bounds on a
+//! connection: how many may be open, how much a client may have sent and not
+//! yet had run, and how much reply output is held before it is written.
+
+use std::{
+    sync::{
+        Arc,
+        atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering},
+    },
+    time::Duration,
+};
+
+use tokio::{
+    io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt},
+    net::{TcpListener, TcpStream},
+    sync::Semaphore,
+};
+
+use crate::{
+    commands::{Connection, Dispatcher, Effect, ReplyMode, Response},
+    error::RedisError,
+    resp::{self, Frame, Reply},
+};
+
+/// How much is read from a socket at a time. Large enough that a pipelined
+/// burst usually arrives whole, small enough not to hold a large read buffer
+/// per connection.
+const READ_CHUNK: usize = 64 * 1024;
+
+/// Replies held for one pipelined burst before they are written out, so a
+/// burst of large `GET`s does not hold every value in memory at once.
+const REPLY_FLUSH_BYTES: usize = 1024 * 1024;
+
+/// How long the listener waits after an `accept` failure that means the
+/// process is out of file descriptors, so it does not spin on the same error.
+const ACCEPT_BACKOFF: Duration = Duration::from_millis(100);
+
+pub struct Gateway {
+    dispatcher: Arc<Dispatcher>,
+    shutdown: tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<bool>,
+    max_connections: usize,
+}
+
+impl Gateway {
+    pub fn new(
+        dispatcher: Arc<Dispatcher>,
+        shutdown: tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<bool>,
+        max_connections: usize,
+    ) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            dispatcher,
+            shutdown,
+            max_connections,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Serves until the process is asked to stop. A failed `accept` loses that
+    /// one connection, never the listener.
+    pub async fn serve(self, listener: TcpListener) -> std::io::Result<()> {
+        let mut shutdown = self.shutdown;
+        let permits = Arc::new(Semaphore::new(self.max_connections));
+        loop {
+            tokio::select! {
+                _ = shutdown.changed() => {
+                    if *shutdown.borrow() {
+                        return Ok(());
+                    }
+                }
+                accepted = listener.accept() => {
+                    let (socket, address) = match accepted {
+                        Ok(accepted) => accepted,
+                        Err(error) => {
+                            tracing::warn!(%error, "redis gateway could not accept a connection");
+                            if is_resource_exhaustion(&error) {
+                                tokio::time::sleep(ACCEPT_BACKOFF).await;
+                            }
+                            continue;
+                        }
+                    };
+                    let dispatcher = self.dispatcher.clone();
+                    let permit = permits.clone().try_acquire_owned();
+                    tokio::spawn(async move {
+                        let result = match permit {
+                            Ok(_permit) => serve_connection(dispatcher, socket).await,
+                            Err(_) => refuse(socket).await,
+                        };
+                        if let Err(error) = result {
+                            tracing::debug!(%address, %error, "redis gateway connection ended");
+                        }
+                    });
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+fn is_resource_exhaustion(error: &std::io::Error) -> bool {
+    // EMFILE and ENFILE: the process or the system is out of descriptors.
+    matches!(error.raw_os_error(), Some(23 | 24))
+}
+
+/// Redis's answer once `maxclients` connections are open.
+async fn refuse(mut socket: TcpStream) -> std::io::Result<()> {
+    let mut out = Vec::new();
+    let error = RedisError::new("ERR", "max number of clients reached");
+    resp::encode(&error.to_reply(), resp::Protocol::Resp2, &mut out);
+    socket.write_all(&out).await
+}
+
+async fn serve_connection(dispatcher: Arc<Dispatcher>, socket: TcpStream) -> std::io::Result<()> {
+    // A reply that waits on another request to be written is a reply that
+    // waits on the cluster, so Nagle would add latency to every command that is
+    // not part of a pipeline.
+    let _ = socket.set_nodelay(true);
+    let (mut reader, mut writer) = socket.into_split();
+    let mut connection = Connection::new(next_connection_id(), !dispatcher.requires_auth());
+    let mut pending: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(READ_CHUNK);
+    let mut chunk = vec![0_u8; READ_CHUNK];
+    let mut replies = Vec::new();
+    loop {
+        let read = reader.read(&mut chunk).await?;
+        if read == 0 {
+            // The client closed between commands, which is not an error.
+            return Ok(());
+        }
+        pending.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..read]);
+        // Checked on what has arrived, before anything in it runs, so the
+        // bound does not depend on how the socket happened to split the bytes.
+        let buffer_limit = match connection.authenticated {
+            true => dispatcher.limits(),
+            false => dispatcher.limits().unauthenticated(),
+        }
+        .max_query_buffer_bytes;
+        if pending.len() > buffer_limit {
+            return close_with(
+                &mut writer,
+                &mut replies,
+                &connection,
+                "query buffer limit reached",
+            )
+            .await;
+        }
+        let mut consumed = 0;
+        loop {
+            // A connection is held to the handshake's bounds until it has
+            // authenticated, which can change between two pipelined requests.
+            let limits = match connection.authenticated {
+                true => dispatcher.limits(),
+                false => dispatcher.limits().unauthenticated(),
+            };
+            match resp::parse(&pending[consumed..], &limits) {
+                Frame::Command { args, length } => {
+                    consumed += length;
+                    if args.is_empty() {
+                        continue;
+                    }
+                    let response = dispatcher.execute(&mut connection, &args).await;
+                    let (reply, close) = settle(&mut connection, response);
+                    if let Some(reply) = reply {
+                        resp::encode(&reply, connection.protocol, &mut replies);
+                    }
+                    if close {
+                        writer.write_all(&replies).await?;
+                        return Ok(());
+                    }
+                    if replies.len() >= REPLY_FLUSH_BYTES {
+                        writer.write_all(&replies).await?;
+                        replies.clear();
+                    }
+                }
+                Frame::Incomplete => break,
+                Frame::Invalid(message) => {
+                    // The stream cannot be resynchronized after a bad frame,
+                    // so the error goes out and the connection ends.
+                    return close_with(&mut writer, &mut replies, &connection, &message).await;
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        pending.drain(..consumed);
+        if !replies.is_empty() {
+            writer.write_all(&replies).await?;
+            replies.clear();
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+async fn close_with(
+    writer: &mut tokio::net::tcp::OwnedWriteHalf,
+    replies: &mut Vec<u8>,
+    connection: &Connection,
+    message: &str,
+) -> std::io::Result<()> {
+    let error = RedisError::protocol(format!("Protocol error: {message}"));
+    resp::encode(&error.to_reply(), connection.protocol, replies);
+    writer.write_all(replies).await
+}
+
+/// Applies a command's effect to its connection and decides whether its reply
+/// is written: the reply to send, if any, and whether to close afterwards.
+fn settle(connection: &mut Connection, response: Response) -> (Option<Reply>, bool) {
+    let reply = response.reply.unwrap_or_else(|error| error.to_reply());
+    match response.effect {
+        // `ON` is answered; `OFF` and `SKIP` are not, which is how Redis tells
+        // a client the switch took effect. `SKIP` while replies are off
+        // changes nothing, as in Redis.
+        Effect::ReplyMode(mode) => {
+            if !(mode == ReplyMode::Skip && connection.reply_mode == ReplyMode::Off) {
+                connection.reply_mode = mode;
+            }
+            ((mode == ReplyMode::On).then_some(reply), false)
+        }
+        Effect::Close => (visible(connection, reply), true),
+        Effect::None => (visible(connection, reply), false),
+    }
+}
+
+/// The reply as the connection's reply mode lets it through, consuming a
+/// pending `SKIP`.
+fn visible(connection: &mut Connection, reply: Reply) -> Option<Reply> {
+    match connection.reply_mode {
+        ReplyMode::On => Some(reply),
+        ReplyMode::Skip => {
+            connection.reply_mode = ReplyMode::On;
+            None
+        }
+        ReplyMode::Off => None,
+    }
+}
+
+fn next_connection_id() -> u64 {
+    static COUNTER: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(1);
+    COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
+}
+

+//! The commands this gateway claims, and how much of each one it implements.
+//!
+//! `COMMAND` answers from this table, and the dispatcher checks every request
+//! against it before a handler runs: whether the command exists, whether it is
+//! declined, its arity, and whether it may run before `AUTH`. So what a client
+//! is told the server supports is what the server enforces. Arity, flags and
+//! key positions follow Redis, because clients use them to check a command
+//! before sending it and to split a multi-key command across a cluster.
+
+use crate::resp::Reply;
+
+/// One command as `COMMAND` describes it.
+pub struct CommandInfo {
+    pub name: &'static str,
+    /// Negative means "at least this many arguments", as in Redis.
+    pub arity: i64,
+    pub flags: &'static [&'static str],
+    pub first_key: i64,
+    pub last_key: i64,
+    pub step: i64,
+    /// Known but refused; see docs/redis-compatibility.md.
+    pub declined: bool,
+    /// Reaches the cluster without naming a key: it walks the keyspace.
+    pub keyspace: bool,
+}
+
+const READ: &[&str] = &["readonly", "fast"];
+const WRITE: &[&str] = &["write", "denyoom"];
+const ADMIN: &[&str] = &["admin", "loading", "stale"];
+const LOCAL: &[&str] = &["loading", "stale", "fast"];
+
+const fn command(name: &'static str, arity: i64, flags: &'static [&'static str]) -> CommandInfo {
+    CommandInfo {
+        name,
+        arity,
+        flags,
+        first_key: 0,
+        last_key: 0,
+        step: 0,
+        declined: false,
+        keyspace: false,
+    }
+}
+
+const fn declined(name: &'static str, arity: i64, flags: &'static [&'static str]) -> CommandInfo {
+    CommandInfo {
+        declined: true,
+        ..command(name, arity, flags)
+    }
+}
+
+const fn keyspace(name: &'static str, arity: i64, flags: &'static [&'static str]) -> CommandInfo {
+    CommandInfo {
+        keyspace: true,
+        ..command(name, arity, flags)
+    }
+}
+
+const fn keyed(
+    name: &'static str,
+    arity: i64,
+    flags: &'static [&'static str],
+    first_key: i64,
+    last_key: i64,
+    step: i64,
+) -> CommandInfo {
+    CommandInfo {
+        name,
+        arity,
+        flags,
+        first_key,
+        last_key,
+        step,
+        declined: false,
+        keyspace: false,
+    }
+}
+
+/// Every command this gateway answers, and the commands it knows but declines.
+pub const COMMANDS: &[CommandInfo] = &[
+    // Connection and administration. These answer from the gateway itself and
+    // never reach the cluster.
+    command("ping", -1, &["fast"]),
+    command("echo", 2, READ),
+    command("hello", -1, &["no_auth"]),
+    command("auth", -2, &["no_auth", "loading", "stale"]),
+    command("select", 2, LOCAL),
+    command("client", -2, ADMIN),
+    command("reset", 1, &["no_auth", "loading", "stale"]),
+    command("quit", -1, &["no_auth", "loading", "stale"]),
+    command("command", -1, LOCAL),
+    command("info", -1, LOCAL),
+    command("config", -2, ADMIN),
+    // Strings. Every value in this gateway is a byte string.
+    keyed("get", 2, READ, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("getdel", 2, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("getex", -2, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("getrange", 4, READ, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("set", -3, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("setex", 4, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("psetex", 4, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("setnx", 3, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("setrange", 4, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("mset", -3, WRITE, 1, -1, 2),
+    keyed("msetnx", -3, WRITE, 1, -1, 2),
+    keyed("mget", -2, READ, 1, -1, 1),
+    keyed("getset", 3, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("append", 3, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("strlen", 2, READ, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("incr", 2, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("decr", 2, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("incrby", 3, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("decrby", 3, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("incrbyfloat", 3, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    // Keys.
+    keyed("del", -2, WRITE, 1, -1, 1),
+    keyed("unlink", -2, &["write", "fast"], 1, -1, 1),
+    keyed("exists", -2, READ, 1, -1, 1),
+    keyed("touch", -2, READ, 1, -1, 1),
+    keyed("type", 2, READ, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("rename", 3, WRITE, 1, 2, 1),
+    keyed("renamenx", 3, WRITE, 1, 2, 1),
+    // Expiry.
+    keyed("expire", -3, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("pexpire", -3, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("expireat", -3, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("pexpireat", -3, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("persist", 2, WRITE, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("ttl", 2, READ, 1, 1, 1),
+    keyed("pttl", 2, READ, 1, 1, 1),
+    // The keyspace. These walk every owner rather than naming keys.
+    keyspace("keys", 2, &["readonly"]),
+    keyspace("scan", -2, &["readonly"]),
+    keyspace("dbsize", 1, &["readonly", "fast"]),
+    keyspace("randomkey", 1, &["readonly"]),
+    // Declined. Listed so that a client asking what the server knows is told
+    // the command exists and was refused, rather than that the server does not
+    // exist. See docs/redis-compatibility.md for why each one is absent.
+    declined("flushdb", -1, WRITE),
+    declined("flushall", -1, WRITE),
+];
+
+pub fn lookup(name: &str) -> Option<&'static CommandInfo> {
+    COMMANDS
+        .iter()
+        .find(|command| command.name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
+}
+
+impl CommandInfo {
+    /// `given` counts the command name, as Redis's arity does.
+    pub fn accepts(&self, given: usize) -> bool {
+        let given = given as i64;
+        if self.arity < 0 {
+            given >= -self.arity
+        } else {
+            given == self.arity
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// May run before the connection authenticates.
+    pub fn pre_auth(&self) -> bool {
+        self.flags.contains(&"no_auth")
+    }
+
+    /// Changes data, so a command that passes its deadline may have done so.
+    pub fn writes(&self) -> bool {
+        self.flags.contains(&"write")
+    }
+
+    /// Names keys, at the positions `first_key`, `last_key` and `step` give.
+    pub fn has_keys(&self) -> bool {
+        self.first_key != 0
+    }
+
+    /// Reaches the cluster, rather than answering from the gateway.
+    pub fn reaches_cluster(&self) -> bool {
+        self.has_keys() || self.keyspace
+    }
+
+    /// Key arguments, using Redis's inclusive positive final-key position.
+    pub fn keys<'a>(&self, args: &'a [Vec<u8>]) -> Vec<&'a [u8]> {
+        if !self.has_keys() {
+            return Vec::new();
+        }
+        let first = usize::try_from(self.first_key).unwrap_or(0);
+        let end = if self.last_key < 0 {
+            args.len()
+                .saturating_sub(self.last_key.unsigned_abs() as usize - 1)
+        } else {
+            usize::try_from(self.last_key)
+                .unwrap_or(0)
+                .saturating_add(1)
+                .min(args.len())
+        };
+        let step = usize::try_from(self.step).unwrap_or(1).max(1);
+        (first..end)
+            .step_by(step)
+            .map(|at| args[at].as_slice())
+            .collect()
+    }
+
+    pub fn to_reply(&self) -> Reply {
+        Reply::Array(vec![
+            Reply::bulk(self.name),
+            Reply::Integer(self.arity),
+            Reply::Array(self.flags.iter().map(|flag| Reply::bulk(*flag)).collect()),
+            Reply::Integer(self.first_key),
+            Reply::Integer(self.last_key),
+            Reply::Integer(self.step),
+        ])
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+
+    #[test]
+    fn key_arguments_include_the_positive_final_position() {
+        let args = ["RENAME", "source", "destination"].map(|value| value.as_bytes().to_vec());
+        assert_eq!(
+            lookup("rename").unwrap().keys(&args),
+            vec![b"source".as_slice(), b"destination".as_slice()]
+        );
+        let args = ["MSET", "one", "value", "two", "value"].map(|value| value.as_bytes().to_vec());
+        assert_eq!(
+            lookup("mset").unwrap().keys(&args),
+            vec![b"one".as_slice(), b"two".as_slice()]
+        );
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn only_the_handshake_runs_before_authentication() {
+        let pre_auth: Vec<_> = COMMANDS
+            .iter()
+            .filter(|command| command.pre_auth())
+            .map(|command| command.name)
+            .collect();
+        assert_eq!(pre_auth, ["hello", "auth", "reset", "quit"]);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn arity_counts_the_name_and_a_negative_one_is_a_minimum() {
+        let get = lookup("get").unwrap();
+        assert!(get.accepts(2) && !get.accepts(1) && !get.accepts(3));
+        let set = lookup("set").unwrap();
+        assert!(set.accepts(3) && set.accepts(9) && !set.accepts(2));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn multi_key_commands_report_their_key_positions() {
+        let mget = lookup("mget").unwrap();
+        assert_eq!((mget.first_key, mget.last_key, mget.step), (1, -1, 1));
+        let mset = lookup("mset").unwrap();
+        assert_eq!((mset.first_key, mset.last_key, mset.step), (1, -1, 2));
+        let rename = lookup("rename").unwrap();
+        assert_eq!((rename.first_key, rename.last_key), (1, 2));
+        assert_eq!(lookup("get").unwrap().first_key, 1);
+        assert_eq!(lookup("ping").unwrap().first_key, 0);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn keyspace_commands_reach_the_cluster_without_naming_keys() {
+        for name in ["keys", "scan", "dbsize", "randomkey"] {
+            let command = lookup(name).unwrap();
+            assert!(!command.has_keys() && command.reaches_cluster(), "{name}");
+        }
+        assert!(!lookup("ping").unwrap().reaches_cluster());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_command_reply_matches_the_redis_shape() {
+        let Reply::Array(items) = lookup("get").unwrap().to_reply() else {
+            panic!("expected an array");
+        };
+        assert_eq!(items.len(), 6);
+        assert!(matches!(&items[0], Reply::Bulk(Some(name)) if name == b"get"));
+    }
+}

A read the shortened history can no longer explain is reported as inconclusive rather than as an impossible value, and it fails the round in either scenario, because an unverified read is not a pass; the failure, also written to `observations.fault_failures`, names the truncated window, the states the round's keys have dropped over the whole run, and a sample of the reads. Three seed-1 runs passed with 3/3/4 rolled-back keys, no dropped acknowledged state, and zero impossible and zero inconclusive reads; `--seed 7 --fault-rounds 2` killed two different owners and rolled back 3 and 2 keys, with no impossible read and no state dropped. Each round reports only the states it dropped and `observations.fault_dropped_acknowledged_states` adds them up. +## English
+
+Use the current defaults for the main profile: RF=3, `OwnerOnly`, `minimum_admitted_copies=1`, and `minimum_healthy_followers=0`. Each range desires two asynchronous followers, but an `OwnerOnly` write waits for neither follower's ACK. Keep the default 30-second logical operation deadline; runs with a longer deadline are separate diagnostics.
+
+Shared baselines so far (all recorded in Git-tracked documents; raw `results/` files are not tracked, so do not assume teammates have them):
+
+- One-million-key bulk-write ACK policy comparisons: three runs per policy on clean source `89d23fa` ([repeated measurement notes](optimizations/replica-ack-performance.md#repeated-measurements-on-committed-source)), and a clean-build repeat on `8b58d79` after the routing and receipt-cleanup optimizations ([clean-build comparison](optimizations/write-path-cleanup-and-routing.md#clean-build-throughput-across-all-acknowledgement-policies)).
+- Twenty 20k-key `FirstSuccessor` migration runs, all passing ([reliability notes](optimizations/replica-ack-performance.md#firstsuccessor-20k-scale-out-reliability)).
+- Open-loop latency, overload ladder, and load balance on source `52adf85`: [latency-acceptance.md](latency-acceptance.md).
+- The scaling-under-load matrix on clean source `b0ce975`: [scaling-under-load.md §0.1](scaling-under-load.md).
+- Course acceptance metrics (balance, migration rate, failover recovery, consecutive failures): [acceptance-metrics.md](acceptance-metrics.md).
+
+The work below targets load shapes, fault behavior, and correctness checks that are not yet covered, instead of repeating those baselines. Repeat performance comparisons at least three times under comparable machine conditions and retain every raw run, including partial evidence from failures.
+

[x] **Steady-state capacity, latency, and deadlines.** On 10 nodes with RF=3 and `OwnerOnly`, measure sustained PUT, GET, and mixed PUT/GET/DELETE traffic: throughput and p50/p95/p99 latency during load, retries by cause, deadline outcomes, per-node CPU/RSS, and follower lag; verify writes, reads, and deletes after each phase. Do not treat the few serial PUTs sampled after bulk loading as loaded tail latency.
+
+   **Status: complete.** The `latency` mode offers requests at fixed rates and records in-load percentiles, errors (including deadlines) and retries, dropped requests, per-node CPU and request distribution, then verifies every key. [latency-acceptance.md](latency-acceptance.md) records GET:PUT:DELETE = 90:9:1 with 128 B values, uniform and Zipf 0.99, four rates with three repetitions each, plus an overload ladder. A concurrency sweep (16–512) of the bulk-load phase is in [write-path-saturation.md](optimizations/write-path-saturation.md). The `OwnerOnly` write-rate variation has had one diagnostic round: removing redundant receipt scans and per-request topology copies raised throughput, but the [remaining work](optimizations/write-path-cleanup-and-routing.md#remaining-work) notes that policy ranges still overlap and the variation is not fully explained. Not covered: other read/write mixes, 4 KiB values, and in-load per-node RSS and follower-lag sampling (the experiment crate does not collect them).

+   **Status: complete.** `experiment --mode fault --fault-scenario follower` starts with four members plus one spare per round, selects keys whose owner stays alive and whose victim is a follower, and keeps the load running across the kill, publication, replacement, and RF repair. `requests.jsonl` records each request's result, version, epoch, and retry reasons; each `fault_rounds` entry records pre-failure replica progress, publication and first-read/write recovery, `live_rf`, under-replicated/not-writable ranges, capacity backpressure, and whether every selected key kept its owner. Every duration is counted from the kill. Three 1,000-key runs had zero application errors, zero rollbacks, and zero impossible reads; all 180 selected ranges kept their owner after publication, and the load completed about 64,000 reads and 18,000 writes after the kill. Capacity backpressure is split into the requests that ended with a capacity error and the retries the client made because of capacity (about 510 `resource_exhausted` retries per run, no capacity errors). Measure affected-range unavailability, topology publication, read/write recovery, new-owner distribution, and RF repair. Count acknowledged changes rolled back under `OwnerOnly` separately when the recorded history and replica progress can explain them, including an older value reappearing or an acknowledged delete being lost. Do not treat “recent” as a fixed time window or classify every old value as a permitted rollback. Report outcomes with insufficient evidence as inconclusive, not as passes. Values impossible under the recorded history, new writes accepted by the old owner after fencing or lease expiry, and failure to recover remain failures.

+   **Status: complete.** `experiment --mode fault --fault-scenario owner` keeps `GET:PUT:DELETE=70:20:10` traffic running before, during, and after failure. `requests.jsonl` records each request's arguments, times, result, version, and epoch, while `fault_rounds` holds the pre-failure follower progress of the selected ranges, kill-to-publication, first read/write/delete recovery, `live_rf`, new-owner distribution, and time to full RF; every duration is counted from the kill. A per-key single-register model records exact versions for definite mutations, keeps both branches for `MayHaveApplied`, classifies a read of an acknowledged older state as `older_value_reappeared`, `acknowledged_delete_lost`, or `acknowledged_value_lost`, and fails on a value the history cannot explain. The acknowledged history is kept as digests and bounded per key by `--fault-acknowledged-window` (4096 states by default, and a state that is acknowledged again moves to the back of the window); the window has to cover the writes one key takes during the load, or a rollback outside it becomes inconclusive and fails the round. A read the shortened history can no longer explain is reported as inconclusive rather than as an impossible value, and it fails the round in either scenario, because an unverified read is not a pass; the failure, also written to `observations.fault_failures`, names the truncated window, the states the round's keys have dropped over the whole run, and a sample of the reads. Three seed-1 runs passed with 3/3/4 rolled-back keys, no dropped acknowledged state, and zero impossible and zero inconclusive reads; `--seed 7 --fault-rounds 2` killed two different owners and rolled back 3 and 2 keys, with no impossible read and no state dropped. Each round reports only the states it dropped and `observations.fault_dropped_acknowledged_states` adds them up. See [fault-under-load.md](fault-under-load.md#owner-丢失3-次同一配置) and [the multi-round run](fault-under-load.md#多次-owner-故障与不同-seed).

-### 阶段 3：V=200 的 5% 目标
-
-V=200 的三种口径（CV 6.2%、max/mean−1 7.8%、极差 19.3%）都高于 5%。这不是采样噪声：100k 键对 10 个节点的计数误差只有约 0.3%，差异来自 token 位置；三个 seed 的 CV 是 6.2/6.6/8.1%。
-

-### 阶段 4：单节点下线的 10% 线
-
-单节点下线时，迁移率就是被移除节点在环上的份额，理论上限 1/N。N=10 时正好压在 10% 线上：V=128、seed 1 实测 10.51%（高 0.5 个百分点），而同一个环从 11 节点移除一个节点是 6.45%。这条验收在 N=10 时本质上是“均值等于门槛”的抽样问题，单次运行可能落在两侧。
-
-要让 N=10 也稳定低于 10%，需要降低单个节点份额的波动（更高 V，或上述放置策略）；否则目标应写成 1/N，而不是固定 10%。

-### 阶段 4：连续 3 节点故障
-
-`availability` 模式的 `--availability-rounds 3` 顺序注入 3 次 owner 故障。每轮：取当前 probe key 的 owner，抽样它拥有的至多 128 个键 → 向最后一个**不等于上一轮 tail 的**抽样键写入 1 MiB 新值（节点值上限小于 1 MiB 时用上限本身，且不小于 `--value-bytes`）并杀掉该 owner → 等自动故障转移发布、读探针恢复 → 在抽样键空间之外写一个键并读回（证明集群恢复可写）→ 读回抽样键和上一轮的尾部写入 → 加入一个替换节点（走扩容的播种路径）→ 等 RF 恢复 → 统计存活节点、以及“从未故障的节点”各持有的键数。第 2 轮起选中的键可能不是“最后一个”，因为上一轮的 tail 键要留给上一轮 tail 存活检查；上一轮 tail 被复用（只剩一个可选键）时，该轮的 `previous_tail_survived` 记为 `null`。
-
-6 个初始节点 + 3 个替换节点（`--nodes 9`）、100k 键、RF=3、`FirstSuccessor`、seed 1、每组 3 次重复、每次独立输出目录。这次矩阵运行来自提交 `41db8a2`，每次运行的 manifest 记录 `source_reproducible=true`、提交与源码摘要。同一 seed 的环是确定的，3 次重复的受害节点、存活成员序列和均衡数字完全相同，重复给出的是时延波动。

+# 验收指标对照（挑战实验 17）
+
+把《分布式缓存动态扩容与高可用系统》阶段 2–6 的量化验收项对到本仓库可复现的实验。原始 `results/` 不纳入 Git，这里只记录数值、来源和局限；每节末尾给出复现命令。
+
+## 共同前提
+
+除非该节另有说明：干净源码（`c92e0e9` 到 `4d27ae9`，每次运行的 manifest 记录当时提交）、`--require-clean-source`、10 节点、RF=3、`OwnerOnly`、128 B 值、seed 1、24 逻辑 CPU 的共享桌面主机。每个运行有独立输出目录和 manifest，记录实际配置与源码摘要。
+
+## 阶段 2：没有虚拟节点时的倾斜
+
+`latency` 模式按节点统计真实拥有键数（`load_balance.per_node.owned_keys`，对 100k 键逐个哈希得出），V=1 即每个物理节点只有一个 token：
+
+| V | 最大 | 最小 | max/min |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | 47,982 | 249 | 192.7 |
+| 16 | 11,998 | 5,669 | 2.12 |
+
+阶段 2 要求「10 个物理节点时最大/最小负载比 > 3」，V=1 时 192.7，现象成立。同时可以看到 V=16 就已经把比值压到 2.12。
+
+V=1 时新增一个节点（3→4）的迁移率实测 **7.29%**（7,289/100,000，1 个 range），低于 20% 的门槛。但 V=1 时新节点只占一个弧段，份额完全由环决定，换一个 seed 可能远高于此；这正是阶段 3 引入虚拟节点的原因。
+
+## 阶段 3（及阶段 6-2）：虚拟节点均衡与迁移率
+
+### 均衡度
+
+10 节点、100k 键、uniform，`latency` 模式实测（max/min、(max−min)/mean、max/mean−1 与 CV 都由每节点拥有键数直接算出）：
+
+| V | seed | RF | max/min | (max−min)/mean | max/mean−1 | owned keys CV |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | 1 | 3 | 192.70 | 477.3% | 379.8% | 1.412 |
+| 16 | 1 | 3 | 2.116 | 63.3% | 20.0% | 0.178 |
+| 64 | 1 | 3 | 1.611 | 47.6% | 25.5% | 0.139 |
+| 128 | 1 | 3 | 1.276 | 24.1% | 11.6% | 0.088 |
+| 200 | 1 | 3 | 1.218 | 19.3% | 7.8% | 0.062 |
+| 200 | 2 | 3 | 1.272 | 24.4% | 14.0% | 0.066 |
+| 200 | 3 | 3 | 1.371 | 31.1% | 15.0% | 0.081 |
+| 256 | 1 | 3 | 1.157 | 14.8% | 8.7% | 0.048 |
+| 500 | 1 | 3 | 1.214 | 19.4% | 10.4% | 0.052 |
+| 1000 | 1 | 1 | 1.090 | 8.7% | 5.5% | 0.026 |
+| 1500 | 1 | 1 | 1.094 | 8.9% | 3.9% | 0.028 |
+
+**阶段 3 要求「V=200 时各物理节点数据量差异 ≤ 5%」，本实现在 V=200 未达到**：三种常见算法给出的差异分别是 CV 6.2%、max/mean−1 7.8%、(max−min)/mean 19.3%，三个 seed 下 CV 为 6.2/6.6/8.1%。原因是 token 位置由哈希随机决定，N 个节点的份额是随机变量，CV≈1/√V：V=200 时理论 CV 约 7%，实测 6.2%，与模型一致；要压到 5% 需要 V≈400（按 CV 口径）到 V≈3000（按极差口径）。
+
+### 上限提高与更大 V 的实测
+
+原来的 replica-task 上限是 16,384，10 节点 RF=3 时 V≤546（V=1000 直接报
+`topology exceeds the 16384 replica-task limit`）。提交 `a39975c` 把
+`MAX_REPLICA_OBLIGATIONS` 提到 131,072，覆盖 10 成员、RF=3、V=4096 的法定上限
+（81,920 条义务）。提高后 10 节点 RF=3 实测（100k 键、uniform；内存是协调器进程
+RSS 峰值，每秒采样）：
+
+| V | max/min | (max−min)/mean | max/mean−1 | CV | 协调器 RSS 峰值 | 预载后满 RF | 一次 10→11 变更 |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 128 | 1.276 | 24.1% | 11.6% | 0.088 | 0.13 GB | 1.6 s | 2.4 s |
+| 1000 | 1.090 | 8.7% | 5.5% | 0.026 | 1.4 GB | 19 s | 107 s 到发布 |
+| 2000 | 1.070 | 6.8% | 4.0% | 0.017 | 5.2 GB | 58 s | 复制 235 s，380 s 内未发布 |
+| 4096 | 1.039 | 3.8% | 2.1% | 0.011 | 16.9 GB | 175 s | 复制阶段 410 s 仍未完成 |
+
+- V=200 的数字不变：差异由 V 本身决定，提高上限不会改善 V=200。
+- 按 max/mean−1 口径，V=2000 达到 4.0%；按极差口径要到 V≈3000–4096。
+- 代价很实在：协调器内存随 token 数增长（V=1000 约 1.4 GB、V=2000 约 5.2 GB、
+  V=4096 约 17 GB），成员变更耗时随 range 数增长（V=1000 约 107 s 到发布；
+  V=2000 复制 235 s、380 s 内未发布；V=4096 复制阶段 410 s 仍未完成）。V=4096 只适合静态均衡实验，不适合频繁扩缩容；
+  默认配置仍是 128。
+- 因此要让「V=200、≤5%」成为常态，应当改放置策略（有界负载的一致性哈希），
+  而不是继续加大 V。
+
+### 迁移率
+
+迁移率 = 本次 change 前后 owner 变化的键数 / 总键数，由 experiment 直接比较 base 与 target 两份拓扑、逐键计算；`snapshot_records` 是协调器复制路径实际搬运的记录数。direct merge 不产生 range，所以 records 为 0，但键仍然换主。
+
+| 变更 | 键数 | owner 变化 | 迁移率 | range 数 | snapshot records |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 9→10 | 100,000 | 10,508 | 10.51% | 128 | 10,670 |
+| 9→10 | 1,000,000 | 105,296 | 10.53% | 128 | 105,460 |
+| 10→11 | 100,000 | 6,446 | 6.45% | 128 | 6,611 |
+| 10→11 | 1,000,000 | 64,761 | 6.48% | 128 | 64,926 |
+| 10→9（direct merge） | 100,000 | 10,508 | 10.51% | 0 | 0 |
+| 11→10（direct merge） | 100,000 | 6,446 | 6.45% | 0 | 0 |
+
+- 9→10 的 10.51% ≈ 1/(9+1)：新增一个节点拿走环上约 1/10 的键，接近理论下限；三次重复结果完全相同（同一 seed 的环是确定的）。
+- 10→11 的 6.45% 是新增节点在这个 seed 的环上实际占的份额（期望 1/11 = 9.09%；用 11 节点、V=128 的 `latency` 运行核对，node-11 拥有 6,446 个键，与迁移量一致）。环上各节点份额本身是随机变量，单次运行可能低于期望值；关键是换主键数与新节点份额相等，而不是把整个键空间重排。
+- 阶段 6-2 要求「N≥10 时迁移率 ≤ 10%」：10→11 为 6.45%/6.48%，满足；9→10 的 10.51% 对应 1/N（N=9）的理论下限 11.1%，也低于它。
+- 单节点下线的迁移率就是被移除节点的环份额：11→10 为 6.45%，10→9 为 10.51%（见“未达标项与未验证项”）。

+| 阶段 2 1000 键暴力对照 | 归属与暴力枚举一致 | 未做 | 无证据 | 按需求跳过；现有校验是端到端读回全部键 |
+| 阶段 6 读成功率下界 | ≥ 99.9% 的统计证据 | 11 次闭环运行 0 失败 | 不能给出失败率上界 | 统计功效 |
+
+### 阶段 3：V=200 的 5% 目标
+
+V=200 的三种口径（CV 6.2%、max/mean−1 7.8%、极差 19.3%）都高于 5%。这不是采样噪声：100k 键对 10 个节点的计数误差只有约 0.3%，差异来自 token 位置；三个 seed 的 CV 是 6.2/6.6/8.1%。
+
+加大 V 只能缓解、不能解决：V=2000 时 max/mean−1 到 4.0%（极差仍有 6.8%），V=4096 时极差 3.8%，但协调器 RSS 到 5.2/16.9 GB，且一次 10→11 变更在 380 s 内没有发布（数据见上一节）。**结论：V=200 这个点不可能靠调 V 达标**；要让 5% 成为常态，需要改放置策略，例如有界负载的一致性哈希（先限制单节点份额再选 owner），或按节点容量放置。
+
+### 阶段 4：单节点下线的 10% 线
+
+单节点下线时，迁移率就是被移除节点在环上的份额，理论上限 1/N。N=10 时正好压在 10% 线上：V=128、seed 1 实测 10.51%（高 0.5 个百分点），而同一个环从 11 节点移除一个节点是 6.45%。这条验收在 N=10 时本质上是“均值等于门槛”的抽样问题，单次运行可能落在两侧。
+
+要让 N=10 也稳定低于 10%，需要降低单个节点份额的波动（更高 V，或上述放置策略）；否则目标应写成 1/N，而不是固定 10%。
+
+### 阶段 4：连续 3 节点故障
+
+`availability` 模式的 `--availability-rounds 3` 顺序注入 3 次 owner 故障。每轮：取当前 probe key 的 owner，抽样它拥有的至多 128 个键 → 向最后一个**不等于上一轮 tail 的**抽样键写入 1 MiB 新值（节点值上限小于 1 MiB 时用上限本身，且不小于 `--value-bytes`）并杀掉该 owner → 等自动故障转移发布、读探针恢复 → 在抽样键空间之外写一个键并读回（证明集群恢复可写）→ 读回抽样键和上一轮的尾部写入 → 加入一个替换节点（走扩容的播种路径）→ 等 RF 恢复 → 统计存活节点、以及“从未故障的节点”各持有的键数。第 2 轮起选中的键可能不是“最后一个”，因为上一轮的 tail 键要留给上一轮 tail 存活检查；上一轮 tail 被复用（只剩一个可选键）时，该轮的 `previous_tail_survived` 记为 `null`。
+
+6 个初始节点 + 3 个替换节点（`--nodes 9`）、100k 键、RF=3、`FirstSuccessor`、seed 1、每组 3 次重复、每次独立输出目录。这次矩阵运行来自提交 `41db8a2`，每次运行的 manifest 记录 `source_reproducible=true`、提交与源码摘要。同一 seed 的环是确定的，3 次重复的受害节点、存活成员序列和均衡数字完全相同，重复给出的是时延波动。
+
+#### 可用性（V=1024）
+
+每格是 3 次重复的范围或共同值。第 1、2 轮杀的是初始节点，第 3 轮杀的是第 2 轮刚加入的替换节点 `node-8`。
+
+| 指标 | 第 1 轮 `node-1` | 第 2 轮 `node-3` | 第 3 轮 `node-8` |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 检测+发布（s） | 5.15–5.86 | 5.16–5.85 | 4.78–5.42 |
+| 首个成功读（s） | 5.20–5.92 | 5.22–5.85 | 4.78–5.42 |
+| 首个成功写（s） | 10.05–12.08 | 6.94–9.14 | 4.97–14.01 |
+| 实测不可用最长连续（ms） | 4,941–5,664 | 4,948–5,584 | 4,513–5,145 |
+| 替换后满 RF（s） | 93.6–117.2 | 87.3–99.0 | 89.5–108.6 |
+| 故障到满 RF（s） | 109.7–134.6 | 102.4–112.7 | 99.3–128.2 |
+| 已确认键（抽样 128） | 0 丢失，tail 存活 | 0 丢失，tail 与上一轮 tail 存活 | 0 丢失，tail 与上一轮 tail 存活 |
+| 存活节点 max/min | 1.031 | 1.056 | 1.066 |
+| 存活节点 (max−min)/mean | 3.1% | 5.4% | 6.3% |
+| 存活节点 max/mean−1 | 1.5% | 1.8% | 2.5% |
+| 存活节点 CV | 1.0% | 1.8% | 2.1% |
+
+- 每轮的读恢复都在 5 s 量级（4.78–5.92 s），由 5 s 租约决定，与单次故障一致；第 3 轮（最后一次故障）从杀进程到回到完整 RF 是 99.3–128.2 s，其中绝大部分是替换节点的播种与修复。
+- 「首个成功写」从写请求发起时计时（此时读已恢复）：`FirstSuccessor` 要等新的第一后继追平并被准入才放行，所以还要 4.97–14.01 s；集群在每轮故障后都能重新接受写入并读回。
+- 每轮抽样的 128 个已确认键都没有丢失，每轮的 1 MiB 尾部写在 3 次重复中都存活；第 2、3 轮还确认了上一轮写入的尾部值仍然可读。每轮都在满 RF 恢复后才进入下一轮，修复为下一次故障准备了可提升的副本；实测 3 轮没有丢失。
+- 替换节点按扩容路径播种：V=1024、6 个存活节点、100k 键时，从开始变更到满 RF 需要 87–117 s，比故障转移本身（约 5 s）高一个数量级。
+
+#### 剩余节点均衡
+
+存活节点 = 每轮结束时的全部成员（6 个）；从未故障节点 = 初始节点中没被杀过的那几个（第 1 轮后 5 个，第 2、3 轮后 4 个）。差异越小越好，`≤ 10%` 是验收线。
+
+| V | 存活节点 max/min | 存活节点 (max−min)/mean | 存活节点 max/mean−1 | 存活节点 CV | 从未故障节点 (max−min)/mean | 替换后满 RF（s） | 单次总时长（s） |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 128（默认） | 1.11–1.37 | 10.5–31.2% | 4.9–15.6% | 3.6–9.6% | 7.9–20.0% | 2.8–4.0 | ~45 |
+| 512 | 1.14–1.19 | 12.7–18.1% | 4.8–11.3% | 4.3–6.1% | 10.7–15.6% | 22.4–24.1 | ~111 |
+| 1024 | 1.031–1.066 | 3.1–6.3% | 1.5–2.5% | 1.0–2.1% | 3.1–5.2% | 87.3–117.2 | ~335–359 |
+
+- V=1024 时四种口径都低于 10%，阶段 4 的「剩余节点差异 ≤ 10%」达成；默认 V=128 不达成，原因与阶段 3 相同：token 位置随机，节点份额的 CV≈1/√V，6 个存活节点要压到 10% 以内需要 V 在千级。
+- 均衡数字不是 V 的单调函数：每个 V 杀掉的是不同的节点（`128`：`node-1, node-2, node-5`；`512`：`node-1, node-7, node-3`；`1024`：`node-1, node-3, node-8`），环不同。V=512 这一组恰好抽到较差的成员序列，不能据此说 V=512 比 V=128 更差；看的是期望，而验收看单次运行的具体环。
+- 提高 V 的代价很直接：替换节点的播种从 2.8–4.0 s 涨到 87–117 s，因为要复制的 range 数与 token 数成正比；协调器内存也随 token 数增长（阶段 3 测得 10 节点、V=1000 约 1.4 GB）。
+
+### 阶段 5：pull vs push
+
+客户端只有 5 s 定时拉取（满足“10 秒内感知”），协调者没有推送通道，所以无法做对比实验，也没有“元数据更新期间错误率”的 A/B 数据；现有重试统计只能说明拉取模式下 `Moved`/`topology_refresh` 的次数。
+
+补齐需要：协调者在发布拓扑时通过长连接或广播通知客户端，然后对比两种方式的感知时延、更新次数、元数据流量与错误率。
+
+## 复现
+
+```sh
+# 均衡度：V 依次取 1 16 64 128 200 256，10 节点、100k 键、uniform
+target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode latency --output results/balance-v200 \
+  --nodes 10 --keys 100000 --virtual-nodes 200 --target-rates 20000 \
+  --warmup-seconds 3 --duration-seconds 10 --key-distribution uniform \
+  --max-in-flight 1024 --require-clean-source
+
+# 迁移率：矩阵入口带迁移量字段（每 transition 的 observations.<label>_transition.migration）
+KEYS=100000 REPS=1 ./scripts/scaling-matrix.sh
+
+# 10→11 的迁移率（新增节点在 N=10 下的份额）
+target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode scaling --scaling-scenario grow --nodes 11 \
+  --keys 100000 --scaling-pool-seconds 120 --warmup-seconds 10 --scaling-post-seconds 10 \
+  --output results/grow-10-to-11 --require-clean-source
+
+# 故障恢复
+target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode availability --keys 1000 \
+  --output results/availability --require-clean-source
+
+# 连续 3 节点故障：每次顺序杀掉当前 probe key 的 owner，替换并等满 RF 后再杀下一个
+target/release/hashring-rs experiment --mode availability --availability-rounds 3 \
+  --nodes 9 --keys 100000 --virtual-nodes 1024 --output results/availability-consecutive \
+  --require-clean-source
+
+# 连续 3 节点故障的矩阵：V 取 128、512、1024，每组 3 次
+./scripts/availability-matrix.sh
+```
+
+## 局限与未覆盖
+
+- 均衡度只测了 seed 1（阶段 3 另补了 V=200 的 seed 2、3），单机共享 CPU，键空间 100k。V=200 的差距是统计性质，不是某一次运行的偶发。连续 3 节点故障同样只测 seed 1，同一 seed 的环是确定的，三次重复的均衡数字完全相同，重复只给出时延波动。
+- 阶段 1（取模迁移曲线）不在本仓库范围；阶段 2 的 1000 键暴力枚举对照按需求跳过；pull/push 对比见“未达标项与未验证项”。
+- 每个配置的失败样本数为 0 不能给出失败率上界；可用性数字只作为观察值。
+- 连续 3 节点故障的每轮故障都发生在空闲集群：读探针和一次探针写是唯一的负载，结果不能外推到有持续写入时的恢复时间。

-# Configuration
-
-Every flag of the long-running commands, the YAML key that mirrors it, its
-default, and its scope. `--help` lists the same flags; this page adds the scope
-and the rules that keep a setting safe. Values that are fixed in the code are
-listed under [timers and budgets](operations.md#timers-and-budgets).
-
-## How settings resolve
-
-`coordinator`, `node`, `redis-gateway` and `experiment` take `--config <file>`, a
-YAML file whose keys are the flag names with `_` for `-`. For each setting, a flag
-on the command line wins over the file, and the file wins over the default.
-Unknown keys are an error. A relative path in a file is resolved against the
-file's directory. Boolean experiment flags can turn a setting on but not off.
-
-The examples list every key: [`coordinator.yaml`](../examples/coordinator.yaml),
-[`node.yaml`](../examples/node.yaml),
-[`redis-gateway.yaml`](../examples/redis-gateway.yaml) and
-[`experiment.yaml`](../examples/experiment.yaml).
-
-## Scopes
-
-| Scope | Meaning |
-| --- | --- |
-| process | Affects only the process that reads it. Change it on any restart. |
-| per node | A node's own budget or timeout. Nodes in one cluster may differ. |
-| bootstrap | Read only when the coordinator creates a new state store, then stored in the topology. For an existing store they are ignored, except that with `--member` flags every bootstrap setting must match the store. |
-| bootstrap, fixed | Bootstrap settings with no later change command. Every topology copies them, which is what makes them safe to depend on. |
-| experiment | Shapes an experiment run; recorded in its manifest. |

+# Configuration
+
+Every flag of the long-running commands, the YAML key that mirrors it, its
+default, and its scope. `--help` lists the same flags; this page adds the scope
+and the rules that keep a setting safe. Values that are fixed in the code are
+listed under [timers and budgets](operations.md#timers-and-budgets).
+
+## How settings resolve
+
+`coordinator`, `node`, `redis-gateway` and `experiment` take `--config <file>`, a
+YAML file whose keys are the flag names with `_` for `-`. For each setting, a flag
+on the command line wins over the file, and the file wins over the default.
+Unknown keys are an error. A relative path in a file is resolved against the
+file's directory. Boolean experiment flags can turn a setting on but not off.
+
+The examples list every key: [`coordinator.yaml`](../examples/coordinator.yaml),
+[`node.yaml`](../examples/node.yaml),
+[`redis-gateway.yaml`](../examples/redis-gateway.yaml) and
+[`experiment.yaml`](../examples/experiment.yaml).
+
+## Scopes
+
+| Scope | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| process | Affects only the process that reads it. Change it on any restart. |
+| per node | A node's own budget or timeout. Nodes in one cluster may differ. |
+| bootstrap | Read only when the coordinator creates a new state store, then stored in the topology. For an existing store they are ignored, except that with `--member` flags every bootstrap setting must match the store. |
+| bootstrap, fixed | Bootstrap settings with no later change command. Every topology copies them, which is what makes them safe to depend on. |
+| experiment | Shapes an experiment run; recorded in its manifest. |
+

+
+| Flag | YAML key | Default | Scope | Notes |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `--config` | — | none | process | |
+| `--listen` | `listen` | `127.0.0.1:50050` | process | |

-The campaign was run from the commit it was built from, `52adf85`, with no

-`git diff`, and the same source tree digest at build time and at run time,

-git checkout 52adf85
-```

-reason that was the script's own: it wrote the `host.txt` into `<run>/`
-before the first run started, so `git status` of every run saw that one
-untracked file. The diff of every manifest is empty and nothing in the
-source tree differs from the commit. The script writes the `host.txt` after
-the last run now, so a run of a clean tree reports
-`source_reproducible: true` — which needs the tables of the run before it

+The `stages.tsv` columns are the run's own numbers, renamed to fit a table:
+`get_p50` is the p50 of the `GET` latency in microseconds, `err_deadline` is
+the number of requests that ran out of their deadline, `owned_mom` is the
+`owned_keys_max_over_mean` of the load balance, and so on. The `run` column
+names the directory under `results/`, and `kind` says what the run was for:
+`campaign` is the repeated run at the target rates, `ladder` is the run that
+went past the capacity, and `vnode` is the virtual node comparison.
+
+`host_preload_ops` is the rate of the run's own preload, the same 100,000
+key write in every run. It is the run's measure of how fast the machine was
+while it ran, and it is the column to look at first: the machine is shared,
+and its speed moves between campaigns. It moved by a factor of 1.8 between
+two of them, and by 6.8% within the one the report is written from.
+
+## How to reproduce
+
+```sh
+cargo build --release
+./scripts/latency-sweep.sh
+```
+
+The script measures the capacity with `performance` mode, takes the target
+rates from it, runs the campaign, the ladder and the virtual node comparison,
+and writes the tables back here. `scripts/latency-sweep.sh` documents every
+knob it takes.
+
+## The source of the run
+
+The campaign was run from the commit it was built from, `52adf85`, with no
+tracked file changed. Every run's `manifest.json` holds that commit, an empty
+`git diff`, and the same source tree digest at build time and at run time,
+so the source is a checkout away:
+
+```sh
+git checkout 52adf85
+```
+
+The manifests of this run do report `source_reproducible: false`, for one
+reason that was the script's own: it wrote the `host.txt` into `<run>/`
+before the first run started, so `git status` of every run saw that one
+untracked file. The diff of every manifest is empty and nothing in the
+source tree differs from the commit. The script writes the `host.txt` after
+the last run now, so a run of a clean tree reports
+`source_reproducible: true` — which needs the tables of the run before it
+committed, because they live in this tracked directory too.
+
+Formal runs should use `--require-clean-source`. The manifest records the
+commit, tracked diff, working-tree status and source digest; it does not
+archive untracked files. Commit the source before collecting acceptance data.
+
+The `host.txt` holds the hash of the binary. The build is deterministic at a
+fixed path, but the absolute build root is compiled into the binary, so the
+hash comes back only from a build at the same path with the same target
+directory layout; the source tree digest comes back from any path.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Turn the output of `scripts/latency-sweep.sh` into tables.
+
+The experiment writes a `summary.json` per run, with one measurement per
+target rate. This reads those and prints one row per stage, and the medians
+over the repetitions of a stage.
+
+Usage:
+    extract.py <results-dir>              one row per stage
+    extract.py --medians <results-dir>    one row per stage, medians
+    extract.py --capacity <results-dir>   the capacity run
+"""
+
+import json
+import os
+import statistics
+import sys
+
+ERROR_REASONS = ["deadline", "operation", "rpc", "topology", "not_found", "protocol"]
+OPERATIONS = ["get", "put", "delete"]
+
+# The columns of the table the acceptance report holds.
+MEDIAN_COLUMNS = [
+    "kind",
+    "distribution",
+    "virtual_nodes",
+    "target_rate",
+    "reps",
+    "achieved_rate",
+    "get_p50",
+    "get_p95",
+    "get_p99",
+    "get_p999",
+    "get_max",
+    "late",
+    "retries",
+    "saturated_runs",
+    "host_preload_ops",
+    "owned_mom",
+    "owned_cv",
+    "ops_mom",
+    "ops_cv",
+    "cpu_max_percent",
+]
+
+
+def load_runs(results_dir, mode="latency"):
+    """Every latency run in the results directory, with its summary."""
+    runs = []
+    for name in sorted(os.listdir(results_dir)):
+        directory = os.path.join(results_dir, name)
+        summary_path = os.path.join(directory, "summary.json")
+        manifest_path = os.path.join(directory, "manifest.json")
+        if not os.path.isfile(summary_path) or not os.path.isfile(manifest_path):
+            continue
+        with open(summary_path) as handle:
+            summary = json.load(handle)
+        with open(manifest_path) as handle:
+            manifest = json.load(handle)
+        config = manifest.get("config") or {}
+        if config.get("mode") != mode:
+            continue
+        summary["config"] = config
+        runs.append((name, summary))
+    return runs
+
+
+def run_kind(name):
+    """What a run is for. The names come from `scripts/latency-sweep.sh`."""
+    if name.startswith("vnodes-"):
+        return "vnode"
+    if name == "ladder":
+        return "ladder"
+    return "campaign"
+
+
+def stage_row(run, summary, stage, measurement):
+    """One stage of one run, as a flat row."""
+    latency = measurement.get("latency_us") or {}
+    balance = measurement.get("load_balance") or {}
+    per_node = balance.get("per_node") or {}
+    cpus = [node.get("cpu_percent") for node in per_node.values()]
+    cpu_complete = bool(cpus) and all(value is not None for value in cpus)
+    row = {
+        "run": run,
+        "kind": run_kind(run),
+        "distribution": (summary.get("config") or {}).get("key_distribution"),
+        "virtual_nodes": (summary.get("config") or {}).get("virtual_nodes"),
+        "stage": stage,
+        "target_rate": measurement.get("target_rate"),
+        "achieved_rate": round(measurement.get("achieved_rate") or 0.0, 1),
+        "seconds": round(measurement.get("seconds") or 0.0, 1),
+        "sender_saturated": measurement.get("sender_saturated"),
+        "issued": measurement.get("issued"),
+        "late": measurement.get("late"),
+        "retries": measurement.get("retries"),
+        "owned_mom": round(balance.get("owned_keys_max_over_mean") or 0.0, 3),
+        "owned_cv": round(balance.get("owned_keys_cv") or 0.0, 4),
+        "ops_mom": round(balance.get("ops_handled_max_over_mean") or 0.0, 3),
+        "ops_cv": round(balance.get("ops_handled_cv") or 0.0, 4),
+        "cpu_max_percent": round(max(cpus), 1) if cpu_complete else None,
+        "cpu_sum_percent": round(sum(cpus), 1) if cpu_complete else None,
+        "nodes": len(per_node),
+        "verified_keys": (summary.get("observations") or {}).get("latency_verified_keys"),
+        # The preload of the run is the same workload every time, so it is the
+        # run's own measure of how fast the host was.
+        "host_preload_ops": (summary.get("observations") or {}).get("initial_put", {}).get("operations_per_second"),
+    }
+    ops = measurement.get("ops") or {}
+    for operation in OPERATIONS:
+        row[f"ops_{operation}"] = ops.get(operation)
+    errors = measurement.get("errors") or {}
+    for reason in ERROR_REASONS:
+        row[f"err_{reason}"] = errors.get(reason, 0)
+    for operation in OPERATIONS:
+        summary_us = latency.get(operation) or {}
+        for percentile in ("p50", "p95", "p99", "p999", "max"):
+            row[f"{operation}_{percentile}"] = summary_us.get(percentile)
+        row[f"{operation}_samples"] = summary_us.get("samples")
+    return row
+
+
+def rows_of(runs):
+    rows = []
+    for name, summary in runs:
+        for stage, measurement in (summary.get("measurements") or {}).items():
+            if "target_rate" not in measurement:
+                continue
+            rows.append(stage_row(name, summary, stage, measurement))
+    return rows
+
+
+def print_table(rows, columns=None):
+    if not rows:
+        return
+    columns = columns or list(rows[0].keys())
+    print("\t".join(columns))
+    for row in rows:
+        print("\t".join("" if row.get(column) is None else str(row.get(column)) for column in columns))
+
+
+def median_rows(rows):
+    """One row per stage, over the repetitions of it."""
+    groups = {}
+    for row in rows:
+        key = (row["kind"], row["distribution"], row["virtual_nodes"], row["target_rate"])
+        groups.setdefault(key, []).append(row)
+    out = []
+    for key, members in sorted(groups.items(), key=lambda item: (item[0][0], str(item[0][1]), item[0][3])):
+        first = members[0]
+        row = {
+            "kind": key[0],
+            "distribution": key[1],
+            "virtual_nodes": key[2],
+            "target_rate": key[3],
+            "reps": len(members),
+            "runs": ",".join(sorted(member["run"] for member in members)),
+            "saturated_runs": sum(1 for member in members if member.get("sender_saturated")),
+        }
+        for column in first:
+            if column in ("run", "kind", "distribution", "virtual_nodes", "stage", "target_rate"):
+                continue
+            values = [member[column] for member in members if isinstance(member.get(column), (int, float))]
+            if not values:
+                row[column] = None
+                continue
+            row[column] = round(statistics.median(values), 3)
+        # The spread of the two numbers a reader will argue about.
+        for column in ("achieved_rate", "get_p99", "get_p50", "get_max", "late", "retries"):
+            values = [member[column] for member in members if isinstance(member.get(column), (int, float))]
+            if values:
+                row[f"{column}_min"] = min(values)
+                row[f"{column}_max"] = max(values)
+        out.append(row)
+    return out
+
+
+def capacity_rows(results_dir):
+    rows = []
+    for name, summary in load_runs(results_dir, mode="performance"):
+        for stage, measurement in (summary.get("measurements") or {}).items():
+            rows.append({
+                "run": name,
+                "stage": stage,
+                "operations": measurement.get("operations"),
+                "seconds": round(measurement.get("seconds") or 0.0, 3),
+                "operations_per_second": round(measurement.get("operations_per_second") or 0.0, 1),
+            })
+    return rows
+
+
+def markdown_table(rows, columns):
+    """A table a document can hold."""
+    if not rows:
+        return ""
+    lines = ["| " + " | ".join(columns) + " |", "| " + " | ".join("---" for _ in columns) + " |"]
+    for row in rows:
+        lines.append("| " + " | ".join("" if row.get(column) is None else str(row.get(column)) for column in columns) + " |")
+    return "\n".join(lines)
+
+
+REPORT_COLUMNS = {
+    "campaign": [
+        ("Run", "run", "{}"), ("Distribution", "distribution", "{}"),
+        ("Rate", "target_rate", "{:,.0f}"), ("Host", "host_preload_ops", "{:,.0f}"),
+        *[(label, "get_" + label, "{:,.0f} us") for label in ("p50", "p95", "p99", "p999")],
+        ("max", "get_max", "{:,.0f} us"),
+    ],
+    "balance": [
+        ("Distribution", "distribution", "{}"), ("Rate", "target_rate", "{:,.0f}"),
+        ("Owned keys, max over mean", "owned_mom", "{:.3f}"),
+        ("Owned keys, cv", "owned_cv", "{:.3f}"),
+        ("Operations, max over mean", "ops_mom", "{:.3f}"),
+        ("Operations, cv", "ops_cv", "{:.3f}"),
+        ("Busiest node's CPU", "cpu_max_percent", "{:.1f}%"),
+    ],
+    "ladder": [
+        ("Target rate", "target_rate", "{:,.0f}"), ("Achieved", "achieved_rate", "{:,.0f}"),
+        *[(label, "get_" + label, "{:,.0f} us") for label in ("p50", "p95", "p99", "p999")],
+        ("Late", "late", "{:,.0f}"), ("Sender saturated", "sender_saturated", "{}"),
+    ],
+    "vnode": [
+        ("Virtual nodes", "virtual_nodes", "{}"),
+        ("Owned keys, max over mean", "owned_mom", "{:.3f}"),
+        ("Owned keys, cv", "owned_cv", "{:.3f}"),
+        ("Operations, max over mean", "ops_mom", "{:.3f}"),
+        ("Operations, cv", "ops_cv", "{:.3f}"),
+    ],
+}
+
+
+def report_table(rows, kind):
+    columns = REPORT_COLUMNS[kind]
+    def cell(row, key, template):
+        value = row.get(key)
+        if value is None:
+            return "unavailable"
+        if key == "sender_saturated":
+            value = "yes" if value else "no"
+        elif key == "host_preload_ops":
+            value = int(value)
+        return template.format(value)
+    formatted = [{label: cell(row, key, template) for label, key, template in columns} for row in rows]
+    return markdown_table(formatted, [label for label, _, _ in columns])
+
+
+def report(rows):
+    medians = median_rows(rows)
+    vnodes = {}
+    for row in medians:
+        if row["kind"] == "vnode":
+            vnodes.setdefault(row["virtual_nodes"], row)
+    return "\n\n".join([
+        report_table([row for row in rows if row["kind"] == "campaign"], "campaign"),
+        report_table([row for row in medians if row["kind"] == "campaign"], "balance"),
+        report_table([row for row in medians if row["kind"] == "ladder"], "ladder"),
+        report_table([row for _, row in sorted(vnodes.items())], "vnode"),
+    ])
+
+
+def main():
+    arguments = sys.argv[1:]
+    if not arguments:
+        print(__doc__, file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+    mode = "stages"
+    if arguments[0].startswith("--"):
+        mode = arguments[0][2:]
+        arguments = arguments[1:]
+    results_dir = arguments[0]
+    if mode == "capacity":
+        print_table(capacity_rows(results_dir))
+        return 0
+    rows = rows_of(load_runs(results_dir))
+    if mode == "medians":
+        print_table(median_rows(rows))
+    elif mode == "markdown":
+        print(markdown_table(median_rows(rows), MEDIAN_COLUMNS))
+    elif mode == "report":
+        print(report(rows))
+    else:
+        print_table(rows)
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

-# Experimental Redis Lua gateway
-
-**Purely experimental.** `hashring-redis-lua-experimental` adds embedded Lua 5.4
-scripting to `hashring-redis`. Compatibility and resource isolation are incomplete;
-this is not a production-ready Lua sandbox.
-
-## Run
-
-From the repository root, with a cluster running as described in the
-[quick start](../README.md#quick-start):
-
-```sh
-cargo run --features redis-lua-experimental -- redis-lua-experimental-gateway \
-  --config examples/experimental-redis-gateway.yaml
-```
-
-This adds the `redis-lua-experimental-gateway` command to the `hashring-rs` binary.
-`redis-gateway` continues to use the ordinary gateway without scripting, even when
-the feature is enabled. Default builds do not enable the Lua dependency. The
-experimental crate is a library, not a separate executable; it is not published.
-
-To build and run the binary directly instead:
-
-```sh
-cargo build --release --features redis-lua-experimental
-./target/release/hashring-rs redis-lua-experimental-gateway \
-  --config examples/experimental-redis-gateway.yaml
-```
-
-The coordinator is contacted when a command needs cluster data. The gateway can
-start before the cluster; data commands then report a connection error or deadline.
-
-## Try Lua
-
-Using `redis-cli` in another terminal, against the example's default port:
-
-```sh
-# No keys: returns integer 7.
-redis-cli -p 6379 EVAL 'return 1 + 2 * 3' 0
-
-# One key: increment it and give it a 60-second expiry in one script.
-redis-cli -p 6379 EVAL \
-  "local n = redis.call('INCR', KEYS[1]); redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], 60); return n" \
-  1 demo:counter
-redis-cli -p 6379 GET demo:counter
-redis-cli -p 6379 TTL demo:counter
-```
-
-After the script source, `EVAL` takes the number of keys, then those keys, then
-any arguments exposed as `ARGV`. Zero or one key is supported. A script may only
-access the key it declared in `KEYS`.
-
-`SCRIPT LOAD '<source>'` returns a SHA-1 hash; `EVALSHA <hash> <numkeys> [key] [args...]`
-runs a cached script. `SCRIPT EXISTS <hash>...` checks the cache and `SCRIPT FLUSH`
-clears it. The cache holds up to 512 scripts per gateway process and is lost on
-restart; an unknown hash produces `NOSCRIPT`, so clients must resend the source.
-
-## Settings
-
-The experimental command uses the same [settings as `redis-gateway`](configuration.md#redis-gateway), plus
-`--max-bulk-bytes` (`max_bulk_bytes` in YAML). Its default is 16 MiB and the cluster
-ceiling is 128 MiB. This limits each RESP bulk string, including a script's source
-or one command argument. Nodes default to an 8 MiB value admission limit; raise
-their `--max-value-bytes` separately when using larger values.
-
-Flags override YAML, which overrides defaults. Authentication uses `--requirepass`,
-`requirepass` in YAML, or `HASHRING_GATEWAY_PASSWORD`, just as the base gateway does.
-See the [experimental command reference](configuration.md#redis-lua-experimental-gateway)
-for the added setting and `--help` for all flags:
-
-```sh
-cargo run --features redis-lua-experimental -- redis-lua-experimental-gateway --help
-```
-
-For Rust callers, add a dependency on `hashring-redis-lua-experimental` and call
-its `serve(GatewayConfig, shutdown_receiver)` function. The Cargo feature above
-belongs to the root CLI package; depending directly on the library does not
-require that CLI feature.
-
-## Shared implementation
-
-The experiment depends on `hashring-redis`. It shares the RESP parser, encoder,
-connection loop, authentication, cluster client and ordinary command handlers.
-The base gateway's `CommandExtension` API registers additional command metadata
-and handlers. `COMMAND` includes registered commands. `serve_with_extension`
-installs the extension using the existing server.
-
-The generic `Overlay` interface lets an extension run ordinary handlers against
-private state through `Dispatcher::execute_with_store`. Neither base interface
-mentions Lua or depends on a Lua implementation.
-
-Only the Lua runtime, script cache, scripting policy and single-key execution state
-live in the experimental crate. `EVAL`, `EVALSHA` and `SCRIPT LOAD|EXISTS|FLUSH` are
-registered there. The remaining command behavior is described in
-[Redis compatibility](redis-compatibility.md).
-
-## Single-key execution
-
-An attempt reads its one declared key into a private snapshot. Commands read and
-change that snapshot, so later commands see the attempt's own writes. A completed
-attempt publishes its final state with one owner-side conditional write, against
-the original record version (or absence). A conflict discards the private state
-and reruns the whole script, including increments. Intermediate writes never
-reach other gateways or native clients.
-
-Scripts may declare at most one key and may access only that key. Keyspace walks,
-connection changes and recursive scripting are refused. These are experiment
-restrictions, not Redis Cluster's key rules. An error after successful commands
-still commits their staged changes, matching Redis's lack of error rollback;
-a commit with an unknown outcome is reported without replaying it.
-
-The existing instruction hook and command deadline remain. They do not constitute
-complete resource isolation, especially for script-created coroutines and library
-allocations. Redis Lua conversion and library compatibility also remain incomplete.
-
-## Development scope
-
-Review this purely experimental functionality for P0 robustness defects and
-P0/P1 correctness defects. Lower-priority robustness and correctness work is
-outside the current scope. This does not change the review scope of the base
-Redis gateway or shared cluster services.
-
-## Validation
-
-```sh
-cargo test -p hashring-redis
-cargo test -p hashring-redis-lua-experimental
-cargo test --features redis-lua-experimental --test redis_gateway --test experimental_redis_gateway
-```
-
-The existing RSSHub-style Lua cache-claim regression is preserved in
-[`tests/experimental_redis_gateway.rs`](../tests/experimental_redis_gateway.rs).
-It races eight callers across two gateways and requires exactly one successful
-claim, and also exercises a rate-limiter script. Run it specifically with:
-
-```sh
-cargo test --features redis-lua-experimental --test experimental_redis_gateway \
-  a_script_is_run_the_way_a_client_library_sends_it -- --exact
-```
-
-This test validates the Lua scripts through a real cluster and Redis client.
-Full RSSHub application integration requires a separate RSSHub deployment.

+`redis-gateway` continues to use the ordinary gateway without scripting, even when
+the feature is enabled. Default builds do not enable the Lua dependency. The
+experimental crate is a library, not a separate executable; it is not published.
+
+To build and run the binary directly instead:
+
+```sh
+cargo build --release --features redis-lua-experimental
+./target/release/hashring-rs redis-lua-experimental-gateway \
+  --config examples/experimental-redis-gateway.yaml
+```
+
+The coordinator is contacted when a command needs cluster data. The gateway can
+start before the cluster; data commands then report a connection error or deadline.
+
+## Try Lua
+
+Using `redis-cli` in another terminal, against the example's default port:
+
+```sh
+# No keys: returns integer 7.
+redis-cli -p 6379 EVAL 'return 1 + 2 * 3' 0
+
+# One key: increment it and give it a 60-second expiry in one script.
+redis-cli -p 6379 EVAL \
+  "local n = redis.call('INCR', KEYS[1]); redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], 60); return n" \
+  1 demo:counter
+redis-cli -p 6379 GET demo:counter
+redis-cli -p 6379 TTL demo:counter
+```
+
+After the script source, `EVAL` takes the number of keys, then those keys, then
+any arguments exposed as `ARGV`. Zero or one key is supported. A script may only
+access the key it declared in `KEYS`.
+
+`SCRIPT LOAD '<source>'` returns a SHA-1 hash; `EVALSHA <hash> <numkeys> [key] [args...]`
+runs a cached script. `SCRIPT EXISTS <hash>...` checks the cache and `SCRIPT FLUSH`
+clears it. The cache holds up to 512 scripts per gateway process and is lost on
+restart; an unknown hash produces `NOSCRIPT`, so clients must resend the source.
+
+## Settings
+
+The experimental command uses the same [settings as `redis-gateway`](configuration.md#redis-gateway), plus
+`--max-bulk-bytes` (`max_bulk_bytes` in YAML). Its default is 16 MiB and the cluster
+ceiling is 128 MiB. This limits each RESP bulk string, including a script's source
+or one command argument. Nodes default to an 8 MiB value admission limit; raise
+their `--max-value-bytes` separately when using larger values.
+
+Flags override YAML, which overrides defaults. Authentication uses `--requirepass`,
+`requirepass` in YAML, or `HASHRING_GATEWAY_PASSWORD`, just as the base gateway does.
+See the [experimental command reference](configuration.md#redis-lua-experimental-gateway)
+for the added setting and `--help` for all flags:
+
+```sh
+cargo run --features redis-lua-experimental -- redis-lua-experimental-gateway --help
+```
+
+For Rust callers, add a dependency on `hashring-redis-lua-experimental` and call
+its `serve(GatewayConfig, shutdown_receiver)` function. The Cargo feature above
+belongs to the root CLI package; depending directly on the library does not
+require that CLI feature.
+
+## Shared implementation
+
+The experiment depends on `hashring-redis`. It shares the RESP parser, encoder,
+connection loop, authentication, cluster client and ordinary command handlers.
+The base gateway's `CommandExtension` API registers additional command metadata
+and handlers. `COMMAND` includes registered commands. `serve_with_extension`
+installs the extension using the existing server.
+
+The generic `Overlay` interface lets an extension run ordinary handlers against
+private state through `Dispatcher::execute_with_store`. Neither base interface
+mentions Lua or depends on a Lua implementation.
+
+Only the Lua runtime, script cache, scripting policy and single-key execution state
+live in the experimental crate. `EVAL`, `EVALSHA` and `SCRIPT LOAD|EXISTS|FLUSH` are
+registered there. The remaining command behavior is described in
+[Redis compatibility](redis-compatibility.md).
+
+## Single-key execution
+
+An attempt reads its one declared key into a private snapshot. Commands read and
+change that snapshot, so later commands see the attempt's own writes. A completed
+attempt publishes its final state with one owner-side conditional write, against
+the original record version (or absence). A conflict discards the private state
+and reruns the whole script, including increments. Intermediate writes never
+reach other gateways or native clients.
+
+Scripts may declare at most one key and may access only that key. Keyspace walks,
+connection changes and recursive scripting are refused. These are experiment
+restrictions, not Redis Cluster's key rules. An error after successful commands
+still commits their staged changes, matching Redis's lack of error rollback;
+a commit with an unknown outcome is reported without replaying it.
+
+The existing instruction hook and command deadline remain. They do not constitute
+complete resource isolation, especially for script-created coroutines and library
+allocations. Redis Lua conversion and library compatibility also remain incomplete.
+
+## Development scope
+
+Review this purely experimental functionality for P0 robustness defects and
+P0/P1 correctness defects. Lower-priority robustness and correctness work is
+outside the current scope. This does not change the review scope of the base
+Redis gateway or shared cluster services.
+
+## Validation
+
+```sh
+cargo test -p hashring-redis
+cargo test -p hashring-redis-lua-experimental
+cargo test --features redis-lua-experimental --test redis_gateway --test experimental_redis_gateway
+```
+
+The existing RSSHub-style Lua cache-claim regression is preserved in
+[`tests/experimental_redis_gateway.rs`](../tests/experimental_redis_gateway.rs).
+It races eight callers across two gateways and requires exactly one successful
+claim, and also exercises a rate-limiter script. Run it specifically with:
+
+```sh
+cargo test --features redis-lua-experimental --test experimental_redis_gateway \
+  a_script_is_run_the_way_a_client_library_sends_it -- --exact
+```
+
+This test validates the Lua scripts through a real cluster and Redis client.
+Full RSSHub application integration requires a separate RSSHub deployment.

It then scales back to 9 while restoring or deleting the mutation cohorts, and verifies present and absent keys after every stage. | 20,000 | 10 (peak) |
-| `performance` | Nominal acceptance profile | 1,000,000 | 10 |

-Every mode defaults to 128-byte values, concurrency 64, seed 1, 128 virtual
-nodes, and a 30-second operation deadline. The default ACK policy is
-`FirstSuccessor` for availability mode and `OwnerOnly` for the others. Run
-`hashring-rs experiment --help` for every flag.
-
-`experiment --config <file>` reads the same settings from YAML; see

-turn a setting on. Unknown keys are an error, and a relative `output` in the

-configuration, so a run is reproducible without the file.
-

-## Output
-
-The output directory must be new or empty. The runner never overwrites a
-non-empty one. It writes:
-
-- `manifest.json`: the actual configuration, the build-time revision, toolchain,
-  and profile, the runtime source status and diff, and a BLAKE3 digest of the
-  executable
-- `events.jsonl`: the event log
-- stdout and stderr for each process
-- `coordinator.redb`: the coordinator database
-- `summary.json`: the results
-
-The manifest's `runtime_source` holds the source the run was built from: the
-commit, the status of the working tree, the diff of the files that were
-changed, and the files that were never added to the index. The last part is
-there because `git diff` does not hold them, and a run of a tree that was
-never committed is only reproducible if the tree itself is kept. For each of
-those files the manifest holds the path, the size, the digest, and the
-content of the file when it is text and small enough to keep. A file that
-could not be read is held with the error and without a digest, so a file that
-is not there is never recorded as an empty one.
-
-`results/` is ignored by Git, so raw databases and logs stay local.
-
-### Reproducibility
-
-Formal runs use `--require-clean-source`, which refuses to run unless the build
-and the runtime source match the same clean commit. Runs from a dirty tree are
-allowed but are marked `source_reproducible=false` in the manifest.
