-/// Built explicitly rather than via #[tokio::main] so each role can size its
-/// own runtime; see docs/optimizations/worker-pool-sizing.md. Servers default
-/// to one worker per available CPU because in a deployment they own their
-/// machine. `None` builds a single-threaded runtime.
-fn build_runtime(worker_threads: Option<usize>) -> Result<tokio::runtime::Runtime> {
-    let mut builder = match worker_threads {
-        Some(workers) => {
-            let mut builder = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread();
-            builder.worker_threads(workers);
-            builder
-        }
-        None => tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread(),
-    };
-    Ok(builder.enable_all().build()?)
-}

-fn init_tracing(verbose_experiment: bool) -> Result<()> {

-    if verbose_experiment {
-        filter = filter.add_directive("hashring_client=debug".parse()?);
-    }
-    tracing_subscriber::fmt().with_env_filter(filter).init();
-    Ok(())
-}

-/// Both gateway commands use the same server, lifecycle and configuration.
-async fn run_gateway(
-    config: hashring_redis::GatewayConfig,
-    extension: Option<Arc<dyn hashring_redis::commands::CommandExtension>>,
-) -> Result<()> {
-    let (shutdown, mut stopped) = tokio::sync::watch::channel(false);
-    tokio::spawn(async move {
-        shutdown_signal().await;
-        let _ = shutdown.send(true);
-    });
-    match extension {
-        Some(extension) => {
-            hashring_redis::serve_with_extension(config, stopped.clone(), extension).await?
-        }
-        None => hashring_redis::serve(config, stopped.clone()).await?,
-    }
-    stopped.changed().await.ok();
-    Ok(())
-}

-/// Runs an experiment, and stops it when the process is asked to stop.
-///
-/// The experiment starts a coordinator and a node per member as child
-/// processes. They are killed when the experiment's own value is dropped, and
-/// a signal ends the process without running any destructor, so a run that is
-/// interrupted would leave its nodes behind, holding their ports and their
-/// memory. The signal is awaited here instead, so the children are stopped
-/// with their parent.
-async fn run_experiment_command(config: ExperimentConfig) -> Result<()> {
-    tokio::select! {
-        result = run_local_experiment(config) => result,
-        _ = stop_signal() => {
-            // The experiment's own value is dropped here, which stops the
-            // nodes it started.
-            Err(anyhow::anyhow!("the experiment was interrupted"))
-        }
-    }
-}

-/// Waits for the process to be asked to stop.
-async fn stop_signal() {
-    #[cfg(unix)]
-    {
-        let mut terminate =
-            match tokio::signal::unix::signal(tokio::signal::unix::SignalKind::terminate()) {
-                Ok(signal) => Some(signal),
-                Err(error) => {
-                    tracing::error!(%error, "failed to install the terminate handler");
-                    None
-                }
-            };
-        tokio::select! {
-            _ = tokio::signal::ctrl_c() => {}
-            _ = async {
-                match terminate.as_mut() {
-                    Some(signal) => { signal.recv().await; }
-                    None => std::future::pending().await,
-                }
-            } => {}
-        }
-    }
-    #[cfg(not(unix))]
-    {
-        let _ = tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await;
-    }
-}

-async fn run_coordinator(
-    settings: CoordinatorSettings,
-    pre_publish_delay_ms: u64,
-    post_publish_delay_ms: u64,
-) -> Result<()> {
-    let repository = Arc::new(
-        RedbTopologyRepository::open(&settings.state)
-            .with_context(|| format!("opening {}", settings.state.display()))?,
-    );
-    let bootstrap = coordinator_bootstrap(&settings, repository.as_ref())?;
-    let state = load_or_initialize(repository.as_ref(), bootstrap)?;
-    info!(
-        listen = %settings.listen,
-        epoch = state.committed.epoch,
-        digest = %state.committed.digest,
-        members = state.committed.members.len(),
-        active_change = state.active_change.is_some(),
-        range_move_concurrency = settings.range_move_concurrency.get(),
-        replica_repair_concurrency = settings.replica_repair_concurrency.get(),
-        "coordinator ready"
-    );
-    let service = CoordinatorService::new(
-        state,
-        repository,
-        Duration::from_millis(settings.migration_timeout_ms),
-    )
-    .with_range_move_concurrency(settings.range_move_concurrency.get())
-    .with_replica_repair_concurrency(settings.replica_repair_concurrency.get())
-    .with_prepublication_failure_grace(Duration::from_millis(
-        settings.prepublication_failure_grace_ms,
-    ))
-    .with_pre_publish_delay(Duration::from_millis(pre_publish_delay_ms))
-    .with_post_publish_delay(Duration::from_millis(post_publish_delay_ms));
-    let recovery_service = service.clone();
-    tokio::spawn(async move {
-        let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(RECOVERY_INTERVAL);
-        loop {
-            // A registration can make a repair pass runnable that the last tick
-            // could not start, so wake on whichever arrives first. Without this
-            // a cluster booting with an empty ring converges only on a tick,
-            // which is a whole interval of doing nothing after the last node
-            // has already registered.
-            tokio::select! {
-                _ = interval.tick() => {}
-                _ = recovery_service.wait_for_repair_wake() => {}
-            }
-            match recovery_service.resume_interrupted_change().await {
-                Ok(Some(change)) => {
-                    tracing::info!(change_id = %change.change_id, phase = ?change.phase, "resumed topology change");
-                }
-                Ok(None) => {}
-                Err(error) => {
-                    tracing::warn!(%error, "topology change recovery remains pending");
-                }
-            }
-            if let Err(error) = recovery_service.resume_replica_repairs().await {
-                tracing::warn!(%error, "replica repair pass failed");
-            }
-        }
-    });
-    let failure_service = service.clone();
-    tokio::spawn(async move {
-        let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(1));
-        loop {
-            interval.tick().await;
-            if let Err(error) = failure_service.run_failure_pass().await {
-                tracing::warn!(%error, "automatic failure transition is pending");
-            }
-        }
-    });
-    Server::builder()
-        .add_service(
-            CoordinatorServer::new(service)
-                .max_decoding_message_size(MAX_CONTROL_MESSAGE_BYTES)
-                .max_encoding_message_size(MAX_CONTROL_MESSAGE_BYTES),
-        )
-        .serve_with_shutdown(settings.listen, shutdown_signal())
-        .await?;
-    Ok(())
-}

+fn main() -> Result<()> {
+    let cli = Cli::parse();
+    let cpus = std::thread::available_parallelism().map_or(1, NonZeroUsize::get);
+    // A long-running command's config file can set its runtime size, so its
+    // settings are resolved before the runtime is built.
+    match &cli.command {
+        Command::Experiment(args) => {
+            let file = args.config.as_deref().map(config::load).transpose()?;
+            let config = config::experiment::resolve(args, file, cpus)?;
+            init_tracing(config.verbose)?;
+            hashring_core::rpc_profile::start_reporter("driver");
+            return build_runtime(Some(config.worker_threads))?
+                .block_on(run_experiment_command(config));
+        }
+        Command::Node(args) => {
+            let file = args.config.as_deref().map(config::load).transpose()?;
+            let config = config::node::resolve(args, file)?;
+            init_tracing(false)?;
+            hashring_core::rpc_profile::start_reporter("node");
+            return build_runtime(Some(config.runtime_workers(cpus)))?
+                .block_on(run_node(config, args.stop_response_delay_ms));
+        }
+        Command::Coordinator(args) => {
+            let file = args.config.as_deref().map(config::load).transpose()?;
+            let settings = config::coordinator::resolve(args, file)?;
+            init_tracing(false)?;
+            return build_runtime(Some(settings.runtime_workers(cpus)))?.block_on(run_coordinator(
+                settings,
+                args.pre_publish_delay_ms,
+                args.post_publish_delay_ms,
+            ));
+        }
+        Command::RedisGateway(args) => {
+            let file = args.config.as_deref().map(config::load).transpose()?;
+            let settings = config::gateway::resolve(args, file)?;
+            init_tracing(false)?;
+            return build_runtime(Some(settings.runtime_workers(cpus)))?
+                .block_on(run_redis_gateway(settings));
+        }
+        #[cfg(feature = "redis-lua-experimental")]
+        Command::RedisLuaExperimentalGateway(args) => {
+            let file = args
+                .gateway
+                .config
+                .as_deref()
+                .map(config::load)
+                .transpose()?;
+            let settings = config::experimental_gateway::resolve(args, file)?;
+            init_tracing(false)?;
+            return build_runtime(Some(settings.gateway.runtime_workers(cpus)))?
+                .block_on(run_experimental_redis_gateway(settings));
+        }
+        _ => {}
+    }
+    init_tracing(false)?;
+    // One-shot client and admin commands issue a few RPCs and need no worker pool.
+    build_runtime(None)?.block_on(run(cli.command))
+}
+
+/// Built explicitly rather than via #[tokio::main] so each role can size its
+/// own runtime; see docs/optimizations/worker-pool-sizing.md. Servers default
+/// to one worker per available CPU because in a deployment they own their
+/// machine. `None` builds a single-threaded runtime.
+fn build_runtime(worker_threads: Option<usize>) -> Result<tokio::runtime::Runtime> {
+    let mut builder = match worker_threads {
+        Some(workers) => {
+            let mut builder = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread();
+            builder.worker_threads(workers);
+            builder
+        }
+        None => tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread(),
+    };
+    Ok(builder.enable_all().build()?)
+}

+async fn run_gateway(
+    config: hashring_redis::GatewayConfig,
+    extension: Option<Arc<dyn hashring_redis::commands::CommandExtension>>,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    let (shutdown, mut stopped) = tokio::sync::watch::channel(false);
+    tokio::spawn(async move {
+        shutdown_signal().await;
+        let _ = shutdown.send(true);
+    });
+    match extension {

+            hashring_redis::serve_with_extension(config, stopped.clone(), extension).await?
+        }
+        None => hashring_redis::serve(config, stopped.clone()).await?,
+    }
+    stopped.changed().await.ok();
+    Ok(())

+/// Runs an experiment, and stops it when the process is asked to stop.
+///
+/// The experiment starts a coordinator and a node per member as child
+/// processes. They are killed when the experiment's own value is dropped, and
+/// a signal ends the process without running any destructor, so a run that is
+/// interrupted would leave its nodes behind, holding their ports and their
+/// memory. The signal is awaited here instead, so the children are stopped
+/// with their parent.
+async fn run_experiment_command(config: ExperimentConfig) -> Result<()> {
+    tokio::select! {
+        result = run_local_experiment(config) => result,
+        _ = stop_signal() => {
+            // The experiment's own value is dropped here, which stops the
+            // nodes it started.
+            Err(anyhow::anyhow!("the experiment was interrupted"))
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// Waits for the process to be asked to stop.
+async fn stop_signal() {
+    #[cfg(unix)]
+    {
+        let mut terminate =
+            match tokio::signal::unix::signal(tokio::signal::unix::SignalKind::terminate()) {
+                Ok(signal) => Some(signal),
+                Err(error) => {
+                    tracing::error!(%error, "failed to install the terminate handler");
+                    None
+                }
+            };
+        tokio::select! {
+            _ = tokio::signal::ctrl_c() => {}
+            _ = async {
+                match terminate.as_mut() {
+                    Some(signal) => { signal.recv().await; }
+                    None => std::future::pending().await,
+                }
+            } => {}
+        }
+    }
+    #[cfg(not(unix))]
+    {
+        let _ = tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await;
+    }
+}

+async fn run_coordinator(
+    settings: CoordinatorSettings,
+    pre_publish_delay_ms: u64,
+    post_publish_delay_ms: u64,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    let repository = Arc::new(
+        RedbTopologyRepository::open(&settings.state)
+            .with_context(|| format!("opening {}", settings.state.display()))?,
+    );
+    let bootstrap = coordinator_bootstrap(&settings, repository.as_ref())?;
+    let state = load_or_initialize(repository.as_ref(), bootstrap)?;
+    info!(
+        listen = %settings.listen,
+        epoch = state.committed.epoch,
+        digest = %state.committed.digest,
+        members = state.committed.members.len(),
+        active_change = state.active_change.is_some(),
+        range_move_concurrency = settings.range_move_concurrency.get(),
+        replica_repair_concurrency = settings.replica_repair_concurrency.get(),
+        "coordinator ready"
+    );
+    let service = CoordinatorService::new(
+        state,
+        repository,
+        Duration::from_millis(settings.migration_timeout_ms),
+    )
+    .with_range_move_concurrency(settings.range_move_concurrency.get())
+    .with_replica_repair_concurrency(settings.replica_repair_concurrency.get())
+    .with_prepublication_failure_grace(Duration::from_millis(
+        settings.prepublication_failure_grace_ms,
+    ))
+    .with_pre_publish_delay(Duration::from_millis(pre_publish_delay_ms))
+    .with_post_publish_delay(Duration::from_millis(post_publish_delay_ms));
+    let recovery_service = service.clone();
+    tokio::spawn(async move {
+        let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(RECOVERY_INTERVAL);
+        loop {
+            // A registration can make a repair pass runnable that the last tick
+            // could not start, so wake on whichever arrives first. Without this
+            // a cluster booting with an empty ring converges only on a tick,
+            // which is a whole interval of doing nothing after the last node
+            // has already registered.
+            tokio::select! {
+                _ = interval.tick() => {}
+                _ = recovery_service.wait_for_repair_wake() => {}
+            }
+            match recovery_service.resume_interrupted_change().await {
+                Ok(Some(change)) => {
+                    tracing::info!(change_id = %change.change_id, phase = ?change.phase, "resumed topology change");
+                }
+                Ok(None) => {}
+                Err(error) => {
+                    tracing::warn!(%error, "topology change recovery remains pending");
+                }
+            }
+            if let Err(error) = recovery_service.resume_replica_repairs().await {
+                tracing::warn!(%error, "replica repair pass failed");
+            }
+        }
+    });
+    let failure_service = service.clone();
+    tokio::spawn(async move {
+        let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(1));
+        loop {
+            interval.tick().await;
+            if let Err(error) = failure_service.run_failure_pass().await {
+                tracing::warn!(%error, "automatic failure transition is pending");
+            }
+        }
+    });
+    Server::builder()
+        .add_service(
+            CoordinatorServer::new(service)
+                .max_decoding_message_size(MAX_CONTROL_MESSAGE_BYTES)
+                .max_encoding_message_size(MAX_CONTROL_MESSAGE_BYTES),
+        )
+        .serve_with_shutdown(settings.listen, shutdown_signal())
+        .await?;
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+/// Builds the epoch-1 topology for a new store. Members from a config file are
+/// skipped when the store already exists, so one file serves both the first
+/// start and every restart; `--member` flags still must match the store.
+fn coordinator_bootstrap(
+    settings: &CoordinatorSettings,
+    repository: &impl CoordinatorRepository,
+) -> Result<Option<TopologySnapshot>> {
+    if settings.members.is_empty() {
+        return Ok(None);
+    }
+    if let MemberSource::File(path) = &settings.member_source
+        && repository.load_state()?.is_some()
+    {
+        info!(
+            config = %path.display(),
+            "state store exists; ignoring bootstrap keys from the config file"
+        );
+        return Ok(None);
+    }
+    Ok(Some(TopologySnapshot::new_with_timings(
+        1,
+        settings.seed,
+        settings.virtual_nodes,
+        settings.members.clone(),
+        TopologyConfig {
+            desired_replication_factor: settings.desired_replication_factor,
+            write_availability_guard: WriteAvailabilityGuard {
+                minimum_admitted_copies: settings.minimum_admitted_copies,
+                minimum_healthy_followers: settings.minimum_healthy_followers,
+                max_replica_lag_millis: settings.max_replica_lag_ms,
+            },
+            ..TopologyConfig::default()
+        },
+        ClusterTimings {
+            receipt_retention_millis: settings.receipt_retention_ms,
+            lease_duration_millis: settings.lease_duration_ms,
+        },
+    )?))
+}

+async fn run_node(config: NodeConfig, stop_response_delay_ms: u64) -> Result<()> {
+    let service = DataNodeService::connect(config.id.clone(), config.coordinator, config.settings)
+        .await?
+        .with_stop_response_delay(Duration::from_millis(stop_response_delay_ms));
+    let mut remote_shutdown = service.shutdown_receiver();
+    info!(
+        node_id = %config.id,
+        process_instance_id = service.process_instance_id(),
+        listen = %config.listen,
+        "data node ready"
+    );
+    Server::builder()
+        .add_service(
+            DataNodeServer::new(service)
+                .max_decoding_message_size(MAX_DATA_MESSAGE_BYTES)
+                .max_encoding_message_size(MAX_DATA_MESSAGE_BYTES),
+        )
+        .serve_with_shutdown(config.listen, async move {
+            tokio::select! {
+                () = shutdown_signal() => {}
+                result = remote_shutdown.changed() => {
+                    if result.is_err() || *remote_shutdown.borrow() {
+                        tracing::info!("data node received remote shutdown");
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        })
+        .await?;
+    Ok(())
+}

+fn parse_member(value: &str) -> Result<Member> {
+    let (node_id, endpoint) = value
+        .split_once('=')
+        .with_context(|| format!("invalid member {value:?}; expected NODE_ID=HTTP_ENDPOINT"))?;
+    Ok(Member {
+        node_id: node_id.to_owned(),
+        endpoint: endpoint.to_owned(),
+    })

+fn bytes_arg(text: Option<String>, encoded: Option<String>, name: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
+    match (text, encoded) {
+        (Some(text), None) => Ok(text.into_bytes()),
+        (None, Some(encoded)) => {
+            hex::decode(encoded).with_context(|| format!("invalid {name} hex"))
+        }
+        _ => anyhow::bail!("exactly one {name} representation is required"),
+    }
+}

+            "--receipt-retention-ms",
+            "90000",
+            "--lease-duration-ms",
+            "3000",
+        ];
+        let first = settings(state.clone(), &[&member[..], &timings].concat(), None);
+        let bootstrap = coordinator_bootstrap(&first, &repository).unwrap();
+        let stored = load_or_initialize(&repository, bootstrap).unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(stored.committed.timings.receipt_retention_millis, 90_000);
+        assert_eq!(stored.committed.timings.lease_duration_millis, 3_000);

+        // Restarting with the default lease would shorten the startup quarantine.
+        let restart = settings(state, &member, None);
+        let bootstrap = coordinator_bootstrap(&restart, &repository).unwrap();
+        assert!(load_or_initialize(&repository, bootstrap).is_err());
+    }

+#![cfg(feature = "redis-lua-experimental")]
+//! Lua-specific behavior through the shared gateway server and real cluster.

+#[tokio::test]
+async fn lua_commands_use_shared_authentication_and_reject_undeclared_write_targets() {
+    let _guard = test_lock().lock().await;
+    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
+    let cluster = Cluster::start_with_gateway(
+        &directory.path().join("coordinator.redb"),
+        Some("secret"),
+        "redis-lua-experimental-gateway",
+    );
+    let mut unauthenticated = cluster.connect(&cluster.url(None)).await;
+    let error = redis::cmd("EVAL")
+        .arg("return 1")
+        .arg(0)
+        .query_async::<i64>(&mut unauthenticated)
+        .await
+        .unwrap_err();
+    assert!(
+        error.to_string().contains("Authentication required"),
+        "{error}"
+    );
+    let mut connection = cluster.client().await;
+    let info: Vec<redis::Value> = redis::cmd("COMMAND")
+        .arg("INFO")
+        .arg("EVAL")
+        .arg("SCRIPT")
+        .query_async(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(info.len(), 2);
+    assert!(
+        info.iter()
+            .all(|value| matches!(value, redis::Value::Array(_)))
+    );
+    let _: () = redis::cmd("SET")
+        .arg("declared")
+        .arg("original")
+        .query_async(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    for command in ["RENAME", "RENAMENX", "MSET"] {
+        let script = if command == "MSET" {
+            "return redis.call('MSET', KEYS[1], 'changed', 'undeclared', 'bad')".to_owned()
+        } else {
+            format!("return redis.call('{command}', KEYS[1], 'undeclared')")
+        };
+        let error = redis::cmd("EVAL")
+            .arg(script)
+            .arg(1)
+            .arg("declared")
+            .query_async::<redis::Value>(&mut connection)
+            .await
+            .unwrap_err();
+        assert!(error.to_string().contains("declare"), "{error}");
+        let values: (Option<String>, Option<String>) = redis::cmd("MGET")
+            .arg("declared")
+            .arg("undeclared")
+            .query_async(&mut connection)
+            .await
+            .unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(values, (Some("original".into()), None));
+    }
+    // MSETNX uses the same private store as other commands, and later calls
+    // see its staged state before anything is committed to the cluster.
+    let value: String = redis::cmd("EVAL")
+        .arg("redis.call('DEL', KEYS[1]); redis.call('MSETNX', KEYS[1], 'fresh'); return redis.call('GET', KEYS[1])")
+        .arg(1).arg("declared").query_async(&mut connection).await.unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(value, "fresh");
+    // A command error preserves earlier successful commands, in one commit.
+    let error = redis::cmd("EVAL")
+        .arg("redis.call('SET', KEYS[1], 'before-error'); return redis.call('INCR', KEYS[1])")
+        .arg(1)
+        .arg("declared")
+        .query_async::<redis::Value>(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap_err();
+    assert!(error.to_string().contains("not an integer"), "{error}");
+    let value: String = redis::cmd("GET")
+        .arg("declared")
+        .query_async(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(value, "before-error");
+}

+    assert_eq!(nothing, None);
+
+    // KEYS and ARGV carry the bytes the command named, in order, and a script
+    // sees its own writes the way Redis' single thread makes it see them.
+    let echoed: String = redis::cmd("EVAL")
+        .arg("redis.call('SET', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]) return redis.call('GET', KEYS[1])")
+        .arg(1)
+        .arg("echoed:key")
+        .arg("an argument")
+        .query_async(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(echoed, "an argument");
+
+    // The claim a cache client sends. The read and the write are one
+    // operation, so the second caller is told nobody claimed it.
+    const CLAIM: &str = "if redis.call('GET', KEYS[1]) == '1' then return 0 end \
+                         redis.call('SET', KEYS[1], '1', 'EX', ARGV[1]) return 1";
+    let first: i64 = redis::cmd("EVAL")
+        .arg(CLAIM)
+        .arg(1)
+        .arg("claimed:key")
+        .arg(60)
+        .query_async(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(first, 1);
+    let second: i64 = redis::cmd("EVAL")
+        .arg(CLAIM)
+        .arg(1)
+        .arg("claimed:key")
+        .arg(60)
+        .query_async(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(second, 0, "the claim was not exclusive to its caller");
+    let stored: String = redis::cmd("GET")
+        .arg("claimed:key")
+        .query_async(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(stored, "1");
+
+    // Two gateways racing for one key still give one claim. Neither holds a
+    // lock the other can see, so it is the cluster's conditional write, and
+    // the script being run again when it finds the key changed, that makes
+    // this one claim rather than two.
+    let (_second_process, second_url) = cluster.second_gateway();
+    let urls = [cluster.url(None), second_url];
+    let mut racers = Vec::new();
+    for _ in 0..4 {
+        for url in &urls {
+            let url = url.clone();
+            racers.push(tokio::spawn(async move {
+                let mut connection = redis::Client::open(url)
+                    .unwrap()
+                    .get_multiplexed_async_connection()
+                    .await
+                    .unwrap();
+                redis::cmd("EVAL")
+                    .arg(CLAIM)
+                    .arg(1)
+                    .arg("raced:key")
+                    .arg(60)
+                    .query_async::<i64>(&mut connection)
+                    .await
+                    .unwrap()
+            }));
+        }
+    }
+    let mut claimed = 0;
+    for racer in racers {
+        claimed += tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(30), racer)
+            .await
+            .expect("a claim stalled")
+            .unwrap();
+    }
+    assert_eq!(claimed, 1, "a claim was not exclusive");
+
+    // The rate limiter's script, which is the other reason clients send one:
+    // an increment and its deadline in one round trip.
+    const LIMITER: &str = "redis.call('set', KEYS[1], 0, 'EX', ARGV[2], 'NX') \
+                           local consumed = redis.call('incrby', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]) \
+                           local ttl = redis.call('pttl', KEYS[1]) \
+                           if ttl == -1 then \
+                             redis.call('expire', KEYS[1], ARGV[2]) \
+                             ttl = 1000 * ARGV[2] \
+                           end \
+                           return {consumed, ttl}";
+    let consumed: Vec<i64> = redis::cmd("EVAL")
+        .arg(LIMITER)
+        .arg(1)
+        .arg("limited:key")
+        .arg(1)
+        .arg(20)
+        .query_async(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(consumed.len(), 2, "{consumed:?}");
+    assert_eq!(consumed[0], 1, "{consumed:?}");
+    assert!(consumed[1] > 0, "{consumed:?}");
+
+    // SCRIPT LOAD answers the hash a client sends next, and EVALSHA runs it.
+    let hash: String = redis::cmd("SCRIPT")
+        .arg("LOAD")
+        .arg(CLAIM)
+        .query_async(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(
+        hash.len(),
+        40,
+        "a script's hash is forty hex characters: {hash}"
+    );
+    let loaded: i64 = redis::cmd("EVALSHA")
+        .arg(&hash)
+        .arg(1)
+        .arg("sha:key")
+        .arg(60)
+        .query_async(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(loaded, 1);
+    let known: Vec<i64> = redis::cmd("SCRIPT")
+        .arg("EXISTS")
+        .arg(&hash)
+        .arg("0".repeat(40))
+        .query_async(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(known, vec![1, 0]);
+
+    // NOSCRIPT is the code a client watches for to send the source instead,
+    // so it has to arrive as an error and not as a wrong answer.
+    let error = redis::cmd("EVALSHA")
+        .arg("0".repeat(40))
+        .arg(0)
+        .query_async::<i64>(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap_err();
+    assert!(
+        error.to_string().contains("No matching script"),
+        "unexpected error: {error}"
+    );
+    let _: String = redis::cmd("SCRIPT")
+        .arg("FLUSH")
+        .query_async(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    let error = redis::cmd("EVALSHA")
+        .arg(&hash)
+        .arg(0)
+        .query_async::<i64>(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap_err();
+    assert!(
+        error.to_string().contains("No matching script"),
+        "unexpected error: {error}"
+    );
+
+    // A script may only touch the keys it declared, which is the rule that
+    // lets the gateway hold locks for the whole run.
+    let error = redis::cmd("EVAL")
+        .arg("return redis.call('GET', 'not:declared')")
+        .arg(1)
+        .arg("declared:key")
+        .query_async::<i64>(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap_err();
+    assert!(
+        error.to_string().contains("declare"),
+        "unexpected error: {error}"
+    );
+    // An argument that is neither a string nor a number is refused before the
+    // command is built, as Redis refuses it.
+    let error = redis::cmd("EVAL")
+        .arg("return redis.call('GET', KEYS[2])")
+        .arg(1)
+        .arg("declared:key")
+        .query_async::<i64>(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap_err();
+    assert!(
+        error.to_string().contains("must be strings or integers"),
+        "unexpected error: {error}"
+    );
+
+    // A script that declares more than one key is refused: the gateway makes a
+    // script atomic over one key, and a script that touches several keys may
+    // reach nodes that own them separately, which no per-command precondition
+    // can stitch into one run. This experiment intentionally supports one key.
+    let error = redis::cmd("EVAL")
+        .arg("redis.call('SET', KEYS[1], 'a') redis.call('SET', KEYS[2], 'b') return 1")
+        .arg(2)
+        .arg("multi:one")
+        .arg("multi:two")
+        .query_async::<i64>(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap_err();
+    assert!(
+        error.to_string().contains("at most one key"),
+        "unexpected error: {error}"
+    );
+
+    // A script may not change the connection, as in Redis.
+    let error = redis::cmd("EVAL")
+        .arg("return redis.call('SELECT', 1)")
+        .arg(0)
+        .query_async::<i64>(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap_err();
+    assert!(
+        error.to_string().contains("not allowed from a script"),
+        "unexpected error: {error}"
+    );
+
+    // A runaway script is stopped by its step budget rather than held.
+    let error = redis::cmd("EVAL")
+        .arg("while true do end")
+        .arg(0)
+        .query_async::<i64>(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap_err();
+    assert!(
+        error.to_string().contains("maximum number of steps"),
+        "unexpected error: {error}"
+    );
+
+    // None of that left the gateway unable to answer anything else.
+    let pong: String = redis::cmd("PING")
+        .query_async(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(pong, "PONG");
+    let still: i64 = redis::cmd("EVAL")
+        .arg("return 40 + 2")
+        .arg(0)
+        .query_async(&mut connection)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(still, 42);
+}

+    Process(
+        Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_hashring-rs"))
+            .args(arguments)
+            .stdin(Stdio::null())
+            .stdout(Stdio::null())
+            .stderr(Stdio::null())
+            .spawn()
+            .unwrap(),
+    )
+}
+
+/// Runs a process that is expected to exit on its own, and returns whether it
+/// succeeded together with its stderr.
+///
+/// The process is killed when it is still running at the deadline, so a
+/// startup check that no longer fails is a test failure instead of a hang.
+fn run_to_exit(arguments: &[String], timeout: Duration) -> (bool, String) {
+    let mut child = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_hashring-rs"))
+        .args(arguments)
+        .stdin(Stdio::null())
+        .stdout(Stdio::null())
+        .stderr(Stdio::piped())
+        .spawn()
+        .unwrap();
+    let deadline = Instant::now() + timeout;
+    loop {
+        if child.try_wait().unwrap().is_some() {
+            break;
+        }
+        if Instant::now() >= deadline {
+            let _ = child.kill();
+            let _ = child.wait();
+            panic!("process did not exit within {timeout:?}");
+        }
+        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));
+    }
+    let output = child.wait_with_output().unwrap();
+    (
+        output.status.success(),
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).into_owned(),
+    )
+}
+
+fn wait_for_listener(port: u16) {
+    let address = format!("127.0.0.1:{port}").parse().unwrap();
+    for _ in 0..300 {
+        if std::net::TcpStream::connect_timeout(&address, Duration::from_millis(20)).is_ok() {
+            return;
+        }
+        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));
+    }
+    panic!("listener did not become ready on port {port}");
+}
+
+fn coordinator_arguments(
+    coordinator_port: u16,
+    state: &Path,
+    members: &[(String, u16)],
+) -> Vec<String> {
+    let mut arguments = vec![
+        "coordinator".into(),
+        "--listen".into(),
+        format!("127.0.0.1:{coordinator_port}"),
+        "--state".into(),
+        state.display().to_string(),
+        "--virtual-nodes".into(),
+        "32".into(),
+        "--minimum-admitted-copies".into(),
+        "1".into(),
+        "--minimum-healthy-followers".into(),
+        "0".into(),
+    ];
+    for (node_id, port) in members {
+        arguments.extend([
+            "--member".into(),
+            format!("{node_id}=http://127.0.0.1:{port}"),
+        ]);
+    }
+    arguments
+}
+
+async fn connect_eventually(endpoint: &str) -> HashringClient {
+    for _ in 0..50 {
+        if let Ok(client) = HashringClient::connect(endpoint, Duration::from_secs(2)).await {
+            return client;
+        }
+        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
+    }
+    panic!("coordinator did not become ready at {endpoint}");
+}
+
+async fn connect_without_polling(endpoint: &str, timeout: Duration) -> HashringClient {
+    let mut config = ClientConfig::new(timeout);
+    config.topology_poll_interval = None;
+    HashringClient::connect_with_config(endpoint, config)
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+}
+
+async fn wait_for_full_rf(endpoint: &str, epoch: u64, desired_rf: u32) {
+    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(40);
+    let mut coordinator = CoordinatorClient::connect(endpoint.to_owned())
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    loop {
+        let status = tokio::time::timeout(
+            Duration::from_secs(3),
+            coordinator.get_replica_status(Empty {}),
+        )
+        .await
+        .expect("replica status RPC stalled")
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner();
+        if status.topology_epoch == epoch
+            && !status.ranges.is_empty()
+            && status.ranges.iter().all(|range| {
+                range.current_rf == desired_rf
+                    && range.followers.iter().all(|follower| {
+                        follower.admitted && follower.lag_known && follower.lag_millis <= 5_000
+                    })
+            })
+        {
+            break;
+        }
+        assert!(
+            Instant::now() < deadline,
+            "epoch {epoch} replicas did not converge to RF {desired_rf}: {status:?}"
+        );
+        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(250)).await;
+    }
+}
+
+fn promoted_members(members: &[(String, u16)]) -> Vec<Member> {
+    members
+        .iter()
+        .map(|(node_id, port)| Member {
+            node_id: node_id.clone(),
+            endpoint: format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}"),
+        })
+        .collect()
+}
+
+/// The change's work-step timings, summed.
+///
+/// Every step is truncated to whole milliseconds, so a step that is fast on
+/// the machine running the test is legitimately zero. A test can only require
+/// that the change measured and stored some work, not that one particular step
+/// stayed above the truncation.
+fn total_work_ms(timings: &MigrationTimings) -> u64 {
+    timings.snapshot_copy_ms
+        + timings.changelog_replay_ms
+        + timings.pause_writes_ms
+        + timings.verify_ms
+        + timings.publish_ms
+        + timings.activation_ms
+        + timings.merge_proof_ms
+        + timings.catch_up_ms
+}
+
+fn token_in_range(token: u64, range: &RangeMigration) -> bool {
+    if range.start_exclusive < range.end_inclusive {
+        token > range.start_exclusive && token <= range.end_inclusive
+    } else if range.start_exclusive > range.end_inclusive {
+        token > range.start_exclusive || token <= range.end_inclusive
+    } else {
+        true
+    }
+}
+
+fn moving_key_indexes(
+    topology: &TopologySnapshot,
+    keys: &[Vec<u8>],
+    ranges: &[RangeMigration],
+) -> Vec<usize> {
+    keys.iter()
+        .enumerate()
+        .filter_map(|(index, key)| {
+            let token = topology.key_token(key);
+            ranges
+                .iter()
+                .any(|range| token_in_range(token, range))
+                .then_some(index)
+        })
+        .collect()
+}
+
+fn changing_owner_key_indexes(
+    old: &TopologySnapshot,
+    target: &TopologySnapshot,
+    keys: &[Vec<u8>],
+) -> Vec<usize> {
+    keys.iter()
+        .enumerate()
+        .filter_map(|(index, key)| {
+            (old.owner(key).unwrap().node_id != target.owner(key).unwrap().node_id).then_some(index)
+        })
+        .collect()
+}
+
+async fn execute_while_writing_moving_keys(
+    observer: &HashringClient,
+    executor: HashringClient,
+    plan: TopologyChange,
+    keys: &[Vec<u8>],
+    expected: &std::sync::Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<Vec<Vec<u8>>>>,
+    label: &str,
+) -> TopologyChange {
+    let old_topology = observer.topology().await;
+    let indexes = if plan.direct_merge {
+        changing_owner_key_indexes(&old_topology, &plan.target_topology, keys)
+    } else {
+        moving_key_indexes(&old_topology, keys, &plan.ranges)
+    };
+    assert!(!indexes.is_empty(), "test has no keys in moving ranges");
+    let read_index = indexes[0];
+    let read_key = keys[read_index].clone();
+    let read_token = old_topology.key_token(&read_key);
+    let read_source_endpoint = if plan.direct_merge {
+        old_topology.owner(&read_key).unwrap().endpoint.clone()
+    } else {
+        plan.ranges
+            .iter()
+            .find(|range| token_in_range(read_token, range))
+            .unwrap()
+            .source_endpoint
+            .clone()
+    };
+    let read_epoch = plan.base_epoch;
+    let identity = (
+        plan.change_id.clone(),
+        plan.base_epoch,
+        plan.target_topology.epoch,
+    );
+    let execution = tokio::spawn(async move {
+        executor
+            .execute_topology_change(identity.0, identity.1, identity.2)
+            .await
+            .unwrap()
+    });
+
+    let mut observed_transition = false;
+    for _ in 0..2_000 {
+        if let Some(change) = observer.topology_change().await.unwrap()
+            && (matches!(
+                change.phase,
+                MigrationPhase::CopyingSnapshot | MigrationPhase::ReplayingChangelog
+            ) || (plan.direct_merge
+                && matches!(
+                    change.phase,
+                    MigrationPhase::PausingWrites
+                        | MigrationPhase::Verifying
+                        | MigrationPhase::ReadyToPublish
+                )))
+        {
+            observed_transition = true;
+            break;
+        }
+        assert!(
+            !execution.is_finished(),
+            "{label} completed before transition overlap"
+        );
+        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1)).await;
+    }
+    assert!(
+        observed_transition,
+        "{label} never entered its transition phase"
+    );
+
+    let direct_reader = tokio::spawn(async move {
+        let mut source = DataNodeClient::connect(read_source_endpoint).await.unwrap();
+        let mut successful_reads = 0_u64;
+        for attempt in 0_u64..10_000 {
+            let response = source
+                .get(GetRequest {
+                    key: read_key.clone(),
+                    topology_epoch: read_epoch,
+                    request_id: format!("direct-migration-read-{attempt}"),
+                })
+                .await
+                .unwrap()
+                .into_inner();
+            match response.error {
+                None => successful_reads += 1,
+                Some(error) if error.code == ErrorCode::Moved as i32 => {
+                    return (successful_reads, true);
+                }
+                Some(error) if error.code == ErrorCode::RangeBusy as i32 => {
+                    panic!("source GET was fenced with RangeBusy during migration");
+                }
+                Some(error) => panic!(
+                    "source GET failed during migration: {:?}",
+                    ErrorCode::try_from(error.code)
+                ),
+            }
+            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1)).await;
+        }
+        (successful_reads, false)
+    });
+
+    let mut writes_during_migration = 0_usize;
+    while !execution.is_finished() {
+        let index = indexes[writes_during_migration % indexes.len()];
+        let value = format!("{label}-overlap-{writes_during_migration}").into_bytes();
+        observer
+            .put(keys[index].clone(), value.clone())
+            .await
+            .unwrap();
+        expected.lock().await[index] = value;
+        writes_during_migration += 1;
+    }
+    assert!(
+        writes_during_migration > 0,
+        "{label} had no write overlapping migration"
+    );
+    let completed = execution.await.unwrap();
+    let (direct_reads, saw_moved) = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), direct_reader)
+        .await
+        .expect("direct source reader did not observe the ownership handoff")
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(direct_reads > 0, "{label} had no direct source reads");
+    assert!(saw_moved, "{label} source never redirected after cutover");
+    completed
+}

+        ("--minimum-healthy-followers", "1"),

+        let index = args.iter().position(|arg| arg == flag).unwrap() + 1;
+        args[index] = value.into();
+    }

+        "--migration-timeout-ms".into(),
+        "5000".into(),
+        "--post-publish-delay-ms".into(),
+        "8000".into(),
+    ]);
+    let mut coordinator = spawn_process(&args);
+    wait_for_listener(ports[0]);
+    let mut nodes: Vec<_> = members[..3]
+        .iter()
+        .map(|(node_id, port)| {
+            spawn_process(&[
+                "node".into(),
+                "--id".into(),
+                node_id.clone(),
+                "--listen".into(),
+                format!("127.0.0.1:{port}"),
+                "--coordinator".into(),
+                endpoint.clone(),
+            ])
+        })
+        .collect();
+    let client = HashringClient::connect(&endpoint, Duration::from_secs(90))
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    wait_for_full_rf(&endpoint, 1, 3).await;
+    if first_successor {
+        let policy = client
+            .begin_write_policy_change(WriteAckPolicy::FirstSuccessor)
+            .await
+            .unwrap();
+        client
+            .execute_topology_change(
+                &policy.change_id,
+                policy.base_epoch,
+                policy.target_topology.epoch,
+            )
+            .await
+            .unwrap();
+        wait_for_full_rf(&endpoint, policy.target_topology.epoch, 3).await;
+    }
+    let keys: Vec<_> = (0_u64..80)
+        .map(|index| index.to_be_bytes().to_vec())
+        .collect();
+    for (index, key) in keys.iter().enumerate() {
+        client
+            .put(key.clone(), vec![index as u8; 128])
+            .await
+            .unwrap();
+    }
+    let plan = client
+        .begin_topology_change(promoted_members(&members))
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    let old_topology = plan.base_topology.as_ref().unwrap();
+    assert!(keys.iter().any(|key| {
+        let token = old_topology.key_token(key);
+        plan.ranges.iter().any(|range| token_in_range(token, range))
+    }));
+    let first_target_epoch = plan.target_topology.epoch;
+    let original_change_id = plan.change_id.clone();
+    nodes.push(spawn_process(&[
+        "node".into(),
+        "--id".into(),
+        members[3].0.clone(),
+        "--listen".into(),
+        format!("127.0.0.1:{}", ports[4]),
+        "--coordinator".into(),
+        endpoint.clone(),
+    ]));
+    wait_for_listener(ports[4]);
+    let executor = client.clone();
+    let execution = tokio::spawn(async move {
+        executor
+            .execute_topology_change(&plan.change_id, plan.base_epoch, plan.target_topology.epoch)
+            .await
+    });
+    tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(20), async {
+        loop {
+            if client
+                .topology_change()
+                .await
+                .unwrap()
+                .is_some_and(|change| change.phase == MigrationPhase::Published)
+            {
+                break;
+            }
+            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
+        }
+    })

+    .expect("join did not publish");
+    nodes[3].stop();
+    if restart_coordinator {
+        coordinator.stop();
+        let mut restart_args = coordinator_arguments(ports[0], &state, &[]);
+        restart_args.extend(["--migration-timeout-ms".into(), "5000".into()]);
+        coordinator = spawn_process(&restart_args);
+        wait_for_listener(ports[0]);
+    }
+    let recovery = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(45), async {
+        loop {
+            if let Some(change) = client.topology_change().await.unwrap()
+                && change.phase == MigrationPhase::Complete
+                && change.supersedes_change_id.as_deref() == Some(original_change_id.as_str())
+            {
+                break;
+            }
+            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(250)).await;
+        }
+    })
+    .await;
+    if recovery.is_err() {
+        eprintln!(
+            "recovery change: {:?}",
+            tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), client.topology_change()).await
+        );
+        let mut status_client = CoordinatorClient::connect(endpoint.clone()).await.unwrap();

+            .await
+        );

+    }
+    recovery.expect("published join was not superseded after the joiner died");
+    execution.abort();
+    client.refresh_topology().await.unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(client.topology().await.epoch, first_target_epoch + 1);
+    wait_for_full_rf(&endpoint, first_target_epoch + 1, 3).await;
+    for (index, key) in keys.iter().enumerate() {
+        assert_eq!(
+            client.get(key.clone()).await.unwrap().value,
+            vec![index as u8; 128]
+        );
+    }
+    coordinator.stop();
+}

+        for (index, key) in keys.iter().enumerate() {

+                .put(key.clone(), vec![index as u8; 256])
+                .await
+                .unwrap();
+        }
+    })

+    .expect("initial acknowledged writes stalled");
+    let plan = client
+        .begin_topology_change(promoted_members(&members))
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    let old_topology = client.topology().await;
+    let moving_key = (24_u64..10_000)
+        .map(|index| index.to_be_bytes().to_vec())

+            let token = old_topology.key_token(key);
+            plan.ranges.iter().any(|range| token_in_range(token, range))

+        let mut count = 0_u64;
+        while !writer_stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
+            writer_client
+                .put(writer_key.clone(), count.to_be_bytes().to_vec())

+        .execute_topology_change(&plan.change_id, plan.base_epoch, plan.target_topology.epoch)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();

+    for (index, key) in keys.iter().enumerate() {
+        assert_eq!(
+            client.get(key.clone()).await.unwrap().value,
+            vec![index as u8; 256]

+    }
+
+    let plan = client
+        .begin_topology_change(promoted_members(&members[..3]))
+        .await
+        .unwrap();

+    assert!(plan.ranges.is_empty());
+    assert_ne!(
+        expanded.target_topology.owner(&moving_key).unwrap().node_id,
+        plan.target_topology.owner(&moving_key).unwrap().node_id
+    );
+    let contracted = client
+        .execute_topology_change(&plan.change_id, plan.base_epoch, plan.target_topology.epoch)
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(contracted.phase, MigrationPhase::Complete);
+    wait_for_full_rf(&endpoint, contracted.target_topology.epoch, 3).await;
+    stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
+    let writes = writer.await.unwrap();
+    assert!(writes > 0);
+    assert_eq!(
+        client.get(moving_key).await.unwrap().value,
+        (writes - 1).to_be_bytes()
+    );
+    for (index, key) in keys.iter().enumerate() {
+        assert_eq!(
+            client.get(key.clone()).await.unwrap().value,
+            vec![index as u8; 256]
+        );
+    }

+#[tokio::test]
+async fn follower_admissions_are_seeded_and_survive_coordinator_restart() {
+    let _guard = process_test_lock().lock().await;
+    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
+    let state = directory.path().join("coordinator.redb");
+    let ports = unused_ports(4);
+    let coordinator_port = ports[0];
+    let coordinator_endpoint = format!("http://127.0.0.1:{coordinator_port}");
+    let members: Vec<_> = (1..=3)
+        .map(|index| (format!("node-{index}"), ports[index]))
+        .collect();
+    let mut args = coordinator_arguments(coordinator_port, &state, &members);
+    let vnode_position = args.iter().position(|argument| argument == "32").unwrap();
+    args[vnode_position] = "1".into();
+    let mut coordinator = spawn_process(&args);
+    let client = connect_eventually(&coordinator_endpoint).await;
+    let mut nodes: Vec<_> = members
+        .iter()
+        .map(|(node_id, port)| {
+            spawn_process(&[
+                "node".into(),
+                "--id".into(),
+                node_id.clone(),
+                "--listen".into(),
+                format!("127.0.0.1:{port}"),
+                "--coordinator".into(),
+                coordinator_endpoint.clone(),
+            ])
+        })
+        .collect();
+    for index in 0..40_u64 {
+        let key = index.to_be_bytes().to_vec();
+        client
+            .put(key.clone(), index.to_be_bytes().to_vec())
+            .await
+            .unwrap();
+        if index % 3 == 0 {
+            client.delete(key).await.unwrap();
+        }
+    }
+    let stop_writes = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
+    let writer_client = client.clone();
+    let writer_stop = stop_writes.clone();
+    let writer = tokio::spawn(async move {
+        let mut writes = 0_u64;
+        while !writer_stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
+            let key = b"concurrent-replica-seed".to_vec();
+            writer_client
+                .put(key.clone(), writes.to_be_bytes().to_vec())
+                .await
+                .unwrap();
+            if writes.is_multiple_of(3) {
+                writer_client.delete(key).await.unwrap();
+            }
+            writes += 1;
+            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(2)).await;
+        }
+        writes
+    });
+    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(20);
+    let mut admin = CoordinatorClient::connect(coordinator_endpoint.clone())
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    loop {
+        let status = admin
+            .get_replica_status(Empty {})
+            .await
+            .unwrap()
+            .into_inner();
+        if status.ranges.iter().all(|range| {
+            range.current_rf == 3 && range.followers.iter().all(|follower| follower.admitted)
+        }) {
+            break;
+        }
+        assert!(
+            Instant::now() < deadline,
+            "replica admissions did not complete: {status:?}"
+        );
+        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
+    }
+    stop_writes.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
+    assert!(writer.await.unwrap() > 0);
+    loop {
+        let status = admin
+            .get_replica_status(Empty {})
+            .await
+            .unwrap()
+            .into_inner();
+        if status.ranges.iter().all(|range| {
+            range.followers.iter().all(|follower| {
+                follower.lag_known && follower.stream_head == follower.stream_cursor
+            })
+        }) {
+            break;
+        }
+        assert!(
+            Instant::now() < deadline,
+            "replica streams remained behind: {status:?}"
+        );
+        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
+    }
+    coordinator.stop();
+    coordinator = spawn_process(&coordinator_arguments(coordinator_port, &state, &[]));
+    let _client = connect_eventually(&coordinator_endpoint).await;
+    let mut admin = CoordinatorClient::connect(coordinator_endpoint.clone())
+        .await
+        .unwrap();
+    let status = admin
+        .get_replica_status(Empty {})
+        .await
+        .unwrap()
+        .into_inner();
+    assert!(status.ranges.iter().all(|range| range.current_rf == 3));
+    coordinator.stop();
+    for node in &mut nodes {
+        node.stop();
+    }
+}

+#[ignore = "timed latency experiment; run with --ignored"]
+async fn latency_experiment_measures_one_stage_per_target_rate() {
+    let _guard = process_test_lock().lock().await;
+    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
+    let output_directory = directory.path().join("latency");
+    let output = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_hashring-rs"))
+        .args([
+            "experiment",
+            "--mode",
+            "latency",
+            "--output",
+            output_directory.to_str().unwrap(),
+            "--nodes",
+            "3",
+            "--preload-keys",
+            "500",
+            "--target-rates",
+            "200,400",
+            "--warmup-seconds",
+            "1",
+            "--duration-seconds",
+            "2",
+            "--mix",
+            "90:9:1",
+            "--key-distribution",
+            "uniform",
+            "--virtual-nodes",
+            "16",
+            "--operation-timeout-ms",
+            "10000",
+            "--migration-timeout-ms",
+            "60000",
+        ])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        output.status.success(),
+        "latency experiment failed: {}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+    );
+
+    let manifest: serde_json::Value =
+        serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(output_directory.join("manifest.json")).unwrap())
+            .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(manifest["config"]["mode"], "latency");
+    assert_eq!(manifest["config"]["preload_keys"], 500);
+    assert_eq!(manifest["config"]["key_count"], 500);
+    assert_eq!(
+        manifest["config"]["target_rates"],
+        serde_json::json!([200, 400])
+    );
+    assert_eq!(manifest["config"]["mix"], "90:9:1");
+    assert_eq!(manifest["config"]["key_distribution"], "uniform");
+
+    let summary: serde_json::Value =
+        serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(output_directory.join("summary.json")).unwrap())
+            .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(summary["success"], true, "{}", summary["error"]);
+    // One measurement per target rate, and nothing else: the preload and the
+    // check that follows it are observations of a latency run.
+    let measurements = summary["measurements"].as_object().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(measurements.len(), 2);
+    // Every stage accounts for every request it sent. A stage that starts
+    // with the counters of the stage before it reports that stage's requests
+    // as its own, and a stage that misses its last window is short by a
+    // second's worth of them.
+    for (name, stage) in measurements {
+        let sum = |field: &str| -> u64 {
+            stage[field]
+                .as_object()
+                .map(|entries| {
+                    entries
+                        .values()
+                        .map(|value| value.as_u64().unwrap_or_default())
+                        .sum()
+                })
+                .unwrap_or_default()
+        };
+        assert_eq!(
+            sum("ops") + sum("errors"),
+            stage["issued"].as_u64().unwrap(),
+            "stage {name} does not account for every request it issued"
+        );
+        assert!(
+            (stage["achieved_rate"].as_f64().unwrap() - stage["target_rate"].as_f64().unwrap())
+                .abs()
+                < 1.0,
+            "stage {name} did not run at its target rate: {} against {}",
+            stage["achieved_rate"],
+            stage["target_rate"]
+        );
+    }
+    let stage = &measurements["rate_0"];
+    assert_eq!(stage["target_rate"], 200);
+    assert_eq!(stage["sender_saturated"], false);
+    assert_eq!(stage["late"], 0);
+    assert!(stage["achieved_rate"].as_f64().unwrap() > 0.0);
+    assert!(stage["seconds"].as_f64().unwrap() >= 2.0);
+    // Every request the driver sent is accounted for.
+    let completed: u64 = stage["ops"]
+        .as_object()
+        .unwrap()
+        .values()
+        .map(|value| value.as_u64().unwrap())
+        .sum();
+    assert_eq!(completed, stage["issued"].as_u64().unwrap());
+    assert!(stage["latency_us"]["get"]["samples"].as_u64().unwrap() > 0);
+    assert!(stage["latency_us"]["get"]["p99"].as_u64().unwrap() > 0);
+    // The histogram keeps the longest sample and the number of the samples
+    // that were longer than its range, so a reader can tell a truncated
+    // sample from one that was near the bound.
+    let observed = stage["latency_us"]["get"]["max_observed"].as_u64().unwrap();
+    let bucket = stage["latency_us"]["get"]["max"].as_u64().unwrap();
+    assert!(bucket >= observed && bucket - observed <= bucket / 1_000 + 1);
+    assert_eq!(
+        stage["latency_us"]["get"]["over_range"].as_u64().unwrap(),
+        0
+    );
+    let balance = stage["load_balance"].as_object().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(balance["per_node"].as_object().unwrap().len(), 3);
+    assert!(balance["owned_keys_max_over_mean"].as_f64().unwrap() >= 1.0);
+    let owned: u64 = balance["per_node"]
+        .as_object()
+        .unwrap()
+        .values()
+        .map(|node| node["owned_keys"].as_u64().unwrap())
+        .sum();
+    assert_eq!(owned, 500);
+    // The key space the load left behind was checked.
+    assert_eq!(summary["observations"]["latency_verified_keys"], 500);
+
+    let events = std::fs::read_to_string(output_directory.join("events.jsonl")).unwrap();
+    let samples: Vec<serde_json::Value> = events
+        .lines()
+        .filter(|line| line.contains("\"metrics_sampled\""))
+        .map(|line| serde_json::from_str(line).unwrap())
+        .collect();
+    // One sample per second of every stage, the warmup included.
+    assert_eq!(samples.len(), 6);
+    assert_eq!(samples[0]["fields"]["stage"], "rate_0");
+    assert_eq!(samples[0]["fields"]["warmup"], true);
+    assert_eq!(samples[0]["fields"]["target_rate"], 200);
+    assert_eq!(samples[1]["fields"]["stage"], "rate_0");
+    assert_eq!(samples[1]["fields"]["warmup"], false);
+    assert_eq!(samples[3]["fields"]["stage"], "rate_1");
+    assert_eq!(samples[3]["fields"]["warmup"], true);
+    assert_eq!(samples[3]["fields"]["target_rate"], 400);
+    assert_eq!(samples[4]["fields"]["stage"], "rate_1");
+    assert_eq!(samples[4]["fields"]["warmup"], false);
+    assert!(samples[0]["fields"]["issued"].as_u64().unwrap() > 0);
+    // The window reports its own lag and the sender's, which are two
+    // different numbers.
+    assert!(samples[0]["fields"].get("behind").is_some());
+    assert!(samples[0]["fields"].get("sender_lag").is_some());
+    // The ring is recorded, so a run that has ended can still be read.
+    assert!(events.contains("topology_published"));
+}

+            "--max-dedup-bytes",
+            "33554432",
+        ])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        output.status.success(),
+        "round-trip scaling experiment failed: {}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+    );
+    let summary: serde_json::Value =
+        serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(output_directory.join("summary.json")).unwrap())
+            .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(summary["success"], true);
+
+    // S1's cohorts are verified at the start of S2, so a violation cannot be
+    // attributed to the wrong change.
+    let grow = &summary["observations"]["grow_transition"];
+    assert_eq!(grow["verification"], "deferred_to_next_transition");
+    let shrink = &summary["observations"]["shrink_transition"];
+    assert_eq!(shrink["verification"], "passed");
+    assert_eq!(shrink["direct_merge"], true);
+    assert!(
+        grow["retries_by_reason"]["range_busy"].as_u64().unwrap() > 0,
+        "the grow change produced no client-observed RangeBusy rejection"
+    );
+
+    // The write stop is defined by what the client saw, not by the phases.
+    // Publication, completion, and the RF convergence after completion are
+    // separate time points.
+    for transition in [grow, shrink] {
+        let window = &transition["stop_window"];
+        let first = window["first_range_busy_ms"].as_f64().unwrap();
+        let last = window["last_range_busy_ms"].as_f64().unwrap();
+        let first_ok = window["first_write_ok_ms"].as_f64().unwrap();
+        assert!(first <= last, "{window}");
+        assert!(last <= first_ok, "{window}");
+        assert!(window["observed_ms"].as_f64().unwrap() > 0.0, "{window}");
+        // The write that closed the window had seen at least one rejection
+        // when it started, so it cannot be a write that was already in flight
+        // when the stop began.
+        assert!(
+            window["busy_before_first_ok"].as_u64().unwrap() >= 1,
+            "{window}"
+        );
+        let published = transition["published_ms"]
+            .as_f64()
+            .expect("a completed change records a publication time");
+        let complete = transition["complete_ms"].as_f64().unwrap();
+        assert!(published > 0.0, "{transition}");
+        assert!(complete >= published, "{transition}");
+        // The publication time says where it came from, so a time that was
+        // taken at the completion is not read as an observed publication.
+        let source = transition["published_ms_source"]
+            .as_str()
+            .expect("a completed change records where its publication time came from");
+        assert!(
+            matches!(source, "observed" | "completion_fallback"),
+            "{transition}"
+        );
+        if source == "completion_fallback" {
+            assert_eq!(published, complete, "{transition}");
+        }
+        assert!(
+            transition["full_rf_seconds"].as_f64().unwrap() >= 0.0,
+            "{transition}"
+        );
+    }
+
+    // Every change re-read the keys it moved after the publication, so the
+    // run has the read-after-publish evidence it claims.
+    let probes = &summary["observations"]["scaling_after_publish_probes"];
+    let keys_read = probes["keys_read"].as_array().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(keys_read.len(), 2, "{probes}");
+    for read in keys_read {
+        assert!(read.as_u64().unwrap() > 0, "{probes}");
+    }
+
+    // The migration volume is plan-side: the share of the key space whose
+    // owner changes. The copy path also copies records; a direct merge does
+    // not create ranges at all.
+    let grow_migration = &grow["migration"];
+    let grow_rate = grow_migration["rate"].as_f64().unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        grow_rate > 0.0 && grow_rate < 0.6,
+        "a one-node grow of four members moved {grow_rate} of the keys"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        grow_migration["keys_moved"].as_u64().unwrap(),
+        (grow_rate * grow_migration["keys"].as_u64().unwrap() as f64).round() as u64
+    );
+    assert!(grow_migration["snapshot_records"].as_u64().unwrap() > 0);
+    assert!(grow_migration["ranges"].as_u64().unwrap() > 0);
+    let shrink_migration = &shrink["migration"];
+    assert!(shrink_migration["rate"].as_f64().unwrap() > 0.0);
+    assert_eq!(shrink_migration["ranges"].as_u64().unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(shrink_migration["snapshot_records"].as_u64().unwrap(), 0);
+
+    // The two changes never share a key, so the S2 pools cannot see a value
+    // that the S1 settlement left unknown.
+    let events = std::fs::read_to_string(output_directory.join("events.jsonl")).unwrap();
+    assert!(events.contains("scaling_cohorts_verified"));
+    assert!(events.contains("removed_node_exited"));
+}

+                "6",

+                "--concurrency",

+                "--virtual-nodes",
+                "8",
+                "--value-bytes",
+                "32",
+                "--fault-pre-seconds",
+                "1",
+                "--fault-post-seconds",
+                "1",
+                "--operation-timeout-ms",
+                "2000",
+                "--migration-timeout-ms",

+                "2",

+                "2",

+    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(120);
+    let events = loop {
+        let text =
+            std::fs::read_to_string(output_directory.join("events.jsonl")).unwrap_or_default();
+        let events: Vec<serde_json::Value> = text
+            .lines()
+            .filter_map(|line| serde_json::from_str(line).ok())
+            .collect();
+        if let Some(started) = events
+            .iter()
+            .find(|event| event["event"] == "fault_round_started" && event["fields"]["round"] == 2)
+        {
+            let pid = started["fields"]["processes"]["coordinator"]
+                .as_u64()
+                .unwrap();
+            assert!(
+                Command::new("kill")
+                    .args(["-KILL", &pid.to_string()])
+                    .status()
+                    .unwrap()
+                    .success()

+            break events;
+        }
+        assert!(
+            !experiment.has_exited(),
+            "experiment exited early: {}",
+            std::fs::read_to_string(&stderr_path).unwrap()
+        );
+        assert!(Instant::now() < deadline, "round 2 never started");
+        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
+    };
+    loop {
+        if let Some(status) = experiment.0.try_wait().unwrap() {
+            assert!(!status.success());
+            break;
+        }
+        assert!(
+            Instant::now() < deadline,
+            "experiment did not exit after coordinator failure"
+        );
+        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
+    }
+    let summary: serde_json::Value =
+        serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(output_directory.join("summary.json")).unwrap())
+            .unwrap();
+    let observations = &summary["observations"];
+    assert_eq!(summary["success"], false);
+    assert_eq!(observations["fault_rounds_requested"], 2);
+    assert_eq!(observations["fault_rounds_completed"], 1);
+    assert_eq!(observations["fault_rounds"].as_array().unwrap().len(), 1);
+    assert!(
+        observations["fault_failures"]
+            .as_array()
+            .unwrap()
+            .iter()
+            .any(|failure| failure
+                .as_str()
+                .unwrap()
+                .contains("round 2: infrastructure error"))
+    );
+    assert!(summary["measurements"]["fault_round_1_load"].is_object());
+    let completed = events
+        .iter()
+        .find(|event| event["event"] == "fault_round_complete")
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(observations["fault_rounds"][0], completed["fields"]);

+    // The pre-failure status must follow the active pre-window, not precede it.
+    let event_time = |name| {
+        events.iter().find(|event| event["event"] == name).unwrap()["unix_ms"]
+            .as_u64()
+            .unwrap()
+    };
+    assert!(
+        event_time("fault_pre_failure_replica_progress") >= event_time("fault_load_started") + 1000
+    );

+}

+//! Concurrent same-key histories.
+//!
+//! Several clients issue PUT, GET, and DELETE against the same keys. Every
+//! operation records its invocation and completion time, arguments, result,
+//! returned version, and topology epoch. The checker below then asks whether
+//! the mutations, ordered by the versions the owner assigned to them, satisfy
+//! every real-time constraint and explain every read. A history that does not
+//! is not linearizable.
+
+use std::{
+    collections::BTreeMap,
+    fs,
+    path::PathBuf,
+    sync::{
+        Arc,
+        atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering},
+    },
+    time::{Duration, Instant, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH},
+};
+
+use hashring_client::{ClientError, HashringClient};
+use hashring_core::{
+    migration::MigrationPhase,
+    proto::{ErrorCode, RecordVersion},
+    topology::Member,
+};
+use serde_json::json;
+use tokio::sync::{Barrier, Mutex};
+
+use super::{
+    Process, connect_eventually, coordinator_arguments, process_test_lock, spawn_process,
+    unused_ports, wait_for_full_rf, wait_for_listener,
+};
+
+const CLIENTS: usize = 4;
+const OPERATIONS_PER_CLIENT: u64 = 40;
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
+enum MutationKind {
+    Put(Vec<u8>),
+    Delete,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
+struct Mutation {
+    client: usize,
+    sequence: u64,
+    key: u64,
+    kind: MutationKind,
+    version: RecordVersion,
+    invoked: Instant,
+    completed: Instant,
+    invoked_unix_ms: u128,
+    completed_unix_ms: u128,
+    topology_epoch: u64,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
+enum ReadObservation {
+    Present {
+        value: Vec<u8>,
+        version: RecordVersion,
+    },
+    Absent,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
+struct Read {
+    client: usize,
+    sequence: u64,
+    key: u64,
+    observation: ReadObservation,
+    invoked: Instant,
+    completed: Instant,
+    invoked_unix_ms: u128,
+    completed_unix_ms: u128,
+    topology_epoch: u64,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
+enum Entry {
+    Mutation(Mutation),
+    Read(Read),
+}
+
+fn version_key(version: &RecordVersion) -> (u64, u64) {
+    (version.topology_epoch, version.owner_sequence)
+}
+
+fn describe_version(version: &RecordVersion) -> String {
+    format!(
+        "epoch={} sequence={} owner={}",
+        version.topology_epoch, version.owner_sequence, version.owner_node_id
+    )
+}
+
+fn unix_ms_now() -> u128 {
+    SystemTime::now()
+        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
+        .expect("the system clock is after the Unix epoch")
+        .as_millis()
+}
+
+/// A state of the single-key register.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+enum State {
+    Absent,
+    Present {
+        value: Vec<u8>,
+        version: RecordVersion,
+    },
+}
+
+fn state_after(mutations: &[&Mutation], prefix: usize) -> State {
+    match prefix.checked_sub(1).and_then(|index| mutations.get(index)) {
+        None => State::Absent,
+        Some(mutation) => match &mutation.kind {
+            MutationKind::Delete => State::Absent,
+            MutationKind::Put(value) => State::Present {
+                value: value.clone(),
+                version: mutation.version.clone(),
+            },
+        },
+    }
+}
+
+fn observation_matches(state: &State, observation: &ReadObservation) -> bool {
+    match (state, observation) {
+        (State::Absent, ReadObservation::Absent) => true,
+        (
+            State::Present { value, version },
+            ReadObservation::Present {
+                value: observed_value,
+                version: observed_version,
+            },
+        ) => value == observed_value && version == observed_version,
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}
+
+/// Checks one key's history against a single-register model.
+///
+/// Mutations are ordered by the version their owner assigned. That order is
+/// the owner's application order, so a mutation that completed before another
+/// one started must also have a smaller version. A read must fit between two
+/// mutations: every mutation before its serialization point had started before
+/// the read completed, and every mutation after it completed after the read
+/// started.
+fn check_key_history(key: u64, entries: &[Entry], phase: &str) {
+    let mut mutations: Vec<&Mutation> = entries
+        .iter()
+        .filter_map(|entry| match entry {
+            Entry::Mutation(mutation) if mutation.key == key => Some(mutation),
+            _ => None,
+        })
+        .collect();
+    let mut reads: Vec<&Read> = entries
+        .iter()
+        .filter_map(|entry| match entry {
+            Entry::Read(read) if read.key == key => Some(read),
+            _ => None,
+        })
+        .collect();
+    mutations.sort_by_key(|mutation| version_key(&mutation.version));
+    assert!(!mutations.is_empty(), "{phase}: key {key} has no mutations");
+
+    let positions: BTreeMap<(u64, u64), usize> = mutations
+        .iter()
+        .enumerate()
+        .map(|(index, mutation)| (version_key(&mutation.version), index))
+        .collect();
+    assert_eq!(
+        positions.len(),
+        mutations.len(),
+        "{phase}: two mutations of key {key} share a version"
+    );
+    for (index, mutation) in mutations.iter().enumerate() {
+        assert_eq!(
+            positions[&version_key(&mutation.version)],
+            index,
+            "{phase}: version order of key {key} is inconsistent"
+        );
+    }
+
+    // The owner's version order must respect real time. A mutation that
+    // completed before another was invoked cannot be ordered after it.
+    for later in &mutations {
+        for earlier in &mutations {
+            if earlier.completed < later.invoked {
+                let earlier_index = positions[&version_key(&earlier.version)];
+                let later_index = positions[&version_key(&later.version)];
+                assert!(
+                    earlier_index < later_index,
+                    "{phase}: key {key} mutation client {} sequence {} ({}) at epoch {} completed before client {} sequence {} ({}) at epoch {} was invoked, but has the later version",
+                    earlier.client,
+                    earlier.sequence,
+                    describe_version(&earlier.version),
+                    earlier.topology_epoch,
+                    later.client,
+                    later.sequence,
+                    describe_version(&later.version),
+                    later.topology_epoch
+                );
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    // Completion order is a topological order of read-to-read real time.
+    // Choose the earliest matching prefix at or after every predecessor's
+    // position. This greedy choice leaves all later reads the most room;
+    // overlapping reads may still serialize in either order.
+    reads.sort_by_key(|read| read.completed);
+    let mut serialized_reads: Vec<(&Read, usize)> = Vec::new();
+    for read in reads {
+        let minimum_prefix = serialized_reads
+            .iter()
+            .filter(|(earlier, _)| earlier.completed < read.invoked)
+            .map(|(_, prefix)| *prefix)
+            .max()
+            .unwrap_or(0);
+        let matching_prefixes: Vec<usize> = (minimum_prefix..=mutations.len())
+            .filter(|prefix| {
+                observation_matches(&state_after(&mutations, *prefix), &read.observation)
+                    && mutations[..*prefix]
+                        .iter()
+                        .all(|mutation| mutation.invoked < read.completed)
+                    && mutations[*prefix..]
+                        .iter()
+                        .all(|mutation| mutation.completed > read.invoked)
+            })
+            .collect();
+        assert!(
+            !matching_prefixes.is_empty(),
+            "{phase}: key {key} read by client {} sequence {} ({:?}) at epoch {} has no legal serialization point respecting earlier reads among {} mutations",
+            read.client,
+            read.sequence,
+            read.observation,
+            read.topology_epoch,
+            mutations.len()
+        );
+        serialized_reads.push((read, matching_prefixes[0]));
+    }
+}
+
+struct Cluster {
+    endpoint: String,
+    ports: Vec<u16>,
+    members: Vec<(String, u16)>,
+    _coordinator: Process,
+    nodes: Vec<Process>,
+    client: HashringClient,
+}
+
+impl Cluster {
+    fn member_list(&self, prefix: usize) -> Vec<Member> {
+        self.members[..prefix]
+            .iter()
+            .map(|(node_id, port)| Member {
+                node_id: node_id.clone(),
+                endpoint: format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}"),
+            })
+            .collect()
+    }
+}
